reports.title: How to open the MEDICINE 2040 hub
reports.markdown:
# How to open the MEDICINE 2040 hub

## Option 1: single file (no server)
Double-click `deliverables/MEDICINE_2040_Hub.html`. All data and code are inlined (about 7 MB); routing is hash-based, so it works from `file://`.

## Option 2: served app
```bash
cd ~/Desktop/MEDICINE
./launch.sh     # validate -> data -> build -> single file -> test -> serve
# open http://127.0.0.1:4173/
```
Binds to 127.0.0.1 only. Requires Node >= 18 and Python >= 3.9. Manual: `python3 scripts/build_app_data.py`, then in `executive_application/`: `npm install && npm run build && python3 ../scripts/build_single_file.py && npm test && npm run preview`.

## Layout
Top bar (all eleven pillars visible without scrolling at 1200 px and wider; below that the bar wraps to two rows): Overview, Companies, Commercial, R&D / Pipeline, Data · AI · Robotics, Partnerships, Policy, Takeda Baseline, Future Plan (red forward-looking banner on every page), Evidence & Method, Ask. Every Markdown report in the research tree opens in the reader (`#/read/<path>`); claim and source ID chips open the evidence drawer.

## Ask (grounded Q&A)
Default is retrieval-only: BM25 over claims, report sections and sources, answered with cited bullets, or "No evidence in the corpus". No model, no network.

Optional open-source LLM synthesis (toggle on the Ask page, off by default):
```bash
brew install ollama && ollama pull qwen2.5:3b && ollama serve
```
The page checks `http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/tags`. From the served app this works as is. If you opened the single file from `file://`, start Ollama with `OLLAMA_ORIGINS=* ollama serve`. Alternatively choose "OpenAI-compatible endpoint" and enter a base URL, model and key (stored only in this browser's localStorage). Only the question and the retrieved passages are sent; answers are labelled and their citations audited against the retrieved set.

### Notes on synthesis
- The prompt asks the model to answer part by part: what the passages support (with claim IDs) and `Not stated in the passages.` for parts they do not cover. Temperature is 0 and every cited claim ID is audited against the retrieved passages.
- A compound question whose whole text finds no evidence is split into its sub-questions; supported parts are answered and the rest are listed as not covered.
- From a served app (`http://127.0.0.1:4173`) Ollama needs no extra setting. From the single file (`file://`), the browser origin is `null`: start Ollama with `OLLAMA_ORIGINS=* ollama serve`.
- Command-line check without a browser: `cd executive_application && node tests/llm_probe.mjs "<question>"`.

## Deliverables
`deliverables/*.md` (executive summary, competitor comparison, Takeda strategy, investment roadmap, recommendations) open first in the Overview reading guide, in the Future Plan hub and in Evidence & Method.

Refresh after new research lands: `./launch.sh` (the pipeline fails loudly on any unknown claim, assumption or bet ID).

# Deliverables: MEDICINE 2040

Cutoff 2026-11-21. These five documents are the executive output of the project. They summarise, and do not replace, the evidence library and the strategy files. They cite strategy v2, which is the v1 strategy as amended by the [Director decision record](../strategy/critical_challenges/DIRECTOR_DECISION_RECORD.md). The v1 strategy files are not yet rewritten to match (pending the A11c-bis pass), so read the deliverables where the two differ.

| File | What it is | For whom | Evidence lives in |
|---|---|---|---|
| [executive_summary.md](executive_summary.md) | The ten-step storyline (what is changing, who is winning, why, what is defensible, what Takeda has, where the opportunity is, what to build, invest, execute, measure), reader notes for CEO, CFO, R&D, CTO and commercial leaders, and a box on what we could be wrong about | Executive team, Board | [executive_strategy_narrative.md](../strategy/takeda_future_2030_2040/executive_strategy_narrative.md), [counterarguments](../strategy/critical_challenges/counterarguments_and_uncertainty.md) |
| [competitor_comparison.md](competitor_comparison.md) | Answers to the ten comparison questions on Lilly, J&J, AbbVie and Takeda, the valid comparison tables, and the comparisons refused and why | Strategy, corporate development, R&D leadership | [master_comparison.md](../New_mediciine/cross_company_analysis/master_comparison.md), [matrices and lessons](../New_mediciine/cross_company_analysis/map.md), four [company dossiers](../New_mediciine/companies/) |
| [takeda_strategy.md](takeda_strategy.md) | Capability baseline, seven transformation domains, 18 bets with v2 decisions and moat mechanisms, sequencing, what not to do | Executive team, R&D, digital, commercial | [strategic_bets.md](../strategy/investment_theses/strategic_bets.md), [future_of_pharma](../strategy/future_of_pharma/map.md), [capability baseline](../New_mediciine/companies/takeda_public_baseline/capability_baseline/capability_baseline.md) |
| [investment_roadmap.md](investment_roadmap.md) | Three portfolios plus the v2 balanced portfolio, stage gates, half-year roadmap, scenario robustness, sensitivity | CFO, portfolio review committee | [capital_allocation.md](../strategy/financial_cases/capital_allocation.md), [stage_gates.md](../strategy/financial_cases/stage_gates.md), [roadmap](../strategy/strategic_roadmap/roadmap_2027_2040.md), [scenarios](../strategy/scenarios/scenarios_2027_2040.md), [stress test](../strategy/critical_challenges/scenario_stress_test.md) |
| [recommendations.md](recommendations.md) | First 12 months, what to avoid, scale criteria, success metrics, open questions needing Takeda-internal data | Executive team, bet owners | [stage_gates.md](../strategy/financial_cases/stage_gates.md), [internal-validation backlog](../New_mediciine/companies/takeda_public_baseline/internal_validation_backlog/backlog.md) |

Not owned by this set: [OPEN_APPLICATION.md](OPEN_APPLICATION.md) and [MEDICINE_2040_Hub.html](MEDICINE_2040_Hub.html) (the application and hub).

## Rules these documents follow

- Every material sentence cites a claim (CLM-), bet (BET-) or assumption (ASM-) ID, or is labelled INTERPRETATION, HYPOTHESIS, SCENARIO or RECOMMENDATION.
- Claim values were looked up in the [claims registry](../New_mediciine/evidence_library/claims_registry.jsonl); the 42 claims that carry a `correction` field are cited with the correction applied.
- Every dollar figure for a bet is an ASSUMPTION. Takeda's budget, forecasts and internal data are not public. No NPV is reported.
- Scenarios (SCN-1 to SCN-5) are conditional futures, not forecasts.
- Comparisons the audit marks invalid are not made; they are listed in the competitor comparison.
- Where a bet's decision or size differs between the v1 bets file and the Director record, the deliverables say "v2 per Director decision record".

## Known limits

- The bet-level v2 sizes for BET-02 and BET-07, and the v2 horizon split beyond H1, are not in the Director record; the deliverables use the council memo's arithmetic and say so.
- The constrained and ambitious portfolios are v2 figures (rescaled by A11c-bis).
- BET-18's A-M template is not yet written.
- Takeda's Gate 1 verdict was FAIL (repairable); v1.1 repairs are applied and a re-audit is pending.

## How to regenerate

1. Update the evidence: `python3 scripts/validate_registries.py` (expect PASS at 524 sources and 1,401 claims) after any registry change; new claims go through the append-only registry process, not through these files.
2. Update the strategy: run the A11c-bis pass so the strategy files in `strategy/` match the Director record; refresh [strategy/data](../strategy/) if the contract requires it.
3. Re-run the A16 brief ([WAVE5_A16_deliverables.md](../research_methodology/briefs/WAVE5_A16_deliverables.md)) against the updated inputs. Respect the word limits (summary 1,800; comparison 2,500; strategy 3,000; roadmap 2,500; recommendations 1,500).
4. Check links with `python3 scripts/check_links.py` and re-count distinct claim IDs against the registry.

## How to read / evidence standard

524 sources, 1,401 claims, cutoff 2026-11-21. Audit results: Gate 1 passed Lilly, conditionally passed J&J and AbbVie, and failed Takeda as repairable ([verdicts](../quality/citation_audits/gate1_verdicts.md)). Wave-1 scorecard: A1 Lilly 13/16, A2 J&J 14/16, A3 AbbVie 12/16, A9 12/16 and A4 13/16 accepted; A5 Takeda 11/16 and A6 9/16 marked REVISE ([wave 1](../quality/evaluation_results/wave1_scorecard.md)). Wave-2/3 scorecard: A12 13/16 and A14 13/16 accepted; strategy shard 12/16 accepted; A8 policy 9/16 and A7 commercial 11/16 marked REVISE ([wave 2](../quality/evaluation_results/wave2_scorecard.md)). Independent corroboration is recorded on 2 of 1,401 claims, and most company claims rest on a single interested source. The challenge record ran 119 council verdicts (45 support, 64 conditional, 10 oppose) and a 95-item uncertainty register.

reports.title: Competitor comparison: Lilly, J&J, AbbVie and the Takeda baseline
reports.markdown:
# Competitor comparison: Lilly, J&J, AbbVie and the Takeda baseline

Cutoff 2026-11-21. Lilly and AbbVie report calendar years. J&J FY2025 is the 52 weeks to 2025-12-28 [CLM-002005]. Takeda FY2025 is April 2025 to March 2026 [CLM-005000]. 2026 figures are partial periods [CLM-001032] [CLM-005011]. Takeda stays in JPY, so growth rates and shares are compared and absolute JPY is never set against USD. The comparison is descriptive; no score or rank is given. Full detail: [master_comparison.md](../New_mediciine/cross_company_analysis/master_comparison.md).

**Audit corrections applied.** AbbVie and J&J "long-term debt" series include the current portion; non-current is USD 58,941m (AbbVie) and USD 39,438m (J&J) at FY2025 [CLM-000070] [CLM-000132]. OTTAVA has an announced first installation site, not a completed install [CLM-000284]. AbbVie ImmunoGen is USD 9.2bn net of cash, and ImmunoGen plus Cerevel USD 17.5bn net [CLM-003086]. Takeda's cell-therapy impairment is JPY 58.2bn, not 58.0bn [CLM-005025] [CLM-009084]. The restructuring cost series is about JPY 150bn, 170.0bn, then 160.0bn [CLM-005078]. Morphic is USD 3.2bn headline against a 2.55bn audited charge [CLM-009002]. The Lilly lab sold to Arctoris has no supported Strateos link [CLM-006017].

## Answers to the ten comparison questions

**1. Why is Lilly winning where it wins?** Revenue rose from USD 28.3bn to USD 65.2bn (FY2021-FY2025) [CLM-000133] [CLM-000137] because tirzepatide went from launch in 2022 to 56.0% of sales [CLM-001003]. Pre-tax margin rose from 21.7% to 39.5% [CLM-001007]. Capex rose from USD 1.3bn to USD 7.8bn [CLM-000168] [CLM-000172]. The evidenced mechanisms are a launched incretin with strong trial results, capacity built after a shortage, a cash-pay channel and a follow-on pipeline [CLM-001042] [CLM-001030]. Durability is not shown: realised prices fell 15% in Q3 2026 and about USD 900m of that quarter was one-off [CLM-014003]. *(INTERPRETATION)* Lilly is winning in a category where demand exceeded supply; the registry does not show the advantage persisting once supply and competition normalise.

**2. What is distinctive about J&J's pharma and MedTech combination, and where is the synergy unevidenced?** J&J is the only one of the four with a MedTech segment (USD 33.8bn beside Innovative Medicine USD 60.4bn) [CLM-000253]. MedTech grew 2.5% in Q3 2026 and J&J announced the Orthopaedics separation [CLM-002060] [CLM-002037]. J&J claims cardiovascular leadership; no cross-segment synergy is disclosed [CLM-002074]. The evidenced feature is diversification: the largest brand is 15.2% of revenue [CLM-002073]. Offsetting evidence: the Impella recall and the Varipulse pause [CLM-002046] [CLM-002044].

**3. How did AbbVie absorb the Humira loss of exclusivity?** Global Humira fell from USD 21,237m (2022) to 4,540m (2025), -78.6% *(computed)* [CLM-003002]. Skyrizi plus Rinvoq rose by USD 18,179m against a Humira loss of 16,697m, and total revenue passed its 2022 peak only in 2025 [CLM-003014] [CLM-003015]. Three mechanisms are evidenced: successors already marketed and extended across Humira's indications [CLM-003084]; rebate-for-access contracting that held at least 97% of volume to March 2024 [CLM-003007]; and settlements putting Rinvoq entry no earlier than April 2037 [CLM-003021]. Steep U.S. declines (-41% in 2024, -57% in 2025) followed the April 2024 formulary change, an association rather than proven causation [CLM-003010].

**4. Who converts R&D into commercial outcomes best?** No ranking is supported. R&D intensity moved from 24.5% to 20.5% at Lilly, held near 15.6% at J&J, rose from 12.6% to 14.9% at AbbVie and held 14.7-15.0% at Takeda *(computed)* [CLM-001006] [CLM-000085] [CLM-000015] [CLM-005004]. The share of FY2025 revenue from post-2021 molecules (Lilly at least 56.0%, J&J at least 3.2%, AbbVie at least 1.8%) is invalid as a productivity measure: it penalises lifecycle growth, mixes acquired and in-house assets, and Takeda is not computable [CLM-012013] [CLM-012014] [CLM-000270]. *(INTERPRETATION)* The narrow supportable statement is that Lilly's growth comes from a molecule approved inside the window and AbbVie's from molecules approved before it.

**5. Who has the most defensible technology ecosystem?** The registry cannot rank. Lilly has the largest evidenced build (LillyPod, TuneLab) with no outcome shown [CLM-006004] [CLM-000280] [CLM-006007]. J&J holds the only regulator records, and they concern devices [CLM-014022] [CLM-014026]. AbbVie has the ARCH knowledge graph [CLM-006032]. Takeda is partnership-led [CLM-006039] [CLM-006041]. *(HYPOTHESIS)* "Lilly is most defensible" rests on proprietary data the company estimates at over USD 1bn [CLM-000280] [CLM-006055].

**6. Which AI investments are operationally meaningful?** Operational with disclosed scale: LillyPod (1,016 GPUs) [CLM-006004]; ARCH (124 TB, built by fewer than ten full-time staff) [CLM-006032]; Takeda's 170+ Lessines predictive-maintenance agents [CLM-014041]. None has independent evidence of effect on cost, cycle time or revenue [CLM-006054, wording stronger than its sources support per audit]. The NVIDIA lab is an announcement [CLM-000281].

**7. Who has repeatable discovery and development capability?** The evidence shows repetition, not quality. CDER novel approvals in the window: Lilly 8, J&J 5, AbbVie 5, Takeda 3 [CLM-012000] [CLM-012007] [CLM-012008] [CLM-012012] [CLM-012018]. AbbVie's are mostly acquired or partnered, with growth from supplements [CLM-012013] [CLM-012033]. Takeda delivered three positive Phase 3 readouts on its 2024 plan [CLM-005042]. Repeatability is partly unproven everywhere: Takeda's replacement set arrived only in August 2026 [CLM-005029] [CLM-005032].

**8. Which partnerships create durable options?** Option structures exist at AbbVie (ADARx USD 335m upfront) [CLM-009061], Takeda (Innovent USD 1.2bn upfront) [CLM-009078] and Lilly (CVRs) [CLM-009099]. No option from the window has produced an approved product, so durability is a *(HYPOTHESIS)* [CLM-009097]. Realised partnership value so far: J&J Momenta (Imaavy), Lilly Loxo, AbbVie ImmunoGen, and Takeda's Protagonist asset [CLM-009044] [CLM-009031] [CLM-012151].

**9. What does each do better than the other two, and where is each vulnerable?** See the table below.

**10. What would change positions by 2035?** *(HYPOTHESIS; anchors are dated claims.)* Lilly: tirzepatide patent to 2036, Trulicity patent 2027, Medicare prices for Trulicity and Verzenio from 2028 [CLM-000250] [CLM-008015]. J&J: Stelara erosion and talc resolution [CLM-002060] [CLM-002062]. AbbVie: Skyrizi and Rinvoq composition patents 2033, Rinvoq entry no earlier than April 2037 [CLM-003021]. Takeda: Entyvio exclusivity loss and 2032 patents, Trintellix generics after December 2026, launch execution, the Amitiza appeal [CLM-005017] [CLM-005016] [CLM-014048].

## Strengths and vulnerabilities (evidence-limited; relative descriptions, not rankings)

| Company | Distinguishing strength | Largest documented vulnerability |
|---|---|---|
| Lilly | Growth with margin expansion and capacity build [CLM-000137] [CLM-001007] [CLM-000172] | Tirzepatide 56.0% of revenue; 15% price decline in Q3 2026 [CLM-001003] [CLM-014003] |
| J&J | Diversified absorption of a large LOE: group sales +6.0% with Stelara -41.3% [CLM-000253] [CLM-000254] | Stelara still falling (about 690 basis-point drag in Q3 2026); talc [CLM-002060] [CLM-002062] |
| AbbVie | Replacing a dominant franchise with pre-built successors [CLM-003014] | Successor concentration at 42.3% *(computed)*; USD 4.5bn emraclidine impairment [CLM-000266] [CLM-003057] |
| Takeda | Plasma-derived network and in-house orexin discovery [CLM-005063] [CLM-005048] | Entyvio 21% with exclusivity loss ahead; flat revenue; Amitiza provision [CLM-005009] [CLM-005017] [CLM-005014] |

## Valid comparison tables

**FY2025 scale and concentration (within-company shares; do not sum across columns).**

| Measure | Lilly | J&J | AbbVie | Takeda |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Largest product share of revenue | Tirzepatide 56.0% [CLM-001003] | DARZALEX 15.2% [CLM-002073] | Skyrizi + Rinvoq 42.3% *(computed)* [CLM-000266] | Entyvio 21% [CLM-005009] |
| Revenue | USD 65,179m [CLM-000137] | USD 94,193m [CLM-000253] | USD 61,160m [CLM-000262] | JPY 4,505.7bn [CLM-005002] |
| Capex (as filed) | USD 7,841m [CLM-000172] | USD 4,832m [CLM-000110] | USD 1,214m [CLM-000045] | JPY 426.9bn including intangibles [CLM-005007] |
| R&D | USD 13,337m [CLM-014004] | USD 14,665m [CLM-000085] | USD 9,096m [CLM-000015] | JPY 675.9bn [CLM-005004] |

Capex bases differ (Takeda includes intangibles), so the capex row is not compared across columns [CLM-005007].

**Loss-of-exclusivity cliffs (each against its own company's revenue).**

| Product | Peak | Latest | Change | Share of company revenue |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Humira (AbbVie) | USD 21,237m (2022) | 4,540m (2025) | -78.6% *(computed)* | 36.6% to 7.4% *(computed)* [CLM-003002] [CLM-003004] |
| Stelara (J&J) | USD 10,858m (FY2023) | 6,078m (FY2025) | -44.0% *(computed)* | 12.8% to 6.5% *(computed)* [CLM-002022] |
| Vyvanse (Takeda) | JPY 423.2bn (FY2023) | 203.2bn (FY2025) | -52.0% *(computed)* | 9.9% to 4.5% *(computed)* [CLM-005015] |
| Trulicity (Lilly) | USD 7,439.7m (FY2022) | 4,276m (FY2025) | -42.5% *(computed)*; substitution by tirzepatide, not an LOE [CLM-001004] | 26.1% to 6.6% *(computed)* |

Replacement evidence: AbbVie's successors replaced 109% of the Humira loss *(computed)* [CLM-003014]; Tremfya offset about 35% of the FY2025 Stelara loss *(computed)* [CLM-000256] [CLM-002026]; Takeda's replacement set was approved only in August 2026 [CLM-005029] [CLM-005032].

**Capability matrix, selected rows (full 15 rows: [competitive_capability_matrix.md](../New_mediciine/cross_company_analysis/competitive_capability_matrix.md)).**

| Capability | Lilly | J&J | AbbVie | Takeda |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| External assets | Annual acquired IPR&D USD 2.9-3.8bn [CLM-000182] | Abiomed, Shockwave, Intra-Cellular; USD 17.5bn net in FY2025 [CLM-009049] | Two large buys plus USD 0.6-1.0bn a year of early deals [CLM-009097] | One flagship purchase (Nimbus USD 4.0bn upfront), then licences [CLM-009076] [CLM-009098] |
| Payer contracting | Lost then regained CVS Caremark status for Zepbound [CLM-007011] [CLM-007013] | Stelara displaced by PBM-affiliated biosimilars [CLM-007015] [CLM-007016] | At least 97% of volume held to March 2024, then co-brand [CLM-003007] | No contracting evidence found; rebates undisclosed [CLM-007025] |
| Direct-to-patient cash pay | LillyDirect [CLM-001042] [CLM-007002] | TrumpRx listing only [CLM-007009] | TrumpRx for Humira [CLM-003081] | None found [CLM-007039] |
| Data and AI | LillyPod, TuneLab; no outcome [CLM-006004] [CLM-000280] | Self-reported pilots [CLM-006018] | ARCH operational [CLM-006032] | Agent platform; 63.4% usage is an adoption metric [CLM-005058] [CLM-014043] |
| Automation | Remote lab divested [CLM-006013] | Surgical robots with FDA records [CLM-014022] | No evidence found | No robotics evidence; Lessines agents [CLM-005067] [CLM-014041] |
| Stop discipline | Phase 2 programmes stopped on data [CLM-001019] | Aticaprant stopped [CLM-002039] | Emraclidine written down within days [CLM-003054] [CLM-003057] | Soticlestat, cell therapy [CLM-005024] [CLM-005025] |

"No evidence found" means no opened source shows the capability, not that it is absent [CLM-005080].

## Comparisons we refused to make, and why

| Comparison | Why refused |
|---|---|
| Single LOE "resilience score" or management-quality ranking | Cliffs differ in size (36.6%, 12.8% and 9.9% of revenue), age, acquisitions and price mechanism [CLM-003004] [CLM-002022] [CLM-005015] |
| Novel approvals per R&D dollar | Counts of 3 to 8, 2026 approvals funded earlier, acquired sponsors, different R&D boundaries [CLM-012000] [CLM-012013] [CLM-000270] |
| New-molecule revenue share as productivity | Penalises lifecycle growth; Takeda not computable [CLM-012147] |
| Profit-margin ranking | US GAAP with special items against IFRS with a company core measure [CLM-002016] [CLM-003041] [CLM-005014] |
| Leverage ranking | No EBITDA for the three U.S. companies; the Takeda 2.6x could not be located by the audit [CLM-005005] |
| Deal-value ranking | Announced, consideration, net-of-cash, expensed and upfront bases are mixed [CLM-003053] [CLM-009002] [CLM-009098] |
| Patient-programme size | Different units: members, patients, cumulative recipients [CLM-007036] [CLM-007004] [CLM-007037] |
| Robotics "leader" | Product, lab and plant robotics are different things [CLM-006054] |
| Defensible-ecosystem ranking | No outcome evidence for any company [CLM-006054] |
| Takeda against Lilly, J&J or AbbVie on any strategy file | The audit bounds cross-company comparisons used by the bets [CLM-012013] [CLM-009098] [CLM-005007] |

Missing data that blocked comparisons: FY2025 product revenue for several launches, Takeda's pre-FY2023 Vyvanse peak and acquired-IPR&D treatment, the DARZALEX patent dates, the origin of Skyrizi and Rinvoq, the self-pay share of Zepbound, and independent outcomes for AI, patient programmes and robotics ([evidence_gaps.md](../New_mediciine/cross_company_analysis/evidence_gaps.md)).

## What the comparison means for Takeda

*(INTERPRETATION)* The one mechanism that transfers cleanly from the peer record is the pre-built successor: AbbVie's replacement worked because the successors were already launched across the incumbent's indications [CLM-003084]. Takeda's counterpart (zasocitinib breadth, BET-05) is the best-evidenced bet in the set. Lessons and their transfer verdicts: [lessons_for_takeda.md](../New_mediciine/cross_company_analysis/lessons_for_takeda.md). The strategy is in [takeda_strategy.md](takeda_strategy.md).

## How to read / evidence standard

524 sources, 1,401 claims, cutoff 2026-11-21. Numbers come from claim IDs in the [claims registry](../New_mediciine/evidence_library/claims_registry.jsonl), honouring correction fields; *(computed)* marks arithmetic on cited claims. Dossiers: [Lilly](../New_mediciine/companies/eli_lilly/master_report.md), [J&J](../New_mediciine/companies/johnson_johnson/master_report.md), [AbbVie](../New_mediciine/companies/abbvie/master_report.md), [Takeda](../New_mediciine/companies/takeda_public_baseline/master_report.md) (all v1.1). Audit: Gate 1 passed Lilly, conditionally passed J&J and AbbVie, and failed Takeda as repairable with v1.1 repairs applied and a re-audit pending ([verdicts](../quality/citation_audits/gate1_verdicts.md)). Independent corroboration is recorded on 2 of 1,401 claims, and 71 of 83 Takeda claims rest on a single interested source [CLM-000280] [CLM-005033].

reports.title: MEDICINE 2040: executive summary for Takeda
reports.markdown:
# MEDICINE 2040: executive summary for Takeda

Cutoff 2026-11-21. Takeda fiscal year (FY) 2025 = April 2025 to March 2026 [CLM-005000]. Takeda amounts stay in JPY. Every dollar figure for a strategic bet is an ASSUMPTION with an ID in the [assumptions register](../strategy/financial_cases/assumptions_register.md); Takeda's own budget is not public (IVB-014).

**Challenge status.** The Strategic Council (119 verdicts: 45 support, 64 conditional, 10 oppose), the red team and the stress test have run. The Director's decisions of 2026-11-21 are applied here as **strategy v2** ([decision record](../strategy/critical_challenges/DIRECTOR_DECISION_RECORD.md)). The v1 strategy files have not yet been rewritten to match, so where they differ this summary says "v2 per Director decision record".

## 1. What is changing

Entyvio was JPY 958.0bn, 21% of FY2025 revenue [CLM-005009]. Takeda says it loses regulatory exclusivity in the latter half of the decade and that some patents expire in 2032 [CLM-005017] [CLM-014050]. Two biosimilar applications are under FDA review [CLM-014051]. CMS selected Entyvio for a negotiated Medicare price from January 2028 [CLM-007026]. CVS template formularies already prefer Stelara biosimilars [CLM-007015]. Vyvanse fell from JPY 423.2bn to 203.2bn in two years [CLM-005015]. Group revenue fell 1.7% (-2.7% at constant rates) in FY2025 [CLM-005001].

*(SCENARIO, not a forecast)* At the ASM-024 erosion range of 40-80% over three years, Entyvio revenue at risk is JPY 383-766bn a year. The base is global while first entry is a U.S. event, so the figure overstates the first three years [CLM-005012] (ASM-024).

## 2. Who is winning

Lilly's revenue rose from USD 28.3bn to USD 65.2bn between FY2021 and FY2025, with tirzepatide at 56.0% of sales [CLM-000133] [CLM-000137] [CLM-001003]. AbbVie replaced Humira (USD 21,237m to 4,540m) with Skyrizi plus Rinvoq (USD 7,687m to 25,866m) [CLM-003002] [CLM-003014]. J&J absorbed a 41.3% Stelara decline with its largest brand at 15.2% of revenue [CLM-000254] [CLM-002073]. Rankings on new-molecule revenue share or approvals per R&D dollar are not used because the audit marks them invalid [CLM-012013] [CLM-000270].

## 3. Why

*(INTERPRETATION)* Winning here means a successor already marketed before the cliff [CLM-003084], capacity built ahead of demand (Lilly capex USD 7,841m in FY2025) [CLM-000172], and a diversified base. It does not yet mean AI: no independent outcome exists for any company's AI programme [CLM-011052] [CLM-006054, wording stronger than its sources support per audit]. Durability is open: Lilly's realised prices fell 15% in Q3 2026 and about USD 900m of that quarter was one-off [CLM-014003].

## 4. What is defensible

*(INTERPRETATION)* Compute and third-party models can be bought; proprietary decision-linked data, built capacity and clinical execution cannot [CLM-006055] [CLM-011085]. Infrastructure, IP and workflow moats are best evidenced and each is removable: announced capacity is not operating capacity, patents expire, PBM templates change [CLM-007015]. *(HYPOTHESIS)* Lilly's data position is the most defensible of the four; the registry has no outcome to confirm it [CLM-000280].

## 5. What Takeda already has

A plasma network of more than 270 centres with adaptive nomograms and a USD 230m Los Angeles fractionation expansion [CLM-005060] [CLM-005065]. In-house orexin science that produced an FDA approval on 2026-08-05 [CLM-005048] [CLM-005029]. Rusfertide approved 2026-08-28 and a zasocitinib NDA accepted under Priority Review [CLM-005032] [CLM-005035]. Three Phase 3 readouts delivered positive on the 2024 plan [CLM-005042]. Stop discipline, including a JPY 58.2bn cell-therapy impairment [CLM-009084]. Deal flow: Nimbus USD 4.0bn upfront, Innovent USD 1.2bn upfront [CLM-009076] [CLM-009078].

Constraints: leverage 2.6x at March 2026, the Amitiza provision of JPY 403.5bn, a CEO in post since 24 June 2026 and three launches in twelve months [CLM-005005] [CLM-005014] [CLM-005073] [CLM-005074]. AI outcomes, lab automation and patient services are public-evidence gaps, not proven absences [CLM-005080] [CLM-005067] [CLM-005072].

## 6. Where the opportunity is

*(RECOMMENDATION)* In order of evidence strength: (1) defend and extend the dated Entyvio exposure (BET-04, BET-11); (2) back the replacement set already in hand (BET-05); (3) compound the two strengths no peer in the set shares, plasma process data and orexin biology (BET-02, BET-03); (4) buy licences for Phase 2/3 assets, the instrument Takeda has actually used (BET-18); (5) hold capped options on AI and new modalities (BET-06 to BET-09); (6) build the measurement discipline that makes AI claims testable (BET-01, BET-17, BET-12).

## 7. What to build (v2 per Director decision record)

| Decision | Bets |
|---|---|
| BUILD | BET-01 data and decision layer; BET-03 orexin (gated); BET-04 Entyvio defence; BET-11 devices and home/SC |
| INVEST | BET-05 zasocitinib breadth |
| PARTNER | BET-06 options (scorecard first); BET-07 AI-design partnerships; BET-08 federated data; BET-09 rented automation; **BET-18 Phase 2/3 licensing channel (new)** |
| EXPERIMENT | **BET-02 plasma (was BUILD)**; BET-12 launch pathways; BET-17 AI measurement |
| DEFER | BET-13 registry (no funded carry) |
| REJECT | BET-10 owned lab; BET-14 model platform; BET-16 U.S. cash-pay; **BET-15 USD 5bn+ purchase (was DEFER)** |

Details and moat mechanisms: [takeda_strategy.md](takeda_strategy.md).

## 8. What to invest

*(ASSUMPTION; not a Takeda budget)* v1 balanced envelope USD 2,950m (ASM-002) becomes about USD 1,920m committed at gates, plus about USD 1,030m of contingent headroom reserved for BET-18, sized USD 0.5-2bn per deal and released only on IVB-012 (Amitiza cash) and the leverage ceiling ASM-033 (v2 per Director decision record). The core H1 2027-29 tranche is about USD 465m. The headroom is not a saving. Constrained (USD 1,130m, ASM-003) and ambitious (USD 3,155m, ASM-004) are v1 figures pending rescaling. See [investment_roadmap.md](investment_roadmap.md).

*(INTERPRETATION)* BET-15 was rejected because the council's arithmetic puts leverage at 3.13x after a USD 5bn purchase and 3.41x if the Amitiza provision is also debt-funded, against the 3.0x planning ceiling (ASM-033); free cash flow is ignored [CLM-005005] [CLM-005014].

## 9. How to execute

Each bet moves through discovery, feasibility, prototype, pilot, scale and value review, with stop and expansion criteria ([stage_gates.md](../strategy/financial_cases/stage_gates.md)). Dated anchors: Entyvio posture and benefit-channel gate (IVB-004) in 2027 H1; biosimilar-event playbook live 2028 H1 (v2, was 2029 H2); Nabla and Iambic go/no-go 2028 H2 [CLM-006039] [CLM-006041]; plasma scale decision 2029 H2 (RM-025); portfolio review each year against scenario signals SCN-1 to SCN-5.

## 10. How to measure

*(RECOMMENDATION)* Set baselines before claims: AI use cases with owner, baseline and measured benefit (usage and training counts are not value [CLM-014043]); yield and cost per litre at the plasma pilot; time to first dose and persistence for launches; Entyvio net price and persistence by payer segment; option conversion and impairment share; revenue concentration against the Entyvio-era 21% [CLM-005009]. Measurement ownership moves off the CFO, who owns the JPY 200bn savings target [CLM-005059].

## Reader notes

**CEO.** *(RECOMMENDATION)* Treat Entyvio as a dated defence plus a refill problem. The evidence supports that reading over a platform story. Fund the defence and the replacement set, keep AI and new modalities as capped options with stop rules, and decline three expensive alternatives (owned lab, model platform, U.S. cash-pay) where the record shows divestment, distressed sale or poor fit [CLM-006052] [CLM-006051] [CLM-007052]. Execution load is high.

**CFO.** *(ASSUMPTION)* Capital is a range, not a plan. The two binding variables are leverage and Amitiza cash timing (IVB-012). Contingent payments in AI and option deals exceed USD 1bn on single deals and cost nothing without data [CLM-006039] [CLM-006041]. No NPV is reported because it would need internal forecasts (IVB-004, IVB-005). AbbVie wrote off 54% of the Cerevel net price [CLM-009054].

**R&D leader.** *(RECOMMENDATION)* Refill after 2030 depends on early depth that is not public (IVB-008). Fund orexin at USD 300m with a Phase 1 gate and an additionality test against base R&D. Gate CNS assets on Phase 2 quality; neuroscience assets failed at AbbVie, J&J and Takeda [CLM-003054] [CLM-002039] [CLM-012120]. Rent wet-lab automation [CLM-006013].

**CTO.** *(RECOMMENDATION)* Extend the existing agent platform with governance and a decision log; do not build a rival [CLM-005058]. Models converge, so the moat is Takeda's own decision-linked data [CLM-006056] [CLM-006055]. Document model credibility against FDA's January 2025 draft framework [CLM-006046].

**Commercial leader.** *(RECOMMENDATION)* Build payer-contracting depth before January 2028 [CLM-007026]. Humira held at least 97% of volume to March 2024 and still lost 78.6% in three years, so contracting delays erosion rather than preventing it [CLM-003007] [CLM-003002]. Resolve whether subcutaneous conversion helps or hurts after entry (BET-04 and BET-11 conflict) [CLM-007053]. Launch pathways attach to the oveporexton launch. Do not copy a cash-pay channel [CLM-007052].

> **What we could be wrong about**
> - Entyvio entry could come before 2030: widened to 2028-2032 in v2, but no Purple Book or litigation record is in the registry [CLM-014051] (ASM-025).
> - Contracting may not apply: the registry has no Entyvio medical-versus-pharmacy benefit split, and every analogue is a pharmacy-benefit product [CLM-003007] (IVB-004).
> - The council rates no funded bet robust to pricing pressure (SCN-3); the Medicare price is statutory [CLM-007026].
> - Plasma may be demand-bound, not capacity-bound: PDT revenue was -1.5% at constant rates in H1 FY2026 [CLM-005064].
> - Probabilities (ASM-020, 021, 022, 028) are judgment; Takeda cites above 70% for its late-stage set [CLM-014049].
> - Zasocitinib may add concentration, not diversification [CLM-009076] [CLM-012012].
> - 71 of 83 Takeda claims rest on a single interested source, and independent corroboration is recorded on 2 of 1,401 claims [CLM-005033].

## How to read / evidence standard

524 sources, 1,401 claims, cutoff 2026-11-21. Figures are looked up by claim ID in the [claims registry](../New_mediciine/evidence_library/claims_registry.jsonl), honouring correction fields. Labels: FACT (a cited claim), INTERPRETATION, HYPOTHESIS, SCENARIO, RECOMMENDATION, ASSUMPTION (ASM- ID). Scenarios are not forecasts. Audit: Gate 1 passed Lilly, conditionally passed J&J and AbbVie, and failed Takeda as repairable ([verdicts](../quality/citation_audits/gate1_verdicts.md)); wave-2 scorecard: A12 and A14 accepted, strategy shard accepted at 12/16, policy and commercial shards marked REVISE ([scorecard](../quality/evaluation_results/wave2_scorecard.md)). Challenge: [council](../strategy/critical_challenges/council_reviews.md), [red team](../strategy/critical_challenges/red_team.md), [uncertainty register](../strategy/critical_challenges/counterarguments_and_uncertainty.md) (95 items).

reports.title: Investment roadmap 2027-2040 (strategy v2)
reports.markdown:
# Investment roadmap 2027-2040 (strategy v2)

Cutoff 2026-11-21. **Every dollar figure here is an ASSUMPTION, not a Takeda budget, plan or forecast** (IVB-014). Sources: [capital_allocation.md](../strategy/financial_cases/capital_allocation.md), [stage_gates.md](../strategy/financial_cases/stage_gates.md), [roadmap_2027_2040.md](../strategy/strategic_roadmap/roadmap_2027_2040.md), [scenarios_2027_2040.md](../strategy/scenarios/scenarios_2027_2040.md), [scenario_stress_test.md](../strategy/critical_challenges/scenario_stress_test.md) and the [Director decision record](../strategy/critical_challenges/DIRECTOR_DECISION_RECORD.md). "v2 per Director decision record" marks a change from the v1 files, which are not yet rewritten (A11c-bis pending). Amounts are USD m cumulative over 2027-2040, incremental to base R&D (JPY 675.9bn in FY2025) and base plant capex (ASM-035) [CLM-005004].

## 1. Scale anchors (FACT)

FY2025 revenue JPY 4,505.7bn; Core Operating Profit JPY 1,172.5bn; R&D JPY 675.9bn; capex including intangibles JPY 426.9bn [CLM-005002] [CLM-005003] [CLM-005004] [CLM-005007]. Adjusted net debt JPY 3,817.6bn against EBITDA JPY 1,457.2bn gives 2.6x at March 2026 (3.1x at March 2024) [CLM-005005]. The Amitiza provision is JPY 403.5bn; cash timing is unknown [CLM-005014] [CLM-014048].

## 2. Portfolios

Horizons: H1 2027-2029 foundations and dated defence; H2 2030-2034 scale decisions and the Entyvio loss window; H3 2035-2040 compounding or exit. *(SCENARIO framing; dates after 2032 are assumptions.)*

| Portfolio | Total (ASSUMPTION) | H1 | H2 | H3 | Choose when |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Capital-constrained (v2, ASM-003) | 1,130 | 30% (about 339) | 44% (about 497) | 26% (about 294) | Leverage near 3x or Amitiza cash near the full provision |
| Balanced, v1 (superseded; author total before challenge) | 2,950 | 23% | 45% | 32% | Historical reference only |
| **Balanced, v2 (ASM-002, Director decision record)** | **1,920 committed at gates** (+ about 1,030 contingent headroom for BET-18, not a saving) | 31% (about 595: 465 core + 130 gated) | 44% (about 845) | 25% (about 480) | **Recommended start** |
| Ambitious (v2, ASM-004) | 3,155 | 23% (about 726) | 43% (about 1,357) | 34% (about 1,073) | SCN-1 signals appear and leverage allows |

Dollar amounts in brackets are computed from the stated percentages. All three portfolios are strategy v2 figures (rescaled by A11c-bis per the Director decision record; ASM-002..004 updated). The v2 horizon split beyond H1 is not in the record (gap).

*(RECOMMENDATION)* Commit only the H1 tranche and release later tranches at gates. The roughly USD 1,030m headroom is reserved for the Phase 2/3 licensing channel (BET-18, USD 0.5-2bn per deal), released only after IVB-012 (Amitiza cash) is answered and the leverage ceiling (ASM-033, 3.0x) holds. It is not a saving. Contingent payments in AI and option deals (above USD 1bn on single deals) cost nothing without data and sit outside the envelope [CLM-006039] [CLM-006041].

### Balanced portfolio by bet: v1 horizon split and v2 size

| Bet | v1 total | H1 | H2 | H3 | v2 size (per Director decision record unless noted) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BET-01 Data and decision layer | 200 | 60 | 80 | 60 | 200 |
| BET-02 Plasma | 430 | 80 | 200 | 150 | EXPERIMENT; baseline and shadow tranche about 230 (council arithmetic); remainder only after baseline |
| BET-03 Orexin | 500 | 100 | 250 | 150 | 300, Phase 1 gate before H2 tranche |
| BET-04 Entyvio defence | 140 | 40 | 60 | 40 | 140, benefit-channel gate 2027 H1 |
| BET-05 Zasocitinib breadth | 180 | 60 | 100 | 20 | 180 |
| BET-06 Option engine | 700 | 150 | 300 | 250 | 300, balance contingent on scorecard |
| BET-07 AI-design partnerships | 180 | 40 | 80 | 60 | about 80 (council arithmetic) |
| BET-08 Federated consortia | 35 | 10 | 15 | 10 | 35 |
| BET-09 Rented automation | 95 | 25 | 40 | 30 | 95 |
| BET-11 Devices, home, SC | 190 | 50 | 80 | 60 | 190, baseline first |
| BET-12 Launch pathways | 100 | 30 | 40 | 30 | cap 50, start 2027 H1 |
| BET-13 Registry | 80 | 0 | 40 | 40 | 0 carry; USD 25m options paper from BET-12 |
| BET-17 AI measurement | 120 | 40 | 50 | 30 | 120 |
| BET-15 | 0 | | | | REJECT as framed |
| BET-18 Licensing channel | n/a | | | | USD 0.5-2bn per deal from contingent headroom |
| **Total** | **2,950** | **685** | **1,335** | **930** | **about 1,920** |

The v2 column sums to 1,920 (200 + 230 + 300 + 140 + 180 + 300 + 80 + 35 + 95 + 190 + 50 + 0 + 120). Bet-level sizes for BET-02 and BET-07 are council arithmetic carried inside the record's net total, not restated in it.

*(INTERPRETATION)* Why the sizes changed: 49.5% of the v1 balanced envelope (USD 1,460m in BET-03, 06, 07 and 13) sat in bets with payoff eight years or more away, after the Entyvio erosion window, while Takeda's actual refill instrument, mid-size Phase 2/3 licences, had no funded bet [CLM-005050] [CLM-009076] [CLM-009078].

### Leverage test behind BET-15 (council arithmetic; free cash flow and acquired earnings ignored)

| Case | Adjusted net debt JPY bn | Over EBITDA JPY 1,457.2bn |
|---|---|---|
| March 2026 as reported | 3,817.6 | 2.62x |
| Amitiza provision debt-funded | 4,221.1 | 2.90x |
| USD 5bn purchase at JPY 150 | 4,567.6 | 3.13x |
| Both | 4,971.1 | 3.41x |

Adjusted net debt may already include the provision [CLM-005005] [CLM-005014]. The audit could not locate the 2.6x value in the filing (IVB-012).

## 3. Stage gates (stop and expansion criteria)

Each bet moves through discovery, feasibility, prototype, pilot, scale and value review. Rules: decide on the evidence listed, not on spend to date; a missed stop criterion ends or redirects the bet unless the decision authority records a reason in writing; expansion releases the next tranche only; evidence is judged against a baseline set at the preceding gate [CLM-006022]. Owners are roles; delegated limits are an ASSUMPTION. Gate capital is a convention (ASM-037). The table shows the decisive gate per bet; full tables are in [stage_gates.md](../strategy/financial_cases/stage_gates.md).

| Bet | Decisive gate | Stop criterion | Expansion criterion | Owner role |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BET-01 | Prototype (2027 H2 gate) | No measured effect on cycle time, hit rate or cost per decision | Measured effect in at least one decision | Chief Digital and Technology Officer |
| BET-02 | Prototype and pilot (2028-29) | Predictions do not beat the nomogram baseline [CLM-005060]; headroom below ASM-031 (2%) | Predictions beat baseline; pilot at or above threshold with clean inspection | Head of Plasma-Derived Therapies |
| BET-03 | Pilot | Safety or exposure failure; weak Phase 2 design | Clean Phase 1; credible Phase 2 design (v2: required before H2 tranche) | Head of Research |
| BET-04 | Feasibility and pilot | No feasible contracting lever; pilot loses share | Levers identified; pilot retains share (v2: IVB-004 benefit-channel gate) | Head of GI franchise and U.S. business unit |
| BET-05 | Pilot | PsA misses primary endpoint [CLM-005037] | PsA positive | Head of R&D |
| BET-06 | Feasibility to value review | Option fees above band; conversion below 0.05 (ASM-028 low) | Within band; conversion at or above 0.10 | Head of Corporate Development |
| BET-07 | Prototype | Data absent by 2028 H2 or negative [CLM-006039] | Data positive against conventional | Head of Research |
| BET-09 | Pilot | Cost above internal baseline | Cost at or below baseline | Head of R&D |
| BET-11 | Pilot | SC erodes net price faster than it retains patients [CLM-007053] | Persistence higher than IV | Head of GI franchise and U.S. business unit |
| BET-12 | Pilot | No improvement in time to first dose | Improvement shown | Head of Patient Services and Market Access, U.S. |
| BET-17 | Feasibility | No baseline for a use case: stop that use case | Baselines set | v2: an owner independent of the CFO's savings target [CLM-005059] |
| BET-18 | Per deal | Leverage above ASM-033 or IVB-012 unanswered | Both cleared; Phase 2 or later data | Corporate development, Board for large deals |

## 4. Roadmap by half-year

Basis "evidence" means the date comes from a claim; "ASSUMPTION" means a planning date. Full list of 50 milestones: [roadmap_2027_2040.md](../strategy/strategic_roadmap/roadmap_2027_2040.md).

| When | Milestone | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| 2027 H1 | Use-case inventory and baselines (RM-001); thin-slice data standard (RM-002); Entyvio erosion scenarios, patent posture and benefit-channel gate (RM-003); plasma baseline (RM-004); rented-automation contract (RM-005); option scorecard (RM-007); orexin plan (RM-008); zasocitinib FDA action date not in registry (RM-009); v2: launch-pathway pilot starts, attached to oveporexton | ASSUMPTION |
| 2027 H2 | PsA Phase 3 completion, study end May 2027 (RM-010); Nabla first-in-human window (RM-011); two decisions with baselines (RM-015) | evidence [CLM-005037] [CLM-006039]; ASSUMPTION |
| 2028 H1 | Medicare negotiated price for Entyvio effective (RM-016); plasma one-site pilot starts (RM-017); first two option deals (RM-019); **v2: biosimilar playbook live (RM-026, moved from 2029 H2)** | evidence [CLM-007026]; ASSUMPTION |
| 2028 H2 | Nabla and Iambic stop or expand (RM-020); launch baseline gate (RM-021) | ASSUMPTION |
| 2029 H1 | JPY 200bn savings checkpoint (RM-023); scale decision on data layer (RM-024) | evidence [CLM-005059] |
| 2029 H2 | Plasma scale decision (RM-025); first portfolio review and M&A trigger check (RM-029) | ASSUMPTION |
| 2030-2032 | Second orexin candidate first-in-human (RM-030, 2030 H1); earliest biosimilar window (ASM-025, **v2 range 2028-2032**); first option exercises (RM-033); Entyvio 2032 patents (RM-036) | ASSUMPTION; evidence [CLM-005017] [CLM-014051] |
| 2033-2035 | Orexin Phase 2 readout for a second asset (RM-041); SC and home persistence after entry (RM-040); first option-sourced approval check (RM-043) | ASSUMPTION |
| 2036-2038 | Market anchors: tirzepatide patent to 2036, Takhzyro patent to January 2036, Rinvoq entry no earlier than April 2037; orexin platform test (RM-048) | evidence [CLM-000250] [CLM-005019] [CLM-003021] |
| 2040 H2 | Value review: revenue concentration against the Entyvio-era 21% (RM-050) | ASSUMPTION [CLM-005009] |

Dependency chains *(INTERPRETATION)*: measurement, plasma, Entyvio (fixed dates), pipeline and options; see the roadmap file.

## 5. Scenario robustness per bet

Five SCENARIOs, not forecasts: SCN-1 AI accelerates; SCN-2 AI incremental; SCN-3 pricing, regulatory and biosimilar pressure; SCN-4 new modalities and tech-native entrants; SCN-5 combined downside with Amitiza cash near the full provision. Ratings are the council's re-rating of 19 of 85 cells, published as the robustness table per the Director decision record; the author's own rating is kept in [scenarios_2027_2040.md](../strategy/scenarios/scenarios_2027_2040.md). They were made on v1 sizes and are an *(INTERPRETATION)*.

| Bet | SCN-1 | SCN-2 | SCN-3 | SCN-4 | SCN-5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BET-01 | robust | robust | neutral | robust | fragile |
| BET-02 | robust | robust | neutral | neutral | neutral |
| BET-03 | robust | neutral | neutral | neutral | fragile |
| BET-04 | neutral | robust | neutral | neutral | robust |
| BET-05 | neutral | robust | neutral | neutral | fragile |
| BET-06 | neutral | neutral | neutral | robust | fragile |
| BET-07 | option value | fragile | neutral | option value | neutral |
| BET-08 | robust | robust | neutral | neutral | robust |
| BET-09 | robust | robust | neutral | neutral | robust |
| BET-10 (rejected) | option value | fragile | fragile | neutral | fragile |
| BET-11 | neutral | robust | fragile | neutral | neutral |
| BET-12 | neutral | neutral | neutral | option value | neutral |
| BET-13 | option value | neutral | neutral | option value | fragile |
| BET-14 (rejected) | option value | fragile | fragile | fragile | fragile |
| BET-15 (rejected in v2) | neutral | neutral | fragile | neutral | fragile |
| BET-16 (rejected) | fragile | fragile | fragile | neutral | fragile |
| BET-17 | robust | robust | neutral | neutral | robust |

*(INTERPRETATION)* No funded bet is robust to SCN-3, the scenario that matters most for Entyvio: the council finds the exposure of JPY 383-766bn a year at ASM-024 is addressed by no bet except through delay [CLM-007026] [CLM-007015]. In SCN-5, 850 of the USD 1,130m constrained envelope (53%) sits in bets that break (BET-01, 03, 05, 06), against 19% in the author's table; the stranded balanced capital is USD 1,660m (56%) as a ceiling because gates stop spend earlier. SCN-2 is the world the registry currently supports: no independent outcome exists for any AI platform [CLM-011052]. *(RECOMMENDATION)* Protect a floor of discovery spend and the dated defences (BET-04, BET-05); cut registry, platform and AI-scale options first.

Annual review signals (Nabla data, an independent Lilly-NVIDIA result, biosimilar approvals and PBM templates, post-2028 negotiated prices, the Amitiza judgment) are listed in [scenarios_2027_2040.md](../strategy/scenarios/scenarios_2027_2040.md).

## 6. Sensitivity: which assumptions move the answer

| Assumption | Value | What changes if wrong |
|---|---|---|
| ASM-024 Entyvio erosion | 60% (range 40-80%); bracketed by Eylea -42% in one year and Humira -78.6% in three [CLM-011017] [CLM-003002] | Deeper or earlier erosion raises the case for BET-05, BET-18 and shortens time for BET-03; no analogue is an infused biologic |
| ASM-025 first entry year | 2031 (range 2030-2032); v2 widens to 2028-2032 | Early entry makes the 2028 H1 playbook the binding date |
| ASM-033, ASM-034 leverage and Amitiza | 3.0x ceiling; JPY 403.5bn (a base case, not a downside; trebling and appeal outcome excluded) [CLM-005014] [CLM-014047] | Decides constrained versus balanced and releases BET-18 |
| ASM-031 plasma pass mark | 2% (range 1-4%), not anchored to money | Without cost per litre the USD 350m follow-on cannot be justified (IVB-006) |
| ASM-020, 021, 022, 028 probabilities | 0.65, 0.15, 0.6, 0.1; judgment | Rankings are only as good as these; Takeda cites above 70% for its late-stage set [CLM-014049] |
| ASM-002 to ASM-004 envelopes | Sums of bet sizes, not a top-down budget | Real envelope could differ by a multiple (IVB-014) |

*(INTERPRETATION)* The three assumptions that most change the portfolio are Entyvio timing and depth (ASM-024, ASM-025), leverage and Amitiza cash (ASM-033, ASM-034), and plasma headroom (ASM-031). No NPV is reported: it would need Takeda's forecasts, net prices and probabilities of success (IVB-004, IVB-005).

## How to read / evidence standard

524 sources, 1,401 claims, cutoff 2026-11-21. Labels: FACT (cited claim), INTERPRETATION, HYPOTHESIS, SCENARIO, RECOMMENDATION, ASSUMPTION (ASM- IDs in the [register](../strategy/financial_cases/assumptions_register.md)). Scenarios are conditional futures, never forecasts or probability-weighted. Claim values come from the [claims registry](../New_mediciine/evidence_library/claims_registry.jsonl) with corrections honoured. Audit: strategy shard scored 12/16 and was accepted ([scorecard](../quality/evaluation_results/wave2_scorecard.md)); Gate 1 failed Takeda as repairable, v1.1 repairs applied, re-audit pending ([verdicts](../quality/citation_audits/gate1_verdicts.md)). Challenge: [decision memo](../strategy/critical_challenges/decision_memo_to_director.md) (119 council verdicts: 45 support, 64 conditional, 10 oppose), [red team](../strategy/critical_challenges/red_team.md), [95-item uncertainty register](../strategy/critical_challenges/counterarguments_and_uncertainty.md).

reports.title: Recommendations
reports.markdown:
# Recommendations

Cutoff 2026-11-21. Strategy v2: the Director's decisions of 2026-11-21 on the council and red-team challenge are applied ([decision record](../strategy/critical_challenges/DIRECTOR_DECISION_RECORD.md)). All dollar figures are ASSUMPTIONs, not Takeda budgets (IVB-014). Every item below is a *(RECOMMENDATION)* unless it cites a claim.

## 1. What to do first (next 12 months, to 2027 H2)

1. **Close the dated Entyvio questions first (BET-04).** Entyvio is JPY 958.0bn, 21% of revenue, with Medicare negotiation effective January 2028 and two biosimilar applications under FDA review [CLM-005009] [CLM-007026] [CLM-014051]. In 2027 H1 approve erosion scenarios and the patent posture, and run the benefit-channel gate (IVB-004): what share of Entyvio volume sits in the contractable pharmacy channel. The registry has no medical-versus-pharmacy split [CLM-003007]. If most volume sits outside it, redirect part of the USD 140m to provider and site-of-care strategy. Set the target as "delay and measure net price and persistence", not "retain 10 points". Have the biosimilar-event playbook live by 2028 H1 (v2 per Director decision record; was 2029 H2).
2. **Back the replacement set already in hand (BET-05).** Zasocitinib NDA is accepted under Priority Review, and the PsA Phase 3 completes in May 2027 [CLM-005035] [CLM-005037]. Fund breadth and comparative evidence at USD 180m, and measure payer coverage at 6 and 12 months after launch.
3. **Open the Phase 2/3 licensing channel (BET-18, new in v2).** Takeda's approved late-stage set came mostly from licences, and the channel has no funding in v1 [CLM-005050] [CLM-009076] [CLM-009078]. Set a per-deal upfront ceiling of USD 0.5-2bn, tie release to IVB-012 (Amitiza cash) and the 3.0x leverage ceiling (ASM-033), and complete its design template in A11c-bis.
4. **Run the plasma baseline, not the roll-out (BET-02, now EXPERIMENT).** Measure yield, cost per litre and deviations across a sample of centres and Los Angeles (IVB-006). Test whether plasma is demand-bound or capacity-bound: PDT revenue was -1.5% at constant rates in H1 FY2026 [CLM-005064]. Re-base the 2% pass mark (ASM-031) on money before releasing the roughly USD 365m remainder.
5. **Start measurement before value claims (BET-17, BET-01).** Inventory AI and data products with owner and baseline (IVB-001, IVB-003). Adopt a thin-slice data standard and decision log in one franchise and plasma. Move ownership of AI measurement away from the CFO, who owns the JPY 200bn savings target [CLM-005059] [CLM-005078]. Usage counts such as 63.4% workforce use are not value [CLM-014043].
6. **Attach launch pathways to the oveporexton launch (BET-12, capped at USD 50m).** Approval was 2026-08-05; a 2027 H2 pilot would be late [CLM-005029]. Start in 2027 H1 with a named leader.
7. **Rent, do not build, automation (BET-09).** Sign a CRO or cloud-lab pilot with acceptance criteria and a minimal data schema [CLM-006013] [CLM-006016].
8. **Write the stop rules into AI-design contracts before the next payment (BET-07).** First-in-human data from Nabla is expected within one to two years of October 2025; stop or expand in 2028 H2 [CLM-006039]. Wire the benchmark to the BET-01 decision log and the BET-09 cost baseline.
9. **Fund orexin discovery at USD 300m with a Phase 1 gate (BET-03).** Run an additionality test against base R&D and a competitor orexin scan before the H2 tranche [CLM-005048] [CLM-005004].
10. **Build the option engine scorecard first (BET-06, USD 300m).** Release the balance only on the deal-outcome scorecard and the first two deals. No option from the window has yet produced an approved product [CLM-009097].

## 2. What to avoid

- A USD 5bn+ asset purchase (BET-15, REJECT as framed in v2). The council's arithmetic gives 3.13x leverage after the purchase and 3.41x if the Amitiza provision is also debt-funded, against a 3.0x planning ceiling; free cash flow is ignored [CLM-005005] [CLM-005014].
- An owned autonomous lab (BET-10, zero spend). Owned and venture-funded lab models ended in divestment or distressed sale [CLM-006052] [CLM-006051]. Revisit only if three triggers fire: an independent Lilly-lab result, Nabla first-in-human data, a measured CRO cost [CLM-011066] [CLM-000281].
- A TuneLab-style model platform (BET-14). The public record shows no measured Takeda advantage and no external demand [CLM-000280].
- A U.S. cash-pay channel (BET-16). The channel fits infused and specialty-distributed products poorly [CLM-007052].
- Scaling subcutaneous and device spend (BET-11) before baselining it. SC moves patients into the pharmacy benefit, where PBM biosimilar templates operate; persistence after entry is unestablished [CLM-007015] [CLM-007053].
- Redesigning patient programmes without a pilot: AbbVie reversed its loyalty redesign within months [CLM-003033].
- Reading the USD 10-20bn peak range for six late-stage programmes as a forecast; it is not probability-adjusted [CLM-014049].
- Funding the registry (BET-13) now. The v2 carry is removed; a USD 25m options paper is funded from BET-12 in 2029 (RM-028).

## 3. How to decide whether to scale

Decide on the evidence listed at each gate, against a baseline set at the preceding gate, never on spend to date. A missed stop criterion ends or redirects the bet unless the decision authority records a reason in writing. Expansion releases only the next tranche ([stage_gates.md](../strategy/financial_cases/stage_gates.md)).

| Bet | Scale only if | Stop or redirect if |
|---|---|---|
| BET-01 | Measured effect in at least one decision; reuse above the threshold set at feasibility | No attributable benefit in two consecutive annual reviews |
| BET-02 | Shadow-mode predictions beat the nomogram baseline [CLM-005060]; pilot at or above the re-based threshold with clean inspection | No vendor accepts outcome-linked terms; new inspection observations from the pilot [CLM-005020] |
| BET-03 | Clean Phase 1 for a second candidate; Phase 2 design with credible placebo response | Safety or exposure failure; platform claim withdrawn if only one asset by 2040 |
| BET-04 | Pilot retains share; retained share above the scenario midpoint | Retained share below the scenario low case: redirect to lifecycle |
| BET-05 | PsA positive; payer coverage at plan | PsA misses primary endpoint; coverage below plan |
| BET-06 | Conversion at or above 0.10 (ASM-028); fees within band | Conversion below 0.05; impairments above the 54% benchmark [CLM-009054] |
| BET-07 | Data positive and Phase 2 transition at or above conventional | Data absent by 2028 H2 or negative; success-based payments grow faster than data |
| BET-11 | Persistence higher than IV after entry | SC erodes net price faster than it retains patients |
| BET-18 | Leverage at or below ASM-033 after IVB-012; Phase 2 or later data; write-down test passed | Any trigger unmet |

## 4. Measurable success metrics

*(ASSUMPTION targets; Takeda sets the values.)* Metrics and the year each is first read:

- **2028:** inventory of AI and data products with owner, baseline and measured benefit; Entyvio contracting posture and playbook in place (BET-17, BET-01, BET-04).
- **2029:** plasma pilot result against the re-based threshold; AI-partnership decision made on data; checkpoint on the JPY 200bn savings plan with the technology share disclosed internally [CLM-005059].
- **2032:** plasma network status; options exercised; share of Entyvio exposure replaced by labelled indications (BET-02, BET-06, BET-05).
- **2035:** first option-sourced approval check; decisions changed by models with measured effect (BET-06, BET-01).
- **2040:** revenue concentration against the Entyvio-era 21% [CLM-005009].
- **Always:** time to first dose and persistence for launches; Entyvio net price and persistence by payer segment; option conversion and impairment share; cost per data point against the internal baseline. Usage and training counts are not outcomes [CLM-006022] [CLM-014043].

## 5. Open questions that need Takeda-internal data

| Item | Question | Decisions that wait on it |
|---|---|---|
| IVB-004 | Entyvio erosion curve, benefit-channel split, subcutaneous conversion, patent litigation posture | BET-04, BET-11 sizing; playbook timing |
| IVB-005 | Internal probabilities of success and launch forecasts | BET-05 value; M&A triggers; replacement gap |
| IVB-006 | Plasma yield per centre, cost per litre, fractionation automation | BET-02 follow-on |
| IVB-012 | Amitiza judgment timing, trebling, reserve adequacy and cash plan | BET-18 release; leverage |
| IVB-014 | Approved technology capital envelope | Every envelope total |
| IVB-001, IVB-003 | AI and data inventory; realised against targeted savings | BET-01, BET-17 |
| IVB-007, IVB-008 | External-innovation organisation; early-pipeline depth beyond six late-stage programmes | BET-06, BET-03, BET-18 |
| IVB-013 | Patient-services and market-access inventory | BET-12 |
| Research gaps | Competitor orexin programmes; statutory Entyvio exclusivity date and any Purple Book or litigation record | BET-03 additionality; ASM-025 |

Where these are unanswered, dependent recommendations stay labelled ASSUMPTION. Four of the council's ten changes turn on IVB-001, IVB-004, IVB-006 and IVB-012 [CLM-005080].

## How to read / evidence standard

524 sources, 1,401 claims, cutoff 2026-11-21. Labels: FACT (cited claim), INTERPRETATION, HYPOTHESIS, SCENARIO, RECOMMENDATION, ASSUMPTION. Claim values are from the [claims registry](../New_mediciine/evidence_library/claims_registry.jsonl) with corrections honoured. Several load-bearing claims behind these recommendations are PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED or NEEDS_MORE_RESEARCH [CLM-011054] [CLM-011065] [CLM-011066] [CLM-011072]. Audit: strategy shard 12/16 ACCEPT ([scorecard](../quality/evaluation_results/wave2_scorecard.md)); Gate 1 failed Takeda as repairable, repairs applied in v1.1, re-audit pending ([verdicts](../quality/citation_audits/gate1_verdicts.md)). Challenge: [decision memo](../strategy/critical_challenges/decision_memo_to_director.md), [uncertainty register](../strategy/critical_challenges/counterarguments_and_uncertainty.md). Supporting detail: [takeda_strategy.md](takeda_strategy.md), [investment_roadmap.md](investment_roadmap.md).

reports.title: Takeda strategy 2027-2040 (strategy v2)
reports.markdown:
# Takeda strategy 2027-2040 (strategy v2)

Cutoff 2026-11-21. Public evidence only. Takeda's budget, forecasts and internal data are not available (IVB-014), so every dollar figure is an ASSUMPTION with an ID in the [assumptions register](../strategy/financial_cases/assumptions_register.md). Where a decision or size differs between the v1 [strategic bets](../strategy/investment_theses/strategic_bets.md) and the [Director decision record](../strategy/critical_challenges/DIRECTOR_DECISION_RECORD.md), the record wins and the text says "v2 per Director decision record". Challenge status: the Strategic Council (119 verdicts), red team and stress test ran; the v1 files are not yet rewritten (pending the A11c-bis pass), so the bet-level v2 sizes below follow the council memo's arithmetic where the record gives only the net total.

## 1. Baseline: what Takeda has

Classification from the [capability baseline](../New_mediciine/companies/takeda_public_baseline/capability_baseline/capability_baseline.md). EVIDENCE_GAP means public evidence is missing, not that the capability is absent [CLM-005080].

| Class | Capability areas | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| EXISTING_STRENGTH | GI and immunology franchise (Entyvio JPY 958.0bn, 21%) | [CLM-005009] [CLM-005012] |
| | Plasma network (270+ centres) and manufacturing | [CLM-005063] [CLM-005060] [CLM-005065] |
| | Rare disease and orexin science | [CLM-005048] [CLM-005029] |
| | Late-stage execution (three positive readouts, three approvals or filings) | [CLM-005042] [CLM-005035] |
| | External innovation deal flow; portfolio stop discipline | [CLM-005050] [CLM-005024] [CLM-005025] |
| EXISTING_BUT_UNDERDEVELOPED | LOE replacement depth; enterprise data and AI platform (outcomes unproven); manufacturing quality (one closed failure); cost transformation (plan, not realised) | [CLM-005015] [CLM-005058] [CLM-005020] [CLM-005059] |
| POTENTIAL_NEW_CAPABILITY | New-brand launch execution | [CLM-005069] [CLM-005074] |
| EVIDENCE_GAP | AI-enabled discovery, lab automation, supply-chain AI, patient services | [CLM-005049] [CLM-005067] [CLM-005072] |
| Exited | Cell therapy (JPY 58.2bn impairment) | [CLM-009084] |

*(INTERPRETATION)* The evidenced strengths are franchise scale, plasma operations and on-schedule late-stage delivery. The least-evidenced areas are those where later modules propose spend, so recommendations there stay labelled ASSUMPTION until the internal-validation backlog is closed.

## 2. The seven transformation domains

Each domain states the problem, what competitors show, and Takeda's position. Sources: [strategy/future_of_pharma](../strategy/future_of_pharma/map.md).

**1. Data advantage.** Proprietary data is the one input rivals cannot buy [CLM-006055]. AbbVie built ARCH with fewer than ten full-time staff and opened data from 2,000+ trials to all R&D [CLM-006032] [CLM-006034]; Lilly's TuneLab rests on data it estimates cost over USD 1bn [CLM-000280]. None has independent outcome evidence [CLM-011052]. Takeda has an agent platform and 63.4% workforce usage, both adoption measures [CLM-005058] [CLM-014043]. *(RECOMMENDATION)* BET-01 and BET-08.

**2. Next-generation R&D.** Every competitor AI-discovery deal found is at concept or prototype [CLM-011057]. Takeda's Nabla and Iambic collaborations carry success-based payments above USD 1bn and USD 1.7bn, payable only on data [CLM-006039] [CLM-006041]. AI-origin Phase 2 success is cited as about the same as conventional (secondary source) [CLM-006049]. Takeda's approved late-stage set is mostly licensed in, with orexin the in-house exception [CLM-005050] [CLM-005048]. *(RECOMMENDATION)* BET-03, BET-06, BET-07, BET-18.

**3. Robotics and autonomous science.** Scripted automation is a commodity service: Arctoris runs the former Lilly platform as a CRO [CLM-006013] [CLM-006016]. Owned or venture-funded labs ended in divestment or distressed sale [CLM-006052] [CLM-006051]. *(INTERPRETATION)* The Lilly-NVIDIA lab (up to USD 1bn, joint) can also be read as re-platforming at larger scale, so "owned labs fail" is weaker than first stated [CLM-000281] [CLM-006017]. *(RECOMMENDATION)* BET-09 rents; BET-10 stays at zero with triggers.

**4. Care models.** No company publishes adherence, persistence or time-to-therapy outcomes; reported figures are enrolment or access counts [CLM-007039]. Entyvio SC is approved in three regions and Takeda cites it as driving uptake; HYHUB received 510(k) clearance [CLM-007041] [CLM-007042]. Effect after biosimilar entry is unestablished [CLM-007053]. *(RECOMMENDATION)* BET-11, BET-12.

**5. Commercial models.** PBM template formularies decide biosimilar outcomes [CLM-007015]. Humira's contracting delayed but did not stop erosion [CLM-003007] [CLM-003002]. Takeda's contracting and patient-services evidence is a gap [CLM-007025] [CLM-005072]. A U.S. cash-pay channel fits infused and specialty-distributed products poorly [CLM-007052]. *(RECOMMENDATION)* BET-04, BET-16 rejected.

**6. Partnerships and ecosystem.** AbbVie runs an early-option stream of USD 0.6-1.0bn a year; Lilly expenses early purchases as IPR&D; J&J buys large commercial assets [CLM-009097] [CLM-009095] [CLM-009096]. Value destruction concentrates in neuroscience, gene and cell therapy and robotics [CLM-009100]. Takeda's pattern is one flagship purchase (Nimbus), then mid-size licences (Innovent, Protagonist) [CLM-009076] [CLM-009078] [CLM-012151]. *(RECOMMENDATION)* BET-06, BET-18; BET-15 rejected.

**7. People and operating model.** The thinnest domain in public evidence. J&J reviewed about 900 AI use cases and moved ownership to departments [CLM-006018]. Takeda targets over JPY 200bn gross annual savings by FY2028, at a restructuring cost series of about JPY 150bn, 170.0bn, then 160.0bn, with about 4,500 roles affected per press [CLM-005059] [CLM-005078]. The CEO changed on 24 June 2026 [CLM-005073]. *(RECOMMENDATION)* BET-17, with ownership off the CFO's savings target.

## 3. The bets: decisions and moat mechanisms

Sizes are balanced-portfolio USD m, cumulative 2027-2040, ASSUMPTION. "v2" marks a change per the Director decision record. Moat mechanisms use the [taxonomy](../strategy/platform_moats/moat_mechanisms_taxonomy.md); each moat statement is an *(INTERPRETATION)*.

| Bet | v2 decision and size | Moat mechanism | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| BET-01 Governed R&D data and decision layer | BUILD thin slice, 200 | Data, learning, workflow integration; compounds only if decisions are logged against a baseline [CLM-011082] | ARCH shows low build cost [CLM-006032] |
| BET-02 Plasma process intelligence | **EXPERIMENT** (v2; was BUILD), baseline and shadow-mode tranche about 230 | Infrastructure, data, learning; regulatory experience supports it [CLM-011085] | PDT revenue -1.5% at constant rates does not show a capacity limit [CLM-005064]; no peer data set [CLM-011056] |
| BET-03 Orexin platform | BUILD, **300** (v2; was 500), Phase 1 gate before the H2 tranche | IP, learning, regulatory experience; platform claim needs a second asset [CLM-011038] | Base R&D probably funds the work already; competitor orexin scan missing |
| BET-04 Entyvio defence | BUILD, 140; **benefit-channel gate** (IVB-004, 2027 H1); outcome "delay and measure" | Workflow integration, IP; removable by PBM template or patent revocation [CLM-011086] | Dated exposure [CLM-007026] [CLM-014051] [CLM-005017] |
| BET-05 Zasocitinib breadth | INVEST, 180 | Regulatory experience, label breadth [CLM-003084] | NDA accepted; head-to-head data [CLM-005035] |
| BET-06 Option engine | PARTNER, **300** (v2; was 700), scorecard first | Ecosystem and selection skill [CLM-005042] | No option from the window has produced an approval [CLM-009097] |
| BET-07 AI-design partnerships | PARTNER, about 80 per council arithmetic; prerequisites re-wired to BET-01 and BET-09; stop rules in contracts | Learning and data only if Takeda keeps data ownership [CLM-011087] | Models converge [CLM-006056] |
| BET-08 Federated consortia | PARTNER, 35 | Network effects accrue to the best user, so the moat is BET-01 | Takeda joined AISB late [CLM-006042] [CLM-006044] |
| BET-09 Rented automation | PARTNER, 95 | Data and workflow, not robots | Service model survived [CLM-006013] |
| BET-10 Owned lab | REJECT, 0, trigger set | None evidenced | Distressed outcomes [CLM-006051] |
| BET-11 Devices, home and SC | BUILD, 190; baseline first; confidence relabelled hypothesis | IP and workflow integration | Conflicts with BET-04 because SC moves patients into the PBM channel [CLM-007015] [CLM-007053] |
| BET-12 Launch pathways | EXPERIMENT, **cap 50**, attached to the oveporexton launch, start 2027 H1 | Workflow integration, ecosystem | No published benchmark [CLM-007039] |
| BET-13 Neutral registry | DEFER, **carry removed** (v2); a USD 25m options paper funded from BET-12 | Data and network effects only with neutrality [CLM-011050] | Needs BET-12 evidence |
| BET-14 Model platform | REJECT, 0 | None evidenced | No measured advantage [CLM-000280] |
| BET-15 Large purchase | **REJECT** as framed (v2; was DEFER) | None from the purchase itself | Leverage 3.13x after USD 5bn; 3.41x with Amitiza [CLM-005005] [CLM-005014] |
| BET-16 U.S. cash-pay | REJECT, 0 | None | Structural misfit [CLM-007052] |
| BET-17 AI measurement | EXPERIMENT, 120; owner independent of the savings target | Learning, workflow integration | Prerequisite for credibility of all AI claims [CLM-006022] |
| **BET-18 Phase 2/3 licensing channel** | **New in v2**: PARTNER/INVEST, USD 0.5-2bn per deal, contingent on IVB-012 and ASM-033, funded from the contingent headroom | Ecosystem and selection skill | Takeda's observed instrument: Nimbus, Innovent [CLM-009076] [CLM-009078]; its A-M template is completed in A11c-bis |

v2 balanced net: about USD 1,920m committed at gates plus about USD 1,030m contingent headroom for BET-18 (v2 per Director decision record). BET-02 and BET-07 figures above come from the council memo's arithmetic; the record states only the total.

## 4. Sequencing logic

*(HYPOTHESIS argued from evidence)* Run the data standard and rented automation in parallel from 2027 H1, with a hard gate before any closed-loop (stage 3) work: the full data layer plus three triggers (an independent Lilly-lab result, Nabla first-in-human data, a measured CRO cost) [CLM-011066] [CLM-000281] [CLM-006039]. Plasma can seed its own data because nomogram data already exist at site level [CLM-005060]. The Entyvio chain has fixed dates and cannot slip: erosion scenarios, then the January 2028 posture, then the playbook live by 2028 H1 (v2), then the earliest entry window (ASM-025 widened to 2028-2032 in v2), then the 2032 patents [CLM-007026] [CLM-014051] [CLM-005017]. Licensing deals (BET-18) wait for IVB-012 and the leverage test.

## 5. What Takeda should not do

*(RECOMMENDATION)* Do not buy a USD 5bn+ asset on current leverage (BET-15). Do not build an owned autonomous lab (BET-10) or a TuneLab-style platform (BET-14). Do not launch a U.S. cash-pay channel (BET-16). Do not scale AI-design partnerships before first-in-human data (RM-020, 2028 H2). Do not roll out plasma automation before the baseline shows headroom (ASM-031). Do not read usage or training counts as value [CLM-014043] [CLM-006022]. Do not redesign patient programmes without a pilot: AbbVie reversed its loyalty redesign within months [CLM-003033]. Do not treat the USD 10-20bn peak range for six late-stage programmes as a forecast; it is not probability-adjusted [CLM-014049].

## 6. Where the strategy is weakest

*(INTERPRETATION)* The council rates no funded bet robust to pricing and biosimilar pressure (SCN-3). The Entyvio price from January 2028 is statutory and PBM private-label biosimilars route around contracts, so BET-04 holds value only as delay [CLM-007026] [CLM-007015]. Vyvanse, Trintellix and Takhzyro (patent to January 2036) are exposures the bets do not address [CLM-005015] [CLM-005016] [CLM-005019]. The probabilities behind the ranking (ASM-020, 021, 022, 028) are judgment.

## 7. Internal-validation backlog (pointers)

The [backlog](../New_mediciine/companies/takeda_public_baseline/internal_validation_backlog/backlog.md) holds IVB-001 to IVB-014. The ones that move decisions: IVB-004 (Entyvio erosion, benefit channel and exclusivity); IVB-005 (probability of success and launch forecasts); IVB-006 (plasma yield and cost per litre); IVB-012 (Amitiza cash and reserve); IVB-014 (technology capital envelope); IVB-001 (AI and data inventory); IVB-007 (external-innovation organisation); IVB-008 (early pipeline depth). New research gaps from the Director record: the competitor orexin landscape and the statutory Entyvio exclusivity date.

## How to read / evidence standard

524 sources, 1,401 claims, cutoff 2026-11-21. Labels: FACT (cited claim), INTERPRETATION, HYPOTHESIS, SCENARIO, RECOMMENDATION, ASSUMPTION. Numbers were looked up in the [claims registry](../New_mediciine/evidence_library/claims_registry.jsonl) honouring correction fields. Audit: Gate 1 failed Takeda as repairable and v1.1 applies the repairs, with re-audit pending ([verdicts](../quality/citation_audits/gate1_verdicts.md)); the strategy shard scored 12/16 (ACCEPT) ([scorecard](../quality/evaluation_results/wave2_scorecard.md)). Six v1 bets carried "evidence_backed" labels while load-bearing claims are PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED or NEEDS_MORE_RESEARCH; v2 relabels those bets to hypothesis where the load-bearing claim is weak (the council memo names BET-08, BET-09 and BET-11) [CLM-011054] [CLM-011065] [CLM-011066] [CLM-007053]. Challenge record: [council](../strategy/critical_challenges/council_reviews.md), [uncertainty register](../strategy/critical_challenges/counterarguments_and_uncertainty.md).

| [cross_company_analysis/](cross_company_analysis/map.md) | `master_comparison.md` + 12 matrices + `lessons_for_takeda.md` (21 lessons → `../strategy/data/takeda_lessons.json`) | decision-grade with conditions (A10-bis) |
| [research_coverage/](research_coverage/coverage_summary.md) | computed coverage ledger (85 rows) + Director rows; [gapfill_wave2/](research_coverage/gapfill_wave2/map.md) second-pass findings | current |
| [financial_models/](financial_models/) | `product_revenue_series.json`, EDGAR facts, CT.gov inventories | current |
| [unanswered_questions/](unanswered_questions/research_questions.md) | question decomposition + negative tests | current |
| knowledge_graph/ | generated into `../data/normalized/knowledge_graph.json` and `deals.json` | generated |

## Which report depends on which evidence
| Report | Depends on |
|---|---|
| `companies/*/financials/xbrl_annual_facts.md` | SEC companyfacts + 10-K/20-F records (RUN-0001; A4 shard) |
| `companies/*/master_report.md` v1.1 | company shard (A1/A2/A3/A5) + horizontal shards (A6, A7, A8, A9, A12) + gap-fill (A14) + audit repairs (A10) |
| `cross_company_analysis/*` | all dossiers + horizontals; honours `correction` fields; refuses invalid rankings |
| `../strategy/*` (v2) | accepted claims only (Gate 3) + `ASM-` assumptions; challenged by `../strategy/critical_challenges/` |
| `../deliverables/*` | cross-company layer + strategy v2 + council; 184 claims cited |

## How to add evidence (any agent)
1. Get your shard and next IDs: `~/.local/share/mise/installs/python/3.12/bin/python3 tools/evidence.py ids <shard>` (ranges in `research_methodology/agent_protocols.md`).
2. Append `sources.jsonl` / `claims.jsonl` records (formats in agent_protocols.md §2); `validate --shard <shard> --path <file>` must report 0 errors.
3. Director merges: `python3 scripts/merge_shards.py <shard>` → `python3 scripts/validate_registries.py` PASS.
4. Audit proposals go to `evidence_library/conflicts_proposed_<agent>.jsonl`; the Director applies them with an `apply_audit*.py` script (never edit statements).
5. `python3 scripts/update_coverage.py`, a run note in `research_methodology/research_runs/`, update the folder `map.md`, then `./launch.sh`.
