reports.markdown:
# AbbVie Inc. — master dossier v1.1 (A3, cutoff 2026-11-21)

## Dossier status
- Version: v1.1, 2026-11-21 (supersedes v1.0).
- Gate 1 verdict (A10): **CONDITIONAL PASS** after repairs (15/16 sampled figures correct, one label error; financial reconciliation failed on the debt label and deal-size bases; evidence-gap report weak) [gate1_verdicts.md](../../../quality/citation_audits/gate1_verdicts.md). All four required repairs are applied in v1.1 (see §22).
- Claims in the registry tagged ABBV at 2026-11-21: 338 (316 FACT, 20 INTERPRETATION, 1 HYPOTHESIS, 1 RECOMMENDATION); shard A3_abbvie holds CLM-003000..003090. Wave-2 gap-fill claims CLM-014030..014040 and CLM-014072 are integrated below.
- v1.1 changes: debt basis, deal-size bases, Juvmo date resolution, expanded evidence gaps, single-interested-source flags, §12-17 horizontals.

Shard: `A3_abbvie` (39 sources, 91 claims). FACT/INTERPRETATION labelled; canonical financial claims CLM-000001..000270 reused. Unsourced sentences are marked (INTERPRETATION) or (gap). 2026 figures are partial periods (Q1-Q3), never full-year.

## 1. Executive thesis
AbbVie absorbed the largest U.S. loss of exclusivity in pharma by replacing Humira (global USD 21.2bn in 2022 to 4.5bn in 2025) with Skyrizi and Rinvoq (7.7bn to 25.9bn) [CLM-003002, CLM-003014]. Total revenue dipped 6.4% in 2023 and passed its 2022 peak only in 2025 (61.2bn) [CLM-003015]. The immunology engine is high quality; the diversification layer is mixed: emraclidine failed and cost a USD 4.5bn impairment [CLM-003057], aesthetics shrank [CLM-003031], while Vyalev, Elahere and Juvmo are real but small [CLM-003037, CLM-003036, CLM-003063].

## 2. Research question and scope
How AbbVie survived Humira LOE, what Allergan delivered, quality of the post-Humira engine, where capital was destroyed, and 2030+ positioning. Window 2021-11 to 2026-11. (gap) AI/robotics, policy and full deal inventory are left to A6/A8/A9.

## 3. Business architecture
Single segment; immunology, neuroscience, oncology, aesthetics, eye care. Skyrizi, Humira and Rinvoq were about 47% of 2024 revenue [CLM-003046]. Product tables: [business/business_model.md](business/business_model.md).

## 4. Financial evolution
Revenue 56.2bn (2021), 58.1bn, 54.3bn, 56.3bn, 61.2bn (2025) [CLM-000001..000005]. GAAP operating margin 31.9% to 16.2% (2024) to 24.6% (2025) (INTERPRETATION, arithmetic) [CLM-003039]. GAAP net income 4.2bn in 2025 is depressed by 7.4bn amortization and a 6.5bn contingent-consideration charge [CLM-003040, CLM-003041]. **Debt basis (Gate 1 relabel).** Total long-term debt *including the current portion* fell from USD 75,962m (2021) to 59,245m (2023), then rose to 66,841m (2024) after USD 15.0bn of notes for ImmunoGen/Cerevel, and was 64,503m at end-2025 (63,128m in 2022) [CLM-003042] [CLM-000066] [CLM-000067] [CLM-000068] [CLM-000069] [CLM-000070]. The balance-sheet non-current series is lower: 64,189 / 59,135 / 52,194 / 60,340 / 58,941 (2021-2025) [CLM-003042]. The earlier word "non-current" for the first series was wrong (XBRL tag `LongTermDebt`); the registry correction fields on these claims say the same. Net income basis: consolidated net earnings 4,233m (2025) versus 4,226m attributable to AbbVie; the A4 and RUN-0001 series differ only by this definition (conflicts_proposed_A10 #8) [CLM-000030] [CLM-004152]. Dividends 11.7bn paid in 2025; buybacks small [CLM-003043, CLM-003044].

## 5. Timeline summary
See [timeline.md](timeline.md).

## 6. Humira loss of exclusivity
U.S. exclusivity ended 2023-01-31; nine biosimilars launched in 2023 [CLM-003000, CLM-003006]. The 2017-2022 settlements licensed biosimilars from 2023 in the U.S. (2018 in Europe); terms are undisclosed [CLM-014036]. The 2019 indirect-purchaser antitrust class actions were dismissed in June 2020 and appealed [CLM-014037]; the Seventh Circuit affirmed dismissal of the patent-thicket complaint on 2022-08-01 [CLM-008048]; a January 2025 payor class action over rebating is pending [CLM-007021]. Humira was about 27% of 2023 net revenue [CLM-014038]. Humira kept at least 97% of volume to March 2024 [CLM-003007] *(T3 IQVIA/trade source, not re-opened by the auditor; single-interested-source flag, §22)*; CVS Caremark excluded Humira from major template formularies from 2024-04-01 while AbbVie supplied a co-branded Humira to Cordavis [CLM-003008]. U.S. Humira revenue: 18.6bn (2022), 12.2bn, 7.1bn, 3.1bn (2025) [CLM-003001]. Steepest falls came after the PBM change (association, not proven causation) [CLM-003010].

## 7. Skyrizi and Rinvoq ramp
Indication breadth covers Humira's uses [CLM-003016]. Rinvoq carries a JAK boxed warning since 2021 [CLM-003017] yet grew every year [CLM-003013]. Patents run to 2033; no Rinvoq generic expected before April 2037 [CLM-003021]. 2027 target of more than 31bn combined [CLM-003022]; nine-month 2026 already 23.1bn [CLM-003023].

## 8. Allergan integration
Closed 2020-05-08 [CLM-003048]. USD 2.5bn cost synergies targeted and reported realized in 2022 [CLM-003049]. Revenue side weaker: Botox Therapeutic grew (2.5bn to 3.8bn) [CLM-003030] but Botox Cosmetic and Juvederm declined from 2024 [CLM-003031]; 2029 aesthetics target cut from 9bn to above 7bn [CLM-003034].

## 9. Neuroscience
Vraylar 3.6bn, Botox Therapeutic 3.8bn, Ubrelvy and Qulipta growing [CLM-003028, CLM-003037]. Vyalev approved 2024-10 after two CRLs [CLM-003061]; Juvmo approved by FDA on 2026-09-25 per the FDA novel-approvals record; AbbVie announced it on 2026-09-28 (the earlier 09-25 versus 09-28 question is resolved as FDA action versus company release) [CLM-012017] [CLM-014039] [CLM-003063]. NDA submitted September 2025 [CLM-014040]. Emraclidine failed [CLM-003054].

## 10. Oncology
Imbruvica declining (5.4bn to 2.9bn) and IRA-selected [CLM-003025, CLM-003026]; Venclexta 2.8bn but two Phase 3 misses [CLM-003027]; Elahere growing [CLM-003036]; Emrelis accelerated approval on 35% ORR [CLM-003066]; Epkinly DLBCL missed OS [CLM-003067] (company-reported; Phase 3 PFS improved, OS not statistically significant per the 10-K [CLM-012118]).

## 11. Pipeline quality
About 90 programs, 60 mid/late [CLM-003047]. Details: [pipeline/late_stage_assets.md](pipeline/late_stage_assets.md). (HYPOTHESIS) breadth outside immunology is thin on proven peak sales [CLM-003089]. FDA novel approvals 2022-2026: Elahere (2022-11-14, ImmunoGen sponsor), Epkinly (2023-05-19, Genmab sponsor), Emrelis (2025-05-14), Decnupaz (2026-05-27), Juvmo (2026-09-25) [CLM-012013] [CLM-012014] [CLM-012015] [CLM-012016] [CLM-012017]. Setbacks: ABBV-951 CRLs (March 2023 device; June 2024 third-party manufacturer inspection, approved Oct 2024), Imbruvica accelerated approvals withdrawn (May 2023), navitoclax TRANSFORM-2 stopped (April 2024), emraclidine Phase 2 miss (November 2024), Venclexta VERONA OS miss (June 2025), Epkinly Phase 3 PFS win with non-significant OS (January 2026) [CLM-012111] [CLM-012112] [CLM-012113] [CLM-012114] [CLM-012115] [CLM-012117] [CLM-012118]. Horizontals: [pipeline quality assessment](../../industry_transformation/pipeline_regulatory/pipeline_quality_assessment.md), [setbacks](../../industry_transformation/pipeline_regulatory/setbacks_crls_withdrawals.md), [late-stage snapshot](../../industry_transformation/pipeline_regulatory/late_stage_pipeline_snapshot.md).

## 12. Commercial and patient
[commercial_market_access/commercial.md](commercial_market_access/commercial.md). Horizontals: [commercial models](../../industry_transformation/commercial_patient/commercial_models_comparison.md), [pricing and payer dynamics](../../industry_transformation/commercial_patient/pricing_access_and_payer_dynamics.md), [launch execution](../../industry_transformation/commercial_patient/launch_execution_evidence.md), [patient programmes](../../industry_transformation/commercial_patient/patient_programs_and_care_delivery.md).
- Rebate and chargeback provisions USD 65.1bn (2025), 59.3bn (2024), 56.8bn (2023) against 2025 net revenue of USD 61.2bn [CLM-007019].
- Skyrizi USD 17,562m (+49.9%) and Rinvoq USD 8,304m (+39.1%); Humira -49% [CLM-007020]. The 10-K gives share-uptake language only for the drivers.
- Humira contracting: CVS Caremark removal from template formularies (2024-04-01) with co-branded Cordavis Humira [CLM-003008] [CLM-003009]; the percentage figures rest on trade sources (flagged, §22).
- Patient support: Allē had over six million members across 19,000 practices (January 2024); the October 2024 redesign was reversed in early 2025 [CLM-007036] [CLM-003033]. No adherence or time-to-therapy outcomes for any company [CLM-007039].

## 13. R&D model and external innovation
External innovation is an explicit strategy pillar; acquired IPR&D charges rose from 0.6bn (2023) to 4.8bn (2025) [CLM-003075, CLM-003045]. Yearly early-stage upfronts of USD 0.6-1.0bn [CLM-009069]; AbbVie Ventures founding date unresolved (2009 versus about 2015) [CLM-009074] (see §14).

## 14. Partnerships and M&A
**Deal-size bases (Gate 1 relabel).** ImmunoGen (closed 2024-02-12): USD 10.1bn is the announced total value, 9.8bn is consideration transferred and 9.2bn is net of cash acquired [CLM-003053] [CLM-009056]. Cerevel (closed 2024-08-01): USD 8.7bn consideration, 8.3bn net of cash [CLM-009053] [CLM-014035]. The "18.5bn cash paid" in 2024 is consideration transferred for the two (9.8 + 8.7); net of cash acquired it is 17.5bn [CLM-003086] *(conflicts_proposed_A10 #10)*. Capstan: USD 2.1bn cash paid (1.9bn net of cash acquired), expensed as IPR&D in 2025; lead asset Phase 1 [CLM-014030] [CLM-009058] (CLM-003072's "up to 2.1bn" is the announcement wording). Gubra obesity: USD 350m upfront [CLM-003073]; Apogee closed in 2026 [CLM-003070].
- Other terms: Aliada USD 1.4bn cash (announced 2024-10-28, closed December 2024), co-founded by J&J's JJDC [CLM-014032] [CLM-009063]; Landos USD 20.42 a share (about USD 137.5m) plus a CVR worth up to about USD 75m [CLM-014033]; Nimble USD 288m (USD 210m upfront plus contingent consideration; up to USD 130m further) [CLM-014034] [CLM-009057]; Celsius USD 250m [CLM-009064]. FY2025 upfronts: Gilgamesh USD 906m, Ichnos Glenmark USD 700m, Gubra USD 350m, ADARx option USD 335m; FY2024: Aliada USD 1.4bn, Celsius USD 250m [CLM-014031].
- Cerevel assumed a Pfizer licence with up to USD 1.6bn of milestones [CLM-014035]. Horizontals: [deal inventory](../../industry_transformation/partnerships_ecosystem/deal_inventory.md), [scorecard](../../industry_transformation/partnerships_ecosystem/deal_outcomes_scorecard.md), [external-innovation machinery](../../industry_transformation/partnerships_ecosystem/external_innovation_machinery.md).
- Outcomes: ImmunoGen contributed USD 578m revenue and a USD 682m operating loss through 2024 [CLM-009056]; Cerevel's emraclidine failed Phase 2 in November 2024 with a USD 4.5bn impairment, about 54% of the net price (the horizontal's arithmetic, 4.5 of 8.3) [CLM-009054]. DJS (USD 287m, 2022), Syndesi (USD 130m), Soliton (USD 535m) are older bolt-ons [CLM-009065] [CLM-009066] [CLM-009067]. Calico extension (USD 500m AbbVie share) and ADARx are option structures [CLM-009068] [CLM-009061]. Aliada, Landos, Celsius and Nimble were listed without terms in v1.0 [CLM-003074]; terms are now above. Unspecified smaller arrangements: USD 602m / 975m / 582m upfronts in 2025 / 2024 / 2023 [CLM-009069]. AbbVie Ventures founding is 2009 (web page) versus about 2015 (impact report): unresolved [CLM-009074] *(conflicts_proposed_A10 #5)*; one source is sponsored content [CLM-009075]. AbbVie is a BaseLaunch partner [CLM-009094].

## 15. Policy and regulatory
IRA selections: Imbruvica, Vraylar, Botox [CLM-003080]; January 2026 U.S. agreement with 100bn pledge [CLM-003081] (company announcement; single interested source); the brief's USD 10bn 2025 pledge was not found [CLM-003082]. Neutral: activity and outcomes only, no causal inference about influence [CLM-008007]. Horizontals: [policy landscape](../../industry_transformation/policy/policy_landscape.md), [IRA exposure](../../industry_transformation/policy/ira_negotiation_exposure.md), [pricing and pledges](../../industry_transformation/policy/pricing_tariffs_manufacturing_pledges.md), [litigation](../../industry_transformation/policy/litigation_with_policy_dimension.md), [lobbying](../../industry_transformation/policy/lobbying_and_political_activity.md).
- Negotiated prices: Linzess USD 136 (-75%) and Vraylar USD 770 (-44%) from 2027; Imbruvica USD 9,319 (-38%, shared with J&J) from 2026; Botox selected for 2028, price not located [CLM-008012] [CLM-008013] [CLM-008010] [CLM-008015] [CLM-008018]. USD 2.1bn pre-tax Imbruvica impairment in Q3 2023 after selection (fair value 1.9bn vs carrying 4.0bn) [CLM-008019].
- January 2026 agreement: three-year voluntary agreement with USD 100bn of U.S. R&D and capital investment over a decade, low Medicaid prices, TrumpRx offerings and tariff exemption [CLM-008032]. From 2025 the Part D coverage-gap discount became a 10% manufacturer discount [CLM-008020].
- Litigation: Humira antitrust history in §6 [CLM-008048] [CLM-008049]. Lobbying totals not obtained; AbbVie PAC active 2022-2026 cycles [CLM-008004].

## 16. Leadership
Gonzalez to Michael (CEO 2024-07-01, chairman 2025-07-01) [CLM-003076]; internal, continuity heavy [CLM-003079]. See [leadership/leadership.md](leadership/leadership.md).

## 17. AI and data
Horizontals: [landscape](../../industry_transformation/ai_data_robotics/ai_data_robotics_landscape.md), [maturity matrix](../../industry_transformation/ai_data_robotics/maturity_matrix.md), [mechanism cards](../../industry_transformation/ai_data_robotics/capability_mechanism_cards.md).
- Valkai (2026-09-29): announcement only, concept [CLM-003083] [CLM-000285] [CLM-006037].
- ARCH knowledge graph (conceived 2020; fewer than ten FTE plus contractors; over 124 TB; graph of over 30 million nodes and nearly 2 billion relationships): maturity operational; no outcome beyond a preprint; the head of AI said the first version was built "quick, not cheap, not right [or final]" (company speaker relayed by trade press; single interested source) [CLM-006032] [CLM-006033] [CLM-006034]. The source describes a knowledge graph, not generative AI.
- BigHat collaboration (2023-12-05): USD 30m upfront, up to about USD 325m milestones; prototype [CLM-006035]. Founding member of the AISB OpenFold3 consortium (pilot; vendor benchmark, not peer-reviewed) and AISB Bind (concept) [CLM-006042] [CLM-006043] [CLM-006044].
- The 10-K discloses AI skills investment and an adoption-failure risk, with no outcomes [CLM-006036]. Michael (Q4 2025 call): record USD 61.2bn ex-IPR&D revenue despite nearly USD 16bn of U.S. Humira erosion [CLM-014072].

## 18. Successes (top 5) and failures (>=5)
See [successes_failures/successes_failures.md](successes_failures/successes_failures.md).

## 19. Moats (INTERPRETATION)
See [competitive_advantage/moats.md](competitive_advantage/moats.md) and the cards below.

## 20. Capability Mechanism Cards (INTERPRETATION)
**Card 1: successor sequencing.** Problem: 37% of revenue exposed to LOE. Built/bought: Skyrizi/Rinvoq expanded across Humira indications, plus head-to-head data. Enablers: immunology sales force, IL-23/JAK science. Outcome: 25.9bn in 2025. Replicate: launch the successor 3-5 years before the cliff [CLM-003084, CLM-003016].
**Card 2: contracting defence.** Problem: biosimilar entry. Mechanism: rebate-for-access kept >=97% volume to March 2024, then co-branded Humira via Cordavis took 23% of switchers vs 60% for co-promoted Hyrimoz. Limit: 2025 U.S. -57% [CLM-003085].
**Card 3: BD&L refill.** Problem: pipeline gap. Mechanism: buy late-stage/commercial assets (18.5bn consideration transferred in 2024 for ImmunoGen and Cerevel; 17.5bn net of cash acquired). Outcome: one 4.5bn write-down, Elahere growth, Juvmo approval; returns not yet demonstrated [CLM-003086].
**Card 4: settlement-based IP.** Rinvoq entry deferred to 2037 after 2025 settlements; Humira history unverified [CLM-003087].
**Card 5: aesthetics channel (risk).** Loyalty redesign cut share and price; reversed within months [CLM-003033, CLM-003088].

## 21. Lessons for Takeda (HYPOTHESIS/RECOMMENDATION)
Pre-build successors in the same franchise; expect PBM structure to matter as much as patents; size acquisitions to survive a write-down; treat first-in-class psychiatry BD as high variance [CLM-003090].

## 22. Evidence register and gaps
39 sources (20 retrieved, 7 registry API, 8 metadata-only, 3 blocked, 1 unavailable), 91 claims. Gaps: [evidence_gaps.md](evidence_gaps.md) (expanded in v1.1 to list each metadata-only and blocked source). Brief premises tested: impairment ~3.5bn in 2025 CONTRADICTED (4.5bn in Q4 2024) [CLM-003058]; USD 10bn pledge INCONCLUSIVE [CLM-003082].

### v1.1 audit repairs applied (A10 Gate 1: CONDITIONAL PASS)
1. **Debt basis** (CLM-003042 and CLM-000066..000070): the series 75,962 / 63,128 / 59,245 / 66,841 / 64,503 is total long-term debt including the current portion; balance-sheet non-current is 64,189 / 59,135 / 52,194 / 60,340 / 58,941. Corrected in §4, [business model](business/business_model.md) and the Card 3 context [CLM-003042] [CLM-000070].
2. **Deal-size bases** (CLM-003086; master Card 3 and the §14 ImmunoGen line): ImmunoGen 10.1bn announced total value, 9.8bn consideration, 9.2bn net of cash; 18.5bn is consideration transferred for ImmunoGen plus Cerevel (17.5bn net of cash acquired) [CLM-003053] [CLM-003086] [CLM-009056] [CLM-009053].
3. **Evidence gaps** expanded: the eight metadata-only sources, three blocked sources, one unavailable source and the Ventures founding-date conflict are now listed in [evidence_gaps.md](evidence_gaps.md) [CLM-009074].

Where a flagged claim carries a strategic conclusion in this dossier it is marked in text: Humira contracting percentages [CLM-003007] [CLM-003009] [CLM-003085] (T3 IQVIA/trade sources not re-opened by the auditor); CVS exclusion [CLM-003008]; 2027 Skyrizi plus Rinvoq target and nine-month 2026 figures [CLM-003022] [CLM-003023]; aesthetics slowdown and Allē [CLM-003032] [CLM-003033] [CLM-003034]; Allergan synergies [CLM-003049]; the January 2026 U.S. agreement [CLM-003081]; deal announcements [CLM-003052] [CLM-003072] [CLM-003073]; Valkai and ARCH [CLM-000285] [CLM-006032] [CLM-006033] [CLM-006035]; sponsored-content Ventures claim [CLM-009075]. 5. **Juvmo date:** FDA action 2026-09-25 (FDA novel-approvals record), company announcement 2026-09-28 [CLM-012017] [CLM-014039].

reports.title: Successes and failures (A3)
reports.markdown:
# Successes and failures (A3)
## Successes
1. Skyrizi/Rinvoq replacement of Humira [CLM-003014]. 2. Rinvoq IP to 2037 [CLM-003021]. 3. Vyalev approval and 482m 2025 sales [CLM-003037]. 4. Elahere growth [CLM-003036]. 5. Vraylar and Botox Therapeutic growth [CLM-003028, CLM-003030]. Also Juvmo approval (FDA 2026-09-25; AbbVie release 2026-09-28) [CLM-003063] [CLM-012017] [CLM-014039].
## Failures
1. Emraclidine: Phase 2 miss, 4.5bn impairment in Q4 2024 [CLM-003054, CLM-003057]; brief's "3.5bn in 2025" CONTRADICTED [CLM-003058]. 2. Imbruvica decline and IRA selection, 2.1bn impairment [CLM-003025, CLM-003026]. 3. Aesthetics slowdown and loyalty misstep [CLM-003033, CLM-003034, CLM-003035]. 4. Rova-T termination, 1.0bn (2019, older) [CLM-003051]. 5. ABBV-951 two CRLs [CLM-003061]. 6. Humira international erosion [CLM-003003]. 7. Venclexta CANOVA/VERONA misses [CLM-003027]. 8. AGN-151607 630m impairment [CLM-003060]. 9. Epkinly DLBCL OS miss [CLM-003067]. Total intangible impairments 4.2bn, 4.5bn, 0.8bn (2023-25) [CLM-003059]. 10. Cerevel: USD 4.5bn impairment against an 8.3bn net price; ImmunoGen contributed USD 578m revenue and a USD 682m operating loss in its first partial year [CLM-009054] [CLM-009056]. 11. ABBV-951 CRLs (device; third-party manufacturer), Imbruvica accelerated approvals withdrawn, navitoclax discontinued [CLM-012111] [CLM-012112] [CLM-012113] [CLM-012114]. 12. Venclexta VERONA OS miss [CLM-012117].

reports.title: Eli Lilly and Company: master dossier v1.1
reports.markdown:
# Eli Lilly and Company: master dossier v1.1

## Dossier status
- Version: v1.1, 2026-11-21 (supersedes v1.0). Research cutoff 2026-11-21.
- Gate 1 verdict (A10): **PASS with minor repairs** (17/17 sampled figures correct, 12 locator fixes, no blocking defect) [gate1_verdicts.md](../../../quality/citation_audits/gate1_verdicts.md); re-inspection detail in [audit_wave1_reinspection.md](../../../quality/citation_audits/audit_wave1_reinspection.md).
- Claims in the registry tagged LLY at 2026-11-21: 386 (370 FACT, 15 INTERPRETATION, 1 HYPOTHESIS); shard A1_lilly holds CLM-001000..001069. Wave-2 gap-fill claims CLM-014000..014017, 014053..014057, 014058..014059, 014063, 014067..014068 are integrated below.
- v1.1 changes: audit repairs (locators, basis labels, TuneLab wording, FY2021 IPR&D definition), guidance attribution correction, announced-versus-operating manufacturing table (§9), horizontal summaries in §8-13. Repair list in §22.

Research cutoff 2026-11-21. Claim IDs resolve in the evidence registry and shard A1_lilly. 2026 figures are partial periods. Interpretation is labelled.

## 1. Executive thesis
Lilly grew from USD 28.3bn to 65.2bn revenue (FY2021-25) [CLM-000133] [CLM-000137] on tirzepatide, which reached 56% of revenue [CLM-000242] [CLM-001003]. Nine-month 2026 revenue was USD 67.2bn [CLM-001032]. The USD 91-92bn 2026 revenue guidance was raised in the Q3 2026 release of 2026-10-29 from USD 85-87bn; the initial February 2026 guidance was USD 80-83bn [CLM-014001] [CLM-014002]. It financed this with margin expansion [CLM-001005], debt [CLM-000202] and USD 21bn+ Indiana plus >USD 50bn U.S. site commitments [CLM-001039] [CLM-001041]. Whether it is positioned beyond incretins remains *(HYPOTHESIS)*: orforglipron is approved [CLM-001030], retatrutide has positive Phase 3 [CLM-001060].

## 2. Business model
See [business/business_model.md](business/business_model.md). [CLM-001000] [CLM-001001] [CLM-001002] Product detail FY2025 [CLM-000240] [CLM-000241] [CLM-000243] [CLM-000244] [CLM-000245].

## 3. Five-year transformation timeline
See [timeline.md](timeline.md).

## 4. Financial evolution
Net income USD 5.6bn to 20.6bn [CLM-000153] [CLM-000157]; operating cash flow 7.3bn to 16.8bn [CLM-000163] [CLM-000167]; capex [CLM-000172]; capital return [CLM-001008]; margins [CLM-001005] [CLM-001007] [CLM-001006].
- FY2025 per the Q4 2025 release (8-K Ex. 99.1, 2026-02-04): revenue USD 65,179m (+45%), Mounjaro USD 22,965m, Zepbound USD 13,542m, Verzenio USD 5,723m [CLM-014000]; R&D USD 13,337m and acquired IPR&D USD 2,910m; Q4 realized price -5%, volume +46% [CLM-014004].
- Q3 2026 (partial period): revenue USD 24,397m (+39%) [CLM-014002], including about USD 900m of one-off benefits (USD 410m Jardiance milestones, rebate and discount estimate adjustments); realized price -15%, volume +53% [CLM-014003].
- Acquired IPR&D is quoted on two bases that must not be mixed: **expense** USD 2,910m / 3,280m / 3,800m (2025 / 2024 / 2023) [CLM-009000]; **cash paid** USD 3,008m / 3,346m / 3,944m (cash-flow statement, reported in whole USD m for FY2025) [CLM-001014] [CLM-000247]. Morphic: USD 3.2bn headline [CLM-009002] versus USD 2,549m expensed [CLM-009001] and USD 3.35bn cash paid in 2024 *(contested, resolved as different measures: conflicts_proposed_A10 #1, #13)*.
- FY2021 acquired IPR&D is USD 874.9m under the FY2021 line item and USD 970.1m under the FY2022 line item that adds development milestones (+95.2); a definition change, not a restatement [CLM-009022] [CLM-000178] *(conflicts_proposed_A10 #3, resolved)*.

## 5. R&D operating model
R&D grew to USD 13.3bn [CLM-000147] while intensity fell [CLM-001006]. Pipeline 45 to 50 candidates [CLM-001025]; growth through acquired IPR&D (cash paid, USD 3,944m / 3,346m / 3,008m for FY2023-25 [CLM-001014]; expense basis in §4). *(gap)* internal productivity metrics. Ricks said R&D should run at 20-25% of sales (single podcast source) [CLM-014067].

## 6. Pipeline and late-stage assets
See [pipeline/late_stage_assets.md](pipeline/late_stage_assets.md). [CLM-001026]

## 7. Scientific innovations
Efficacy: [CLM-001056] [CLM-001058] [CLM-001060] [CLM-001057]. Peer-reviewed abstracts of company-funded trials.

## 8. AI and data
Horizontal: [landscape](../../industry_transformation/ai_data_robotics/ai_data_robotics_landscape.md), [maturity matrix](../../industry_transformation/ai_data_robotics/maturity_matrix.md), [mechanism cards](../../industry_transformation/ai_data_robotics/capability_mechanism_cards.md), [autonomous-lab check](../../industry_transformation/ai_data_robotics/autonomous_lab_reality_check.md).
- TuneLab (launched 2025-09-09): maturity operational; no scientific or revenue outcome is shown. It is a data-for-access platform in which partners contribute training data; Lilly puts the underlying data cost at over USD 1bn (company estimate) [CLM-000280] [CLM-014055]. *(Wording repair: no source shows TuneLab earning revenue.)* Benchling distribution to 1,300+ customers is opt-in "later this year" (pilot) [CLM-006008]. At least four partners had announced TuneLab collaborations by September 2026, with no participant count or retraining result [CLM-014056]. A vendor blog reports 2 million Lilly and 675,000 partner data points by October 2026 (single interested source) [CLM-009028].
- LillyPod: 1,016 Blackwell Ultra GPUs, more than 9,000 petaflops, assembled in about four months; maturity operational (infrastructure only), no reported result [CLM-006003] [CLM-006004] [CLM-014054] [CLM-006007].
- NVIDIA co-innovation lab: up to USD 1bn over five years, announced 2026-01-12, work "expected to begin" in South San Francisco; no opened source confirms it is operating; maturity concept [CLM-000281] [CLM-014053].
- External models (concept to prototype): Isomorphic Labs USD 45m upfront [CLM-006012]; insitro ADMET [CLM-006009]; Chai custom antibody model, hit-rate claim is the vendor's [CLM-006010]; OpenAI antimicrobials, June 2024 [CLM-006011].
- Retreat and contrary evidence: the Life Sciences Studio robotic lab was sold to Arctoris in 2024 [CLM-006013]. The Strateos link and "about 2020 launch" in CLM-006017 are not found in the cited pages (A10 NOT_FOUND_IN_SOURCE; *contested, see conflicts_proposed_A10 #6*); the reported December 2023 Strateos acquisition by Multiply Labs has no primary source [CLM-014057] [CLM-006015].
- Leadership view: GLP-1s are "probably 80% of the economic value" and AI use is framed as an experiment (single podcast) [CLM-014067] [CLM-014068]. AI appears in the 10-K as a risk factor only (maturity unknown) [CLM-000252].

## 9. Robotics and automation
Horizontal: [autonomous-lab reality check](../../industry_transformation/ai_data_robotics/autonomous_lab_reality_check.md). Richmond site described as using ML, AI and digital automation (announcement, concept/pilot) [CLM-001040]; NVIDIA digital-twin and plant-robot statements are vendor descriptions with no counts (pilot) [CLM-000282] [CLM-006006]. Lilly Lebanon Advanced Therapies opened 2026-05-06; robotic dosing and sealing was seen on a press tour with no performance data [CLM-006002]. The USD 4.5bn Medicine Foundry is planned for late 2027 [CLM-006000] [CLM-006001]. *(gap)* operating evidence for any robotic programme.

### Manufacturing: announced versus operating (gap-fill, wave 2)
| Site | Announced | Stated operational date | Evidence of production | Claim |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Concord, NC | 2022-01-28, USD 1bn, later USD 2bn | n/a | Trade report quoting the site head: commercial production and shipments from end-2024 (partially supported) | [CLM-014014] |
| Lebanon, IN (Advanced Therapies) | part of USD 4.5bn (2026-05-06) | opened 2026-05-06 | Opened (company release) | [CLM-014015] |
| Lebanon, IN (API) | USD 9bn total (2024) plus USD 4.5bn | "opens in 2027" | Not operating | [CLM-014015] [CLM-001038] |
| Kenosha, WI | USD 3bn expansion (2024-12-05; USD 4bn Wisconsin total) | Spokesperson: 2028 (partially supported) | Acquired plant exists; expansion under construction | [CLM-014013] |
| Alzey, DE | USD 2.5bn (2023-11) | "beginning in 2027" | None found | [CLM-014012] |
| Limerick, IE | USD 2bn total (expansion 2024-09) | "on track to start in 2026" | Not confirmed; Kinsale (USD 800m) producing since 2023 | [CLM-014011] |
| Houston, TX | USD 6.5bn (2025-09-23) | within five years | Groundbreaking 2026-09-21 | [CLM-014008] |
| Huntsville, AL | more than USD 6bn (2025-12-09) | completion 2032 | None; construction from 2026 | [CLM-014009] |
| Lehigh Valley, PA | more than USD 3.5bn (2026-01-30) | operational 2031 | None | [CLM-014010] |
| Richmond/Goochland, VA | USD 5bn (2025-09-16) | n/a | Groundbreaking listed in the Q3 2026 8-K | [CLM-014016] [CLM-001040] |

- The FY2025 10-K names only Indiana, North Carolina, Puerto Rico and Wisconsin as major production sites and says further facilities "are expected to come online in future periods" [CLM-014016]. Capex was USD 7.8bn in 2025 (USD 5.1bn in 2024); construction in progress was USD 13,013m at year-end 2025 versus USD 8,245m [CLM-014017].
- *(INTERPRETATION)* Most of the USD 50bn+ pledge [CLM-001039] is under construction or pre-construction; only Concord, Kinsale and the Lebanon genetic-medicine plant show operating evidence.

## 10. Commercial strategy
See [commercial.md](commercial_market_access/commercial.md). [CLM-001042] [CLM-001068] Horizontals: [commercial models](../../industry_transformation/commercial_patient/commercial_models_comparison.md), [pricing and payer dynamics](../../industry_transformation/commercial_patient/pricing_access_and_payer_dynamics.md), [launch execution](../../industry_transformation/commercial_patient/launch_execution_evidence.md).
- Zepbound LillyDirect vial prices fell from USD 399/549 (Aug 2024) to USD 299/399/449 (1 Dec 2025) [CLM-007000] [CLM-007002]; KwikPen self-pay from USD 299 (Feb 2026) [CLM-007044].
- CVS Caremark preferred Wegovy and removed Zepbound from 2025-07-01 (Lilly stock closed more than 11% lower that day), then added Zepbound back as an additional preferred option from 2026-10-01 [CLM-007011] [CLM-007012] [CLM-007013]. Switching away from tirzepatide rose from about 0.6% to 10.2% a month in a second-hand analysis (partially supported) [CLM-007014].
- 2025 growth came from volume partly offset by lower realized prices [CLM-007024]; Q3 2026 realized price -15%, volume +53% [CLM-014003].
- LillyDirect: the 10-K gives no dollar figure [CLM-014006]; neither earnings exhibit contains a LillyDirect or self-pay statement [CLM-014005]; Lilly says over 1 million patients used it in 2025 (company-reported, partially supported) [CLM-007004].

reports.title: Successes and failures
reports.markdown:
# Successes and failures
## Successes (verified)
1. Tirzepatide: approvals [CLM-001028] [CLM-001029], efficacy [CLM-001056], revenue share [CLM-001003].
2. Revenue and margin expansion [CLM-001005] [CLM-001007] [CLM-000137].
3. Kisunla approval after 11-0 panel [CLM-001067] [CLM-001063].
4. Oral GLP-1 approval [CLM-001030].
5. New-launch breadth (Jaypirca, Omvoh, Ebglyss, Inluriyo) [CLM-001061] [CLM-001062] [CLM-001064] [CLM-001065].
## Failures and weaknesses
1. Trulicity decline [CLM-001004].
2. Vitrakvi impairment and USD 435m litigation charge [CLM-001013].
3. Donanemab and lebrikizumab CRLs [CLM-001024]; donanemab ARIA-E 24%, treatment-related deaths [CLM-001057].
4. Supply shortage Dec 2022 to 2024 and compounding [CLM-001066] [CLM-001018].
5. COVID antibody write-down [CLM-001010]; Alimta generics [CLM-001011]; Loxo/GBA1 impairments [CLM-001012].
6. Concentration risk [CLM-001003]; litigation [CLM-001069]; discontinued programs [CLM-001019].
7. DICE DC-806 discontinued 2024 after a USD 1,916m acquisition charge; Prevail GBA1 impaired 2022 [CLM-009003] [CLM-009009].
8. Most announced U.S. capacity is not yet operating [CLM-014014] [CLM-014008] [CLM-014009] [CLM-014010].
9. Q3 2026 growth included about USD 0.9bn of one-off benefits and realized price fell 15% [CLM-014003].

reports.title: Evidence gaps — Johnson & Johnson (A2; updated v1.1, 2026-11-21)
reports.markdown:
# Evidence gaps — Johnson & Johnson (A2; updated v1.1, 2026-11-21)

## Closed in v1.1
- 510(k)/De Novo database entries: MONARCH K260382, VELYS K240211/K260480/K253551/K233227/K202769 and the OTTAVA De Novo grant letter are now cited [CLM-014022] [CLM-014025] [CLM-014026]. MONARCH QUEST 3 is registered [CLM-014025].
- Varipulse: FDA correction notice read [CLM-014018]. Talc: 2025-03-31 dismissal and 2026-07-27 resolution terms registered [CLM-014027] [CLM-014029]. DePuy Synthes timing: 18-24 months per the 10-K [CLM-014021]. JLABS scale: contraction documented [CLM-014064]; JJDC/AI: [CLM-014066] [CLM-006018].
- Wording defects fixed: OTTAVA install, 24-month derivation, debt basis, broken links (master_report §22).

## Still open

- **"26 drugs with >USD 1bn potential by 2030":** searched; no primary source opened. Comparison with actual approvals not done.
- **Stelara EU biosimilar entry (2024-07)**, Xarelto and Imbruvica details, Carvykti/Rybrevant/Spravato label-by-label dates: not individually sourced.
- **CMS Maximum Fair Prices** per drug: CMS fact sheet registered metadata_only (SRC-002021) [CLM-002054].
- **MedTech adoption:** no VELYS, MONARCH or OTTAVA installed-base or procedure numbers after gap-fill [CLM-014026]; MONARCH Middle East (2026-07-28) and NVIDIA Isaac collaboration seen only as search snippets. The link between K260382 and the "QUEST 3" name is inferred [CLM-014025]. The 2026-11-19 OTTAVA release date is not shown in the page text read by the auditor; install completion unconfirmed [CLM-000284]. OTTAVA filing date conflicts (2026-01-07 versus FDA receipt 2025-12-18) [CLM-014022].
- **Impella:** only two FDA recall records; no FDA warning-letter or sales-impact analysis. Impella 510(k)/PMA entries not opened.
- **340B:** court opinion itself not opened; STAT article paywalled after the third paragraph; J&J participation in HRSA pilot unverified.
- **Talc:** court records are via Bailey Glasser and Bloomberg Law, not docket; the 2026-07-27 resolution is company and Reuters/CNBC only; participation outcome unknown.
- **Financial detail:** capex and cash returned FY2021–24, restated margins FY2021–23 not extracted.
- **JJDC portfolio counts, Polyphonic hospital counts, posdinemab, Rybrevant/Lazcluze clinical data:** not found or not researched [CLM-014066] [CLM-006030]. J&J's AI results are self-reported without baselines [CLM-006020]; WSJ original paywalled [CLM-006019]. New York JLABS closure rests on a snippet [CLM-014065].
- **Single-interested-source claims** (CLM-002037, -002039, -002040, -002041, -002044, -002060, -002061, -002064) flagged in master_report §19; independent corroboration exists only for Varipulse [CLM-014018], aticaprant [CLM-012135] and the Orthopaedics timing [CLM-014021]. Talc claim sources are secondary (Bailey Glasser, Bloomberg Law, Reuters/CNBC); participation outcome unknown [CLM-014029].
- **Horizontal gaps:** [ai_data_robotics](../../industry_transformation/ai_data_robotics/evidence_gaps.md), [partnerships](../../industry_transformation/partnerships_ecosystem/evidence_gaps.md), [pipeline](../../industry_transformation/pipeline_regulatory/evidence_gaps.md), [policy](../../industry_transformation/policy/evidence_gaps.md), [commercial](../../industry_transformation/commercial_patient/evidence_gaps.md).
- **Q3 2026 and 2026-dated press releases** are company documents; no independent corroboration.

## Suggested next queries
J&J 10-Q 2026 talc note; DARZALEX patent/biosimilar timeline; FDA 510(k) database Impella/VELYS; Stelara biosimilar share (IQVIA); JLABS press releases.

reports.markdown:
# Johnson & Johnson — master dossier (v1.1)

## Dossier status
- Version: v1.1, 2026-11-21 (supersedes v1.0).
- Gate 1 verdict (A10): **CONDITIONAL PASS** (13/13 sampled figures correct; five required repairs, all applied in v1.1 except where noted in §22) [gate1_verdicts.md](../../../quality/citation_audits/gate1_verdicts.md); detail in [audit_wave1_reinspection.md](../../../quality/citation_audits/audit_wave1_reinspection.md) and [audit_wave1_status_discipline.md](../../../quality/citation_audits/audit_wave1_status_discipline.md).
- Claims in the registry tagged JNJ at 2026-11-21: 330 (313 FACT, 17 INTERPRETATION); shard A2_jnj holds CLM-002000..002075. Wave-2 gap-fill claims CLM-014018..014029, 014064..014066, 014069..014071 are integrated below.
- v1.1 changes: OTTAVA wording (announced installation site), derivation withdrawn, regulator-record labels, debt-basis wording, broken links fixed, single-interested-source flags, §8-13 horizontals. Repair list in §22.

Cut-off 2026-11-21. Claim IDs resolve in `../../evidence_library/claims_registry.jsonl` (CLM-000xxx) and `../../evidence_library/shards/A2_jnj/claims.jsonl` (CLM-002xxx). Fiscal years are 52 weeks ending on the Sunday nearest 31 December (FY2025 ended 2025-12-28; FY2026 has 53 weeks) [CLM-002005]. Q3 2026 data are a partial period [CLM-002060]. Sources are mostly company documents (interested party); regulator, court and registry sources are flagged.

## 1. Executive thesis
J&J is the only one of the three comparator companies with two operating segments after separating Consumer Health: Innovative Medicine (USD 60.4bn, +6.0%) and MedTech (USD 33.8bn) in FY2025 [CLM-000253]. Its distinctive FY2025 outcome is absorbing the largest loss of exclusivity in its portfolio: STELARA fell 41.3% to USD 6.1bn [CLM-000254] while DARZALEX (USD 14.4bn) [CLM-000255], TREMFYA [CLM-000256] and CARVYKTI [CLM-000257] grew, and group sales still rose 6.0% [CLM-000253]. Excluding STELARA, sales grew about 12%, about 1 point acquired [CLM-002075] *(INTERPRETATION)*. The cost was debt: net debt rose to USD 27.8bn [CLM-002014]. Vulnerabilities: talc [CLM-002062], DARZALEX concentration [CLM-002073], MedTech margin and growth [CLM-002004] [CLM-002060].

## 2. Business model
Two segments: Innovative Medicine 36.9% pre-tax margin and 19.6% R&D intensity; MedTech 12.2% and 8.4% [CLM-002004]. Segment series FY2021–25 [CLM-002000] [CLM-002001] [CLM-002002] [CLM-002003]. U.S. 57% of sales [CLM-002033]. Detail: [business/business_model.md](business/business_model.md).

## 3. Five-year timeline
See [timeline.md](timeline.md).

## 4. Financial evolution
Revenue, R&D, net income: [financials/xbrl_annual_facts.md](financials/xbrl_annual_facts.md); FY2025 net earnings USD 26,804m versus 14,066m in 2024 (litigation charges) [CLM-000261]. Net debt USD 2.1bn → 16.1bn (FY2022) → 27.8bn (FY2025) [CLM-002010] [CLM-002014]. Q3 2026 net earnings USD 210m after a special talc charge; FY2026 guidance USD 101.0–101.4bn [CLM-002060] [CLM-002061].

## 5. R&D model
Innovative Medicine R&D USD 11.8bn in FY2025 [CLM-002004]; 2023 prioritisation exited infectious disease/vaccines [CLM-002018]; IPR&D impairments USD 313m/211m/81m [CLM-002031]. R&D is complemented by acquisitions [CLM-002012] [CLM-002013].

## 6. Pipeline
Approvals and late-stage assets: [pipeline/late_stage_assets.md](pipeline/late_stage_assets.md); registry inventory [pipeline/ctgov_inventory.md](pipeline/ctgov_inventory.md). Icotrokinra approved 2026 [CLM-002065] with PsA/UC/CD Phase 3 [CLM-002055]. Aticaprant failed [CLM-002039].

## 7. Science and platforms
Cell therapy (CARVYKTI), bispecifics, ADC (Ambrx), RIPTAC (Halda), oral IL-23 peptide [CLM-002012] [CLM-002013] [CLM-002065]. Deeper scientific review not performed (gap).

## 8. AI and data
Horizontals: [landscape](../../industry_transformation/ai_data_robotics/ai_data_robotics_landscape.md), [maturity matrix](../../industry_transformation/ai_data_robotics/maturity_matrix.md), [mechanism cards](../../industry_transformation/ai_data_robotics/capability_mechanism_cards.md). Every metric below is self-reported by J&J executives (single interested source, no baselines).
- Enterprise gen-AI: nearly 900 use cases reviewed and a move from proofs of concept to deployment (pilot to operational) [CLM-006018]; 10-15% of use cases drive about 80% of value (relayed; partially supported) [CLM-006019]; "up to 2.6x" trial-site enrolment at better-performing sites, baseline and method undisclosed (retagged pilot, self-reported) [CLM-006020]; quality-control answers in minutes instead of weeks [CLM-006021]; 47,000 employees completed a required gen-AI course (a training metric, not a deployment) [CLM-006022].
- Duato (Bernstein, 2026-05-27): AI used in molecule design and clinical operations, with no named programmes or metrics [CLM-014071].
- Polyphonic digital surgery: early access "to select hospitals only" (2025-10-27) [CLM-006030]; Abu Dhabi deployment announced 2026-05-21 and expected, not operating (concept) [CLM-006031]. J&J is a founding member of the federated AISB OpenFold3 consortium (pilot) [CLM-006042].
- The FY2025 10-K gives a generic AI statement and risk language, with no OTTAVA or MONARCH text [CLM-006025].

## 9. Robotics and automation
OTTAVA: FDA De Novo DEN250068 granted 2026-07-21 per the FDA grant letter (request received 2025-12-18) [CLM-014022]; J&J announced the authorization on 2026-07-22 [CLM-000283]. On 2026-11-19 J&J announced Memorial Hermann-Texas Medical Center as the **first hospital to install** OTTAVA under an early-access commercial programme [CLM-014024]; the release uses future tense, so this is an announced installation site and not a completed install [CLM-000284] *(contested wording, see conflicts_proposed_A10 #11)*. Maturity: pilot (regulator-authorised; no installed-base or procedure data) [CLM-014022]. MONARCH: QUEST 3 clearance announced 2026-08-17 [CLM-014025]; openFDA K260382 (decided 2026-07-25) and K243219 (auditor record) [CLM-014025] [CLM-000286]; TARGET data (company-sponsored) [CLM-002067]. VELYS: openFDA lists K260480 (2026-06-25) and K240211 (2024-06-05) among five clearances [CLM-014026]; VELYS Spine [CLM-002066]; the 10-K reports pull-through with no system or procedure counts, so VELYS is operational, not scaled [CLM-006026]. No installed-base figure exists for any platform *(gap)*. OTTAVA De Novo was granted earlier than Duato's stated expectation of "by the end of this year, beginning of next year" [CLM-014070]. Detail: [robotics_automation/medtech_robotics_status.md](robotics_automation/medtech_robotics_status.md); FDA record labelling: OTTAVA, MONARCH and VELYS milestones are now backed by FDA records (De Novo grant letter, openFDA 510(k)); other statements about adoption remain company-reported.

## 10. Commercial and market access
[commercial_market_access/commercial.md](commercial_market_access/commercial.md): Stelara biosimilars [CLM-002052], Tremfya conversion [CLM-002026], IRA [CLM-002021] [CLM-002054], 340B [CLM-002069] [CLM-002070]. Horizontals: [commercial models](../../industry_transformation/commercial_patient/commercial_models_comparison.md), [pricing and payer dynamics](../../industry_transformation/commercial_patient/pricing_access_and_payer_dynamics.md), [launch execution](../../industry_transformation/commercial_patient/launch_execution_evidence.md).
- Stelara: Optum Rx excluded it from two main formularies from 2025-07-01 with nine biosimilars on the market (partially supported, trade commentary) [CLM-007016]; CVS Caremark prefers Pyzchiva and Yesintek over Stelara from 2026-07-01 [CLM-007015]. U.S. Stelara sales were about USD 3.8bn in FY2025 and the decline cut Innovative Medicine growth [CLM-007017].
- Part D redesign reduced Erleada, Invega, Opsumit and Uptravi sales [CLM-007018].
- Launch curves FY2025: Carvykti USD 1,887m vs 963m (capacity-limited), Spravato USD 1,696m vs 1,077m (certified-setting restriction under its REMS), Tremfya USD 5,155m vs 3,670m [CLM-007029] [CLM-007030].
- No gross-to-net figure for J&J was found in the passages read [CLM-007024].

## 11. Patient care
J&J withMe (formerly Janssen CarePath), free, no income requirement for its savings programme [CLM-002071] [CLM-007035]; no adherence or time-to-therapy outcome data for any company's support programme [CLM-007039]. Horizontal: [patient programmes](../../industry_transformation/commercial_patient/patient_programs_and_care_delivery.md). *(gap)*

## 12. Partnerships and M&A
Abiomed [CLM-002009], Shockwave [CLM-002068], Ambrx/Proteologix/Numab/V-Wave [CLM-002012], Intra-Cellular [CLM-002041], Halda [CLM-002013]. Horizontals: [deal inventory](../../industry_transformation/partnerships_ecosystem/deal_inventory.md), [scorecard](../../industry_transformation/partnerships_ecosystem/deal_outcomes_scorecard.md), [external-innovation machinery](../../industry_transformation/partnerships_ecosystem/external_innovation_machinery.md).
- Capital: USD 15.1bn (FY2024) and USD 17.5bn (FY2025) of business acquisitions [CLM-009049]. Abiomed USD 17.1bn net with a CVR that was reduced in 2025 [CLM-009041] [CLM-009042]; Intra-Cellular USD 14.5bn, CAPLYTA MDD approved in Q4 2025, nine months after close [CLM-009030] [CLM-009031]; Shockwave USD 12.6bn [CLM-009033]; Halda about USD 3.05bn net [CLM-009032].
- Write-downs: Auris/OTTAVA partial impairment USD 0.9bn (FY2021) [CLM-009047]; bermekimab about USD 0.8bn (FY2022) [CLM-009046]; M710 (Momenta) about USD 0.2bn in each of 2023 and 2024 [CLM-009045]; Laminar pivotal study suspended 2025 after USD 0.4bn plus a USD 0.3bn milestone [CLM-009039] [CLM-009040]; NM26 interim analysis met early-termination criteria 2025, direction unknown [CLM-009037]. Momenta yielded IMAAVY (2025-04-30) [CLM-009044].
- Ecosystem: JLABS planned in 2016 at six sites with capacity for 225 companies [CLM-009051]; J&J withdrew from Toronto, Houston and Washington D.C. in 2025, leaving 11 sites in August 2025 [CLM-014064]; a snippet says New York is closing (not opened) [CLM-014065] [CLM-009052]. J&J claims more than 150 partnerships (company statement) [CLM-009050]. No JJDC portfolio count or fund size was found [CLM-014066].
- AbbVie's Aliada was co-founded by JJDC and built on J&J-created BBB-shuttle science before AbbVie bought it for USD 1.4bn [CLM-014032].

## 13. Policy and regulation
IRA negotiation [CLM-002021] [CLM-002054]; Part D redesign [CLM-002025]; 340B [CLM-002069] [CLM-002070]; opioid settlement [CLM-002032]. Neutral: activity and outcomes only, no causal inference about influence [CLM-008007]. Horizontals: [policy landscape](../../industry_transformation/policy/policy_landscape.md), [IRA exposure](../../industry_transformation/policy/ira_negotiation_exposure.md), [pricing and pledges](../../industry_transformation/policy/pricing_tariffs_manufacturing_pledges.md), [litigation](../../industry_transformation/policy/litigation_with_policy_dimension.md), [lobbying](../../industry_transformation/policy/lobbying_and_political_activity.md).
- Negotiated 2026 prices: Stelara USD 4,695 (-66% vs list), Xarelto USD 197 (-62%), Imbruvica USD 9,319 (-38%) [CLM-008008] [CLM-008009] [CLM-008010]; Stelara and Xarelto leave the programme from 2027 [CLM-008011]; Erleada is a third-cycle drug for 2028, price not located [CLM-008015]. Janssen's constitutional challenge ended when the Supreme Court denied certiorari on 2026-05-18 [CLM-008023] [CLM-008024].
- Pledges and agreements: more than USD 55bn of U.S. investment over four years (2025-03-21) [CLM-008030]; voluntary agreement of 2026-01-08 with TrumpRx participation, Medicaid pricing and a tariff exemption [CLM-008031].
- 340B: D.C. Circuit held on 2026-07-21 that rebate models need HRSA approval (consolidated appeal including J&J's 2024-11-12 suit) [CLM-008039]; Stelara and Xarelto are outside the 2027 HRSA rebate pilot cohort [CLM-008041].
- Talc: prepackaged plan about USD 6.475bn present value (May 2024), Red River bankruptcy (September 2024) dismissed in March 2025 [CLM-008050] [CLM-014027]; about USD 7bn of reserve reversed, no appeal, USD 3.4bn reserve at Q4 2025 [CLM-014028]; on 2026-07-27 a USD 5.5bn conditional resolution of about 76,000 ovarian claims (at least 95% participation; first payment at most USD 3bn in 2027), outcome unknown [CLM-014029]. Opioids: up to USD 5.0bn, about 80% paid by FY2025 end [CLM-008051].
- Lobbying: PhRMA dues above USD 500,000 in 2023 (about 8% used for federal lobbying); J&J PAC active 2022-2026 cycles; annual lobbying totals not obtained [CLM-008006] [CLM-008003].

## 14. Leadership
[leadership/leadership.md](leadership/leadership.md) [CLM-002035] [CLM-002064]. Duato (2026-05-27): 2026 guidance of 6.1% adjusted operational growth and more than USD 100bn of revenue [CLM-014069].

## 15. Successes
DARZALEX, CARVYKTI/bispecifics, Stelara absorption, Kenvue exit, cardiovascular M&A integration: [successes_failures/successes_failures.md](successes_failures/successes_failures.md).

## 16. Failures and weaknesses
Talc [CLM-002015] [CLM-002043], aticaprant [CLM-002039], RSV/COVID vaccine exits [CLM-002018] [CLM-002019], bermekimab [CLM-002020], Varipulse [CLM-002045] (FDA correction notice: 4 of 132 U.S. External Evaluation patients, about 3%, had stroke or TIA versus about 1% or less expected; Instructions for Use updated 2025-02-14 for all lots, a correction and not a removal [CLM-014018]), Impella recalls [CLM-002046] [CLM-002047]; aticaprant VENTURA stopped 2025-03-06 for insufficient efficacy, safety acceptable (company release only) [CLM-014019]; OTTAVA/Auris impairment of USD 0.9bn (FY2021) [CLM-009047].

## 17. Competitive advantages and moats
*(INTERPRETATION)* myeloma depth [CLM-002072]; dual platform unproven [CLM-002074]; M&A capacity. See [competitive_advantage/moats.md](competitive_advantage/moats.md).

## 18. Capability Mechanism Cards

### Card 1 — Replacing a lost franchise (Stelara → Tremfya/Icotyde)
- Problem: STELARA USD 10.4bn (FY2024) at loss of exclusivity [CLM-002022].
- Built/bought: TREMFYA IL-23 antibody with UC/Crohn's labels [CLM-002053]; oral icotrokinra approved [CLM-002065].
- Enablers: earlier launch of a successor; head-to-head data vs STELARA in Crohn's per J&J [CLM-002053].
- Pilot vs production: production; TREMFYA +40.5% [CLM-000256].
- Outcome: offset about one third of the 2025 Stelara loss [CLM-002026]; Immunology still -11.8%.
- Cost: not disclosed. Defensibility: depends on IL-23 competitors *(gap)*. Maturity: demonstrated_outcome (partial).

### Card 2 — Cardiovascular device roll-up (Abiomed + Shockwave + Biosense Webster)
- Problem: need for higher-growth MedTech segments [CLM-002037] (company release only: single interested source). Orthopaedics separation targets completion 18-24 months after the 2025-10-14 announcement; FY2025 Orthopaedics sales USD 9.3bn (+1.1%) [CLM-014020] [CLM-014021].
- Bought: Abiomed USD 17.1bn net [CLM-002009]; Shockwave at USD 335/share [CLM-002011].
- Outcome: Cardiovascular USD 8.9bn (+15.8%), Abiomed 1.75bn, Shockwave 1.15bn [CLM-002027] [CLM-002011]; offset: PFA competition and Varipulse pause [CLM-002028] [CLM-002045]; Impella recalls [CLM-002046].
- Defensibility: safety record and competition are the risk; synergy with pharma not evidenced [CLM-002074]. Maturity: scaled (Abiomed/Shockwave), mixed (EP).

### Card 3 — Surgical robotics (OTTAVA/MONARCH/VELYS)
- Problem: lack of a soft-tissue robot; competitor incumbency *(INTERPRETATION)*.
- Built: OTTAVA from IDE (2024-11) to De Novo (2026-07) and an announced first installation site (2026-11; not a completed install) [CLM-002048] [CLM-002049] [CLM-000283] [CLM-000284] [CLM-014022] [CLM-014024]; MONARCH with 679-patient dataset [CLM-002067]; VELYS Spine [CLM-002066].
- Pilot vs production: one announced early-access installation site (Memorial Hermann) only; no completed-install evidence. Outcome: no adoption or clinical-superiority evidence. Cost: not disclosed. Maturity: pilot for OTTAVA (regulator-authorised, no installed base); operational, not scaled, for MONARCH and VELYS [CLM-006026] [CLM-014025].

## 19. Contradictions and uncertainty
Impella recalls vs continued growth [CLM-002046] [CLM-002027]; company attribution of Varipulse events to use [CLM-002045]; talc total cost USD 5.5bn+ (company) vs 7bn+ (plaintiff counsel) vs reserve USD 3.4bn at FY2025 [CLM-002062] [CLM-002063] [CLM-002016]; 2026-03-17 ICOTYDE date from company release only [CLM-002065] (FDA novel-approvals record lists Icotyde on 2026-03-17 [CLM-012012]). OTTAVA De Novo date: FDA grant letter 2026-07-21 [CLM-014022] versus J&J announcement 2026-07-22 [CLM-000283]; De Novo filing date: J&J said it submitted in January 2026 (2026-01-07) [CLM-002049] versus FDA record of receipt on 2025-12-18 [CLM-014022] *(contested; the FDA letter is the regulator record)*. Segment recast: FY2021 Pharmaceutical 52,080 and Consumer Health 14,635 versus 51,680 and 15,035 in the FY2022 comparatives (conflicts_proposed_A10 #9) [CLM-002000] [CLM-002001].

**Single-interested-source flags (A10).** These claims rest only on J&J-issued documents; treat any outcome wording in them as company-reported: CLM-002037 (Orthopaedics separation), CLM-002039 (aticaprant), CLM-002040 (Kenvue exchange results), CLM-002041 (Intra-Cellular accretion statement), CLM-002044 (Varipulse pause; partly corroborated by FDA's correction notice [CLM-014018]), CLM-002060 (Q3 2026 results), CLM-002061 (FY2026 guidance), CLM-002064 (Taubert retirement). Aticaprant is corroborated by a registry record [CLM-012135]; the separation intent is corroborated in the 10-K [CLM-014021].

## 20. Implications (INTERPRETATION / HYPOTHESIS)
J&J's playbook is successor launch plus bolt-on M&A, funded with debt; durability depends on DARZALEX [CLM-002073], talc settlement uptake [CLM-002062] and MedTech execution [CLM-002060].

## 21. Lessons for Takeda (HYPOTHESIS)
LOE can be absorbed when successors are launched before the cliff (TREMFYA/ICOTYDE); acquisitions bridge gaps but raise net debt [CLM-002014]; an earlier draft derived "about 24 months from IDE to first commercial install" from [CLM-002049]; that derivation is withdrawn because the release describes an announced installation site, not a completed install [CLM-000284].

## 22. Evidence register and gaps
Shard A2_jnj: 38 sources (32 retrieved, 5 api_json, 1 metadata_only), 76 claims (72 FACT, 4 INTERPRETATION). See [evidence_gaps.md](evidence_gaps.md) and [map.md](map.md).

### v1.1 audit repairs applied (A10 Gate 1: CONDITIONAL PASS)
1. **OTTAVA wording** (§9, Card 3, §21, [timeline.md](timeline.md), [robotics status](robotics_automation/medtech_robotics_status.md)): "announced Memorial Hermann as first installation site", not a completed install; the "about 24 months from IDE to first commercial install" derivation removed (the registry correction on CLM-000284 and CLM-002049's arithmetic remain; the registry text was not edited).
2. **Regulator-record labels:** MONARCH (openFDA K260382, K243219), VELYS (K260480, K240211) and the OTTAVA De Novo (DEN250068 grant letter) now cite FDA records [CLM-014025] [CLM-014026] [CLM-014022]; adoption and installed-base claims stay company-reported. "Regulator-verified" wording in CLM-000286 and CLM-006054 is treated as company-reported for anything beyond the FDA record itself.
3. **Single-interested-source flags** on the eight T2-only claims (§19). The registry field `single_interested_source` is not edited here.
4. **Debt basis** (CLM-000128..000132): see [business model](business/business_model.md): non-current USD 39,438m, debt-note subtotal USD 41,438m including the current portion of USD 2,000m, and USD 47.9bn including loans and notes payable [CLM-000132] [CLM-002014].
5. **Broken relative links** in [business/business_model.md](business/business_model.md) fixed (three).
6. Maturity retags relevant here: CLM-006026 VELYS SCALED to operational; CLM-006020 OPERATIONAL to pilot (self-reported); CLM-006022 not a deployment [CLM-006026] [CLM-006020] [CLM-006022]. Registry retags are pending; the dossier uses the corrected values.

# J&J business architecture, FY2021–FY2025

## Established
- **Segment sales.** FY2021 Pharmaceutical USD 52,080m, Medical Devices 27,060m, Consumer Health 14,635m [CLM-002000]; FY2022 recast 52,563 / 27,427 / 14,953 (Consumer Health later discontinued) [CLM-002001]; FY2023 Innovative Medicine 54,759 (+4.2%) and MedTech 30,400 (+10.8%) [CLM-002002]; FY2024 56,964 (+4.0%) and 31,857 (+4.8%) [CLM-002003]; FY2025 60,401 (+6.0%) and 33,792 [CLM-000253]. Totals and net income: [CLM-000261]; full series in [financials/xbrl_annual_facts.md](../financials/xbrl_annual_facts.md).
- **Margins and R&D, FY2025.** Segment pre-tax margin 36.9% (Innovative Medicine) vs 12.2% (MedTech); R&D USD 11,827m (19.6% of segment sales) vs 2,838m (8.4%) [CLM-002004].
- **Geography, FY2025.** U.S. USD 53.8bn (+6.9%), international 40.4bn (+5.0%) [CLM-002033].
- **Therapeutic areas, FY2025.** Oncology USD 25,380m (+22.1%) [CLM-002024]; Immunology 15,728m (-11.8%) [CLM-002026]; Neuroscience 7,837m (+10.1%) [CLM-002025].
- **MedTech franchises.** Cardiovascular USD 8,928m (+15.8%), Electrophysiology 5,634m (+7.0%) with PFA competitive pressure [CLM-002028]; Orthopaedics 9,258m (+1.1%) [CLM-002029]; Abiomed 1,751m [CLM-002027]; Shockwave 1,146m [CLM-002011].
- **Capital deployment.** Debt USD 33.8bn (FY2021) → 39.7bn (FY2022) after Abiomed [CLM-002010]; 47.9bn at FY2025 with net debt 27.8bn after Intra-Cellular and Halda [CLM-002014] [CLM-002013]. **Debt bases (Gate 1 relabel):** three different measures are in use. (1) Balance-sheet non-current long-term debt: USD 39,438m at FY2025 (30,651m at FY2024). (2) The debt-note subtotal USD 41,438m (32,400m at FY2024) includes the current portion of USD 2,000m; the XBRL claims CLM-000128..000132 call it "non-current", which is wrong, and the series 32,116 / 28,439 / 27,350 / 32,400 / 41,438 (FY2021-25) is gross long-term debt including the current portion [CLM-000128] [CLM-000129] [CLM-000130] [CLM-000131] [CLM-000132]. (3) USD 47.9bn is total debt including loans and notes payable [CLM-002014]. Net debt 27.8bn is a fourth, net measure [CLM-002014]. FY2025 dividends ~USD 12.4bn and buybacks USD 6.0bn [CLM-002014]. Acquisitions: [CLM-002009] [CLM-002012] [CLM-002013].
- **Perimeter changes.** Kenvue IPO and exchange offer [CLM-002006] [CLM-002007] [CLM-002040]; Orthopaedics separation intended (announced 2025-10-14; FY2024 Orthopaedics sales about USD 9.2bn; completion targeted 18-24 months after announcement) [CLM-002037] [CLM-002030] [CLM-014020] [CLM-014021].
- **Q3 2026 (partial period).** Sales USD 25,399m (+5.9%), Innovative Medicine +7.7%, MedTech +2.5% [CLM-002060]; FY2026 guidance USD 101.0–101.4bn [CLM-002061] (both Q3 items are company-release only: single interested source). Duato's 2026 growth framing: 6.1% adjusted operational growth [CLM-014069].

## Interpretation
- MedTech earns about one third of the Innovative Medicine margin on about 36% of sales; this gap frames the Orthopaedics separation [CLM-002004].
- Ex-Stelara growth was about +12% in FY2025, of which about 1 point was acquired [CLM-002075].

## Unknown
Capex series, cash returned FY2021–FY2024 and per-segment margins before FY2024 were not extracted (see [evidence_gaps.md](../evidence_gaps.md)); consult [financials/xbrl_annual_facts.md](../financials/xbrl_annual_facts.md). Segment recast note: FY2021 Pharmaceutical 52,080 / Consumer Health 14,635 versus 51,680 / 15,035 in FY2022 comparatives; use as-reported for levels and recast only for like-for-like growth (conflicts_proposed_A10 #9) [CLM-002000] [CLM-002001].

reports.title: Commercial and market access
reports.markdown:
# Commercial and market access

## Established
- **Stelara cliff.** Sales 9,134 (FY2021) → 10,858 (FY2023 peak) → 10,361 (FY2024) → 6,078 (FY2025, -41.3%); U.S. 6.7bn → 3.8bn [CLM-002022]. First U.S. biosimilars: Wezlana January 2025, then Pyzchiva, Yesintek, Selarsdi by late February [CLM-002052].
- **Successors.** TREMFYA 5,155 (+40.5%) covering about one third of Stelara's USD 4.3bn loss [CLM-002026]; Crohn's approval March 2025 [CLM-002053]; ICOTYDE approved 2026 [CLM-002065]. Immunology segment fell 11.8% [CLM-002026]. Q3 2026: Stelara ~690 bp drag [CLM-002060].
- **Medicare negotiation.** XARELTO, STELARA and IMBRUVICA were selected; Janssen sued in July 2023 [CLM-002021]; negotiated prices effective 2026-01-01, per-drug figures not inspected [CLM-002054]. Medicare Part D redesign cited for Invega and Stelara declines [CLM-002025].
- **340B.** J&J's contract-pharmacy delivery policy [CLM-002034]; 2025-06-27 court ruling that HRSA could require approval of the rebate model [CLM-002069]; HRSA's own rebate pilot enjoined 2025-12-29 [CLM-002070].
- **Patient support.** Janssen CarePath becoming J&J withMe, free with no income requirement for its savings programme [CLM-002071] [CLM-007035].
- **Negotiated prices (2026).** Stelara USD 4,695 (-66% vs 2023 list), Xarelto USD 197 (-62%), Imbruvica USD 9,319 (-38%) [CLM-008008] [CLM-008009] [CLM-008010]; Stelara and Xarelto deselected from 2027 [CLM-008011]; Erleada selected for 2028 [CLM-008015]; Supreme Court denied certiorari to Janssen on 2026-05-18 [CLM-008024].
- **Payer events.** Optum Rx excluded Stelara from two main formularies on 2025-07-01 with nine biosimilars on the market (trade commentary, partially supported) [CLM-007016]; CVS Caremark prefers Pyzchiva and Yesintek from 2026-07-01 [CLM-007015]. U.S. Stelara about USD 3.8bn in FY2025 [CLM-007017]. Part D redesign cut Erleada, Invega, Opsumit and Uptravi sales [CLM-007018].
- **Launch curves.** Carvykti USD 1,887m vs 963m (capacity-limited); Spravato USD 1,696m vs 1,077m, restricted to certified settings [CLM-007029] [CLM-007030]. 340B: D.C. Circuit 2026-07-21 [CLM-008039]; Stelara and Xarelto outside the 2027 HRSA pilot cohort [CLM-008041].
- **Other.** ERISA class action over J&J's own prescription-drug benefit management (allegation) [CLM-007050]. Horizontals: [commercial_patient](../../../industry_transformation/commercial_patient/map.md), [policy](../../../industry_transformation/policy/map.md).

## Contested / unknown
Payer rebate levels, net price erosion, J&J withMe uptake and the 340B financial impact are undisclosed in inspected sources. Stelara biosimilar share data not retrieved (gap).

reports.title: Moats (INTERPRETATION; mechanism and replication path)
reports.markdown:
# Moats (INTERPRETATION; mechanism and replication path)

1. **Myeloma franchise depth.** Mechanism: CD38 antibody, BCMA CAR-T, two bispecifics in one commercial organisation; USD 17.4bn in 2025 [CLM-002072]. Replication: multi-year clinical programmes plus cell-therapy manufacturing; erosion risk from DARZALEX concentration [CLM-002073]. Confidence: medium.
2. **Pharma + MedTech dual platform.** Mechanism claimed by J&J: cardiovascular leadership across Abiomed, Biosense Webster and Shockwave [CLM-002074]. No disclosed cross-segment revenue synergy; the margin gap and the Orthopaedics separation point the other way [CLM-002004] [CLM-002037]. Confidence: low (HYPOTHESIS).
3. **Immunology scale and successor sequencing.** Mechanism: TREMFYA and ICOTYDE as IL-23 successors with Crohn's/UC trials [CLM-002055] [CLM-002053]. Replication: requires an IL-23 asset launched 3–5 years pre-LOE. Confidence: medium; Immunology still fell 11.8% [CLM-002026].
4. **M&A bridge capacity.** USD 17.5bn in 2025 alone, funded by debt [CLM-002013] [CLM-002014]; replicable by any well-capitalised peer.
5. **JLABS/JJDC ecosystem.** Contracting rather than expanding: JLABS planned at six sites with capacity for 225 companies in 2016 [CLM-009051]; Toronto, Houston and Washington D.C. exited, 11 sites in August 2025 [CLM-014064]; New York closure is a snippet [CLM-014065]. J&J claims more than 150 partnerships [CLM-009050]; no JJDC portfolio count or fund size found [CLM-014066]. Not evidenced as a moat *(gap)*.
6. **Surgical robotics option.** FDA records exist for OTTAVA (De Novo), MONARCH and VELYS [CLM-014022] [CLM-014025] [CLM-014026], but no installed base or procedure volume; OTTAVA has one announced installation site [CLM-000284]. Confidence: low *(INTERPRETATION)*.

reports.title: Late-stage assets, approvals and discontinuations
reports.markdown:
# Late-stage assets, approvals and discontinuations

Registry-level inventory (140 registrations; 76 Phase 3-containing) is in [ctgov_inventory.md](ctgov_inventory.md).

## Approvals (established)
- CARVYKTI 2022-02-28 and label updates through 2025-10-10 [CLM-002051]; TECVAYLI 2022-10-25, TALVEY 2023-08-09, LAZCLUZE 2024-08-19, IMAAVY 2025-04-29 per FDA CDER lists [CLM-002050]; IMAAVY approval 2025-04-30 per company [CLM-002042].
- 2025 U.S. approvals listed in the 10-K: AKEEGA, CAPLYTA adjunctive MDD, DARZALEX smoldering MM, INLEXZO, IMAAVY, RYBREVANT subcutaneous, SPRAVATO monotherapy, TREMFYA indications; filings for icotrokinra and TECVAYLI MajesTEC-3 [CLM-002036].
- ICOTYDE (icotrokinra) approved ~2026-03-17 for plaque psoriasis [CLM-002065].
- TREMFYA Crohn's approval March 2025 [CLM-002053].

## Late-stage programmes (registry facts)
- Icotrokinra: Phase 3 in PsA, UC and Phase 2/3 Crohn's [CLM-002055].
- Pasritamig (mCRPC), bleximenib (AML), seltorexant, teclistamab/talquetamab combinations [CLM-002057].
- CARTITUDE-5 estimated primary completion 2029-02-14 [CLM-002058].

## Discontinued / failed
- Aticaprant Phase 3 VENTURA stopped 2025-03-06 for insufficient efficacy [CLM-002039] [CLM-002056].
- Bermekimab impaired ~USD 0.8bn in FY2022 [CLM-002020]; RSV adult vaccine, hepatitis, HIV exited in FY2023 [CLM-002018]; IPR&D impairments USD 313m / 211m / 81m (FY2023/24/25) [CLM-002031].
- Seltorexant MDD3002 terminated after an interim analysis [CLM-002057].

## Regulator record and setbacks (horizontal)
- FDA novel approvals: Tecvayli, Talvey, Lazcluze, Imaavy, Icotyde [CLM-012008] [CLM-012009] [CLM-012010] [CLM-012011] [CLM-012012]; other applications: Akeega 2023-08-11, Inlexzo 2025-09-09, Rybrevant Faspro 2025-12-17 [CLM-012022] [CLM-012023] [CLM-012024]. See [fda_approvals_2022_2026.md](../../../industry_transformation/pipeline_regulatory/fda_approvals_2022_2026.md), [late_stage_pipeline_snapshot.md](../../../industry_transformation/pipeline_regulatory/late_stage_pipeline_snapshot.md), [setbacks_crls_withdrawals.md](../../../industry_transformation/pipeline_regulatory/setbacks_crls_withdrawals.md).
- Setbacks: bermekimab terminated January 2022 (IPR&D impairment about USD 0.6bn in the pipeline horizontal [CLM-012109] versus about USD 0.8bn in claim CLM-002020; the two figures are unreconciled *(contested)*) [CLM-012109] [CLM-002020]; RSV adult vaccine discontinued FY2023 [CLM-012110]; aticaprant stopped 2025-03-06 [CLM-012135] [CLM-014019].
- Pipeline depth is broadest in modality (bispecifics, CAR-T, oral peptide, drug-device); Stelara replacement adequacy cannot be sized without forecasts *(INTERPRETATION)* [CLM-012012].

## Contested / unknown
The management statement of "26 drugs with >USD 1bn potential by 2030" was not found in an inspected source; no comparison with actual approvals is possible (gap). Posdinemab outcome not verified.

*(INTERPRETATION)* Icotrokinra extends J&J's IL-23 position beyond TREMFYA into an oral format [CLM-002055] [CLM-002065].

reports.title: MedTech robotics status (summary level; mechanism depth belongs to A6)
reports.markdown:
# MedTech robotics status (summary level; mechanism depth belongs to A6)

| System | Status (evidence) | Maturity |
|---|---|---|
| OTTAVA (soft-tissue surgery, table-integrated) | IDE approved 2024-11-12 [CLM-002048]; first IDE cases early 2025, J&J said it filed the De Novo on 2026-01-07 (FDA record: request received 2025-12-18), second IDE (inguinal hernia) late 2025 [CLM-002049] [CLM-014022]; FDA De Novo DEN250068 granted 2026-07-21 (grant letter), announced by J&J 2026-07-22 [CLM-014022] [CLM-000283]; on 2026-11-19 J&J announced Memorial Hermann-TMC as the first hospital to install it under an early-access programme (future tense in the release; a completed install is not shown) [CLM-000284] [CLM-014024] | pilot (regulator-authorised; one announced installation site; not scaled) |
| MONARCH (bronchoscopy, urology) | TARGET: 679 patients, 98.7% reach, 83.2% diagnostic yield, single-arm, company-sponsored [CLM-002067]; MONARCH QUEST 3 clearance announced 2026-08-17; openFDA lists K260382 (Auris Health, decided 2026-07-25), whose link to the QUEST 3 name is inferred; K243219 is also an openFDA record (auditor) [CLM-014025] [CLM-000286]; AI nodule segmentation is described in the release [CLM-006027]; Middle East first case remains a snippet (gap) | operational (no installed-base figure) |
| VELYS (knee, spine, hip) | VELYS Spine 510(k) announced 2024-08-02, commercial availability expected H1 2025 [CLM-002066]; openFDA lists five 510(k)s incl. K240211 (2024-06-05) and K260480 (2026-06-25) [CLM-014026]; knee: 10-K cites ATTUNE "pull through related to VELYS" without placement counts [CLM-002029] [CLM-006026] | operational (not scaled; no adoption numbers; the earlier SCALED tag is retracted) |

## Interpretation
- An earlier draft derived "about 24 months from IDE to first commercial install"; that derivation is withdrawn (Gate 1) because the release describes an announced installation site, not a completed install [CLM-000284]. A single installation site is not evidence of share against established incumbents *(INTERPRETATION)*.
- Labelling: FDA records exist for all three platforms (De Novo grant letter, openFDA 510(k)); adoption, efficiency and survey statements remain company-reported (OTTAVA efficiency survey n=20, 12 surgeons and 8 staff) [CLM-006028]. Duato said he hoped for approval "by the end of this year, beginning of next year"; FDA acted earlier [CLM-014070].
- Adjacent: Polyphonic digital ecosystem in early access to select hospitals [CLM-006030]; Abu Dhabi network expected, not operating [CLM-006031]. Impairment history: Auris/OTTAVA partial impairment USD 0.9bn (FY2021) [CLM-009047]. Horizontal: [maturity matrix](../../../industry_transformation/ai_data_robotics/maturity_matrix.md).
- Orthopaedics growth of 1.1% [CLM-002029] means VELYS has not visibly changed segment growth (INTERPRETATION).

## Unknown
Installed base for any platform, procedure volumes, NVIDIA/Polyphonic digital integration outcomes (a 2025 NVIDIA Isaac collaboration press release was seen only as a search snippet); no VELYS, MONARCH or OTTAVA installed-base figure was found after gap-fill [CLM-014026].

reports.title: Successes and failures
reports.markdown:
# Successes and failures

## Top successes
1. DARZALEX USD 14,351m in FY2025 from 6,023m in FY2021 [CLM-002023]; myeloma brands total USD 17.4bn [CLM-002072].
2. Absorbing the Stelara loss: group sales +6.0% in FY2025 with Stelara -41.3% [CLM-000254] [CLM-002075].
3. CARVYKTI USD 1,887m (+95.9%) [CLM-000257] and bispecifics TECVAYLI 670 / TALVEY 463 [CLM-002024].
4. Kenvue separation executed in two steps in 2023 with a USD 21.0bn gain [CLM-002006] [CLM-002007].
5. Shockwave and Abiomed integration: Shockwave 1,146m in FY2025; Abiomed 1,751m (+17.1%) [CLM-002011] [CLM-002027]; ICOTYDE approval [CLM-002065].
6. Intra-Cellular: CAPLYTA MDD approved in Q4 2025, nine months after the USD 14.5bn close; Momenta delivered IMAAVY (2025-04-30) [CLM-009030] [CLM-009031] [CLM-009044].
7. Regulatory firsts in devices: OTTAVA De Novo [CLM-014022]; MONARCH and VELYS 510(k) clearances [CLM-014025] [CLM-014026].

## Failures and weaknesses
1. Talc: three bankruptcy attempts, two dismissed (LTL 2021, 2023), Red River not confirmed 2025-03-31; USD ~7.0bn charge in FY2023 and ~5.0bn in 2024 [CLM-002015] [CLM-002016] [CLM-002017] [CLM-002043]; 2026 proposed USD 5.5bn+ resolution [CLM-002062] [CLM-002063].
2. Aticaprant Phase 3 stopped for insufficient efficacy [CLM-002039] [CLM-002056].
3. RSV adult vaccine and infectious-disease exits [CLM-002018]; COVID-19 vaccine exit costs USD 1.5bn [CLM-002019].
4. Bermekimab write-off ~USD 0.8bn [CLM-002020].
5. Varipulse U.S. pause: 4 of 132 patients with stroke/TIA vs ≤1% expected [CLM-002044] [CLM-002045]; PFA competition [CLM-002028].
6. Impella Class I recalls: 66,390 pumps, 129 serious injuries incl. 49 deaths (IFU correction); controller purge-retainer recall 2025 [CLM-002046] [CLM-002047].
7. Stelara cliff and Orthopaedics at 1.1% growth [CLM-002022] [CLM-002029]; IRA price negotiation [CLM-002054].
8. Varipulse: FDA correction notice records 4 of 132 (about 3%) stroke/TIA in the U.S. External Evaluation versus about 1% or less expected; Instructions for Use updated 2025-02-14 for all lots (correction, not removal) [CLM-014018].
9. Talc: Red River dismissed 2025-03-31, about USD 7bn of reserve reversed, USD 3.4bn reserve at Q4 2025; 2026-07-27 conditional USD 5.5bn resolution of about 76,000 claims needs at least 95% participation, outcome unknown [CLM-014027] [CLM-014028] [CLM-014029].
10. Acquisition write-downs: OTTAVA/Auris USD 0.9bn (FY2021), M710 about USD 0.2bn in each of 2023 and 2024, Laminar pivotal study suspended 2025, NM26 early-termination interim [CLM-009047] [CLM-009045] [CLM-009039] [CLM-009037]. Wave-2 corrections: aticaprant discontinuation date and cause confirmed (company release only) [CLM-014019].
11. OTTAVA: De Novo authorised but one announced installation site only; no adoption evidence [CLM-014022] [CLM-000284].

## Contested
Impella sales kept growing despite recalls [CLM-002046]; whether Varipulse harm was device or use-related is disputed (company attribution to use outside instructions) [CLM-002045].
