## 1. Financial position

**Established.**
- Revenue (IFRS, JPY bn): FY2021 3,569.0; FY2022 4,027.5; FY2023 4,263.8; FY2024 4,581.6; FY2025 4,505.7 [CLM-005000]. FY2025 fell 1.7% at actual exchange rates and 2.7% at constant rates; U.S. revenue fell 9.0% AER to JPY 2,164.8bn [CLM-005001].
- FY2025 geographic mix: U.S. about 48% of revenue, Japan about 10%, China about 4% (arithmetic on reported figures) [CLM-005002].
- Core Operating Profit (company non-IFRS): about 955 (FY2021, implied), 1,188.4, 1,054.9, 1,162.6, 1,172.5 [CLM-005003]. Reported operating profit fell to JPY 6.2bn in FY2025 after a JPY 403.5bn legal provision [CLM-005014] (see also CLM-000272, CLM-000273).
- R&D expense: 526.1, 633.3, 729.9, 730.2, 675.9 [CLM-005004].
- Leverage (adjusted net debt / adjusted EBITDA): 2.6x (Mar 2023), 3.1x (Mar 2024), 2.8x (Mar 2025), 2.6x (Mar 2026) [CLM-005005]. A10 could not locate these; they are now confirmed against the 20-F text: the 20-F for the year to March 2024 (file `TAK_20-F_2024-03-31_0001395064-24-000086.txt`, line 2803) shows 2.6x and 3.1x, and the 20-F for the year to March 2026 (file `TAK_20-F_2026-03-31_0001395064-26-000177.txt`, line 2353) shows 2.8x and 2.6x with adjusted EBITDA JPY 1,441.0bn and 1,457.2bn.
- Progressive dividend policy: JPY 200 per share in FY2025, JPY 204 intended for FY2026; dividends paid JPY 313.2bn in FY2025 [CLM-005006]. Capex JPY 496.7bn, 319.4bn, 426.9bn for FY2023-FY2025 [CLM-005007].
- Concentration: ENTYVIO JPY 958.0bn (21%), immunoglobulins JPY 790.6bn (18%), TAKHZYRO JPY 223.9bn (5%) [CLM-005009]; Growth & Launch Products were 43%, 48%, 51% of revenue in FY2023-FY2025 [CLM-005008].
- H1 FY2026 (Apr-Sep 2026, partial year): revenue JPY 2,407.0bn (+8.4% AER, -1.0% CER); FY2026 Core Operating Profit guidance JPY 1,190bn [CLM-005011]; ENTYVIO +2.7% CER [CLM-005012].

**Contested.** Core measures exclude items such as the Amitiza provision, so reported and core figures diverge in FY2025. Takeda disputes the verdict and intends to appeal [CLM-005013].

**Unknown.** Buyback amounts, FX hedging policy and the FY2021 leverage ratio were not extracted *(gap)*.

## 2. LOE exposure
See [loe_risk/loe_exposure.md](loe_risk/loe_exposure.md). VYVANSE fell from JPY 423.2bn to 203.2bn in two years [CLM-005015]; TRINTELLIX faces generics after December 2026 [CLM-005016]; ENTYVIO loses regulatory exclusivity in the latter half of the decade, with 2032 patents [CLM-005017]. Takeda's replacement plan is the late-stage pipeline, with a stated USD 10-20bn combined peak potential [CLM-005041]. That range is a **company statement (T2)**: the 2024 R&D Day footnote says it is not adjusted for probability of technical and regulatory success and "should not be considered a forecast or target" [CLM-014049]. Entyvio: some patents expire in 2032 and UK/Netherlands revocation actions were filed February-April 2026 [CLM-014050]; two biosimilar BLAs (Alvotech AVT16, Fresenius/Polpharma) were accepted for FDA review, exclusivity status unconfirmed [CLM-014051].

## 3. Pipeline
See [pipeline/late_stage_assets.md](pipeline/late_stage_assets.md). Oveporexton was approved by the FDA on 5 August 2026 [CLM-005029]; rusfertide on 28 August 2026 [CLM-005032]; the zasocitinib NDA was accepted under Priority Review on 14 September 2026 [CLM-005035]. Failures in the window: soticlestat [CLM-005024], cell therapy exit [CLM-005025], ALOFISEL/EXKIVITY write-downs [CLM-005022], TAK-994 [CLM-005023]. The cell-therapy impairment was announced on 2025-10-01 as an expected JPY 58.0bn [CLM-005025]; the FY2025 20-F recognises JPY 58.2bn on the gamma delta T-cell platform, plus JPY 31.9bn on ALUNBRIG [CLM-009084] [CLM-012123] *(not a contradiction: estimate versus recognised amount; conflicts_proposed_A10 #14)*. Full list with successes: [successes_failures/successes_failures.md](successes_failures/successes_failures.md). FDA novel approvals: Fruzaqla 2023-11-08, Orzeyful 2026-08-05, Mimrylo 2026-08-28 [CLM-012018] [CLM-012019] [CLM-012020]; platform view [CLM-012149] [CLM-012150] [CLM-012151] *(INTERPRETATION)*. Horizontals: [pipeline quality](../../industry_transformation/pipeline_regulatory/pipeline_quality_assessment.md), [FDA approvals](../../industry_transformation/pipeline_regulatory/fda_approvals_2022_2026.md), [setbacks](../../industry_transformation/pipeline_regulatory/setbacks_crls_withdrawals.md), [scientific platforms](../../industry_transformation/pipeline_regulatory/scientific_platforms.md).

## 4. R&D operating model
Takeda describes a modality-diversified, partnership-driven model [CLM-005046], with sites in Massachusetts, Shonan and Vienna [CLM-005047]. Four of the six late-stage programs were licensed or acquired externally *(INTERPRETATION)* [CLM-005050]; oveporexton is an in-house discovery [CLM-005048]. The Nimbus acquisition (USD 4.0bn upfront) is the largest deal [CLM-005036]. Takeda Ventures, Inc. is a 100%-owned consolidated subsidiary; no fund size, portfolio count or Center for External Innovation description was found in primary sources [CLM-014052] [CLM-005052]; the Center's head (Alison Handley) sits on BaseLaunch's investment board [CLM-009091] and an aggregator says Takeda Ventures sits under it (inconclusive) [CLM-009092] *(gap)*. Andrew Plump has led R&D since 2015 [CLM-005051].

## 5. Data, digital and AI
See [data_ai/digital_ai_baseline.md](data_ai/digital_ai_baseline.md). Public evidence is aspiration and platform statements, not outcomes [CLM-005053, CLM-005058, CLM-005057]. Horizontals: [landscape](../../industry_transformation/ai_data_robotics/ai_data_robotics_landscape.md), [maturity matrix](../../industry_transformation/ai_data_robotics/maturity_matrix.md), [autonomous-lab reality check](../../industry_transformation/ai_data_robotics/autonomous_lab_reality_check.md).
- Annual Integrated Report 2026 (FY2025; opened via pypdf, 55 pages; company document, single interested source): 63.4% of the workforce actively used generative AI at 31 March 2026 versus 46.6% a year earlier, and 30.9% took at least one data, digital and technology course [CLM-014043]; named AI partners Nabla Bio, TetraScience and APHERIS, with AI/ML in study design and operations [CLM-014045]; the Takami programme standardises end-to-end processes with qualitative benefits and no spend disclosed [CLM-014044].
- Manufacturing and supply AI: more than 170 AI-enabled predictive-maintenance agents at Lessines (maturity operational, self-reported) [CLM-014041]; One Day Batch Release completed six-site pilots in 2025, targeting 60% shorter release lead time by 2028 and global rollout by 2029 (pilot, target) [CLM-014042]; on-time in-full 99.6% in FY2025, with personalised plasma-donation nomograms and Smart Donor Care rolled out at BioLife [CLM-014046].
- Partner deals (prototype): Nabla Bio second collaboration, October 2025, with over USD 1bn of success-based payments and first-in-human data expected in one to two years (company statements) [CLM-006039]; Iambic, February 2026, payments that could exceed USD 1.7bn [CLM-006041]; AISB OpenFold3 member since October 2025 [CLM-006042].
- Leadership statements: Weber (Semafor, January 2026) aims to double research productivity with AI and cites about 30% shorter narcolepsy development time (single source, partially supported) [CLM-014073]; Kim's May 2026 letter sets "two horizons" and an AI-heavy reorganisation [CLM-014074].
- No first-party deployment with outcome metrics was found for discovery AI [CLM-006045]; lab and manufacturing robotics remain an evidence gap [CLM-005067].

## 6. Manufacturing and plasma network
Plasma centers grew from 233 to 275 over FY2022-FY2024 [CLM-005063]; a USD 230m Los Angeles expansion adds up to 2 million litres/year of fractionation capacity [CLM-005065]; a 2020 FDA warning letter at Hikari led to a supply shortage and a USD 505m award to AbbVie [CLM-005020]. Automation and continuous manufacturing are an evidence gap [CLM-005067], apart from the Lessines predictive-maintenance agents and One Day Batch Release pilots in §5 [CLM-014041] [CLM-014042]. BioLife plasma centres: 233 (FY2022), 260 (FY2023), 275 (FY2024) [CLM-005063].

## 7. Commercial reach
U.S., International and Japan business units [CLM-005069]. Japan JPY 433.1bn and China JPY 195.1bn in FY2025 [CLM-005071]. QDENGA revenue JPY 40.8bn [CLM-005045]. The "~80 markets" figure could not be verified [CLM-005070]; patient-assistance detail is limited to Help at Hand, which reports more than 100,000 patients cumulatively (company-stated) [CLM-007037] [CLM-005072]. Horizontals: [commercial models](../../industry_transformation/commercial_patient/commercial_models_comparison.md), [pricing and payer dynamics](../../industry_transformation/commercial_patient/pricing_access_and_payer_dynamics.md), [launch execution](../../industry_transformation/commercial_patient/launch_execution_evidence.md), [transfer to Takeda](../../industry_transformation/commercial_patient/transfer_to_takeda.md).
- Entyvio is 21% of revenue (JPY 958.0bn) and Growth & Launch Products 51% [CLM-007027]; the subcutaneous Entyvio pen (UC September 2023, Crohn's April 2024) drives uptake, with FDA application records on 2023-09-27 (SC) and 2024-04-18 (pen) [CLM-007033] [CLM-007041] [CLM-012029] [CLM-012030]. Rebate details are not public; formulary exclusion directly reduces usage [CLM-007025].
- Entyvio selected for Medicare negotiation effective January 2028; Part D redesign expected to reduce profit; May 2025 MFN executive order [CLM-007026]. The HYHUB needle-free Hyqvia transfer device received 510(k) clearance in July 2025 (clearance, not adoption) [CLM-007042]. Call summary credits Entyvio pen adoption and formulary wins and Qdenga +22.1% (aggregator, partially supported) [CLM-007043].
- *(INTERPRETATION)* Transfer logic: subcutaneous/home conversion is the best-evidenced transferable mechanism; a cash-pay DTC channel fits poorly [CLM-007053] [CLM-007052] [CLM-007054] [CLM-007055] [CLM-007056] [CLM-007057] [CLM-007058].

## 8. Partnerships
In-licensing roster [CLM-005050]; Innovent oncology license [CLM-005043]; AI-oriented research alliances [CLM-005049]; Teva generics JV dissolution (JPY 18.9bn impairment, JPY 56.5bn proceeds) [CLM-005021] [CLM-009085]. Horizontals: [deal inventory](../../industry_transformation/partnerships_ecosystem/deal_inventory.md), [scorecard](../../industry_transformation/partnerships_ecosystem/deal_outcomes_scorecard.md), [external-innovation machinery](../../industry_transformation/partnerships_ecosystem/external_innovation_machinery.md).
- Upfronts (20-F): HUTCHMED USD 400m (April 2023; up to USD 730m more) and Protagonist USD 300m (April 2024) [CLM-014060]; Keros USD 200m (February 2025) and Innovent USD 1.2bn (December 2025) [CLM-014061]; Nimbus USD 4.0bn (paid USD 3.0bn February 2023, 0.9bn April 2023, 0.1bn August 2023) with two USD 1.0bn sales milestones [CLM-014062] [CLM-009076]; AC Immune USD 100m [CLM-014062]. Innovent: US$1.2bn including equity, up to US$11.4bn in total [CLM-009078] [CLM-009079].
- Takeda states there were no significant acquisitions in the three years to March 2026 [CLM-009087]. Terminations: Denali collaboration ended April 2026; Neurocrine terminated TAK-041/TAK-831 in March 2025 [CLM-009089] [CLM-009090]. Write-offs of earlier purchases: Maverick JPY 27.8bn, soticlestat JPY 21.5bn, gamma delta T-cell JPY 58.2bn [CLM-009083] [CLM-009084]. Takeda holds an AbbVie licence for mirvetuximab in Japan [CLM-009093]. BaseLaunch partner alongside AbbVie and J&J [CLM-009091].

## 9. Leadership and organisation
Julie Kim became President and CEO on 24 June 2026; Christophe Weber retired [CLM-005073]. Kim's background is PDT and U.S. commercial [CLM-005074]. Three external directors joined, including Paul Stoffels [CLM-005075]. Milano Furuta is CFO and Gabriele Ricci CDTO [CLM-005076, CLM-005056]. Restructuring: May 2024 program [CLM-005077]; March 2026 transformation targeting over JPY 200bn gross annual savings by FY2028 [CLM-005059]. **Restructuring-cost series (Gate 1 rewrite of CLM-005078):** about JPY 150bn (Takeda release, 25 March 2026) → JPY 170.0bn (original FY2026 forecast, May 2026) → JPY 160.0bn (revised forecast, H1 FY2026 report, October 2026); the 170bn is Takeda's own forecast, not only a press figure [CLM-005078] [CLM-005011] (conflicts_proposed_A10 #4). The H1 report text is preserved in [evidence_notes/h1_fy2026_extracts.md](evidence_notes/h1_fy2026_extracts.md). "About 4,500 roles" is a trade-press figure [CLM-005078]; the "137 Massachusetts roles" element could not be verified and is not used [CLM-005025]. Dual listing in Tokyo and on the NYSE [CLM-005079]. Weber's January 2026 and Kim's May 2026 statements are in §5 [CLM-014073] [CLM-014074].

## 10. Capability baseline
Detail in [capability_baseline/capability_baseline.md](capability_baseline/capability_baseline.md).

| Capability area | Class | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| GI / immunology franchise | EXISTING_STRENGTH | [CLM-005009, CLM-005012] |
| Plasma network and PDT manufacturing | EXISTING_STRENGTH | [CLM-005063, CLM-005064, CLM-005065] |
| Late-stage pipeline delivery | EXISTING_STRENGTH | [CLM-005042, CLM-005029, CLM-005032, CLM-005035] |
| Orexin / rare-disease science | EXISTING_STRENGTH | [CLM-005048, CLM-005027] |
| LOE replacement (revenue depth) | EXISTING_BUT_UNDERDEVELOPED | [CLM-005015, CLM-005017, CLM-005016] |
| External innovation / BD | EXISTING_STRENGTH (deals); organisation EVIDENCE_GAP | [CLM-005050, CLM-005036, CLM-005052] |
| Enterprise data and AI platform | EXISTING_BUT_UNDERDEVELOPED (outcomes unproven) | [CLM-005058, CLM-005055, CLM-005053] |
| AI-enabled discovery | EVIDENCE_GAP | [CLM-005049, CLM-005053] |
| Lab / manufacturing automation, robotics | EVIDENCE_GAP | [CLM-005067] |
| Manufacturing quality | EXISTING_BUT_UNDERDEVELOPED (one documented failure) | [CLM-005020] |
| Patient services / market access | EVIDENCE_GAP | [CLM-005072] |
| New-brand launch execution | POTENTIAL_NEW_CAPABILITY (to be proven) | [CLM-005069, CLM-005074] |

## 11. Internal-validation backlog
See [internal_validation_backlog/backlog.md](internal_validation_backlog/backlog.md).

## 12. Evidence register and gaps
Shard `A5_takeda`: 40 sources (31 retrieved, 5 metadata-only, 3 blocked, 1 paywalled), 83 claims. See [evidence_gaps.md](evidence_gaps.md). The Annual Integrated Report PDF body was not read in v1.0 [CLM-005081] and was opened in wave 2 [CLM-014041]; the takeda.com pipeline asset table was not read [CLM-005082].

## 13. Policy and regulation
Neutral: activity and outcomes only, no causal inference about influence [CLM-008007]. Horizontals: [policy landscape](../../industry_transformation/policy/policy_landscape.md), [IRA exposure](../../industry_transformation/policy/ira_negotiation_exposure.md), [pricing and pledges](../../industry_transformation/policy/pricing_tariffs_manufacturing_pledges.md), [litigation](../../industry_transformation/policy/litigation_with_policy_dimension.md).
- Entyvio, Takeda's highest-selling product in FY2025, was selected by CMS for negotiation effective January 2028; CMS announced on 2026-03-13 that the manufacturers of all 15 third-cycle drugs chose to participate [CLM-008022] [CLM-008015] [CLM-008016]; third-cycle prices were not located [CLM-008017].
- A May 2025 executive order encouraged Most Favored Nation pricing, which could lower Takeda's U.S. prices; Takeda made no U.S. manufacturing pledge in the 20-F text searched [CLM-008035]. Japan's annual NHI price revisions since April 2021 have brought more frequent downward revisions, with a surcharge on long-listed originator drugs from 2026-06-01 [CLM-008036].
- AMITIZA antitrust: jury verdict of 2026-05-18 for USD 884.9m single damages (wholesaler class and individual retailers, subject to trebling for two groups); Takeda booked a JPY 403.5bn provision and plans post-trial motions and an appeal; the final judgment amount and post-trial status are unverified [CLM-005013] [CLM-005014] [CLM-014047] [CLM-014048].
- The 2020 Hikari warning letter and the USD 505m award to AbbVie [CLM-005020].

## 14. v1.1 audit repairs applied (A10 Gate 1: FAIL, repairable)
1. **Timeline** extended to FY2021 (Nov 2021 to Mar 2022) and FY2022 events already in the registry: [timeline.md](timeline.md) [CLM-009086] [CLM-012119].
2. **Business model** created: [business/business_model.md](business/business_model.md).
3. **Successes and failures** created: [successes_failures/successes_failures.md](successes_failures/successes_failures.md).
4. **Restructuring series** rewritten in §9 (150bn → 170.0bn → 160.0bn) [CLM-005078].
5. **Impairment:** recognised JPY 58.2bn (FY2025 20-F) cited beside the October 2025 estimate of 58.0bn (§3) [CLM-009084] [CLM-012123] [CLM-005025].
6. **Evidence preservation:** the H1 FY2026 report (SRC-005015) has no extracted text file in the registry; the passages A10 and this task re-read are copied to [evidence_notes/h1_fy2026_extracts.md](evidence_notes/h1_fy2026_extracts.md). SRC-005018 (BioSpace, about JPY 170bn) was not re-opened; the 170bn figure is anchored to Takeda's own forecast instead. "137 Massachusetts roles" is dropped (Fierce returned 403) [CLM-005025].
7. **Leverage** (CLM-005005): verified against the 20-F text (see §1).
8. **USD 10-20bn** treated as a company statement (T2) in §2, [loe_risk/loe_exposure.md](loe_risk/loe_exposure.md), [pipeline/late_stage_assets.md](pipeline/late_stage_assets.md) and the backlog [CLM-014049].
9. Gate 1 tier note: the H1 FY2026 Kessan Tanshin (SRC-005015) is a company results document; the auditor suggests T2 for earnings releases and T1 for audited statements and regulator-filed forms. Registry retag pending.

reports.title: Takeda business model and financial architecture
reports.markdown:
# Takeda business model and financial architecture

Research cutoff 2026-11-21. Takeda fiscal years run April-March (FY2025 = April 2025 to March 2026). Amounts are IFRS, JPY billion unless stated. Annual XBRL series are in [../financials/xbrl_annual_facts.md](../financials/xbrl_annual_facts.md) and [../financials/edgar_annual_facts.md](../financials/edgar_annual_facts.md) (not modified). H1 FY2026 (April-September 2026) is a partial year.

## Established
- **Scale and trend.** Revenue FY2021-FY2025: 3,569.0; 4,027.5; 4,263.8; 4,581.6; 4,505.7 [CLM-005000]. FY2025 fell 1.7% at actual exchange rates (2.7% at constant rates); U.S. revenue fell 9.0% to JPY 2,164.8bn [CLM-005001]. Mix FY2025: U.S. about 48%, Japan about 10%, China about 4% (arithmetic on reported figures) [CLM-005002] [CLM-005071].
- **Profit.** Core Operating Profit (company non-IFRS): about 955.2 (FY2021, implied), 1,188.4, 1,054.9, 1,162.6, 1,172.5 [CLM-005003]. FY2021 profit attributable to owners was JPY 230.2bn and operating cash flow JPY 1,123.1bn [CLM-000219] [CLM-000227]. Reported FY2025 operating profit was JPY 6.2bn and net loss JPY 152.1bn after a JPY 403.5bn legal provision for the AMITIZA verdict; Core Operating Profit was unaffected [CLM-005014].
- **Reinvestment.** R&D expense 526.1; 633.3; 729.9; 730.2; 675.9 (FY2021-25) [CLM-005004]. Capex 496.7; 319.4; 426.9 (FY2023-25) [CLM-005007].
- **Product concentration.** ENTYVIO JPY 958.0bn (21%), immunoglobulins 790.6bn (18%), TAKHZYRO 223.9bn (5%) [CLM-005009]. Growth & Launch Products were 43%, 48% and 51% of revenue in FY2023-FY2025 [CLM-005008] [CLM-007027].
- **Plasma-derived therapies.** Collection network: 233 centres (FY2022), 260 (FY2023), 275 (FY2024) [CLM-005063]; USD 230m Los Angeles expansion [CLM-005065]; 99.6% on-time in-full order release in FY2025 (company report) [CLM-014046].
- **Capital allocation.** Dividend JPY 200 a share in FY2025 (JPY 204 intended for FY2026), dividends paid JPY 313.2bn [CLM-005006]. Adjusted net debt to adjusted EBITDA: 2.6x (March 2023), 3.1x, 2.8x, 2.6x (March 2026) [CLM-005005] (confirmed in the 20-F text; see [../master_report.md](../master_report.md) §1). Takeda reports no significant acquisitions of businesses or assets in the three years to March 2026 [CLM-009087]; business development is licensing and upfronts [CLM-014060] [CLM-014061] [CLM-014062].
- **Write-downs.** ALOFISEL JPY 74.0bn and EXKIVITY JPY 28.5bn (FY2023) [CLM-012122]; Maverick JPY 27.8bn and soticlestat JPY 21.5bn (FY2024) [CLM-009083]; gamma delta T-cell platform JPY 58.2bn and ALUNBRIG JPY 31.9bn (FY2025) [CLM-009084] [CLM-012123]; Teva JV dissolution JPY 18.9bn [CLM-009085].
- **Cost programme.** May 2024 efficiency programme [CLM-005077]; March 2026 transformation targeting over JPY 200bn annualised gross savings by FY2028 [CLM-005059]. Restructuring cost series: about JPY 150bn (25 March 2026) → 170.0bn (original FY2026 forecast, May 2026) → 160.0bn (revised, October 2026) [CLM-005078] [CLM-005011].
- **H1 FY2026 (partial year).** Revenue JPY 2,407.0bn (+8.4% actual rates, -1.0% constant rates); Core Operating Profit guidance JPY 1,190bn [CLM-005011]; ENTYVIO +2.7% at constant rates [CLM-005012].

## Contested
- Core measures exclude items such as the AMITIZA provision, so reported and core profit diverge in FY2025; Takeda disputes the verdict [CLM-005013]. The final judgment amount and post-trial status are unverified [CLM-014048] [CLM-014047].
- The USD 10-20bn combined peak range for six late-stage programmes is a company statement, not adjusted for probability of success and "not a forecast or target" [CLM-005041] [CLM-014049] *(INTERPRETATION)* so it cannot be used to size replacement of the revenue at risk in [../loe_risk/loe_exposure.md](../loe_risk/loe_exposure.md).

## Unknown *(gap)*
Buyback amounts, FX hedging policy, segment-level margins (Takeda reports a single segment), net price and rebate levels (not public [CLM-007025]), cost per litre of plasma, and realised versus targeted savings (backlog IVB-003 in [../internal_validation_backlog/backlog.md](../internal_validation_backlog/backlog.md)).

## v1.1 update
Row 5 (external innovation): Takeda Ventures, Inc. is a 100%-owned subsidiary with no public fund size [CLM-014052]. Row 6: cell-therapy write-off recognised at JPY 58.2bn [CLM-009084]. Rows 9-13 (data, AI, automation): wave-2 evidence adds manufacturing AI agents and process pilots at operational or pilot maturity, still without outcome data [CLM-014041] [CLM-014042] [CLM-014043]; robotics remains EVIDENCE_GAP [CLM-005067]. Row 16: restructuring cost series 150bn → 170.0bn → 160.0bn [CLM-005078]. Row 14 transfer analysis: [transfer_to_takeda.md](../../../industry_transformation/commercial_patient/transfer_to_takeda.md).

## Reading notes
*(INTERPRETATION)* Evidenced strengths are franchise scale, plasma operations and delivery of three late-stage approvals or filings on a pre-announced timetable. The least-evidenced areas (AI outcomes, automation) are those later strategy modules may target, so recommendations there must be labelled ASSUMPTION until the backlog is validated.

# Data, digital and AI baseline

Research cutoff 2026-11-21. Takeda fiscal years run April-March (FY2025 = April 2025 to March 2026). Claim IDs resolve in `New_mediciine/evidence_library/shards/A5_takeda/claims.jsonl`; `CLM-000xxx` IDs resolve in the canonical `claims_registry.jsonl`. Only public sources were used.

Maturity scale: concept, prototype, pilot, operational, scaled, demonstrated_outcome, unknown.

| Item | What is evidenced | Maturity | Source quality | Claim |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Strategy | Aspiration to embed AI in every stage of drug discovery and enterprise productivity | concept | 20-F | [CLM-005053] |
| Investment | DD&T spend inside SG&A; efficiency program invests in digital, data, technology (amount not quantified) | operational spend; outcome unknown | 20-F | [CLM-005055] |
| Leadership | Gabriele Ricci CDTO since Feb 2022 | n/a | 20-F | [CLM-005056] |
| Operating model | 80% of digital workforce was external; insourcing via "digital factories" | operational (self-reported) | executive interview via BCG | [CLM-005057] |
| AI platform | Databricks-based agent platform for 10,000+ employees; regulatory-submission agent listed as production use case; provisioning cut from 60-70 tickets to one click (~20 min) | operational (vendor-hosted self-report) | vendor page | [CLM-005058] |
| Research alliances | Iambic, Nabla Bio, BridGene, Charles River, MIT J-Clinic | unknown (no outcomes) | 20-F listing | [CLM-005049] |
| Plasma personalisation | Adaptive nomograms across 270+ centers | operational; benefit unquantified | 20-F | [CLM-005060] |
| Technology-enabled savings | Over JPY 200bn gross savings by FY2028 target, partly via technology-enabled process simplification | concept (plan) | company release | [CLM-005059] |
| Risk | Company warns AI models may be flawed or create liability; NIST-based cybersecurity | n/a | 20-F | [CLM-005054, CLM-005061] |

## Wave-2 additions (Annual Integrated Report 2026, company document; single interested source)
| Item | What is evidenced | Maturity | Claim |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lessines predictive maintenance | More than 170 AI-enabled agents deployed; expansion planned | operational (self-reported) | [CLM-014041] |
| One Day Batch Release | Pilots at six sites in 2025; 60% shorter release lead time targeted by 2028, global rollout by 2029 | pilot (target) | [CLM-014042] |
| Workforce use | 63.4% of workforce actively used generative AI at 31 March 2026 (46.6% a year earlier); 30.9% took a DD&T course | operational (usage metric, not outcome) | [CLM-014043] |
| Takami programme | End-to-end process standardisation; qualitative benefits; no spend disclosed | pilot to operational (unquantified) | [CLM-014044] |
| R&D AI partners | Nabla Bio, TetraScience, APHERIS | prototype | [CLM-014045] |
| Supply and plasma | On-time in-full 99.6% in FY2025; BioLife nomogram and Smart Donor Care rolled out | operational | [CLM-014046] |
| Leadership statements | Weber: double research productivity with AI; about 30% shorter narcolepsy development time (single source); Kim: "two horizons" | n/a (statements) | [CLM-014073] [CLM-014074] |

Horizontals: [landscape](../../../industry_transformation/ai_data_robotics/ai_data_robotics_landscape.md), [maturity matrix](../../../industry_transformation/ai_data_robotics/maturity_matrix.md). Partner deals: Nabla Bio (2025-10-14) and Iambic (2026-02-09) at prototype [CLM-006039] [CLM-006041]; AISB OpenFold3 member [CLM-006042]; no first-party discovery deployment with metrics found [CLM-006045].

## Established
Takeda has a named C-level owner, a funded DD&T function, an insourcing decision, a governed agent platform and AI-focused research alliances.

## Contested
Depth of production use is described only by Takeda and a vendor; the BCG interview and Databricks page are interested sources. Fortune and Informatica leads were not verified [CLM-005062].

## Unknown *(gap)*
Number of AI systems in production, value or time saved, share of R&D decisions informed by models, lab automation, and whether the AIR PDF holds quantified results [CLM-005081, CLM-005080].

## Classification
Enterprise data and AI platform: EXISTING_BUT_UNDERDEVELOPED (outcomes unproven). AI-enabled discovery and robotics: EVIDENCE_GAP.

reports.title: LOE exposure and revenue-replacement logic
reports.markdown:
# LOE exposure and revenue-replacement logic

Research cutoff 2026-11-21. Takeda fiscal years run April-March (FY2025 = April 2025 to March 2026). Claim IDs resolve in `New_mediciine/evidence_library/shards/A5_takeda/claims.jsonl`; `CLM-000xxx` IDs resolve in the canonical `claims_registry.jsonl`. Only public sources were used.

## Established
- **VYVANSE/ELVANSE:** JPY 423.2bn (FY2023) to 350.6bn to 203.2bn (FY2025). U.S. composition-of-matter patent and pediatric exclusivity expired August 2023; Takeda expects the decline to continue in FY2026 [CLM-005015].
- **AZILVA** fell to JPY 7.1bn after a February 2023 Japanese generic approval. **TRINTELLIX** (JPY 121.8bn) faces generics after certain patent rights expire in December 2026 [CLM-005016].
- **ENTYVIO** (JPY 958.0bn, 21% of revenue): regulatory exclusivity ends in the latter half of the decade; some patents expire in 2032; biosimilar timing is uncertain [CLM-005017]. Disclosed defences: subcutaneous Pen and pediatric labels [CLM-005018]. H1 FY2026 ENTYVIO growth is +2.7% at constant rates [CLM-005012].
- **TAKHZYRO** U.S. patent is listed to January 2036; no U.S. generic of GATTEX had launched by March 2026 [CLM-005019].
- **Leuprorelin:** the Hikari supply disruption produced a USD 505m award to AbbVie [CLM-005020].
- Velcade history was not examined *(gap)*.

## Replacement plan as stated by Takeda
Growth & Launch Products were 51% of FY2025 revenue [CLM-005008]. Takeda says six late-stage programs could reach USD 10-20bn combined peak revenue [CLM-005041] (a company statement, T2: not adjusted for probability of success and "not a forecast or target" [CLM-014049]), and the CEO cited three launches within 12 months of June 2026 [CLM-005074]. The estimate is a company statement; its basis footnote was not captured.

## Interpretation
*(INTERPRETATION)* Vyvanse removed about JPY 220bn of annual revenue in two years. Trintellix and Entyvio together are about 24% of FY2025 revenue. The launch wave starts from a base still shrinking at constant currency (H1 FY2026 revenue -1.0% CER) [CLM-005011].

## Contested / unknown
Entyvio erosion after 2030-32 depends on biosimilar timing and litigation, which are unknown: some patents expire in 2032 with UK and Netherlands revocation actions filed February-April 2026, and two biosimilar BLAs (Alvotech AVT16, Fresenius/Polpharma PB016) are accepted for FDA review, exclusivity status unconfirmed [CLM-014050] [CLM-014051]. Entyvio was selected for Medicare negotiation from January 2028 [CLM-007026] [CLM-008022]. Internal erosion curves are on the backlog (IVB-004).

FDA record: Orzeyful 2026-08-05, Mimrylo 2026-08-28 [CLM-012019] [CLM-012020]; registry snapshot of late-stage trials in [late_stage_pipeline_snapshot.md](../../../industry_transformation/pipeline_regulatory/late_stage_pipeline_snapshot.md) [CLM-012077] [CLM-012078] [CLM-012079] [CLM-012080] [CLM-012081] [CLM-012082] [CLM-012083].

## Discontinuations and failures (2021-2026)
- TAK-994 stopped after clinical hold [CLM-005023].
- EXKIVITY withdrawn; ALOFISEL Phase 3 miss and impairment [CLM-005022].
- Soticlestat Phase 3 failure, discontinued January 2025 [CLM-005024].
- Cell therapy exit: JPY 58.0bn expected impairment (2025-10-01), JPY 58.2bn recognised in the FY2025 20-F [CLM-005025] [CLM-009084] [CLM-012123].
- Full list with dates and amounts: [../successes_failures/successes_failures.md](../successes_failures/successes_failures.md).
- TAK-004 discontinued (single secondary source) [CLM-005026].

## Contested / unknown
Efficacy data are company-reported; no peer-reviewed publications were read. Competitive position (deucravacitinib, IL-23 agents) and launch curves are not evidenced *(gap)*. The NCT06505031-to-RadiantLight mapping is inferred [CLM-005028]. The pipeline page asset table was not captured [CLM-005082].

reports.title: Takeda: successes and failures, November 2021 to November 2026
reports.markdown:
# Takeda: successes and failures, November 2021 to November 2026

Research cutoff 2026-11-21. FY2025 = April 2025 to March 2026. Outcomes are listed as disclosed; Takeda's efficacy statements are company-reported unless a regulator or peer-reviewed source is cited. Sentences marked *(INTERPRETATION)* are the analyst's reading.

## Successes
1. **Three novel FDA approvals in the window**: Fruzaqla 2023-11-08 [CLM-012018]; Orzeyful (oveporexton, narcolepsy type 1) 2026-08-05 [CLM-012019]; Mimrylo (rusfertide, polycythemia vera) 2026-08-28 [CLM-012020] [CLM-005029] [CLM-005032]. The zasocitinib NDA was accepted with Priority Review on 2026-09-14 [CLM-005035]; the R&D Day plan was met for the first three assets by November 2026 [CLM-005042].
2. **ENTYVIO subcutaneous conversion**: SC pen approved for UC (September 2023) and Crohn's disease (April 2024) and described as driving uptake [CLM-007033] [CLM-007041] [CLM-005018]; ENTYVIO JPY 958.0bn, 21% of revenue, +2.7% at constant rates in H1 FY2026 [CLM-007027] [CLM-005012].
3. **Growth & Launch Products reached 51% of revenue** in FY2025 (43% in FY2023) [CLM-005008]; QDENGA JPY 40.8bn [CLM-005045].
4. **Plasma network and operations**: 233 to 275 centres over FY2022-FY2024; 99.6% on-time in-full in FY2025 [CLM-005063] [CLM-014046].
5. **Portfolio discipline**: stopped programmes early (TAK-994, soticlestat, cell therapy) while Core Operating Profit stayed near JPY 1.05-1.19 trillion [CLM-005023] [CLM-005024] [CLM-005025] [CLM-005003] *(INTERPRETATION)*.

## Failures and weaknesses
1. **TAK-994**: Phase 2 stopped in 2021 for a liver-related safety signal and not developed further (decision June 2022); the Phase 3 pevonedistat MDS trial missed its event-free-survival endpoint [CLM-012119] [CLM-005023].
2. **EXKIVITY withdrawn globally** (October 2023) after EXCLAIM-2 missed its primary endpoint; JPY 28.5bn impairment [CLM-012121] [CLM-012122] [CLM-005022].
3. **ALOFISEL**: JPY 74.0bn impairment after the Phase 3 ADMIRE-CD II topline [CLM-012122].
4. **Soticlestat**: Phase 3 SKYLINE and SKYWAY missed primary endpoints (June 2024); no filing; JPY 21.5bn impairment; discontinued January 2025 [CLM-012120] [CLM-009083] [CLM-005024].
5. **Cell therapy exit**: all cell-therapy efforts discontinued on 2025-10-01; expected impairment JPY 58.0bn, recognised JPY 58.2bn on the gamma delta T-cell platform plus JPY 31.9bn on ALUNBRIG in the FY2025 20-F [CLM-005025] [CLM-009084] [CLM-012123].
6. **AMITIZA verdict**: jury verdict of 2026-05-18 for USD 884.9m single damages (subject to trebling for two groups); JPY 403.5bn provision; reported FY2025 operating profit JPY 6.2bn; Takeda intends post-trial motions and an appeal; final judgment amount and post-trial status unverified [CLM-005013] [CLM-005014] [CLM-014048] [CLM-014047].
7. **VYVANSE loss of exclusivity**: JPY 423.2bn (FY2023) to 203.2bn (FY2025); TRINTELLIX generics expected after December 2026 [CLM-005015] [CLM-005016].
8. **Partnership terminations**: Denali collaboration ended April 2026; Neurocrine terminated TAK-041 and TAK-831 (March 2025); TAK-004 discontinued (single secondary source) [CLM-009089] [CLM-009090] [CLM-005026].
9. **Manufacturing quality**: the 2020 Hikari warning letter led to a leuprorelin shortage and a USD 505m award to AbbVie (Delaware court, December 2023) [CLM-005020].
10. **Teva Takeda Pharma JV dissolved** with a JPY 18.9bn impairment [CLM-009085].

## Contested
- Whether the write-downs reflect disciplined stopping or weak early-stage selection is not established; the sample is of Takeda disclosures only *(INTERPRETATION)* [CLM-005023] [CLM-005025].
- Efficacy for the three 2026 approvals is company-reported or from publications at abstract level [CLM-012149] [CLM-012150] [CLM-012151].

## Unknown
AMITIZA final judgment and appeal outcome; Entyvio biosimilar exclusivity timing (BLAs accepted for review; Purple Book entry not opened) [CLM-014051]; launch curves for Orzeyful and Mimrylo. Horizontal context: [setbacks](../../../industry_transformation/pipeline_regulatory/setbacks_crls_withdrawals.md), [deal scorecard](../../../industry_transformation/partnerships_ecosystem/deal_outcomes_scorecard.md).

reports.title: Commercial capabilities comparison
reports.markdown:
# Commercial capabilities comparison

Cutoff 2026-11-21. Source base: A7 commercial and patient reports, company dossiers and A14 gap-fill. "None found" means not found in the sources opened, not that the capability is absent [CLM-007039]. Takeda amounts are in JPY; no FX conversion is used, and growth rates are quoted as reported.

## 1. What is established

| Mechanism | Lilly | J&J | AbbVie | Takeda |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Direct-to-patient and cash channel | LillyDirect launched 2024-01-04; Zepbound self-pay vials from August 2024 at USD 399 / 549, cut on 2025-12-01 to USD 299 / 399 / 449; Walmart pickup; KwikPen from USD 299. The 10-K says self-pay sales through LillyDirect were "a growing portion" with no dollar figure. Lilly says over 1 million patients accessed treatments through LillyDirect in 2025 and one in three new branded weight-management starts were Zepbound self-pay vials (company statements, footnotes unverified) | Listed on TrumpRx; no own cash platform found | Humira on TrumpRx under the January 2026 agreement; Allē is a provider and consumer loyalty scheme for aesthetics, not a cash pharmacy | None found |
| PBM and formulary exposure | Caremark preferred Wegovy and removed Zepbound from 2025-07-01 (CNBC reported Lilly's stock closed more than 11% lower on the announcement day); Zepbound re-added as an additional preferred option from 2026-10-01 | Stelara removed from Optum Rx's two main formularies from 2025-07-01; Caremark prefers two biosimilars from 2026-07-01; nine biosimilars on the market by July 2025, four of them from PBM-affiliated private labels | Humira removed from Caremark template formularies 2024-04-01 with a co-branded Cordavis Humira; rebate and chargeback provisions of USD 65.1bn in 2025 against net revenue of USD 61.2bn | Rebate details not public; formulary exclusion risk stated; "formulary wins" for Entyvio appear only in a call summary |
| Medicare negotiation and Part D | Jardiance (2026), Trulicity and Verzenio (2028) | Stelara and Xarelto (2026), Imbruvica (2026), Erleada (2028); Part D redesign cut Erleada, Invega, Opsumit and Uptravi sales | Imbruvica (2026), Vraylar and Linzess (2027), Botox (2028) | Entyvio (2028); Part D redesign expected to lower profit; MFN executive order cited as a risk |
| Patient-support programmes (counts are enrolment, not outcomes) | Insulin list-price cut of 70% and USD 35 cap (March 2023); LillyDirect over 1 million patients (company, 2025) | J&J withMe (formerly Janssen CarePath), free, savings programme without an income requirement | Allē more than 6 million members across 19,000 practices (January 2024); October 2024 redesign reversed in early 2025 | Help at Hand more than 100,000 patients cumulative; EntyvioConnect described in snippets only |
| Self-administration and device shifts | Zepbound vial and KwikPen | Tremfya subcutaneous share gains; Spravato restricted to certified settings | none checked | Entyvio SC pen (UC September 2023, Crohn's April 2024); HYHUB needle-free Hyqvia transfer cleared by FDA 510(k) in July 2025 |
| Launch or growth curves, latest full year | Mounjaro USD 22,965m vs 11,540m; Zepbound USD 13,542m vs 4,926m | Carvykti USD 1,887m vs 963m (capacity-driven); Spravato USD 1,696m vs 1,077m; Tremfya USD 5,155m vs 3,670m | Skyrizi USD 17,562m (+49.9%); Rinvoq USD 8,304m (+39.1%) | Entyvio JPY 958.0bn (+4.8%); QDENGA JPY 40.8bn (+14.6%) |

Claims for the rows above, in order. Lilly: [CLM-001042] [CLM-007000] [CLM-007002] [CLM-007003] [CLM-007044] [CLM-007005] [CLM-007004] [CLM-007011] [CLM-007013] [CLM-001036]. J&J: [CLM-007009] [CLM-007016] [CLM-007015] [CLM-007018] [CLM-007035] [CLM-007029] [CLM-007030]. AbbVie: [CLM-003081] [CLM-007036] [CLM-003008] [CLM-003009] [CLM-007019] [CLM-003033] [CLM-007020]. Takeda: [CLM-007039] [CLM-007025] [CLM-007043] [CLM-007026] [CLM-007037] [CLM-007038] [CLM-007041] [CLM-007042] [CLM-000274] [CLM-005045]. Medicare negotiation: [CLM-007023] [CLM-002021] [CLM-003080] [CLM-008022] [CLM-007022] [CLM-008015]. Launch curves: [CLM-007031] [CLM-007029] [CLM-007020] [CLM-007027].

Note on one Lilly cell: the Lilly claim for the 2025 Caremark change records the announcement as 1 July 2025 in CVS's statement and "1 May 2025" for the day Lilly's stock fell, which is an internal inconsistency in the source claim; the effective date used here is 1 July 2025 as stated in the Lilly 10-K [CLM-007011] [CLM-007012].

### 1.1 Price versus volume in the growth years

Lilly's 2025 revenue growth came from volume, partly offset by lower realised prices, mostly on Mounjaro and Zepbound. In Q4 2025 realised prices were 5% lower and volume 46% higher; in Q3 2026 realised prices were 15% lower and volume 53% higher, and the quarter included about USD 900m of one-off benefits (USD 410m of Jardiance milestones plus rebate and discount estimate adjustments) [CLM-007024] [CLM-014004] [CLM-014003]. J&J's Stelara decline cut Innovative Medicine growth by about 10.4 points in FY2025 [CLM-007017]. AbbVie's reported provisions for rebates and chargebacks (USD 65.1bn in 2025, 59.3bn in 2024, 56.8bn in 2023) show the scale of its gross-to-net, which none of the other three companies disclose in the sources read [CLM-007019].

### 1.2 Launch-execution evidence

- Supply or site capacity governed the pace of two launches: Carvykti ("share gains and capacity expansion") and Spravato (certified sites only) [CLM-007029] [CLM-007030].
- Kisunla reached USD 484m in the first nine months of 2026; a USD 21m Q1 2025 figure rests on a search snippet from a blocked source, and reasons for slow uptake are not established [CLM-001032] [CLM-007032].
- Takeda's U.S. business unit is focused on the Entyvio pen and on preparing oveporexton and zasocitinib launches; the Kim-era CEO said three launches fall within about 12 months of June 2026 [CLM-007033] [CLM-005074].

## 2. What is contested

- Whether cash channels take volume from insured patients: copay-accumulator and anti-kickback limits restrict combining discounts with insurance, and Lilly's "one in three new starts" is a new-start measure [CLM-007010] [CLM-007004].
- Whether PBM preference reflected net price (CVS says Wegovy's was lower) or leverage; Zepbound was re-added after about 11 months [CLM-007011] [CLM-007013].
- Whether TrumpRx volumes are material: Congressional Research Service reports listings and manufacturer counts, not sales [CLM-007009].
- Whether the Pear Therapeutics failure was reimbursement or product-market fit, which matters for any digital-therapeutic commercial model [CLM-007045] [CLM-007046].

## 3. What is unknown

- Self-pay share of Zepbound revenue, net price per prescription and gross-to-net for any company except AbbVie's provisions [CLM-007005] [CLM-007019].
- Field-force size, omnichannel metrics and hub-service performance for any company; adherence, persistence or time-to-therapy outcomes for any support programme [CLM-007039].
- Takeda's patient-assistance and market-access programme inventory beyond Help at Hand [CLM-005072].

## 4. Comparison validity

- Patient-programme figures are different units: Allē is loyalty members, LillyDirect is patients who accessed treatments, Help at Hand is cumulative free-medication recipients. They must not be compared [CLM-007036] [CLM-007004] [CLM-007037].
- Launch growth rates are not comparable across products at different life stages (Mounjaro in its third year versus Entyvio in its second decade) *(INTERPRETATION)* [CLM-007031] [CLM-007027].
- The only company-level evidence of commercial *execution quality* across all four is outcome revenue and formulary events; none discloses field-force or hub metrics, so no capability ranking is offered [CLM-007039].

reports.title: Data and AI maturity matrix (levels only, no scores)
reports.markdown:
# Data and AI maturity matrix (levels only, no scores)

Cutoff 2026-11-21. Scale: concept < prototype < pilot < operational < scaled < demonstrated_outcome. A press release proves an announcement, not an outcome. "Outcome evidence" means an independently verifiable result (regulator record, peer-reviewed paper, audited number); company-stated results count as no [CLM-006054]. Sources are the A6 matrix and mechanism cards plus A14 gap-fill claims; no initiative was re-researched.

**Audit retags applied (A10, status-discipline audit).** CLM-006020 (J&J trial-site recommendation, "up to 2.6x" enrolment) is read as self-reported pilot-level evidence, not operational. CLM-006022 (30,000 course completions, 47,000 gen-AI course completions of 130,000+ employees) is a training metric, not a deployment, and is excluded from the maturity cells. CLM-006026 (VELYS "pull through") is read as operational, not scaled. CLM-006047, CLM-006049 and CLM-006051 describe Recursion, Exscientia/BenevolentAI and Zymergen, not the four companies, and are used only as industry calibration. CLM-000284 is read as an announced first installation site, not a completed installation [CLM-000284] [CLM-006020] [CLM-006022] [CLM-006026].

## 1. Matrix

Each cell gives the maturity level, the evidence, and whether independent outcome evidence exists (Y/N). "No evidence found" means no source opened for this project shows it; it is not a finding that the capability is absent.

| Layer | Lilly | J&J | AbbVie | Takeda |
|---|---|---|---|---|

## 2. What is established

- Across the 29 company-level A6 entries, 18 sit at concept, prototype or pilot, and none reaches demonstrated outcome [CLM-006054].
- Lilly has the largest evidenced infrastructure build and the only owned-compute and data-as-product pair; the registry shows no scientific, cycle-time or financial result from either [CLM-006053] [CLM-006007].
- J&J's devices carry the only regulator records among the four companies' AI-adjacent products, and those records concern devices, not discovery [CLM-006054] [CLM-014022] [CLM-014025].
- AbbVie internalises data (ARCH, a knowledge graph, not generative AI) and buys models (BigHat, Valkai) [CLM-006032] [CLM-006035] [CLM-000285].
- Takeda's disclosed strategy is partnership-led, and its 2026 integrated report adds company-reported operating items in manufacturing AI and workforce adoption that the earlier baseline did not have [CLM-006053] [CLM-014041] [CLM-014043].

## 3. Answers to the two comparison questions

**Which technology ecosystem is most defensible?** The registry cannot support a ranking. The candidate moat the A6 analysis identifies is Lilly's proprietary experimental data (company-estimated to cost over USD 1bn to generate) paired with a federated platform, but the same analysis rates the moat claim only partially supported and finds no outcome [CLM-006055] [CLM-000280]. Federated consortia and open models are available substitutes [CLM-006056]. The statement "Lilly has the most defensible ecosystem" is therefore a *(HYPOTHESIS)*, not a finding.

**Which AI investments are operationally meaningful?** Operationally meaningful here means operational or higher status plus a disclosed operating scale. On that test the items are LillyPod (compute online) [CLM-006004], ARCH (internal graph with disclosed size) [CLM-006032], Takeda's Lessines predictive maintenance and plasma nomograms (company-reported scale, benefit unquantified) [CLM-014041] [CLM-005060], and J&J's gen-AI quality-control tool (qualitative) [CLM-006021]. No item has an independently verified effect on cost, cycle time or revenue. Announcement-stage items (NVIDIA lab, Valkai, Isomorphic, OpenAI) are not operationally meaningful on this evidence [CLM-000281] [CLM-000285] [CLM-006012] [CLM-006011].

## 4. Industry calibration

AI-platform pipelines still show ordinary attrition (Recursion ended four of 11 programmes in 2025), the best public AI-origin clinical data are a small Phase IIa (rentosertib, 71 patients, 12 weeks, with liver-related discontinuations), and owned automation ventures ended in divestment or distressed sale (Lilly's studio, Zymergen sold at about one-tenth of its IPO valuation) [CLM-006047] [CLM-006048] [CLM-006052] [CLM-006051]. FDA's January 2025 draft AI guidance is non-binding [CLM-006046].

## 5. What is contested

- Why Lilly divested the Studio (model failed, low utilisation or portfolio reasons) and whether Strateos closed or was acquired (an unverified aggregator snippet says Multiply Labs acquired it in December 2023); the two cited pages date the Studio to 2017 and mention no Strateos or 2020 launch [CLM-006017] [CLM-006015] [CLM-014057].
- Whether Takeda's executive and vendor accounts of its AI use reflect production scale; both are interested sources [CLM-005057] [CLM-005058].

## 6. What is unknown

- Any peer-reviewed or audited result from an autonomous closed-loop lab at the four companies [CLM-006052].
- TuneLab uptake and retraining counts; NVIDIA lab operating status; ARCH outcomes [CLM-014056] [CLM-014053] [CLM-006032].
- J&J and AbbVie compute capacity; AbbVie manufacturing digitalisation *(gap)*.

# Evidence gaps: comparisons not made or only partly made

Cutoff 2026-11-21. No new sources or claims were registered for this synthesis (shard A11_strategy, range 011500-011999, unused).

## 1. Comparisons judged invalid or unsupported
| Comparison | Why not made | Where stated |
|---|---|---|
| Single LOE "resilience score" or management-quality ranking | Cliffs differ in size (Humira 36.6% of revenue vs Stelara 12.8% vs Vyvanse 9.9%), age, acquisitions and price mechanism [CLM-003004] [CLM-002022] [CLM-005015] | loe_resilience_comparison.md |
| Novel approvals per R&D dollar | Window includes 2026 approvals, counts of 3-8, acquired sponsors, different R&D boundaries [CLM-012000] [CLM-012013] [CLM-000270] | rd_investment_and_productivity.md |
| New-molecule revenue share as productivity | Penalises lifecycle growth; Takeda not computable [CLM-012147] [CLM-005029] | pipeline_and_revenue_dependence.md |
| Profit-margin ranking | US GAAP with special items vs IFRS with company core measure [CLM-002016] [CLM-003041] [CLM-005014] | rd_investment_and_productivity.md |
| Leverage ranking | No EBITDA for three US firms; Takeda ratio 2.6x not located by audit [CLM-005005] | competitive_capability_matrix.md |
| Deal-value ranking | Announced, consideration, net-of-cash, expensed and upfront bases mixed [CLM-003053] [CLM-009002] | partner_ecosystem_comparison.md |
| Patient-programme size comparison | Different units (members, patients accessed, cumulative recipients) [CLM-007036] [CLM-007004] [CLM-007037] | commercial_capabilities_comparison.md |
| Robotics "leader" across categories | Product robotics vs lab vs plant automation are different things [CLM-006054] | robotics_deployment_comparison.md |
| Defensible-ecosystem ranking | No outcome evidence for any company [CLM-006054] | data_ai_maturity_matrix.md |

## 2. Missing data that blocked a comparison
- Product-level FY2025 revenue for Omvoh, Ebglyss, Jaypirca, Inluriyo, Imaavy, Icotyde, Epkinly, Fruzaqla; Xarelto and Linzess; Jardiance collaboration revenue.
- Takeda: pre-FY2023 Vyvanse peak, acquired-IPR&D accounting, EBITDA basis, FY2025 PP&E-only capex, Nov 2021 to Mar 2022 timeline events beyond Hasten and TAK-994 [CLM-009086] [CLM-012119].
- J&J: acquired IPR&D FY2023-FY2025, DARZALEX patent dates, installed bases of OTTAVA, MONARCH, VELYS [CLM-006029].
- AbbVie: company-wide U.S. share, origin of Skyrizi and Rinvoq, Skyrizi biosimilar timing, AbbVie Ventures founding date [CLM-009074].
- AbbVie acquired IPR&D 5,016 (XBRL) vs 4,808 (10-K table) unexplained [CLM-000050] [CLM-003045].
- Lilly: self-pay share of Zepbound, tirzepatide volumes, operating status of most announced plants, NVIDIA lab status [CLM-007005] [CLM-014053].
- All: independent outcomes for AI, patient programmes and robotics [CLM-006054] [CLM-007039].

## 3. Source-quality caveats carried into this synthesis
- Policy report cites inconsistent claim IDs for some pledge statements (for example CLM-008030 and CLM-008032 for Lilly 10-K points); this file uses the registry text: Lilly CLM-008029, J&J CLM-008030/008031, AbbVie CLM-008032. No Takeda pledge claim exists; "none found" is a gap [CLM-008035].
- CLM-007011 gives two dates for the Caremark announcement day (1 July and 1 May 2025); 1 July is used [CLM-007012].
- OTTAVA De Novo date: 22 July (company) vs 21 July (FDA record) [CLM-000283] [CLM-014022].
- Takeda baseline classes post-date neither the 2026 integrated report evidence nor Gate 1 repairs (no business_model.md, successes_failures or moats files for Takeda). Automation classed EVIDENCE_GAP although CLM-014041 and CLM-014042 exist [CLM-005067].
- Heavy reliance on company releases (J&J, Takeda H1 FY2026, Lilly) as interested sources; independent corroboration is recorded for no claim [CLM-002060] [CLM-005011].
- A14 tagged CLM-014043 as SCALED and CLM-014073 as DEMONSTRATED_OUTCOME; both read as usage or statement evidence here.

## 4. Suggested next work
1. Extract FY2025 product revenue for the missing launches from the 10-Ks and 20-F.
2. Obtain Takeda IFRS treatment of licence upfronts and a PP&E-only capex series.
3. Open the Purple Book entry for Entyvio and the Abiomed CVR terms.
4. Refresh the Takeda capability baseline with A14 evidence; complete Takeda timeline and business model.
5. Search independent outcomes for TuneLab, ARCH and OTTAVA adoption.

# Lessons for Takeda from Lilly, J&J and AbbVie

Cutoff 2026-11-21. Each lesson states what a competitor did (evidence IDs), a transferability verdict, why, the Takeda capability class from the [public baseline](../companies/takeda_public_baseline/capability_baseline/capability_baseline.md), the Takeda claims that anchor the baseline, and the internal-validation backlog item ([IVB list](../companies/takeda_public_baseline/internal_validation_backlog/backlog.md)) that must be checked with non-public data before acting. Verdicts are *(INTERPRETATION)* built on public evidence only. The same lessons are in `/Users/palrahma/Desktop/MEDICINE/strategy/data/takeda_lessons.json`.

Verdict key: **transfers** = mechanism applies on current evidence; **partially** = applies with a stated condition; **does_not_transfer** = structure or market differs. EVIDENCE_GAP means public evidence is missing, not that the capability is absent [CLM-005080]. Codes: LLY = Eli Lilly, JNJ = Johnson & Johnson, ABBV = AbbVie.

## Summary table

| ID | Area | Competitor | Verdict | Takeda baseline class | IVB |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| LES-17 | Option and early-stage licence volume | ABBV | partially | EXISTING_STRENGTH (class 5: external innovation and BD, deal flow); organisation EVIDENCE_GAP | IVB-007 |
| LES-18 | High variance of first-in-class psychiatry and neuroscience assets | ABBV | partially | EXISTING_STRENGTH (class 3: rare disease and orexin science) | IVB-008 |
