## LES-01 Manufacturing capacity as the binding constraint on a blockbuster (LLY)

- **What they did.** Lilly raised capex from USD 1.3bn (FY2021) to USD 7.8bn (FY2025) and announced more than USD 50bn of U.S. commitments after tirzepatide supply fell short; the FDA removed tirzepatide from the shortage list on 2024-10-02. Most announced sites are still pre-operating, with operating evidence only for Concord, Kinsale and the Lebanon genetic-medicine plant. [CLM-000168] [CLM-000172] [CLM-001039] [CLM-001066] [CLM-014017] [CLM-014008] [CLM-014014]
- **Transferability: partially.** Takeda's plasma-derived therapies are capacity-bound (collection centres and fractionation) and it has a USD 230m Los Angeles expansion, so the capacity logic transfers. The lesson to copy is to track operating capacity, not announced capacity. Takeda's FY2025 capex of JPY 426.9bn includes intangible assets and is not comparable with Lilly's property, plant and equipment capex. *(INTERPRETATION)*
- **Takeda baseline class.** EXISTING_STRENGTH (class 2: plasma network and PDT manufacturing). Anchoring Takeda claims: [CLM-005063] [CLM-005065] [CLM-005007]
- **Internal validation needed.** IVB-006

## LES-02 Cash-pay direct-to-patient channel (LLY)

- **What they did.** Lilly launched LillyDirect on 2024-01-04, sold Zepbound self-pay vials from August 2024 and cut prices on 2025-12-01 to USD 299 / 399 / 449. The company says over 1 million patients accessed treatments through it in 2025; the 10-K gives no dollar share, and copay-accumulator and anti-kickback limits restrict combining discounts with insurance. [CLM-001042] [CLM-007002] [CLM-007004] [CLM-007005] [CLM-007010]
- **Transferability: does_not_transfer.** Cash-pay scaled in an uninsured-gap category (obesity). Takeda's main products are infused or specialty-distributed biologics and plasma therapies sold through payer coverage and hubs, so a cash channel fits poorly. Home and subcutaneous conversion (LES-21) is the better-evidenced mechanism. *(INTERPRETATION)*
- **Takeda baseline class.** EVIDENCE_GAP (class 14: patient services and market access). Anchoring Takeda claims: [CLM-005072] [CLM-007037]
- **Internal validation needed.** IVB-013

## LES-03 Data-for-access platform (federated learning) (LLY)

- **What they did.** Lilly launched TuneLab on 2025-09-09, giving selected biotechs access to Lilly-trained ADMET and safety models in exchange for federated data contributions, with Benchling distribution to more than 1,300 customers opt-in later in 2026. No uptake, retraining count or scientific outcome is disclosed. [CLM-000280] [CLM-006008] [CLM-014055] [CLM-014056] [CLM-006055]
- **Transferability: partially.** Takeda is already in a multi-pharma federated consortium (AISB) and could be a data-for-models participant, which is a cheaper position than building a rival platform. The platform's value is unproven, so participation should wait for independent results. *(INTERPRETATION)*
- **Takeda baseline class.** EXISTING_BUT_UNDERDEVELOPED (class 9: enterprise data and AI platform, outcomes unproven). Anchoring Takeda claims: [CLM-005058] [CLM-005049] [CLM-006042]
- **Internal validation needed.** IVB-001

## LES-04 Owned robotic lab versus rented automation (LLY)

- **What they did.** Lilly built a remote robotic laboratory (Life Sciences Studio) and divested it to the CRO Arctoris in 2024; the reason is undisclosed. Zymergen, an owned biofoundry, was sold at about one-tenth of its IPO-era valuation. The NVIDIA-Lilly co-innovation lab announced in January 2026 is at concept stage. [CLM-006013] [CLM-006017] [CLM-006052] [CLM-006051] [CLM-000281]
- **Transferability: transfers.** The evidence favours buying automation as a service and gating AI-biotech deals on first-in-human data rather than owning a robotic lab. Takeda has no public lab-automation evidence, so there is nothing to retreat from. *(INTERPRETATION)*
- **Takeda baseline class.** EVIDENCE_GAP (class 11: lab automation and robotics). Anchoring Takeda claims: [CLM-005067] [CLM-005080] [CLM-014041]
- **Internal validation needed.** IVB-002

## LES-05 Growth concentration, price erosion and payer leverage (LLY)

- **What they did.** Tirzepatide reached 56.0% of Lilly's FY2025 revenue (15.6% in FY2023). Realised prices fell 5% in Q4 2025 and 15% in Q3 2026 while volume rose 46% and 53%; CVS Caremark removed Zepbound from its template formularies for 15 months (1 July 2025 to 1 October 2026); Trulicity and Verzenio face Medicare-set prices from 2028. [CLM-001003] [CLM-014003] [CLM-014004] [CLM-007011] [CLM-007013] [CLM-008015]
- **Transferability: transfers.** Entyvio is 21% of Takeda's revenue, faces Medicare negotiation from 2028 and a coming biosimilar event. Lilly's record shows that volume growth in a dominant franchise comes with net-price pressure and PBM leverage, so Takeda should plan for price erosion in its core franchise, not only for volume loss. *(INTERPRETATION)*
- **Takeda baseline class.** EXISTING_STRENGTH (class 1: GI and immunology franchise). Anchoring Takeda claims: [CLM-005009] [CLM-005017] [CLM-008022]
- **Internal validation needed.** IVB-004

## LES-06 Steady cadence of early-asset purchases versus a concentrated bet (LLY)

- **What they did.** Lilly expensed USD 3.8bn, 3.3bn and 2.9bn of acquired IPR&D in 2023-2025 (Morphic USD 2,548.5m, DICE USD 1,915.5m); none of those assets had been approved in the sources reviewed, and DICE's lead asset was discontinued in 2024. [CLM-014058] [CLM-009095] [CLM-009000] [CLM-009002] [CLM-009003]
- **Transferability: partially.** A cadence of purchases keeps options open but had produced no approval by cutoff. Takeda's one large asset purchase (Nimbus, February 2023) reached an accepted NDA in September 2026, so the two models have different risk profiles; Takeda's organisation for external innovation is not documented publicly. *(INTERPRETATION)*
- **Takeda baseline class.** EXISTING_STRENGTH (class 5: external innovation and BD, deal flow); organisation EVIDENCE_GAP. Anchoring Takeda claims: [CLM-009098] [CLM-005036] [CLM-005035] [CLM-005052]
- **Internal validation needed.** IVB-007

## LES-07 Successor sequencing before the cliff (JNJ)

- **What they did.** J&J had TREMFYA (IL-23) on the market with Crohn's and UC labels and approved the oral IL-23 peptide ICOTYDE on about 2026-03-17. In FY2025 Tremfya grew USD 1,485m, offsetting about 35% of Stelara's USD 4,283m loss, yet Immunology still fell 11.8%. [CLM-002026] [CLM-002053] [CLM-002065] [CLM-000256] [CLM-012012]
- **Transferability: partially.** The mechanism requires a successor in the same prescriber base launched years before the loss. Takeda's zasocitinib is an oral TYK2 inhibitor in psoriasis, not a successor to Entyvio in gastroenterology, so it replaces revenue but not the franchise. J&J's record also shows that even a pre-launched successor offsets only part of the loss in the first year. *(INTERPRETATION)*
- **Takeda baseline class.** EXISTING_BUT_UNDERDEVELOPED (class 7: LOE replacement). Anchoring Takeda claims: [CLM-005017] [CLM-005035] [CLM-005041]
- **Internal validation needed.** IVB-005

## LES-08 Debt-funded acquisition bridge (JNJ)

- **What they did.** J&J acquired businesses for USD 15.1bn (FY2024) and USD 17.5bn (FY2025) net of cash; net debt rose from USD 2.1bn (FY2021) to USD 27.8bn (FY2025) while it paid about USD 12.4bn of dividends and USD 6.0bn of buybacks in FY2025. [CLM-009049] [CLM-002010] [CLM-002014] [CLM-000105]
- **Transferability: partially.** J&J's bridge rests on USD 24.5bn of operating cash flow and a large MedTech and pharma base. Takeda stated no significant acquisitions in three years, carries a company-defined adjusted leverage ratio (2.6x, not verified by the audit) and has a JPY 403.5bn Amitiza provision, so its bridge capacity depends on legal cash timing that is not public. *(INTERPRETATION)*
- **Takeda baseline class.** EXISTING_BUT_UNDERDEVELOPED (class 16: cost transformation) with class 5 deal flow. Anchoring Takeda claims: [CLM-005005] [CLM-005014] [CLM-009087]
- **Internal validation needed.** IVB-012

## LES-09 Claimed pharma and MedTech synergy (JNJ)

- **What they did.** J&J asserts that pairing Abiomed, Biosense Webster and Shockwave creates cardiovascular leadership, but no cross-segment revenue synergy is disclosed. MedTech earns a 12.2% segment margin against 36.9% for Innovative Medicine, and J&J announced the Orthopaedics separation on 2025-10-14. [CLM-002074] [CLM-002004] [CLM-002037]
- **Transferability: does_not_transfer.** Takeda has no MedTech segment, so the structure does not apply. The transferable point is to test a claimed combination synergy against segment margins and disclosed revenue links before building strategy on it. *(INTERPRETATION)*
- **Takeda baseline class.** NOT_APPLICABLE (Takeda has no MedTech segment; six key business areas). Anchoring Takeda claims: [CLM-005010]
- **Internal validation needed.** none; public evidence suffices or the topic is outside the backlog

## LES-10 Inspection findings, not clinical data, behind approval delays (LLY)

- **What they did.** Lilly's lebrikizumab CRL (October 2023) came from third-party manufacturer inspection findings, with no concern on clinical data, safety or label; lebrikizumab was approved as Ebglyss on 2024-09-13. AbbVie's second ABBV-951 CRL (June 2024) also cited third-party manufacturer observations. [CLM-012134] [CLM-001024] [CLM-001064] [CLM-012112]
- **Transferability: transfers.** Takeda's baseline already records a 2020 FDA warning letter at Hikari with a Leuprorelin supply shortage. Launch timing for its 2026 approvals and the zasocitinib NDA depends on site inspection status, including third-party sites. *(INTERPRETATION)*
- **Takeda baseline class.** EXISTING_BUT_UNDERDEVELOPED (class 12: manufacturing quality, one documented failure). Anchoring Takeda claims: [CLM-005020] [CLM-005029] [CLM-005035]
- **Internal validation needed.** IVB-011

## LES-11 Litigation overhang and reserve volatility (JNJ)

- **What they did.** J&J's talc subsidiaries filed three Chapter 11 petitions (two dismissed, Red River not confirmed on 2025-03-31); J&J reversed about USD 7bn of reserve, held about USD 3.4bn at FY2025 end, then proposed a USD 5.5bn ovarian resolution on 2026-07-27 that needs 95% participation. Plaintiff counsel says the cost could reach USD 7bn or more. [CLM-002015] [CLM-002038] [CLM-002016] [CLM-002062] [CLM-002063]
- **Transferability: partially.** Talc is product liability and Takeda's AMITIZA case is pay-for-delay antitrust, so legal mechanics differ. The transferable point is that reserve and settlement estimates moved by billions within a year at J&J; Takeda's JPY 403.5bn provision follows a jury verdict it intends to appeal, and the final judgement and cash timing are not public. *(INTERPRETATION)*
- **Takeda baseline class.** NOT_APPLICABLE (legal exposure is not a baseline capability class). Anchoring Takeda claims: [CLM-005013] [CLM-005014] [CLM-014047]
- **Internal validation needed.** IVB-012

## LES-12 Self-reported AI metrics without baselines (JNJ)

- **What they did.** J&J's CIO reported nearly 900 gen-AI use cases reviewed, trial-site recommendations with 'up to 2.6x' enrolment, and 47,000 employees completing a gen-AI course. The enrolment figure has no baseline or method, and course completions are a training metric. The audit retagged both. [CLM-006018] [CLM-006019] [CLM-006020] [CLM-006022]
- **Transferability: transfers.** Takeda's own reported measures (63.4% of the workforce actively using gen-AI tools; a vendor-hosted agent platform) are also usage or self-report measures. Takeda should define outcome baselines (time saved, cycle time, cost) before treating usage as value. *(INTERPRETATION)*
- **Takeda baseline class.** EXISTING_BUT_UNDERDEVELOPED (class 9: enterprise data and AI platform, outcomes unproven). Anchoring Takeda claims: [CLM-014043] [CLM-005058] [CLM-005057]
- **Internal validation needed.** IVB-001

## LES-13 Extend the successor across the incumbent's indications before the cliff (ABBV)

- **What they did.** Skyrizi and Rinvoq gained psoriatic arthritis, Crohn's, ulcerative colitis and atopic dermatitis labels between 2022 and 2025 and, with head-to-head data, covered Humira's major indications. Together they rose from USD 7,687m (2022) to USD 25,866m (2025) against a Humira loss of USD 16,697m. [CLM-003084] [CLM-003016] [CLM-003014] [CLM-003015]
- **Transferability: transfers.** Takeda has psoriatic arthritis Phase 3 studies for zasocitinib running to May 2027 and a head-to-head Phase 3 win over deucravacitinib, which is the same pattern of indication breadth and comparative data. The AbbVie successors were already marketed before the cliff; Takeda's are not yet. *(INTERPRETATION)*
- **Takeda baseline class.** EXISTING_BUT_UNDERDEVELOPED (class 7: LOE replacement). Anchoring Takeda claims: [CLM-005037] [CLM-005034] [CLM-005018]
- **Internal validation needed.** IVB-005

## LES-14 Contracting defence against PBM-driven biosimilar substitution (ABBV)

- **What they did.** AbbVie kept at least 97% of adalimumab volume through March 2024 with rebate-for-access contracts, then supplied a co-branded Humira to CVS's Cordavis when Caremark removed Humira from template formularies on 2024-04-01; U.S. Humira revenue still fell 41% in 2024 and 57% in 2025. [CLM-003007] [CLM-003008] [CLM-003009] [CLM-003010] [CLM-007016]
- **Transferability: partially.** PBM private labels now handle large biosimilar events (nine Stelara biosimilars by July 2025, four from PBM-affiliated labels), so payer contracting depth matters as much as patents. Takeda has no public evidence on rebate or contracting structure, and two Entyvio biosimilar BLAs are under FDA review. *(INTERPRETATION)*
- **Takeda baseline class.** EVIDENCE_GAP (class 14: patient services and market access) with class 1 GI franchise. Anchoring Takeda claims: [CLM-007025] [CLM-005072] [CLM-014051]
- **Internal validation needed.** IVB-004

## LES-15 Size acquisitions to survive a write-down (ABBV)

- **What they did.** AbbVie recorded a USD 4.5bn impairment in Q4 2024 after emraclidine failed, 54% of the USD 8.3bn Cerevel net price. The same year's ImmunoGen purchase supplied a growing product (Elahere) and Cerevel's tavapadon was approved as Juvmo in September 2026. [CLM-009054] [CLM-003057] [CLM-003086] [CLM-003090]
- **Transferability: transfers.** Takeda's largest purchase (Nimbus, USD 4.0bn upfront) has the same single-asset risk profile and has so far delivered. Takeda's baseline already shows that stop decisions and write-downs (cell therapy, soticlestat) are absorbed; the lesson is to size any next large purchase so one failure does not breach leverage or dividend policy. *(INTERPRETATION)*
- **Takeda baseline class.** EXISTING_STRENGTH (class 6: portfolio discipline, with write-down cost). Anchoring Takeda claims: [CLM-005036] [CLM-005025] [CLM-009084]
- **Internal validation needed.** IVB-005

## LES-16 Settlement-based IP to convert patent dates into entry dates (ABBV)

- **What they did.** AbbVie's September 2025 settlements with all Rinvoq generic filers mean no generic tablet entry is expected before April 2037, four years after the 2033 composition patent; Humira biosimilar entry was negotiated to 2023. [CLM-003021] [CLM-003087] [CLM-014036]
- **Transferability: partially.** Entyvio patents expire in some cases in 2032 and third parties filed UK and Netherlands revocation actions in early 2026, so Takeda faces litigation rather than settled entry dates. What is transferable is the posture; the outcome depends on Takeda's litigation position, which is not public. *(INTERPRETATION)*
- **Takeda baseline class.** EXISTING_BUT_UNDERDEVELOPED (class 7: LOE replacement). Anchoring Takeda claims: [CLM-014050] [CLM-005017] [CLM-014051]
- **Internal validation needed.** IVB-004

## LES-17 Option and early-stage licence volume (ABBV)

- **What they did.** AbbVie runs a yearly stream of USD 0.6bn to 1.0bn of early-stage upfronts and option deals (ADARx USD 335m upfront with up to USD 7.5bn of milestones; Gubra USD 350m; Ichnos USD 700m). None had produced an approved product by cutoff. [CLM-009061] [CLM-009062] [CLM-009060] [CLM-009069] [CLM-009097]
- **Transferability: partially.** Takeda's Innovent arrangement (USD 1.2bn upfront including USD 100m equity, with an option) is the same shape on a smaller number of deals. The evidence does not show that volume produces approvals, and Takeda's external-innovation organisation is not documented in primary sources. *(INTERPRETATION)*
- **Takeda baseline class.** EXISTING_STRENGTH (class 5: external innovation and BD, deal flow); organisation EVIDENCE_GAP. Anchoring Takeda claims: [CLM-009078] [CLM-005050] [CLM-005052]
- **Internal validation needed.** IVB-007

## LES-18 High variance of first-in-class psychiatry and neuroscience assets (ABBV)

- **What they did.** AbbVie's emraclidine Phase 2 missed its primary endpoint in November 2024; J&J stopped aticaprant on insufficient efficacy in March 2025; Takeda's soticlestat Phase 3 missed in June 2024. Neuroscience and psychiatry is the common failure site across three companies in the window. [CLM-003054] [CLM-003057] [CLM-002039] [CLM-012135] [CLM-012115] [CLM-012120]
- **Transferability: partially.** Takeda's oveporexton succeeded in a different neuroscience area (orexin, with discovery in Shonan) after TAK-994 was stopped in 2022 for liver safety. The lesson is to gate psychiatry and CNS assets on Phase 2 quality and placebo response, and not to infer that orexin success transfers to other CNS bets. *(INTERPRETATION)*
- **Takeda baseline class.** EXISTING_STRENGTH (class 3: rare disease and orexin science). Anchoring Takeda claims: [CLM-005024] [CLM-005048] [CLM-005029] [CLM-005023]
- **Internal validation needed.** IVB-008

## LES-19 Redesigning a patient or provider programme without a pilot (ABBV)

- **What they did.** AbbVie launched a revised Alle loyalty programme in October 2024 and reinstated the original in early 2025 after providers found the new one too complex; U.S. Botox Cosmetic revenue fell 11% in 2025 on pricing from programme changes, lower share and lower demand. [CLM-003033] [CLM-003032] [CLM-003088]
- **Transferability: does_not_transfer.** Takeda has no aesthetics business, and Alle is a consumer loyalty scheme. The narrower point, that a support-programme redesign can cost share within months and should be piloted, applies to Takeda's Help at Hand and EntyvioConnect programmes, which have no public outcome data. *(INTERPRETATION)*
- **Takeda baseline class.** EVIDENCE_GAP (class 14: patient services and market access). Anchoring Takeda claims: [CLM-007037] [CLM-007038] [CLM-005072]
- **Internal validation needed.** IVB-013

## LES-20 Packaging price concessions with tariff relief and investment pledges (LLY)

- **What they did.** Lilly (2025-11-06), J&J (2026-01-08) and AbbVie (2026-01-12) each announced a voluntary agreement pairing price or access concessions with tariff relief and a U.S. investment pledge (Lilly more than USD 50bn since 2020, J&J more than USD 55bn over four years, AbbVie USD 100bn over a decade). [CLM-001036] [CLM-008031] [CLM-008032] [CLM-008029] [CLM-008030] [CLM-008037]
- **Transferability: partially.** Takeda's 20-F records MFN pricing and Japan's annual price revisions as risks and the registry holds no Takeda pledge or agreement. Whether such a package is available or advisable for Takeda cannot be judged from public evidence; the competitor agreements are company announcements, and their terms and realised value are not independently verified. *(INTERPRETATION)*
- **Takeda baseline class.** NOT_APPLICABLE (policy engagement is not a baseline capability class). Anchoring Takeda claims: [CLM-008035] [CLM-008036] [CLM-008022]
- **Internal validation needed.** none; public evidence suffices or the topic is outside the backlog

## LES-21 Home and subcutaneous administration as a growth and defence mechanism (JNJ)

- **What they did.** TREMFYA subcutaneous share gains accompanied USD 5,155m of FY2025 sales (+40.5%); Zepbound moved to vials and a KwikPen with self-pay pricing from USD 299. [CLM-007029] [CLM-007044] [CLM-000256] [CLM-007053]
- **Transferability: transfers.** This is the best-evidenced transferable mechanism for Takeda: the ENTYVIO subcutaneous pen is approved for UC (September 2023) and Crohn's disease (April 2024), the 20-F says it continues to drive uptake, and HYHUB needle-free Hyqvia transfer received FDA 510(k) clearance in July 2025. Effect on net price and erosion after biosimilar entry is not established. *(INTERPRETATION)*
- **Takeda baseline class.** EXISTING_STRENGTH (class 1: GI and immunology franchise). Anchoring Takeda claims: [CLM-005018] [CLM-007041] [CLM-007042] [CLM-005012]
- **Internal validation needed.** IVB-004

## Cross-lesson reading *(INTERPRETATION)*

- The lessons bearing most directly on Entyvio (21% of revenue) are LES-05, LES-14 and LES-21 [CLM-005009] [CLM-007016] [CLM-007053].
- AI-infrastructure lessons (LES-03, LES-04) point to partnering and renting: competitor evidence shows no outcome and one divestment [CLM-006007] [CLM-006013].
- No lesson rests on an independently verified AI outcome; the only regulator-verified items are device records [CLM-006054].
- Takeda's 2026 integrated-report evidence post-dates the capability baseline and should update classes 9, 11 and 13 at the next refresh [CLM-014041] [CLM-014042] [CLM-014043].

reports.title: Loss-of-exclusivity (LOE) resilience: Lilly, J&J, AbbVie, Takeda
reports.markdown:
# Loss-of-exclusivity (LOE) resilience: Lilly, J&J, AbbVie, Takeda

Cutoff 2026-11-21. Period labels: Lilly and AbbVie report calendar years; J&J's FY2025 is the 52 weeks ended 2025-12-28 [CLM-002005]; Takeda's FY2025 is April 2025 to March 2026 [CLM-005000]. No currency conversion is used. Every ratio below is a within-company ratio or a growth rate, so JPY and USD are never compared in absolute terms. Ratios marked *(computed)* are arithmetic on the cited claims, not figures any company reported.

## 1. What is established

### 1.1 The four observed cliffs, aligned by year since LOE

| Item | Company | LOE event | Peak-year sales | Year 1 | Year 2 | Year 3 | Share of company revenue: peak year → latest | Claims |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Humira (global) | AbbVie | U.S. exclusivity ended 2023-01-31 | USD 21,237m (2022) | 14,404m (2023), -32.2% *(computed)* | 8,993m (2024), -57.7% *(computed)* | 4,540m (2025), -78.6% *(computed)* | 36.6% (2022) → 7.4% (2025) *(computed)* | [CLM-003000] [CLM-003002] [CLM-003004] [CLM-003015] |
| Stelara (global) | J&J | U.S. biosimilars launched from January 2025; J&J says settlements permit launches in Europe and the U.S. from 2025 | USD 10,858m (FY2023) | 10,361m (FY2024), -4.6% | 6,078m (FY2025), -44.0% vs peak *(computed)* | not yet reached | 12.8% (FY2023) → 6.5% (FY2025) *(computed)*; 6.5% reported | [CLM-002022] [CLM-002052] [CLM-007017] |
| Vyvanse/Elvanse (global) | Takeda | U.S. patent and pediatric exclusivity ended August 2023 | JPY 423.2bn is the FY2023 value; an earlier peak was not extracted | 350.6bn (FY2024), -17.2% vs FY2023 *(computed)* | 203.2bn (FY2025), -52.0% vs FY2023 *(computed)* | expected to keep falling in FY2026 | 9.9% (FY2023) → 4.5% (FY2025) *(computed)* | [CLM-005015] [CLM-000275] [CLM-005000] |
| Trulicity (global) | Lilly | not an LOE: sales fell as patients moved to tirzepatide; U.S. compound patent expires 2027 | USD 7,439.7m (FY2022) | 7,132.6m (FY2023) | 5,253.5m (FY2024) | 4,276m (FY2025), -42.5% vs FY2022 *(computed)* | 26.1% (FY2022) → 6.6% (FY2025) *(computed)* | [CLM-001004] [CLM-000243] [CLM-000250] |

Notes on the table:
- The Lilly row is substitution inside its own franchise, not a generic or biosimilar cliff, so it is not an LOE case in the strict sense *(INTERPRETATION)* [CLM-001004] [CLM-000250]. Lilly's one patent-driven loss in the window was Alimta: USD 2,061.4m in FY2021 to 927.7m in FY2022, -55%, after multiple generics entered, which was 7.3% of FY2021 revenue *(computed)* [CLM-001011] [CLM-001000]. The earlier skeleton comparison's statement that Lilly had no LOE exposure until 2027 is therefore incorrect and is superseded here.
- Vyvanse years are counted from FY2023 because the sale series starts there; the patent expiry fell in August 2023, so FY2023 already includes four months of exposure [CLM-005015]. The Vyvanse peak is understated as a base and the decline is a lower bound *(INTERPRETATION)*.
- Stelara's fall is still under way. J&J reported Stelara as a roughly 690 basis point drag on Q3 2026 Innovative Medicine growth [CLM-002060], and CVS Caremark moved to prefer two Stelara biosimilars from 2026-07-01 [CLM-007015]. Year 3 is therefore unobserved [CLM-002060].

### 1.2 Replacement evidence

| Company | Replacement mechanism evidenced | Size of replacement | Organic vs acquired | Claims |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AbbVie | Skyrizi and Rinvoq, already marketed and extended across Humira's indications before and after U.S. LOE | Skyrizi + Rinvoq rose USD 7,687m (2022) → 25,866m (2025), +18,179m, against a Humira loss of 16,697m, i.e. 109% *(computed)*; total revenue returned above the 2022 peak only in 2025 (USD 61,160m vs 58,054m) | Both products were on the market before the LOE; whether they were licensed in or discovered internally is not established in the registry *(gap)*. The 2024 acquisitions (ImmunoGen, Cerevel) contributed small product revenue in the window, e.g. Elahere U.S. USD 607m in 2025 | [CLM-003014] [CLM-003015] [CLM-003036] [CLM-003084] |
| J&J | TREMFYA (+USD 1,485m in FY2025), SIMPONI, plus oncology and acquisitions | Tremfya offset about 35% of the FY2025 Stelara loss of USD 4,283m *(computed)*. Immunology still fell 11.8% to USD 15,728m. Group sales excluding Stelara rose about 12.3% against +6.0% reported *(computed)* | Mixed. Intra-Cellular added about USD 0.7bn of 2025 sales at closing (company guidance) and CAPLYTA recorded USD 700m; J&J's own commentary puts about one point of group growth on acquisitions | [CLM-000254] [CLM-000256] [CLM-002026] [CLM-002075] [CLM-002041] [CLM-002025] |
| Takeda | Growth & Launch Products were 51% of FY2025 revenue; late-stage programmes are the stated replacement | Group revenue fell 1.7% at actual rates (-2.7% at constant rates) in FY2025; H1 FY2026 revenue was +8.4% at actual and -1.0% at constant rates. The first two novel approvals of the replacement set came in August 2026, after the FY2025 close | Mostly in-licensed or acquired programmes (Nimbus, Protagonist, Keros, Arrowhead); oveporexton is an in-house discovery per Takeda | [CLM-005008] [CLM-005001] [CLM-005011] [CLM-005029] [CLM-005032] [CLM-005050] [CLM-005048] |
| Lilly | Tirzepatide launch (Mounjaro 2022, Zepbound 2023) replaced Trulicity and Alimta and then supplied most of group growth | Mounjaro + Zepbound USD 36,507m = 56.0% of FY2025 revenue *(computed)* [CLM-001003] | Not established whether tirzepatide was internally discovered; Lilly's window deals did not supply a revenue-bearing product in the sources reviewed | [CLM-001028] [CLM-001029] [CLM-009000] [CLM-001003] |

## 2. Why the four cases cannot be ranked on one number

1. **Different cliff sizes.** Humira was 36.6% of AbbVie revenue at peak; Stelara 12.8% of J&J's; Vyvanse 9.9% of Takeda's (FY2023 base) *(computed)* [CLM-003004] [CLM-002022] [CLM-005015]. A smaller cliff is absorbed more easily regardless of management quality, so equal replacement ratios would not imply equal capability *(INTERPRETATION)*.
2. **Different elapsed time.** AbbVie's cliff is observed for three years, J&J's for two, Takeda's for two. A replacement ratio computed at different ages is not a like-for-like measure. The only like-for-like comparison available is year-2 decline: Humira -57.7% (2024 vs 2022 peak), Stelara -44.0% (FY2025 vs FY2023 peak), Vyvanse -52.0% (FY2025 vs FY2023) *(computed)* [CLM-003002] [CLM-002022] [CLM-005015].
3. **Different segment boundaries and acquisitions.** J&J's replacement mixes organic growth with acquired revenue (Intra-Cellular, Abiomed, Shockwave) [CLM-002041] [CLM-002011] [CLM-002027], which the registry does not separate fully; AbbVie's replacement products were pre-existing [CLM-003084]. J&J's "ex-Stelara +12.3%" therefore overstates organic resilience by an amount only partly disclosed (about one point per J&J) [CLM-002075].
4. **Different currencies and fiscal years.** Takeda's JPY series embeds exchange-rate effects (FY2025: -1.7% actual versus -2.7% constant) [CLM-005001], and its FY ends in March, so its FY2025 overlaps the other three companies' 2025 by nine months only [CLM-005000].
5. **Different price mechanisms.** AbbVie's defence was contracting (at least 97% of adalimumab volume retained through March 2024) followed by a CVS Caremark / Cordavis co-branded arrangement; the steepest declines (-41% in 2024, -57% in 2025 for U.S. Humira) followed the April 2024 formulary change, which the registry treats as association, not proven causation [CLM-003007] [CLM-003008] [CLM-003010]. J&J's Stelara faced nine biosimilars including four sold by PBM-affiliated private labels by July 2025, plus a Medicare negotiated price 66% below the 2023 list price from January 2026 [CLM-007016] [CLM-008008]. Takeda has not yet faced its Entyvio event [CLM-005017].

**Comparison status:** valid as a side-by-side description and for year-2 decline; **invalid** as a single "resilience score" or as a ranking of management quality.

## 3. Forward LOE and price exposure (what each company has disclosed)

| Company | Next disclosed exposures | Claims |
|---|---|---|
| AbbVie | Skyrizi and Rinvoq U.S. composition patents expire 2033; Rinvoq generic entry not expected before April 2037 after September 2025 settlements; Skyrizi, a biologic, has no disclosed settlement date; Vraylar next patent expiry September 2029 per an analyst source; Imbruvica, Vraylar, Linzess and Botox are Medicare-negotiation selected | [CLM-003021] [CLM-003029] [CLM-003080] |
| J&J | Further Stelara erosion in 2026; two SIMPONI biosimilars pursuing U.S. approval; Stelara and Xarelto were deselected from negotiation from 2027 while Erleada was selected for 2028; DARZALEX patent dates not in the registry | [CLM-002026] [CLM-008011] [CLM-008015] [CLM-002073] |
| Lilly | Trulicity U.S. compound patent 2027, Verzenio 2031, tirzepatide 2036; Jardiance negotiated price from 2026, Trulicity and Verzenio from 2028 | [CLM-000250] [CLM-008021] [CLM-008015] |
| Takeda | TRINTELLIX generics expected after December 2026; Entyvio regulatory exclusivity ends in the latter half of the decade with patents to 2032, UK and Netherlands revocation actions filed February to April 2026, and two biosimilar BLAs accepted by the FDA; Entyvio selected for Medicare negotiation from 2028 | [CLM-005016] [CLM-005017] [CLM-014050] [CLM-014051] [CLM-008022] |

## 4. What is contested

- Whether Humira's decline after April 2024 was caused by the CVS Caremark change: the data show timing only [CLM-003010].
- Whether J&J's Stelara absorption is complete or flattered by acquisitions: J&J's own breakdown is partial [CLM-002075] [CLM-002041].
- Takeda's USD 10-20bn peak range for six late-stage programmes is a company scenario. It is not adjusted for probability of success and Takeda says it should not be treated as a forecast or target [CLM-005041] [CLM-014049].

## 5. What is unknown

- The Takeda Vyvanse peak and the U.S. share of Vyvanse's decline (gap).
- Skyrizi's biosimilar timing after 2033 (gap) [CLM-003021].
- Any LOE-adjusted net-price data for Entyvio; whether the Entyvio biosimilar BLAs are blocked by 12-year reference-product exclusivity was not confirmed in the Purple Book [CLM-014051].

reports.title: Master comparison: Lilly, J&J, AbbVie and the Takeda public baseline
reports.markdown:
# Master comparison: Lilly, J&J, AbbVie and the Takeda public baseline

Cutoff 2026-11-21. This file replaces the v0.1 skeleton. It answers the ten comparison questions, each with evidence, and points to the detailed files. No standardized scores or rankings are used; where a comparison is invalid the file says so. Periods: Lilly and AbbVie calendar years; J&J 52-week years (FY2025 ended 2025-12-28) [CLM-002005]; Takeda FY2025 = April 2025 to March 2026 [CLM-005000]. Takeda amounts stay in JPY; growth rates and shares are compared, not absolute JPY against USD. 2026 is partial [CLM-001032] [CLM-003023] [CLM-002060] [CLM-005011]. Gate 1 status: Lilly pass, J&J and AbbVie conditional, Takeda fail (repairable), so Takeda timeline and business-model gaps carry through.

## 0. Corrections from the audit that this file applies

- AbbVie and J&J "long-term debt (noncurrent)" series are total long-term debt including the current portion; non-current was USD 58,941m (AbbVie) and USD 39,438m (J&J) at FY2025 [CLM-000070] [CLM-000132] [CLM-003042]. Non-current balance-sheet figures: [CLM-000287] (AbbVie) [CLM-000288] (J&J); the XBRL LongTermDebt series includes the current portion (see corrections on CLM-003042, CLM-000066..070, CLM-000128..132).
- OTTAVA: J&J announced Memorial Hermann-TMC as the first hospital to install; a completed installation is not shown, and no IDE-to-install duration is derived [CLM-000284] [CLM-014024].
- AbbVie ImmunoGen is USD 10.1bn announced, 9.8bn consideration, 9.2bn net of cash; USD 18.5bn for ImmunoGen plus Cerevel is consideration, 17.5bn net of cash [CLM-003053] [CLM-003086].
- Takeda restructuring cost series: about JPY 150bn (March 2026), 170.0bn (original FY2026 forecast), 160.0bn (revised); the cell-therapy impairment recognised is JPY 58.2bn, not 58.0bn [CLM-005078] [CLM-005025].
- Morphic: USD 3.2bn headline, 2.55bn audited charge, 3.35bn cash paid [CLM-009002]. Lilly FY2021 acquired IPR&D is 970.1 on the FY2022 definition [CLM-009022]. AbbVie net income differs by basis (consolidated vs attributable) [CLM-000026].
- J&J's eight T2-only claims are single-interested-source, and "regulator-verified" for OTTAVA, VELYS and MONARCH rests partly on J&J releases, now supplemented by openFDA records [CLM-002037] [CLM-000286] [CLM-014026].

## 1. Why is Lilly winning where it wins?

Lilly's revenue rose from USD 28.3bn to USD 65.2bn (FY2021 to FY2025), 23.2% a year *(computed)*, because tirzepatide went from first revenue in 2022 to 56.0% of sales [CLM-000133] [CLM-000137] [CLM-001001] [CLM-001003]. Pre-tax margin rose from 21.7% to 39.5% and gross margin from 74.2% to 83.0% while R&D roughly doubled [CLM-001007] [CLM-001005] [CLM-000143] [CLM-000147]. The mechanisms evidenced are: a launched incretin with strong trial results (SURMOUNT-1 weight loss up to 20.9%) [CLM-001056]; capacity spending (capex USD 1.3bn to 7.8bn) after a shortage that ended in 2024 [CLM-000172] [CLM-001066]; a cash-pay channel [CLM-001042]; and a follow-on oral and triple-agonist pipeline [CLM-001030] [CLM-001060]. What the evidence does not show is durability: realised prices fell 15% in Q3 2026 and about USD 900m of that quarter was one-off [CLM-014003]. *(INTERPRETATION)* Lilly is winning in a category where demand exceeded supply; the registry does not show whether the advantage persists once supply and competition normalise.

## 2. What makes J&J's pharma and MedTech combination distinctive, and where is the synergy unevidenced?

J&J is the only one of the four with a MedTech segment (USD 33.8bn) beside Innovative Medicine (USD 60.4bn) [CLM-000253]. MedTech earns a 12.2% segment margin against 36.9%, grew 2.5% in Q3 2026, and J&J announced the Orthopaedics separation [CLM-002004] [CLM-002060] [CLM-002037]. J&J claims cardiovascular leadership across Abiomed, Biosense Webster and Shockwave; no cross-segment revenue synergy is disclosed, so the pharma and MedTech synergy is unevidenced [CLM-002074]. The distinctive, evidenced feature is diversification: the largest brand is 15.2% of revenue and Cardiovascular grew 15.8% [CLM-002073] [CLM-002028]. Offsetting evidence: Impella recalls and the Varipulse pause [CLM-002046] [CLM-002044].

## 3. How did AbbVie absorb the Humira loss of exclusivity?

Global Humira fell from USD 21,237m (2022) to 4,540m (2025), -78.6% *(computed)*, after U.S. exclusivity ended on 2023-01-31 [CLM-003002] [CLM-003000]. Skyrizi plus Rinvoq rose USD 18,179m against a Humira loss of 16,697m; total revenue passed its 2022 peak only in 2025 [CLM-003014] [CLM-003015]. Three mechanisms are evidenced: successors already marketed and extended across Humira's indications [CLM-003084] [CLM-003016]; rebate-for-access contracting that held at least 97% of volume to March 2024, then a Cordavis co-brand [CLM-003007] [CLM-003008]; and patent settlements (Rinvoq entry not before April 2037) [CLM-003021]. Steep U.S. declines came after the April 2024 formulary change, which is an association, not proven causation [CLM-003010]. See [loe_resilience_comparison.md](loe_resilience_comparison.md).

## 4. Who converts R&D into commercial outcomes best?

Metric definitions and results are in [rd_investment_and_productivity.md](rd_investment_and_productivity.md) and [pipeline_and_revenue_dependence.md](pipeline_and_revenue_dependence.md). On R&D intensity, Lilly fell from 24.5% to 20.5%, J&J stayed at 15.6-15.7%, AbbVie rose from 12.6% to 14.9%, Takeda stayed at 14.7-15.0% *(computed)* [CLM-001006] [CLM-000085] [CLM-000015] [CLM-005004]. On the share of FY2025 revenue from molecules approved after 2021-11-21, Lilly is at least 56.0%, J&J at least 3.2%, AbbVie at least 1.8% and Takeda not computable *(computed)* [CLM-001003] [CLM-002024] [CLM-003036] [CLM-003037]. **That comparison is invalid as a productivity ranking**: it rewards new-molecule growth and penalises lifecycle growth (Skyrizi and Rinvoq), acquired assets are mixed with in-house ones (sponsor of record for Elahere is ImmunoGen, for Epkinly Genmab) [CLM-012013] [CLM-012014], approval counts (8, 5, 5, 3) are small and include 2026 approvals funded earlier [CLM-012000] [CLM-012007], and R&D accounting boundaries differ [CLM-000270]. The evidence supports only a narrower statement: Lilly's recent growth comes from a molecule approved inside the window, AbbVie's from molecules approved before it *(INTERPRETATION)*.

## 5. Who has the most defensible technology ecosystem?

The registry cannot support a ranking. Lilly has the largest evidenced build (LillyPod, TuneLab, external model partners) with no outcome shown; J&J has the only regulator records (devices, not discovery); AbbVie has an internal knowledge graph; Takeda is partnership-led with 2026 company-reported operating items [CLM-006004] [CLM-000280] [CLM-014022] [CLM-006032] [CLM-014041]. Of 29 company-level entries, 18 sit at concept, prototype or pilot and none shows a demonstrated outcome [CLM-006054; counts computed from data_ai_maturity_matrix.md — INTERPRETATION]. "Lilly is most defensible" is a *(HYPOTHESIS)* resting on proprietary data (company-estimated at over USD 1bn) [CLM-006055] [CLM-000280]. See [data_ai_maturity_matrix.md](data_ai_maturity_matrix.md).

## 6. Which AI investments are operationally meaningful?

Operational status plus disclosed scale: LillyPod (1,016 GPUs) [CLM-006004], AbbVie's ARCH (124 TB, over 30 million nodes) [CLM-006032], Takeda's 170+ Lessines predictive-maintenance agents and plasma nomograms [CLM-014041] [CLM-005060], and J&J's quality-control tool (qualitative) [CLM-006021]. None has independent evidence of effect on cost, cycle time or revenue. NVIDIA lab, Valkai, Isomorphic and OpenAI are announcements [CLM-000281] [CLM-000285] [CLM-006012] [CLM-006011].

## 7. Who has repeatable discovery and development capability?

Evidence of repetition, not of quality: Lilly eight novel approvals across incretin, immunology, neurology and oncology [CLM-012000] [CLM-012007]; J&J five spanning bispecifics, a TKI, an FcRn antibody and an oral peptide [CLM-012008] [CLM-012012]; AbbVie five, mostly acquired or partnered, with growth from supplements [CLM-012013] [CLM-012033]; Takeda three, with three Phase 3 readouts delivered positive on the 2024 plan [CLM-012018] [CLM-005042]. Repeatability is partly unproven for all: AbbVie's neuroscience record is one approval and one failure, Takeda's replacement set arrived in August 2026, and Lilly's expensed 2023-2025 purchases had no approval by cutoff [CLM-012148] [CLM-005029] [CLM-009000]. Attrition appears in every company: see [strengths_and_vulnerabilities.md](strengths_and_vulnerabilities.md) and [rd_investment_and_productivity.md](rd_investment_and_productivity.md).

## 8. Which partnerships create durable options?

Option structures exist at AbbVie (ADARx, Calico, Gubra, Ichnos), Takeda (Innovent licence, equity and option) and Lilly (Beam opt-in, CVRs) [CLM-009061] [CLM-009068] [CLM-009062] [CLM-009060] [CLM-009078] [CLM-014058] [CLM-009099]. No option from the window has yet produced an approved product, so durability is a *(HYPOTHESIS)* [CLM-009095] [CLM-009097]. Realised value from partnerships so far: J&J Momenta (IMAAVY) and Intra-Cellular (CAPLYTA MDD), Lilly Loxo (Jaypirca), AbbVie ImmunoGen (Elahere), Takeda HUTCHMED (Fruzaqla) and Protagonist (Mimrylo) [CLM-009044] [CLM-009031] [CLM-009015] [CLM-009056] [CLM-012018] [CLM-012020]. Deal-value comparisons are invalid across bases; see [partner_ecosystem_comparison.md](partner_ecosystem_comparison.md).

## 9. What does each do better than the other two, and where is each vulnerable?

See [strengths_and_vulnerabilities.md](strengths_and_vulnerabilities.md). In one line each, on evidence: Lilly combines growth with margin expansion and capacity build [CLM-000137] [CLM-001007] [CLM-000172]; J&J absorbs a large LOE with a diversified base [CLM-000253] [CLM-000254]; AbbVie replaces a dominant franchise with pre-built successors [CLM-003014]; Takeda has a plasma-derived franchise and in-house orexin discovery [CLM-005063] [CLM-005048]. Largest vulnerabilities: Lilly, concentration of 56.0% and price erosion [CLM-001003] [CLM-014003]; J&J, talc and a still-falling Stelara [CLM-002062] [CLM-002060]; AbbVie, successor concentration at 42.3% *(computed)* and a USD 4.5bn neuroscience write-down [CLM-000266] [CLM-003057]; Takeda, Entyvio at 21% with exclusivity loss ahead, flat revenue and the AMITIZA provision [CLM-005009] [CLM-005017] [CLM-005001] [CLM-005014].

## 10. What would change positions by 2035? *(HYPOTHESIS; anchors are evidenced dates)*

- Lilly: tirzepatide patent to 2036; Trulicity patent 2027; Trulicity and Verzenio negotiated prices from 2028; retatrutide, lepodisiran and orforglipron outcome trials read out 2029-2031 [CLM-000250] [CLM-008015] [CLM-001047] [CLM-001050] [CLM-001045].
- J&J: Stelara erosion through 2026-2027, talc resolution needing 95% participation, the Orthopaedics separation 18-24 months after October 2025, DARZALEX concentration (patent dates not in the registry) [CLM-002060] [CLM-002062] [CLM-002030] [CLM-002073].
- AbbVie: Vraylar patent September 2029 (analyst source), Skyrizi and Rinvoq composition patents 2033, Rinvoq entry 2037, obesity and in-vivo CAR-T programmes at Phase 1 [CLM-003029] [CLM-003021] [CLM-003073] [CLM-003072].
- Takeda: Entyvio exclusivity loss in the latter half of the decade and 2032 patents, Trintellix generics after December 2026, launch execution of oveporexton, rusfertide and zasocitinib, Amitiza appeal [CLM-005017] [CLM-005016] [CLM-005035] [CLM-014048].
- All four: Medicare negotiation rounds and government pricing agreements [CLM-008015] [CLM-008037].

## 11. Cross-company capital deployment, FY2025 (as filed; do not sum across rows)

| | Lilly (USD m) | J&J (USD m) | AbbVie (USD m) | Takeda (JPY bn) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Capex | 7,841 [CLM-000172] | 4,832 [CLM-000110] | 1,214 [CLM-000045] | 426.9 including intangibles [CLM-005007]; PP&E-only FY2024 200.8 [CLM-000234] |
| Cash for business acquisitions | 661 [CLM-000192] | 17,541 [CLM-000122] | 204 [CLM-000060] | none significant [CLM-009087] |
| Acquired IPR&D | 2,910 expense; 3,008 cash [CLM-000182] [CLM-000177] | not extracted | 5,016 XBRL; 4,808 10-K table [CLM-000050] [CLM-003045] | not extracted |
| R&D | 13,337 [CLM-000147] | 14,665 [CLM-000085] | 9,096 [CLM-000015] | 675.9 [CLM-005004] |

Basis differences (expense vs cash, business combination vs asset acquisition, US GAAP vs IFRS) make cross-column totals invalid [CLM-009095] [CLM-009098].

## 12. Companion files

[competitive_capability_matrix.md](competitive_capability_matrix.md), [five_year_timeline_comparison.md](five_year_timeline_comparison.md), [pipeline_and_revenue_dependence.md](pipeline_and_revenue_dependence.md), [rd_investment_and_productivity.md](rd_investment_and_productivity.md), [data_ai_maturity_matrix.md](data_ai_maturity_matrix.md), [robotics_deployment_comparison.md](robotics_deployment_comparison.md), [partner_ecosystem_comparison.md](partner_ecosystem_comparison.md), [loe_resilience_comparison.md](loe_resilience_comparison.md), [commercial_capabilities_comparison.md](commercial_capabilities_comparison.md), [strengths_and_vulnerabilities.md](strengths_and_vulnerabilities.md), [lessons_for_takeda.md](lessons_for_takeda.md), [evidence_gaps.md](evidence_gaps.md).

# Partner and deal ecosystem comparison

Cutoff 2026-11-21. Source base: A9 deal inventory, outcome scorecard, external-innovation machinery and graph edges, plus A14 gap-fill terms. Amounts are shown on the basis the source states (announced total, consideration transferred, net of cash acquired, expensed IPR&D, upfront). **Amounts on different bases are never added or ranked** (section 4). Takeda's deal amounts are in USD where Takeda states them in USD, otherwise in JPY as filed [CLM-009076] [CLM-009086].

## 1. What is established

### 1.1 Deal shape by company *(classification is analyst interpretation)*

| Company | Dominant shape in the window | Largest items on a stated basis | Platform or ecosystem layer | Claims |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lilly | Early-stage asset purchases expensed as acquired IPR&D, capability purchases as business combinations, and a 2025-26 data and compute layer | Morphic: USD 2,548.5m IPR&D charge (USD 3.2bn headline); DICE: USD 1,915.5m; Scorpion: USD 1,412m; POINT: about USD 1.0bn net of cash | Catalyze360 (Ventures, Gateway Labs, ExploR&D) and TuneLab; NVIDIA co-innovation lab (announced, up to USD 1bn jointly) | [CLM-009095] [CLM-009001] [CLM-009002] [CLM-014058] [CLM-009011] [CLM-009006] [CLM-009025] [CLM-009029] |
| J&J | A few large commercial or late-stage acquisitions plus smaller platform buys | Abiomed USD 17.1bn net of cash (plus a CVR of up to USD 35 per share); Intra-Cellular about USD 14.5bn; Shockwave USD 12.6bn (USD 11.5bn net) | JLABS and JJDC, "150+ partnerships" claimed by J&J | [CLM-009096] [CLM-002009] [CLM-002013] [CLM-009033] [CLM-009050] |
| AbbVie | Two large purchases plus a steady stream of USD 130m to 2.1bn early-stage buys and option licences | ImmunoGen USD 9.8bn consideration (10.1bn announced, 9.2bn net of cash); Cerevel USD 8.7bn (8.3bn net); Capstan USD 2.1bn (1.9bn net) | AbbVie Ventures (founding date unresolved: 2009 vs about 2015) and BaseLaunch membership | [CLM-009097] [CLM-003053] [CLM-014035] [CLM-014030] [CLM-009074] [CLM-009094] |
| Takeda | One flagship asset purchase, then licences and options, divestitures and write-offs; Takeda states no significant acquisitions in the years to March 2024, 2025 and 2026 | Nimbus USD 4.0bn upfront plus two USD 1.0bn sales milestones; Innovent USD 1.2bn including USD 100m equity (up to USD 11.4bn total) | Center for External Innovation on the BaseLaunch board (aggregator says Takeda Ventures sits under it); Takeda Ventures, Inc. is a 100%-owned subsidiary with no disclosed fund size | [CLM-009098] [CLM-009087] [CLM-005036] [CLM-009078] [CLM-009091] [CLM-009092] [CLM-014052] |

### 1.2 Graph inventory counts (coverage, not a census)

The A9 ecosystem graph holds 49 evidence-linked edges: Lilly 12, J&J 10, AbbVie 18, Takeda 9. These counts show how many dealings A9 could evidence from filings and releases; they are not counts of each company's deals. J&J's 10-Ks list few licences with disclosed values, and Takeda's evidenced licence terms are thin, so the counts understate both [CLM-009049] [CLM-009087]. One edge value (Lilly-Morphic, 3,200) uses the headline figure rather than the audited charge, so the edge values must not be summed [CLM-009002].

### 1.3 Which deals produced approved products or written-down assets

| Company | Approved or marketed product from a window or lookback deal | Written down or terminated | Claims |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lilly | Loxo (USD 6.92bn, 2019): Retevmo (2020) and Jaypirca (approved 2023; first-line CLL/SLL 2026-10-02). None of the 2023-2025 IPR&D-expensed assets was approved in the sources reviewed | DICE DC-806 discontinued 2024 (USD 1,916m charge); Prevail GBA1 impaired 2022; Vitrakvi impaired 2024 | [CLM-009014] [CLM-009015] [CLM-009003] [CLM-009009] [CLM-009016] |
| J&J | Momenta: nipocalimab (IMAAVY) approved 2025-04-30 (2020 deal); Intra-Cellular: CAPLYTA MDD indication approved about nine months after close | Auris/OTTAVA USD 0.9bn partial impairment (FY2021); bermekimab about USD 0.8bn; M710 about USD 0.2bn in each of 2023 and 2024; Laminar pivotal study suspended 2025 | [CLM-009044] [CLM-009030] [CLM-009031] [CLM-009047] [CLM-009046] [CLM-009045] [CLM-009039] [CLM-009040] |
| AbbVie | ImmunoGen: Elahere marketed (USD 578m revenue and a USD 682m operating loss in the first partial year; U.S. USD 607m in 2025); Genmab epcoritamab marketed; Cerevel's tavapadon approved as Juvmo 2026-09-25 | Cerevel emraclidine failed, USD 4.5bn impairment (54% of the USD 8.3bn net price *(computed)*) | [CLM-009056] [CLM-003036] [CLM-009072] [CLM-012017] [CLM-009054] |
| Takeda | HUTCHMED: Fruzaqla approved 2023-11-08; Protagonist: rusfertide (Mimrylo) approved 2026-08-28; Nimbus: zasocitinib Phase 3 positive, NDA accepted 2026-09-14 | Maverick JPY 27.8bn, soticlestat JPY 21.5bn, gamma-delta T-cell platform JPY 58.2bn; Denali ended April 2026; Neurocrine TAK-041/831 terminated | [CLM-009082] [CLM-012018] [CLM-012020] [CLM-005035] [CLM-009083] [CLM-009084] [CLM-009100] [CLM-009088] [CLM-009093] |

Patterns in the A9 scorecard *(INTERPRETATION)*: value destruction concentrates in neuroscience (Cerevel), gene and cell therapy (Prevail, gamma-delta T-cell) and robotics (Auris); speed from deal to approval ranged from about nine months (a new indication for Intra-Cellular's CAPLYTA) to about five years (Momenta) [CLM-009100] [CLM-009031] [CLM-009044].

### 1.4 Option-style and contingent structures

| Company | Structure | Terms on stated basis | Outcome evidence | Claims |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AbbVie | ADARx option licence; Calico option; Gubra amylin licence; Ichnos licence | ADARx USD 335m upfront, up to USD 385m plus USD 7.5bn; Gubra USD 350m upfront and up to USD 1.875bn; Ichnos USD 700m upfront and up to USD 1.2bn; Calico USD 500m (AbbVie share) with an option after Phase 2a | none beyond early stage | [CLM-009061] [CLM-009062] [CLM-009060] [CLM-009068] [CLM-003073] |
| Lilly | Beam opt-in; CVRs in Prevail, Akouos and Verve deals | Beam opt-in USD 216.3m (2023); CVRs up to about USD 160m, 122m and 300m | GBA1 asset impaired; Verve clinical | [CLM-014058] [CLM-009099] [CLM-009008] [CLM-009007] [CLM-009010] |
| J&J | Abiomed CVR; Laminar milestone; V-Wave contingent consideration | CVR of up to USD 35.00 per share, of which one milestone pays USD 17.50 if Abiomed net sales exceed USD 3.7bn in fiscal Q2 2027 to Q1 2028 (USD 8.75 if met later); V-Wave up to about USD 1.1bn further milestones | Abiomed CVR liability reduced in 2025 | [CLM-002009] [CLM-009041] [CLM-009042] [CLM-009038] [CLM-009040] |
| Takeda | Nimbus milestones; Innovent option and equity; Ascentage option | Nimbus two USD 1.0bn milestones at USD 4.0bn and USD 5.0bn annual net sales; Innovent up to USD 11.4bn total | Innovent assets in Phase 3; closed around December 2025 | [CLM-005036] [CLM-009078] [CLM-009079] [CLM-009088] |

## 2. Which partnerships create durable options

Durable here means the structure leaves the company with a right but not an obligation, over several years, at bounded upfront cost. On the evidence:
- AbbVie has the most option-type structures in the audited record, and its yearly early-stage upfronts run at USD 0.6bn to 1.0bn [CLM-009097] [CLM-009069].
- Takeda's Innovent arrangement combines a licence, equity and an option at USD 1.2bn upfront [CLM-009078].
- No option from the window has yet produced an approved product or an independent outcome, so durability is a *(HYPOTHESIS)* for all four companies.
- Lilly's only data-for-access structure (TuneLab) creates an option on partner data and models, with no uptake result [CLM-009026] [CLM-014056].

## 3. External-innovation machinery (venture and incubation arms)

- Lilly: Catalyze360 bundles Lilly Ventures, Gateway Labs, ExploR&D and TuneLab; a USD 500m a16z fund is Lilly-funded; no stand-alone Lilly Ventures fund size was found; the CEO describes Gateway Labs as hosting "scale ups, not startups" and as an experiment that "may not work" [CLM-009025] [CLM-014063] [CLM-014068].
- J&J: JLABS was planned in 2016 at six sites with capacity for 225 companies; by August 2025 11 sites were active after exits from Toronto, Houston and Washington D.C., and a snippet says New York is closing, which would leave San Diego, San Francisco and Boston; no JJDC portfolio count is in primary sources [CLM-009051] [CLM-014064] [CLM-014065] [CLM-014066].
- AbbVie: AbbVie Ventures' founding is 2009 or about 2015 depending on the source (unresolved), and one source is sponsored content [CLM-009074] [CLM-009075].
- Takeda: no fund size or Center for External Innovation description in primary sources [CLM-014052].

## 4. Comparison validity

- **Deal values are not comparable across companies.** The registry holds announced totals, consideration transferred, net-of-cash amounts, expensed IPR&D and upfronts for different deals. Examples: ImmunoGen 10.1 / 9.8 / 9.2bn; Morphic 3.2 / 2.55 / 3.35bn; Lilly IPR&D expense 2,910m versus cash paid 3,008m for FY2025 [CLM-003053] [CLM-009002] [CLM-000182] [CLM-000177].
- **US GAAP versus IFRS.** Asset acquisitions are expensed as acquired IPR&D at Lilly and AbbVie, so the same economic purchase appears as R&D expense for them; whether Takeda capitalises is not established (gap) [CLM-009095] [CLM-009098].
- **Deal count is not capability.** A9's own tables count rows, and for Takeda eight rows meet its target only by counting write-offs and divestitures [CLM-009098].
- **Contract-term completeness differs.** Lilly and AbbVie terms come from audited notes; J&J and Takeda licence terms are thin or undisclosed [CLM-009049] [CLM-009087].

## 5. What is contested and unknown

- Contested: Morphic headline versus charge; AbbVie Ventures founding date [CLM-009002] [CLM-009074].
- Unknown: revenue realised per acquisition beyond year one (Impella, Shockwave, Elahere), NM26 early-termination direction, venture-arm fund sizes for all four companies [CLM-009042] [CLM-009037] [CLM-014066].

reports.title: Pipeline and revenue dependence
reports.markdown:
# Pipeline and revenue dependence

Cutoff 2026-11-21. FY2025 = Lilly and AbbVie calendar 2025; J&J 52 weeks ended 2025-12-28 [CLM-002005]; Takeda April 2025 to March 2026 [CLM-005000]. Shares are within-company ratios and need no currency conversion. *(computed)* means arithmetic on the cited claims.

## 1. What is established

### 1.1 Concentration in FY2025 revenue

| Measure | Lilly | J&J | AbbVie | Takeda |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | USD 65,179m [CLM-000239] | USD 94,193m [CLM-000253] | USD 61,160m [CLM-000262] | JPY 4,505.7bn [CLM-005000] |
| Largest single brand and share | Mounjaro USD 22,965m, 35.2% *(computed)* [CLM-000240] | DARZALEX USD 14,351m, 15.2% [CLM-002073] | Skyrizi USD 17,562m, 28.7% *(computed)* [CLM-000264] | ENTYVIO JPY 958.0bn, 21% [CLM-005009] |
| Largest molecule or franchise and share | Tirzepatide (Mounjaro + Zepbound) USD 36,507m, 56.0% [CLM-001003] [CLM-000242] | Four myeloma brands USD 17,371m, 18.4% [CLM-002072] | Skyrizi + Rinvoq USD 25,866m, 42.3% *(computed)* [CLM-000266] | ENTYVIO plus immunoglobulin brand group (three brands) JPY 1,748.6bn, 38.8% *(computed)* [CLM-005009] |
| Prior-year anchor for the same franchise | Tirzepatide 36.6% in FY2024, 15.6% in FY2023 [CLM-001003] | STELARA 6.5% of FY2025 revenue, falling [CLM-000254] | Skyrizi + Humira + Rinvoq about 47% of 2024 revenue [CLM-003046] | Growth & Launch Products 43%, 48%, 51% of revenue in FY2023-FY2025 (company category) [CLM-005008] |
| Geographic dependence on the U.S. | 66.7% of revenue *(computed)* [CLM-000239] | 57% [CLM-002033] | Skyrizi U.S. share 86.6% *(computed)*; company-wide U.S. share not extracted (gap) [CLM-000264] | About 48%, down from about 52% in FY2024 [CLM-005002] |

Reading *(INTERPRETATION)*: Lilly is the most concentrated by a wide margin, and its concentration rose from 15.6% to 56.0% in two years [CLM-001003]. AbbVie's concentration moved from one franchise (Humira, 36.6% of 2022 revenue) to another (Skyrizi + Rinvoq, 42.3%) rather than diversifying [CLM-003004] [CLM-000266]. J&J has the lowest single-brand dependence and the most segment diversification (Innovative Medicine plus MedTech) [CLM-000253]. Takeda's single-brand share is similar to AbbVie's and J&J's top brand but its top-two product groups together hold 38.8% *(computed)* [CLM-005009]. The "top franchise" rows use different groupings (molecule, indication cluster, brand group), so the second row is a descriptive comparison, not a like-for-like index.

### 1.2 Medicare-negotiation scope of FY2025 revenue (descriptive upper bound)

| Company | Products selected (price year) | Summed FY2025 sales of those products | Share of FY2025 revenue | Claims |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lilly | Jardiance via collaboration (2026), Trulicity and Verzenio (2028) | Trulicity USD 4,276m + Verzenio USD 5,723m = USD 9,999m; Jardiance collaboration revenue not extracted | at least 15.3% *(computed)* | [CLM-008021] [CLM-000243] [CLM-000244] |
| J&J | Stelara and Xarelto (2026, deselected from 2027), Imbruvica (2026), Erleada (2028) | Stelara 6,078 + Erleada 3,574 + Imbruvica 2,823 = USD 12,475m; Xarelto sales not extracted | at least 13.2% *(computed)* | [CLM-008008] [CLM-008011] [CLM-008015] [CLM-002024] [CLM-000254] |
| AbbVie | Imbruvica (2026), Vraylar and Linzess (2027), Botox (2028) | Imbruvica 2,869 + Vraylar 3,621 + Botox Therapeutic 3,769 + Botox Cosmetic 2,602 = USD 12,861m; Linzess not extracted | at least 21.0% *(computed)* | [CLM-003080] [CLM-003025] [CLM-003028] [CLM-003030] [CLM-003031] |
| Takeda | Entyvio (2028) | JPY 958.0bn | 21% | [CLM-008022] [CLM-005009] |

Validity: the table sums global sales of selected brands, but the negotiated price applies only to Medicare Part D or Part B spending. It shows revenue in scope, not revenue lost. J&J's Imbruvica figure is J&J's reported sales of a product AbbVie also reports, so the two columns must not be added [CLM-002024] [CLM-003025]. Price-impact estimates are not possible from the registry (gap) [CLM-008017].

### 1.3 Late-stage pipeline and replacement evidence

| Company | Novel (CDER) approvals Nov 2021 to Nov 2026 | Late-stage evidence relevant to replacement | Claims |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lilly | 8: Mounjaro, Jaypirca, Omvoh, Kisunla, Ebglyss, Inluriyo, Foundayo, Onswik | Orforglipron approved 2026-04-01; retatrutide Phase 3 TRIUMPH-1 published November 2026 with 25.0% weight reduction at 12 mg versus 3.9% placebo; outcomes trials run to 2029-2031. Most Phase 3 assets extend the incretin franchise, so the risk is concentration, not shortage of products | [CLM-012000] [CLM-012001] [CLM-012002] [CLM-012003] [CLM-012004] [CLM-012005] [CLM-012006] [CLM-012007] [CLM-001030] [CLM-001060] [CLM-012047] [CLM-001045] [CLM-012124] |
| J&J | 5: Tecvayli, Talvey, Lazcluze, Imaavy, Icotyde | Icotyde approved 2026-03-17 as an oral IL-23 successor to Stelara and Tremfya; bispecific and CAR-T lifecycle trials to 2031; adequacy of replacement cannot be sized without forecasts | [CLM-012008] [CLM-012009] [CLM-012010] [CLM-012011] [CLM-012012] [CLM-002065] [CLM-012065] |
| AbbVie | 5: Elahere (sponsor ImmunoGen), Epkinly (sponsor Genmab), Emrelis, Decnupaz, Juvmo | 2022-2025 growth came from Skyrizi and Rinvoq supplemental indications; novel approvals are smaller in revenue so far (Elahere U.S. USD 607m, Vyalev USD 482m in 2025) | [CLM-012013] [CLM-012014] [CLM-012015] [CLM-012016] [CLM-012017] [CLM-012033] [CLM-012036] [CLM-003036] [CLM-003037] |
| Takeda | 3: Fruzaqla, Orzeyful, Mimrylo | Two approvals in August 2026 and a zasocitinib NDA under Priority Review accepted 2026-09-14; company-stated USD 10-20bn combined peak range for six programmes is unrisked | [CLM-012018] [CLM-012019] [CLM-012020] [CLM-005029] [CLM-005032] [CLM-005035] [CLM-005041] [CLM-014049] |

## 2. Replacement-cohort revenue: a defined metric and why it is only partly computable

**Metric.** FY2025 revenue from molecules first approved by the FDA after 2021-11-21 as a share of FY2025 revenue (the "window cohort"). It measures how much current revenue comes from newly approved molecules.

| Company | Window-cohort revenue found in the registry | Share (lower bound) | Why it is a lower bound |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lilly | Mounjaro + Zepbound USD 36,507m [CLM-001003]; Kisunla USD 484m, Foundayo USD 281m (nine months 2026, not FY2025) [CLM-001032] | at least 56.0% of FY2025 revenue *(computed)* | Omvoh, Ebglyss, Jaypirca, Inluriyo FY2025 revenues were not extracted |
| J&J | Carvykti 1,887 + Tecvayli 670 + Talvey 463 = USD 3,020m [CLM-002024] | at least 3.2% *(computed)* | Imaavy, Inlexzo, Akeega and Rybrevant/Lazcluze components were not separable; Carvykti is licensed with a partner |
| AbbVie | Elahere U.S. USD 607m (global grew 43%) + Vyalev USD 482m [CLM-003036] [CLM-003037] | at least 1.8% *(computed)* | Epkinly revenue share and Emrelis not extracted; Skyrizi and Rinvoq were approved before the window and are not in the cohort even though they drive 42.3% of revenue |
| Takeda | none in FY2025; first approvals August 2026; Entyvio SC pen is a new presentation of an older molecule [CLM-012029] [CLM-012030] | not computable | Fruzaqla and Qdenga FY2025 sales not extracted (Qdenga JPY 40.8bn is approved outside the U.S. cohort definition) [CLM-005045] |

**Comparison status.** The metric is invalid as a ranking of R&D productivity because it favours companies whose growth comes from new molecules (Lilly) and penalises companies whose growth comes from lifecycle expansion of older molecules (AbbVie's Skyrizi and Rinvoq, J&J's Tremfya) [CLM-012147] [CLM-002053]. It is reported only to show that Lilly's recent revenue growth depends on a molecule approved inside the window while AbbVie's depends on molecules approved before it *(INTERPRETATION)*.

## 3. What is contested

- Whether Lilly's concentration is a vulnerability or the intended outcome: Lilly's CEO said GLP-1s are "probably 80% of the economic value" and framed R&D investment around that [CLM-014067]; the 10-K lists concentration, price concessions and IRA exposure as risks [CLM-001017] [CLM-001027].
- Whether Q3 2026 growth at Lilly is repeatable: Q3 2026 revenue included about USD 900m of one-off benefits and realized prices fell 15% while volume rose 53% [CLM-014003].

## 4. What is unknown

- Product-level revenue for Omvoh, Ebglyss, Jaypirca, Inluriyo, Imaavy, Icotyde, Epkinly, Fruzaqla (gap).
- Probability-adjusted peak sales for any pipeline asset; Takeda's range is explicitly unrisked [CLM-014049].
- A like-for-like count of Phase 3 assets: A12's snapshot lists 10 Lilly, 8 J&J, 6 AbbVie and 8 Takeda registry records, but the selection was curated rather than a census, so the counts are not a comparison of pipeline depth [CLM-012046] [CLM-012059] [CLM-012068] [CLM-012077].

reports.title: R&D investment and productivity: what can and cannot be compared
reports.markdown:
# R&D investment and productivity: what can and cannot be compared

Cutoff 2026-11-21. Periods: Lilly and AbbVie calendar years; J&J 52-week fiscal years (FY2021 ended 2022-01-02, FY2025 ended 2025-12-28) [CLM-002005]; Takeda fiscal years ending 31 March, so Takeda "FY2021" is April 2021 to March 2022 [CLM-005000]. Amounts stay in each company's reporting currency (USD m for Lilly, J&J, AbbVie; JPY bn for Takeda). No FX conversion is applied. Ratios to revenue are currency-neutral. *(computed)* marks arithmetic on cited claims.

## 1. What is established

### 1.1 R&D expense as reported

| | FY2021 | FY2022 | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 | Claims |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lilly (USD m, excludes acquired IPR&D) | 6,930.7 | 7,190.8 | 9,313.4 | 10,990.6 | 13,337 | [CLM-000143] [CLM-000144] [CLM-000145] [CLM-000146] [CLM-000147] |
| J&J (USD m, total company, includes MedTech) | 14,714 | 14,603 | 15,085 | 17,232 | 14,665 | [CLM-000081] [CLM-000082] [CLM-000083] [CLM-000084] [CLM-000085] |
| AbbVie (USD m, includes intangible impairments, excludes acquired IPR&D) | 7,084 | 6,510 | 7,675 | 12,791 | 9,096 | [CLM-000011] [CLM-000012] [CLM-000013] [CLM-000014] [CLM-000015] [CLM-000270] |
| Takeda (JPY bn, IFRS) | 526.1 | 633.3 | 729.9 | 730.2 | 675.9 | [CLM-005004] |

### 1.2 R&D as a share of revenue *(computed from the cited revenue and R&D claims)*

| | FY2021 | FY2025 | Direction | Revenue claims |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lilly | 24.5% | 20.5% | down 4.0 points while revenue rose 2.3 times | [CLM-001006] [CLM-000133] [CLM-000137] |
| J&J | 15.7% | 15.6% | flat; FY2021 denominator includes Consumer Health | [CLM-000071] [CLM-000075] |
| AbbVie | 12.6% | 14.9% | up 2.3 points; 2024 was 22.7% (12,791 of 56,334) *(computed)* | [CLM-000001] [CLM-000005] [CLM-000004] |
| Takeda | 14.7% | 15.0% | flat; FY2025 R&D fell 7.4% as programmes ended | [CLM-000203] [CLM-005000] [CLM-005004] |

J&J segment split for FY2025: Innovative Medicine R&D USD 11,827m (19.6% of segment sales) and MedTech USD 2,838m (8.4%), so the group ratio understates pharma R&D intensity [CLM-002004]. A pharma-only intensity across the four companies would put J&J's Innovative Medicine at 19.6% against Lilly 20.5%, AbbVie 14.9% and Takeda 15.0%, but only J&J discloses the split and AbbVie's and Takeda's totals include non-pharma items to an unknown degree (gap) [CLM-002004].

### 1.3 External innovation spending (acquired IPR&D and business acquisitions), on its stated basis

| Company | Acquired IPR&D, FY2023 / FY2024 / FY2025 | Basis | Cash paid for business acquisitions FY2024 / FY2025 | Claims |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lilly | 3,799.8 / 3,280.4 / 2,910.0 (expense) | US GAAP expense line, asset acquisitions | 947.7 / 661.0 | [CLM-000180] [CLM-000181] [CLM-000182] [CLM-000191] [CLM-000192] |
| Lilly (same programmes, cash view) | 3,944.5 / 3,345.8 / 3,008.0 | cash paid for acquired IPR&D in asset acquisitions | n/a | [CLM-001014] [CLM-000175] [CLM-000176] [CLM-000177] |
| AbbVie | 778 / 2,757 / 5,016 (XBRL tag as filed); the 10-K table shows 582 / 2,627 / 4,808 for "acquired IPR&D and milestones" | two different tabulations; the 208m difference in 2025 is unexplained (gap) | 0 / 17,493 / 204 | [CLM-000048] [CLM-000049] [CLM-000050] [CLM-003045] [CLM-000058] [CLM-000059] [CLM-000060] |
| J&J | not extracted for FY2023-FY2025; 900 (FY2021) and 783 (FY2022) | XBRL tag; later years sit inside R&D or other lines (gap) | 15,146 / 17,541 | [CLM-000111] [CLM-000112] [CLM-000121] [CLM-000122] [CLM-009049] |
| Takeda | no acquired-IPR&D expense line was extracted | IFRS; whether licence upfronts are capitalised as intangible assets is not established in the registry (gap) | Takeda states no significant acquisitions of businesses or assets in the years to March 2024, 2025 and 2026 | [CLM-009087] [CLM-009098] |

Basis traps that the audit already identified, applied here:
- Lilly's Morphic deal is USD 3.2bn as a headline (Reuters), USD 2,548.5m as the audited IPR&D charge and USD 3.35bn as the 2024 cash paid for acquired IPR&D, "primarily Morphic". These are different measures, not a contradiction [CLM-009001] [CLM-009002].
- Lilly's FY2021 acquired IPR&D is 874.9 in the FY2021 10-K and 970.1 in the FY2022 10-K and in the XBRL series, because the FY2022 line item was widened to include development milestones (+95.2). The series in section 1.3 uses 970.1 for FY2021 [CLM-009022] [CLM-000178].
- AbbVie's ImmunoGen is USD 10.1bn announced total value, USD 9.8bn consideration transferred and USD 9.2bn net of cash acquired; the USD 18.5bn for ImmunoGen plus Cerevel is consideration transferred, USD 17.5bn net of cash acquired, not "cash paid" [CLM-003053] [CLM-003086].
- AbbVie's XBRL net income is consolidated (including non-controlling interest) while the A4 shard series is attributable to AbbVie; the two differ by 7 to 10m a year. Net income is not used in this file [CLM-000026] [CLM-004108].
- J&J FY2021 segment sales were later recast (Pharmaceutical 52,080 → 51,680; Consumer Health 14,635 → 15,035), and Consumer Health was later discontinued, so J&J total revenue FY2021 (93,775) is not comparable with FY2025 (94,193) [CLM-002000] [CLM-002001] [CLM-002002].

### 1.4 Approvals, setbacks and impairments in the same window

| Company | CDER novel approvals Nov 2021 to Nov 2026 | Audited write-downs tied to window-era purchases or programmes | Claims |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lilly | 8 | Prevail GBA1 charges USD 244.6m; Vitrakvi impairment (amount not extracted); DICE DC-806 discontinued after a USD 1,916m charge | [CLM-012000] [CLM-012007] [CLM-009009] [CLM-001013] [CLM-009003] |
| J&J | 5 | Bermekimab about USD 0.8bn (FY2022); Auris/OTTAVA partial impairment USD 0.9bn (FY2021, lookback deal); M710 impairments about USD 0.2bn each in 2023 and 2024; IPR&D impairments of USD 313m, 211m and 81m in FY2023-FY2025 | [CLM-012008] [CLM-012012] [CLM-002020] [CLM-009047] [CLM-009045] [CLM-002031] |
| AbbVie | 5 | Emraclidine USD 4.5bn in Q4 2024 (54% of the USD 8.3bn Cerevel net price *(computed)*); Imbruvica USD 2.1bn after IRA selection; CoolSculpting and Liletta USD 1.4bn; total intangible impairments USD 4,229m, 4,476m and 847m in 2023-2025 | [CLM-012013] [CLM-012017] [CLM-003057] [CLM-009054] [CLM-003026] [CLM-003035] [CLM-003059] |
| Takeda | 3 | ALOFISEL JPY 74.0bn and EXKIVITY JPY 28.5bn (FY2023); Maverick JPY 27.8bn; soticlestat JPY 21.5bn; cell-therapy platform JPY 58.2bn recognised in FY2025 (JPY 58.0bn was the October 2025 estimate) | [CLM-012018] [CLM-012020] [CLM-005022] [CLM-009083] [CLM-009084] [CLM-009100] [CLM-005025] |

The cell-therapy figure follows the audit correction: JPY 58.0bn was the 1 October 2025 expectation, JPY 58.2bn is the amount recognised in the FY2025 20-F [CLM-005025] [CLM-009100].

## 2. Defined metrics and their validity

| Metric | Definition | Computable for | Valid for ranking? |
|---|---|---|---|
| M1 R&D intensity | R&D expense ÷ revenue, as reported | all four (section 1.2) | **Partly.** Currency-neutral, but R&D definitions differ (AbbVie includes impairments; J&J includes MedTech; Lilly excludes acquired IPR&D; Takeda IFRS). Use for direction of travel, not level |
| M2 Window-cohort revenue share | FY2025 revenue of molecules first approved after 2021-11-21 ÷ FY2025 revenue | lower bounds for Lilly, J&J, AbbVie; not for Takeda | **No.** Penalises lifecycle growth (see [pipeline_and_revenue_dependence.md](pipeline_and_revenue_dependence.md)) |
| M3 Write-down ratio | audited impairment ÷ net price of the acquisition it relates to | AbbVie emraclidine only (54%) | **No.** One data point; other companies' window-era impairments have different bases (programme-level, not deal-level) |
| M4 Novel approvals ÷ cumulative R&D | approvals counted 2021-11 to 2026-11 against R&D 2022-2025 | counts exist; ratio rejected | **No**, see below |

**Why M4 is rejected.** (1) The approval window runs to November 2026 and includes seven approvals dated 2026 (Lilly's Foundayo and Onswik, J&J's Icotyde, AbbVie's Decnupaz and Juvmo, Takeda's Orzeyful and Mimrylo) that were funded largely by spending before and after the 2022-2025 window rather than by that spend alone [CLM-012006] [CLM-012007] [CLM-012012] [CLM-012016] [CLM-012017] [CLM-012019] [CLM-012020]. (2) Counts of 3 to 8 per company are too small for a ratio to mean more than noise *(INTERPRETATION)*. (3) The FDA novel list omits sponsor, and the sponsor of record for Jaypirca is Loxo Oncology, for Elahere ImmunoGen and for Epkinly Genmab, so some approvals are acquired or partnered assets rather than outputs of the acquirer's R&D spend [CLM-012001] [CLM-012013] [CLM-012014]. (4) AbbVie's revenue growth in the window rests on supplemental indications for Skyrizi and Rinvoq, not on novel approvals [CLM-012033] [CLM-012036]. (5) J&J's R&D includes MedTech, whose output is device clearances, not drug approvals [CLM-002004] [CLM-014026]. (6) Takeda's FY ends in March and its R&D is in JPY.

**Cumulative R&D over the four most recent fiscal years, for scale only** *(computed)*: Lilly USD 40.8bn, J&J USD 61.6bn, AbbVie USD 36.1bn (includes USD 4.5bn of impairment charged to R&D) and Takeda JPY 2,769bn. These cannot be set against each other without an FX basis and are listed only to show order of magnitude [CLM-000144] [CLM-000145] [CLM-000146] [CLM-000147] [CLM-000082] [CLM-000083] [CLM-000084] [CLM-000085] [CLM-000012] [CLM-000013] [CLM-000014] [CLM-000015] [CLM-005004] [CLM-003057].

## 3. Profit margins: comparison invalid as a ranking

- Lilly pre-tax income was 39.5% of FY2025 revenue (21.7% in FY2021) [CLM-001007].
- J&J pre-tax income USD 32,581m on USD 94,193m is 34.6% *(computed)*, but FY2025 benefited from reversal of about USD 7bn of talc reserve, and FY2024 pre-tax income was USD 16,687m (18.8%) after large litigation charges [CLM-000261] [CLM-002016] [CLM-000116] [CLM-000074].
- AbbVie pre-tax income USD 6,597m is 10.8% *(computed)*, depressed by USD 7.4bn amortisation and a USD 6.5bn change in fair value of contingent consideration [CLM-000055] [CLM-003040] [CLM-003041].
- Takeda reported operating profit fell to JPY 6.2bn after a JPY 403.5bn Amitiza provision; Core Operating Profit (company non-IFRS) was JPY 1,172.5bn, 26.0% of revenue *(computed)* [CLM-000272] [CLM-000273] [CLM-005014].

These are four different accounting bases (US GAAP with and without special items, IFRS with a company-defined core measure), so no margin ranking is offered *(INTERPRETATION)*.

## 4. What is contested

- Whether Lilly's falling R&D intensity reflects scale (denominator growth) or restraint: R&D spend itself roughly doubled (USD 6.9bn to 13.3bn), so the ratio fell because revenue grew faster [CLM-001006] [CLM-000143] [CLM-000147].
- Whether AbbVie's 2024 R&D peak is a research-spend signal: USD 4.5bn of it is an impairment [CLM-003057] [CLM-000270].

## 5. What is unknown

- Internal development cycle time, probability of success and cost per trial for any company; these are on Takeda's validation backlog (IVB-009) and absent for the competitors [CLM-005042].
- Lilly's own productivity metrics (A1 listed this as a gap) [CLM-001006].
- Whether Takeda's licence and acquisition spend sits in R&D, capitalised intangibles or both (gap) [CLM-009098].

reports.title: Robotics and automation deployment comparison
reports.markdown:
# Robotics and automation deployment comparison

Cutoff 2026-11-21. "Robotics" covers three different things in the registry, and the companies are active in different ones. They are compared within a category only. Maturity values follow the A6 scale with the A10 retags applied (see [data_ai_maturity_matrix.md](data_ai_maturity_matrix.md)) [CLM-000284] [CLM-006026].

## 1. Category A: robotics sold as products (surgical and interventional)

Only J&J operates in this category. No Lilly, AbbVie or Takeda product-robotics evidence was found [CLM-006053].

| System | Regulatory record | Commercial and clinical evidence | Maturity | Claims |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| OTTAVA (table-integrated soft-tissue robot) | IDE approval announced 2024-11-12; first IDE cases early 2025 at Memorial Hermann-TMC; De Novo request received 2025-12-18; De Novo DEN250068 granted 2026-07-21 per the FDA record (J&J's release says 2026-07-22), Class II, upper-abdominal general laparoscopic procedures | J&J announced Memorial Hermann-TMC as the first hospital to install OTTAVA under an early-access commercial programme (announcement on 2026-11-19); completion of the installation is not shown. No revenue, unit-sale, order-book or clinical-superiority figure is disclosed. IDE operating rooms were as small as 243 sq ft, from a user survey of n=20 | **pilot** (A6); first installation announced, not shown completed | [CLM-002048] [CLM-002049] [CLM-014022] [CLM-014023] [CLM-000283] [CLM-014024] [CLM-000284] [CLM-006028] [CLM-006029] |
| MONARCH (bronchoscopy and urology) | MONARCH QUEST 3 clearance announced 2026-08-17; openFDA lists K260382 (Auris Health, decided 2026-07-25), whose link to the QUEST 3 name is inferred; K243219 also listed | Company-sponsored single-arm TARGET study: 679 patients, 21 sites, lesion reached in 98.7% of cases; installed base undisclosed | **operational** | [CLM-006027] [CLM-014025] [CLM-002067] [CLM-000286] |
| VELYS (knee, hip, spine) | Five 510(k) clearances in openFDA: K202769 (2021-01-14), K233227 (2023-12-14), K240211 (2024-06-05), K253551 (hip navigation) and K260480 (2026-06-25); VELYS Spine clearance announced 2024-08-02 | FY2025 10-K cites "pull through" for ATTUNE knees but no system or procedure counts; Orthopaedics grew 1.1% in FY2025 | **operational** (A10 retag from scaled) | [CLM-014026] [CLM-002066] [CLM-006026] [CLM-002029] |

Read together: J&J has regulator records for three platforms and company-reported clinical data for one. It has no disclosed installed base, procedure count or revenue for any of them, so deployment *scale* cannot be compared with anyone *(INTERPRETATION)* [CLM-006054]. The OTTAVA acquisition (Auris) carried a USD 0.9bn partial impairment in FY2021 [CLM-009047]. J&J's CEO said on 2026-05-27 that the company hoped for OTTAVA approval "by the end of this year, beginning of next year", and the FDA acted earlier [CLM-014070].

The OTTAVA "about 24 months from IDE to first commercial installation" figure in the earlier J&J dossier must not be used: the installation is announced, not completed, and A10 instructs that no IDE-to-install duration be derived [CLM-000284] [CLM-002049].

Device safety events that sit beside this category but are not robotics: Varipulse U.S. cases were paused on 2025-01-05 and FDA recorded 4 of 132 patients (about 3%) with stroke or TIA against about 1% expected; Impella Class I recall covered 66,390 pumps [CLM-002044] [CLM-014018] [CLM-002046].

## 2. Category B: laboratory automation and robotic labs (R&D infrastructure)

| Company | Evidence | Maturity | Claims |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lilly | Life Sciences Studio (San Diego, remote robotic lab; start 2017 per one source, public launch about 2020 per another, USD 90m reported) was acquired by Arctoris in 2024 and moved to Oxford; the reason for divestment is undisclosed. NVIDIA-Lilly co-innovation lab (agentic wet labs linked to dry labs, up to USD 1bn over five years) announced 2026-01-12, no source shows it operating | Studio: **operational, then divested**; co-innovation lab: **concept** | [CLM-006013] [CLM-006014] [CLM-006017] [CLM-000281] [CLM-014053] |
| J&J | No lab-automation evidence found; AI image analytics on its biosignature platform is qualitative | **operational** (qualitative, self-reported) | [CLM-006024] |
