| AbbVie | BigHat pairs ML with a high-speed wet lab under its own platform, with no result yet | **prototype** | [CLM-006035] |
| Takeda | No public evidence of lab automation in the 20-F, report landing page or press; Nabla reports a three-to-four-week design-to-test loop (a company statement) | **evidence gap**; Nabla loop: **prototype** | [CLM-005067] [CLM-005080] [CLM-006040] |

Calibration: owned and venture-funded cloud-lab and biofoundry models ended in divestment or distressed sale in the cases reviewed (Lilly's studio, Zymergen sold for about USD 300m at about one-tenth of its IPO-era valuation after cumulative net losses of USD 1.2bn) [CLM-006052] [CLM-006051].

## 3. Category C: manufacturing and plant automation

| Company | Evidence | Maturity | Claims |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lilly | Lilly Lebanon Advanced Therapies (first dedicated genetic-medicine plant) opened 2026-05-06 with robotic machines that dose, measure and seal medicines, seen on a guided tour, no performance data. NVIDIA states Lilly uses robots for quality inspection and transport and plans digital twins on Omniverse, no counts. Capex rose from USD 1.3bn to USD 7.8bn (FY2021 to FY2025). Several announced sites are pre-operating: Houston (operational "within five years"), Alabama (completion 2032), Pennsylvania (operational 2031), Alzey (from 2027); only Concord NC (trade report), Kinsale and the Lebanon genetic-medicine plant show operating evidence | plant robotics: **operational** (no metrics); digital twins: **pilot** | [CLM-006002] [CLM-001041] [CLM-006006] [CLM-000168] [CLM-000172] [CLM-014008] [CLM-014009] [CLM-014010] [CLM-014012] [CLM-014014] [CLM-014015] |
| J&J | Gen-AI quality-control tool is the only manufacturing-adjacent item (see the AI matrix); no plant-robotics evidence found | n/a | [CLM-006021] |
| AbbVie | Not searched in depth; construction starts in Illinois and Massachusetts in 2025 are noted without automation detail | gap | [CLM-003082] |
| Takeda | More than 170 AI predictive-maintenance agents at Lessines; One Day Batch Release pilots at six sites with a 60% release-lead-time reduction targeted by 2028; plasma donation nomograms in 270+ centres. No continuous-manufacturing or robotics evidence found; the earlier baseline's "evidence gap" for automation is partly closed for AI-enabled maintenance, not for robotics | AI maintenance: **operational** (company report); batch release: **pilot** | [CLM-014041] [CLM-014042] [CLM-005060] [CLM-005067] |

Baseline note for Takeda: the capability baseline classes lab automation and robotics as EVIDENCE_GAP on the basis of CLM-005067; the 2026 integrated report evidence (CLM-014041, CLM-014042) post-dates that baseline and shows company-reported AI-enabled plant maintenance and a batch-release pilot. This does not change the robotics finding *(INTERPRETATION)* [CLM-005067] [CLM-014041].

## 4. Comparison validity

- Category A is a product business (revenue-bearing devices for hospitals); categories B and C are internal cost and cycle-time investments. A statement such as "J&J leads in robotics" is true only for Category A and says nothing about Lilly's or Takeda's plants *(INTERPRETATION)*.
- Within each category, maturity levels rest on company or vendor statements except the FDA device records [CLM-006054].
- Deployment scale (installed base, units, procedures, plant counts with robots) is undisclosed for every company, so no quantitative comparison is possible.

## 5. What is contested and unknown

- Contested: Lilly Studio start year and cost; Strateos fate [CLM-006014] [CLM-006015] [CLM-014057]. OTTAVA De Novo date (21 vs 22 July 2026) [CLM-014022] [CLM-000283].
- Unknown: installed bases and procedure counts for OTTAVA, MONARCH, VELYS; operating metrics for any pharma plant robotics; whether the NVIDIA lab has begun work [CLM-006029] [CLM-014053].

reports.title: Strengths and vulnerabilities by company
reports.markdown:
# Strengths and vulnerabilities by company

Cutoff 2026-11-21. "Strength" means a documented outcome or structure that distinguishes the company from at least one of the other three on evidence; it is not a score. "Vulnerability" means a documented exposure, not a prediction. Statements drawn from company releases record what the company said, not an outcome unless a filing or regulator record confirms it. Computed ratios are marked *(computed)*. Takeda is the baseline, so it is described on the same evidence rules.

## 1. Eli Lilly

**Strengths**
- Revenue grew 2.3 times between FY2021 and FY2025, from USD 28.3bn to USD 65.2bn (23.2% a year *(computed)*), against +19.6% (J&J excluding Consumer Health) and +8.8% (AbbVie) over the same years *(computed)* [CLM-000133] [CLM-000137] [CLM-002001] [CLM-000253] [CLM-000001] [CLM-000005]. J&J's like-for-like base is its FY2021 Pharmaceutical plus Medical Devices sales as recast, USD 78,740m *(computed)* [CLM-002001].
- Margin expansion alongside growth: gross margin 74.2% → 83.0%, pre-tax margin 21.7% → 39.5%, R&D intensity 24.5% → 20.5% while absolute R&D roughly doubled [CLM-001005] [CLM-001007] [CLM-001006] [CLM-000143] [CLM-000147].
- Capacity investment on a scale none of the others shows in the filed numbers: capex USD 1.3bn → 7.8bn, 12.0% of FY2025 revenue against 5.1% for J&J and 2.0% for AbbVie *(computed)* [CLM-000168] [CLM-000172] [CLM-000110] [CLM-000045].
- The only evidenced direct-to-patient cash channel and the only owned-compute and data-as-product pair among the four (outcomes not shown) [CLM-001042] [CLM-007002] [CLM-006004] [CLM-000280].
- Eight CDER novel approvals in the window, the most of the four [CLM-012000] [CLM-012007].

**Vulnerabilities**
- Concentration: tirzepatide 56.0% of FY2025 revenue, up from 15.6% in FY2023 [CLM-001003].
- Price: realised prices fell 5% in Q4 2025 and 15% in Q3 2026 while volume rose 46% and 53%; Q3 2026 included about USD 900m of one-off benefits [CLM-014004] [CLM-014003]. The 10-K lists price concessions under the November 2025 government agreement [CLM-001027].
- Payer leverage: CVS Caremark removed Zepbound for about 11 months before re-adding it [CLM-007011] [CLM-007013].
- Medicare negotiation reaches Trulicity and Verzenio (USD 9,999m of FY2025 sales in scope, at least 15.3% of revenue *(computed)*) from 2028 [CLM-008015] [CLM-000243] [CLM-000244].
- Capacity is mostly announced, not operating: of ten named sites only a few show operating evidence [CLM-014008] [CLM-014009] [CLM-014010] [CLM-014012] [CLM-014014] [CLM-014015].
- Debt rose from USD 15.3bn to USD 40.9bn (non-current) [CLM-000198] [CLM-000202].
- Litigation: 340B suits, insulin pricing multidistrict litigation, compounding [CLM-001069] [CLM-001018].
- AI and robotics programmes show no outcome; the remote robotic lab was divested [CLM-006007] [CLM-006013].

**Contested:** whether growth is repeatable given one-off Q3 2026 benefits [CLM-014003]. **Unknown:** self-pay share of Zepbound revenue; tirzepatide unit volumes [CLM-007005].

## 2. Johnson & Johnson

**Strengths**
- Most diversified revenue base: largest brand 15.2% of revenue; two operating segments of USD 60.4bn and USD 33.8bn [CLM-002073] [CLM-000253].
- Absorbed the Stelara decline (USD 10,361m → 6,078m in FY2025) while group sales grew 6.0%; excluding Stelara, sales grew about 12.3% *(computed)*, with about one point from acquisitions per J&J [CLM-000254] [CLM-000253] [CLM-002075].
- Myeloma depth: four brands total USD 17,371m, and Oncology grew 22.1% to USD 25,380m [CLM-002072] [CLM-002024].
- The only regulator records for AI-adjacent surgical robotics (OTTAVA De Novo, MONARCH 510(k), VELYS 510(k)s) [CLM-014022] [CLM-014025] [CLM-014026].
- Capacity to execute large acquisitions: USD 15.1bn (FY2024) and USD 17.5bn (FY2025) net of cash [CLM-009049].

**Vulnerabilities**
- Stelara is still falling: roughly a 690 basis-point drag on Q3 2026 Innovative Medicine growth, with CVS Caremark preferring biosimilars from July 2026 [CLM-002060] [CLM-007015].
- Talc: three bankruptcy attempts (two dismissed, one not confirmed), a USD 7.0bn charge in FY2023, a remaining reserve of about USD 3.4bn at FY2025 end, a proposed USD 5.5bn ovarian resolution (plaintiff counsel says USD 7bn or more is possible), and Q3 2026 net earnings of USD 210m after a special charge [CLM-002015] [CLM-002017] [CLM-002016] [CLM-002062] [CLM-002063] [CLM-002060].
- MedTech earns a 12.2% segment margin against 36.9% in Innovative Medicine, grew 2.5% in Q3 2026, and Orthopaedics grew 1.1% in FY2025; J&J announced the Orthopaedics separation [CLM-002004] [CLM-002060] [CLM-002029] [CLM-002037].
- Net debt rose from USD 2.1bn (FY2021) to USD 27.8bn (FY2025) after Abiomed, Shockwave, Intra-Cellular and Halda [CLM-002010] [CLM-002014].
- Device safety events: Impella Class I recall (66,390 pumps) and the Varipulse pause [CLM-002046] [CLM-002044] [CLM-014018].
- Pharma plus MedTech synergy is claimed by J&J and not evidenced in the registry; the margin gap and the separation point the other way [CLM-002074] [CLM-002004].
- Pipeline setbacks include aticaprant, the RSV vaccine, bermekimab and Laminar [CLM-002039] [CLM-002018] [CLM-002020] [CLM-009039].

**Contested:** whether Varipulse harm was device- or use-related [CLM-002045]; talc total cost [CLM-002062] [CLM-002063]. **Unknown:** installed bases of OTTAVA, MONARCH and VELYS; DARZALEX patent dates [CLM-006029].

## 3. AbbVie

**Strengths**
- Replaced a franchise that was 36.6% of 2022 revenue within three years; total revenue passed its 2022 peak in 2025 (USD 61,160m versus 58,054m) *(computed)* [CLM-003004] [CLM-003014] [CLM-003015].
- A contracting defence that kept at least 97% of adalimumab volume through March 2024 and then a co-branded Humira via Cordavis [CLM-003007] [CLM-003008].
- Settlement-based IP: no generic Rinvoq tablet expected before April 2037 [CLM-003021].
- A repeatable early-stage and option deal stream (USD 0.6-1.0bn of yearly upfronts) [CLM-009069] [CLM-009097].
- Skyrizi and Rinvoq growth continued: nine-month 2026 revenue USD 23.1bn combined; Q3 2026 revenue +10.3% [CLM-003023].

**Vulnerabilities**
- Concentration moved from Humira to Skyrizi and Rinvoq (42.3% of FY2025 revenue *(computed)*); Skyrizi biosimilar risk after 2033 has no disclosed settlement date [CLM-000266] [CLM-003021].
- Capital destroyed in neuroscience: emraclidine failed after the Cerevel deal and a USD 4.5bn impairment followed (54% of the USD 8.3bn net price *(computed)*) [CLM-003054] [CLM-003057] [CLM-009054].
- Aesthetics shrank (U.S. Botox Cosmetic -11% and Juvederm -15% in 2025), the 2029 expectation was cut from USD 9bn to north of USD 7bn, and a loyalty-programme redesign was reversed [CLM-003032] [CLM-003034] [CLM-003033].
- Four selected products face Medicare-set prices from 2026 to 2028 (at least 21.0% of FY2025 revenue in scope *(computed)*) [CLM-003080] [CLM-003025] [CLM-003028] [CLM-003030] [CLM-003031].
- GAAP earnings are depressed by amortisation (USD 7.4bn) and contingent-consideration changes (USD 6.5bn); net income was USD 4.2bn in 2025 [CLM-003040] [CLM-003041] [CLM-000030].
- Debt: USD 58.9bn non-current (USD 64.5bn including the current portion) [CLM-000070].
- Several Phase 3 setbacks (Venclexta VERONA, Epkinly overall survival, navitoclax) and device-related CRLs for ABBV-951 [CLM-012117] [CLM-012118] [CLM-012114] [CLM-012111] [CLM-012112].
- Humira antitrust class actions pending [CLM-003011].

**Contested:** causal share of the 2024 formulary change in Humira's decline [CLM-003010]. **Unknown:** Skyrizi and Rinvoq origin (licensed vs internal), AbbVie Ventures founding date, AI outcomes [CLM-009074] [CLM-006054].

## 4. Takeda (public baseline)

**Strengths**
- Plasma-derived therapies: 275 collection centres at FY2024 and immunoglobulin brands at 18% of revenue; no comparable franchise appears in the other three companies' evidence [CLM-005063] [CLM-005064] [CLM-005009].
- In-house orexin science produced oveporexton (FDA approval 2026-08-05), and the three Phase 3 readouts planned for 2025 were reported positive [CLM-005048] [CLM-005029] [CLM-005042] [CLM-005027] [CLM-005033] [CLM-005031].
- Two FDA approvals 23 days apart (August 2026) and an NDA under Priority Review for zasocitinib accepted 2026-09-14 [CLM-005029] [CLM-005032] [CLM-005035].
- Balance-sheet restraint on acquisitions: no significant acquisitions of businesses or assets in the three years to March 2026 [CLM-009087].
- Stop decisions executed despite write-down cost (cell therapy, soticlestat, ALOFISEL, EXKIVITY) [CLM-005025] [CLM-005024] [CLM-005022].

**Vulnerabilities**
- Entyvio is 21% of revenue and faces exclusivity loss in the latter half of the decade, patents to 2032, two FDA-accepted biosimilar BLAs, UK and Netherlands revocation actions, and Medicare negotiation from 2028 [CLM-005009] [CLM-005017] [CLM-014050] [CLM-014051] [CLM-008022].
- Revenue fell 1.7% (-2.7% at constant rates) in FY2025, U.S. revenue fell 9.0%, and H1 FY2026 revenue was -1.0% at constant rates; Vyvanse fell 52.0% in two years *(computed)* [CLM-005001] [CLM-005011] [CLM-005015].
- The AMITIZA verdict (USD 884.9m single damages, subject to trebling for two groups) drove a JPY 403.5bn provision and reported operating profit of JPY 6.2bn; Takeda plans to appeal [CLM-005013] [CLM-005014] [CLM-014047] [CLM-014048].
- Restructuring: about 4,500 roles affected; cost estimates of about JPY 150bn (March 2026), JPY 170.0bn (original FY2026 forecast) and JPY 160.0bn (revised, October 2026), with over JPY 200bn gross annual savings targeted by FY2028 [CLM-005078] [CLM-005059].
- TRINTELLIX generics after December 2026 [CLM-005016].
- The launch wave has to be proven: new-brand launch execution is classed POTENTIAL_NEW_CAPABILITY in the baseline; patient services, AI-enabled discovery and robotics are public-evidence gaps [CLM-005069] [CLM-005072] [CLM-005080].
- A CEO transition in June 2026 and one documented manufacturing quality failure (Hikari, 2020) [CLM-005073] [CLM-005020].

**Contested:** the USD 10-20bn peak range is unrisked and "not a forecast or target" [CLM-014049]. **Unknown:** internal probability of success, Entyvio erosion curve, Amitiza final judgement [CLM-005080] [CLM-005017] [CLM-014048].

## 5. What each does better than the other two (evidence-limited)

| Company | Distinguishing relative strength on evidence | Basis and limit |
|---|---|---|
| Lilly | Growth plus margin expansion while building capacity | Revenue ×2.3 and pre-tax margin 21.7% → 39.5% (own series); the claim "better" is about trajectory, not durability [CLM-000137] [CLM-001007] |
| J&J | Diversified absorption of a large LOE | Group growth +6.0% with Stelara -41.3%; partly acquired growth [CLM-000253] [CLM-000254] [CLM-002075] |
| AbbVie | Replacing a dominant franchise with pre-built successors | Replacement of 109% in three years *(computed)*; successors were already marketed [CLM-003014] [CLM-003084] |
| Takeda | A plasma-derived therapy network and in-house orexin discovery | Specific to Takeda; not a measure of general superiority [CLM-005063] [CLM-005048] |

These are relative descriptions, not rankings *(INTERPRETATION)*.

reports.title: AI, Data & Robotics Landscape: Lilly, J&J, AbbVie, Takeda (A6, wave 1)
reports.markdown:
# AI, Data & Robotics Landscape: Lilly, J&J, AbbVie, Takeda (A6, wave 1)

Window 2021-11 to 2026-11-21. Every claim carries maturity in the shard (`shards/A6_ai_robotics/claims.jsonl`). A press release proves an announcement, not an outcome. Cards: [capability_mechanism_cards.md](capability_mechanism_cards.md). Matrix: [maturity_matrix.md](maturity_matrix.md). Labs: [autonomous_lab_reality_check.md](autonomous_lab_reality_check.md).

## 1. Summary
- Lilly has the largest and best-evidenced build in infrastructure terms: an operating 1,016-GPU cluster [CLM-006004], a live data-as-product platform (TuneLab) [CLM-000280], and several external model partners [CLM-006012, CLM-006009, CLM-006010]. No source opened shows an outcome from any of it [CLM-006007].
- J&J has the only regulator-verified robotics milestones (OTTAVA De Novo; MONARCH QUEST 3 clearance) [CLM-000283, CLM-006027], plus self-reported enterprise AI metrics [CLM-006020]. OTTAVA has one announced installation [CLM-000284].
- AbbVie built an internal knowledge-graph platform (ARCH) with candid cost commentary but no outcome beyond a preprint [CLM-006032, CLM-006033], and buys AI through BigHat and Valkai [CLM-006035, CLM-000285].
- Takeda's disclosed AI strategy is external partnering (Nabla, Iambic, AISB) at prototype stage [CLM-006039, CLM-006041, CLM-006042]; no first-party deployment with metrics was found [CLM-006045].
- Industry calibration: AI-platform pipelines still suffer ordinary attrition [CLM-006047], the best public AI-origin clinical data are a small Phase IIa [CLM-006048], and owned automation ventures have ended in divestment or distressed sale [CLM-006052].

## 2. Eli Lilly

**Established**
- *Compute and data.* Lilly's AI factory is a DGX SuperPOD (B300) with 1,016 Blackwell Ultra GPUs [CLM-006003], inaugurated about February 2026, assembled in about four months, over 9,000 petaflops [CLM-006004]. TuneLab, launched 2025-09-09, offers Lilly-trained models to biotechs via federated learning (company estimates over USD 1 billion of underlying data cost) [CLM-000280]; Benchling will distribute it to 1,300+ customers, opt-in later in 2026 [CLM-006008]. Maturity: operational (LillyPod, TuneLab), pilot (distribution).
- *External models.* Isomorphic (USD 45 million upfront, up to USD 1.7 billion) [CLM-006012]; insitro ADMET models [CLM-006009]; Chai custom antibody model (trade report) [CLM-006010]; OpenAI antimicrobials, announced June 2024, not September 2025 as the brief states [CLM-006011]. Maturity: concept to prototype.
- *Physical.* Lebanon Advanced Therapies opened 2026-05-06 with robotic dosing/sealing seen on a tour [CLM-006002]; the USD 4.5 billion Medicine Foundry remains planned for late 2027 [CLM-006000, CLM-006001]. NVIDIA describes plant robots and digital twins without counts [CLM-006006]. Lilly's capex was USD 7.8 billion in 2025 [CLM-000246].
- *Retreat.* The Life Sciences Studio / Strateos remote robotic lab was sold to Arctoris in 2024 [CLM-006013]; a reported USD 90 million build cost conflicts with another source on dates [CLM-006014].

**Contested:** the reason for divesting the lab [CLM-006017]; whether Strateos closed or was acquired [CLM-006015]; the Chai hit-rate claim [CLM-006010].

**Unknown:** any result from LillyPod, TuneLab uptake, co-innovation lab status (concept at CLM-000281), Lilly Gateway Labs/Catalyze360 outcomes (not assessed), and Lilly's 10-K quantifies no AI outcome [CLM-000252].

## 3. Johnson & Johnson

**Established**
- *Enterprise AI.* J&J's CIO said nearly 900 gen-AI use cases were reviewed and the company moved from proofs of concept to deployment [CLM-006018]; 10–15% of use cases drive about 80% of value [CLM-006019]. Self-reported results: "up to 2.6x" trial-site enrolment [CLM-006020], quality-control answers in minutes [CLM-006021], 47,000 employees through a required gen-AI course [CLM-006022]. Maturity: pilot to operational; outcome evidence none independent.
- *OTTAVA.* De Novo 2026-07-22 [CLM-000283], first installation 2026-11-19 [CLM-000284]; IDE trial fitted ORs as small as 243 sq ft, efficiency survey n=20 [CLM-006028]. Maturity: pilot. FY2025 10-K contains no OTTAVA or MONARCH text [CLM-006025].
- *MONARCH.* QUEST 3 clearance announced 2026-08-17 with AI nodule segmentation [CLM-006027]. Maturity: operational.
- *VELYS.* Only a 10-K statement of pull-through for ATTUNE knees [CLM-006026].
- *Polyphonic.* "Early access to select hospitals only" [CLM-006030]; Abu Dhabi network deployment "expected" [CLM-006031].
- *Federated structure model.* J&J is a founding AISB member [CLM-006042].

**Contested:** executive-reported metrics lack baselines (WSJ original paywalled) [CLM-006019].

**Unknown:** VELYS and MONARCH installed bases, OTTAVA revenue, Polyphonic hospital count. Varipulse was reviewed and excluded as not an AI/robotics initiative.

## 4. AbbVie

**Established**
- ARCH: conceived 2020, built by fewer than ten FTE plus contractors, harmonised data over 124 TB, graph of over 30 million nodes and nearly 2 billion relationships, access for all R&D [CLM-006032, CLM-006034]; cost undisclosed, built "quick, not cheap, not right [or final]" [CLM-006033]. Maturity: operational. The source describes a knowledge graph, not generative AI, contrary to the brief.
- BigHat: USD 30 million upfront, up to about USD 325 million milestones [CLM-006035] (prototype). Valkai: announcement only [CLM-006037] (concept).
- 10-K discloses AI skills investment and an adoption-failure risk, no outcomes [CLM-006036].
- AISB founding member [CLM-006042] and AISB Bind partner [CLM-006044].

**Unknown:** ARCH outcomes (preprint not opened), Allergan Aesthetics digital and manufacturing automation (not searched in depth).

## 5. Takeda (baseline)
- Nabla Bio second collaboration, October 2025: double-digit millions upfront and research, over USD 1 billion success-based [CLM-006039]; first-in-human expected in one to two years [CLM-006039]. Iambic, February 2026: success-based payments could exceed USD 1.7 billion [CLM-006041]. AISB member since October 2025 [CLM-006042, CLM-006043]; not listed in AISB Bind [CLM-006044]. 20-F lists digital transformation and AI risks, no quantified outcome [CLM-000278]; BioLife plasma centres grew to 260 [CLM-000279]. Maturity: prototype to pilot for all named deals [CLM-006045].

## 6. Industry calibration
- FDA draft guidance (January 2025) sets a risk-based credibility framework for AI used in regulatory decisions [CLM-006046].
- Recursion ended four of 11 programmes in 2025 [CLM-006047]; Insilico's rentosertib Phase IIa showed +98.4 mL FVC with liver-related discontinuations [CLM-006048]; Phase III start is an unverified snippet [CLM-006050]; AI-origin Phase 2 success is cited as about 40%, similar to conventional drugs [CLM-006049].
- Zymergen: sold at about one-tenth of IPO valuation [CLM-006051]. Automation track record: [autonomous_lab_reality_check.md](autonomous_lab_reality_check.md) [CLM-006052].

## 7. Cross-company reading (INTERPRETATION)
- Posture: Lilly builds and partners; J&J pursues productivity AI and device robotics; AbbVie internalises data and buys models; Takeda partners [CLM-006053].
- Only J&J's devices have regulator-verified milestones; no discovery or financial outcome is public for the four companies [CLM-006054].
- Lilly's defensibility rests on data, not compute [CLM-006055]; federated consortia are the common mechanism for pooling pharma data [CLM-006056].
- Cost visibility is limited to deal terms and a few capex numbers [CLM-006057].

## 8. Takeda options (RECOMMENDATION)
Partner and watch; gate deals on first-in-human data; use CRO automation; do not match Lilly's compute build [CLM-006058, CLM-006059].

reports.title: Autonomous Lab Reality Check (A6, wave 1)
reports.markdown:
# Autonomous Lab Reality Check (A6, wave 1)

Question: what is technically and commercially mature today in laboratory automation and "autonomous" (closed-loop, AI-directed) discovery, judged only by evidence opened for this review? Cutoff 2026-11-21.

## What is established
- **Lilly built and then divested an open robotic cloud lab.** The Life Sciences Studio in San Diego (public launch about 2020, with Strateos) was acquired by Arctoris in 2024 and relocated to Oxford, with five biochemistry modules, a high-throughput screening module, a BSL2 cell-biology module and storage for 4 million compounds [CLM-006013]. Cost (USD 90 million) and start year (2017 versus about 2020) are reported inconsistently [CLM-006014]. No disclosed discovery outcome came from it in any source opened.
- **The asset continues as a service.** Arctoris (a CRO) runs the platform, expanded its biophysics capacity ten-fold and was selected for a UK ARIA AI Scientist programme [CLM-006016]. Automation is being sold as data generation for AI customers, not as an autonomous discovery engine.
- **Biofoundry automation plus ML did not guarantee commercial success.** Zymergen sold to Ginkgo for about USD 300 million, one-tenth of its roughly USD 3 billion IPO-era valuation, after cumulative net losses of USD 1.2 billion and a discontinued first product [CLM-006051].
- **Lilly's next step is an announcement.** The NVIDIA–Lilly co-innovation lab (up to USD 1 billion over five years) targets a "continuous learning system" linking agentic wet labs with dry labs; it is at concept stage [CLM-000281]. LillyPod is operational as compute, with no reported result [CLM-006004, CLM-006007].
- **Physical automation that is operating is conventional.** The Lilly Lebanon Advanced Therapies plant has robotic machines that dose, measure and seal medicines, seen on a guided tour with no performance data [CLM-006002].
- **A fast-feedback AI-wet-lab loop is claimed by vendors.** Nabla says design-to-test takes three to four weeks and expects first-in-human data within one to two years (both company statements) [CLM-006039, CLM-006040]; BigHat pairs ML with a high-speed wet lab under an AbbVie deal with no result yet [CLM-006035].

## What is contested
- Whether Lilly sold the Studio because the model failed, because utilisation was low or for portfolio reasons: the reason is undisclosed [CLM-006017].
- Whether Strateos closed or was acquired: one unverified aggregator snippet says it was acquired by Multiply Labs in December 2023; no primary source opened, so the research brief's "closure" is not confirmed [CLM-006015].
- Whether AI-originated molecules outperform conventional ones clinically. Rentosertib (Insilico) shows a peer-reviewed Phase IIa FVC signal with liver-safety discontinuations [CLM-006048]; Recursion ended four of 11 programmes in 2025 [CLM-006047]; the cited aggregate Phase 2 success rate for AI-originated compounds is about the same as conventional (secondary citation) [CLM-006049].

## What is unknown
- Any peer-reviewed or audited result from a fully closed-loop autonomous lab at any of the four companies.
- Utilisation, cost per experiment or error-rate data for Lilly's or any pharma's robotic labs.
- Whether Lilly's co-innovation lab has begun operations.
- Emerald Cloud Lab and other cloud-lab track records (not investigated).

## Technology readiness judgement (INTERPRETATION)
| Layer | Readiness (evidence-based) | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| High-throughput, scripted automation (screening, dosing, fill-finish) | operational, commodity | Arctoris platform; Lilly plant [CLM-006013, CLM-006002] |
| Remote/cloud access to a robotic lab | operational but commercially fragile | Studio divested; platform now CRO-run [CLM-006017, CLM-006016] |
| AI-planned experiments in an owned wet-lab loop | prototype to pilot, unproven | Nabla/BigHat claims; co-innovation lab concept [CLM-006040, CLM-006035, CLM-000281] |
| "Autonomous" end-to-end discovery with clinical outcome | not demonstrated | No source opened shows it |

## Implications for Takeda (RECOMMENDATION)
Rent automation and data generation (CRO model) rather than build an owned robotic lab; gate AI-biotech deals on first-in-human data; revisit when an independent outcome from Lilly's lab programme appears [CLM-006052, CLM-006058].

reports.title: Capability Mechanism Cards (A6, wave 1)
reports.markdown:
# Capability Mechanism Cards (A6, wave 1)

Scope: Lilly, J&J, AbbVie, Takeda (baseline), research cutoff 2026-11-21. Maturity scale: concept, prototype, pilot, operational, scaled, demonstrated_outcome. A press release proves an announcement, not an outcome. Claims in `[CLM-…]`; `CLM-000xxx` IDs are canonical registry claims. "Takeda relevance" uses build / buy / partner / watch / reject.

---

## Card 1. Lilly TuneLab (federated model-access platform) — Lilly

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Capability | Lilly-trained ADMET/safety/preclinical prediction models offered to outside biotechs; partners return data via federated learning. |
| Initial problem | Small biotechs lack consistent assay data; Lilly wants more training data and ecosystem pull (Catalyze360). |
| Starting investment | Lilly estimates the underlying data cost more than USD 1 billion to generate (company estimate, unaudited) [CLM-000280]. |
| Execution timeline | Launched 2025-09-09 [CLM-000280]; insitro ADMET models for it announced the same day [CLM-006009]; Benchling distribution announced 2026-01-08, opt-in "later this year" [CLM-006008]; Revvity Signals channel indicated mid-2026 (metadata only, SRC-006035). |
| Enabling assets | Decades of proprietary preclinical data; NVIDIA FLARE federated infrastructure; hosting by a third party [CLM-000280]; distribution through Benchling (1,300+ customers) [CLM-006008]; NVIDIA compute [CLM-006004]. |
| Evidence of value | None independent. No uptake, retraining count or scientific result disclosed [CLM-006008]. |
| Maturity | **operational** (platform live) with distribution at **pilot**. |
| Durability | Data moat is real if volume and consistency are as claimed; federated design means partner data improves Lilly-led models, strengthening lock-in (INTERPRETATION) [CLM-006055]. |
| Competitive response | Multi-pharma consortia (AISB) and open models (OpenFold3, Boltz, Chai) offer substitutes [CLM-006056, CLM-006042]. |
| Takeda relevance | **Watch / partner-as-user.** Takeda could be a TuneLab data-for-models participant; decide after independent results appear [CLM-006059]. |
| Evidence IDs | CLM-000280, CLM-006008, CLM-006009, CLM-006055, CLM-006056; SRC-006010, SRC-006008 |

---

## Card 2. LillyPod AI factory and NVIDIA co-innovation lab — Lilly

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Capability | Owned 1,016-GPU NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD (B300) to train biomedical foundation models; a planned USD 1 billion NVIDIA-Lilly co-innovation lab linking agentic wet labs and dry labs. |
| Initial problem | Wet-lab throughput limits (Lilly cites about 2,000 molecular ideas per target per year) [CLM-006005]. |
| Starting investment | Cluster cost not disclosed. Co-innovation lab: up to USD 1 billion over five years, jointly with NVIDIA [CLM-000281]. |
| Execution timeline | Announced October 2025 [CLM-006003]; inaugurated about February 2026, built in about four months [CLM-006004]; co-innovation lab announced 2026-01-12, work to begin early 2026 [CLM-000281]. |
| Enabling assets | NVIDIA hardware and BioNeMo/Omniverse/Isaac software; 700 TB genomics data [CLM-006004]; internal chief AI officer organisation. |
| Evidence of value | **None disclosed.** No model release, discovery result, cycle-time or cost number attributable to LillyPod [CLM-006007]. |
| Maturity | LillyPod: **operational** (infrastructure online). Co-innovation lab: **concept** [CLM-000281]. |
| Durability | Compute is purchasable; differentiation must come from data and models (INTERPRETATION) [CLM-006055]. Cluster is a capex bet with energy and obsolescence exposure. |
| Competitive response | BMS and Roche announced comparable pharma supercomputers (trade analysis only, not opened). |
| Takeda relevance | **Watch.** Do not match; buy cloud compute and partner [CLM-006058]. |
| Evidence IDs | CLM-000281, CLM-000282, CLM-006003–CLM-006007, CLM-006055; SRC-006001–006003 |

---

## Card 3. Lilly external AI-model partner portfolio (Isomorphic, insitro, Chai, OpenAI) — Lilly

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Capability | Parallel access to external model builders instead of a single in-house model. |
| Initial problem | Reach new small-molecule and antibody design capability faster than internal build. |
| Starting investment | Isomorphic: USD 45 million upfront, up to USD 1.7 billion milestones [CLM-006012]. insitro, Chai, OpenAI: no terms disclosed [CLM-006009, CLM-006010, CLM-006011]. |
| Execution timeline | Isomorphic 2024-01-07; OpenAI 2024-06-25 (brief's Sept 2025 date is wrong); insitro 2025-09-09; Chai early 2026 [CLM-006012, CLM-006011, CLM-006009, CLM-006010]. |
| Enabling assets | Lilly proprietary data (insitro, Chai models trained on it); partner models (AlphaFold lineage, generative antibody models). |
| Evidence of value | None disclosed; no candidate named in any opened source. Chai's double-digit hit rate is Chai's own claim [CLM-006010]. |
| Maturity | **concept** (Isomorphic, OpenAI), **prototype** (insitro, Chai). |
| Durability | Low individually; portfolio breadth hedges model-vendor risk (INTERPRETATION). |
| Competitive response | Every large pharma signs similar deals (Takeda–Nabla/Iambic; AbbVie–BigHat) [CLM-006039, CLM-006041, CLM-006035]. |
| Takeda relevance | **Partner** (already doing so); apply milestone-gated structures [CLM-006058]. |
| Evidence IDs | CLM-006009–CLM-006012; SRC-006004, 006008, 006009, 006011 |

---

## Card 4. Lilly Life Sciences Studio / Strateos remote robotic lab — Lilly (documented retreat)

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Capability | Remote-controlled, cloud-operated robotic lab (San Diego) integrating synthesis, purification, analysis and testing. |
| Initial problem | Faster, more reproducible discovery cycles and access for outside scientists. |
| Starting investment | Reported USD 90 million, established 2017 per one trade source; conflicts with a ~2020 public launch in a Fierce snippet [CLM-006014]. |
| Execution timeline | Public launch about 2020 (with Strateos); sold to CRO Arctoris and relocated to Oxford in 2024 [CLM-006013]. Strateos: one unopened aggregator snippet says acquired by Multiply Labs December 2023 [CLM-006015]; the brief's "closed 2023" is **not confirmed**. |
| Enabling assets | Strateos robotic cloud platform; Lilly demand. |
| Evidence of value | No disclosed discovery outcome from the lab in any source opened. |
| Maturity | Reached **operational**; ended as a divested asset [CLM-006017]. |
| Durability | Low as an owned open-access lab; the equipment survives in a CRO service model [CLM-006016]. |
| Competitive response | CROs (Arctoris) market automated data generation to AI-drug-discovery firms [CLM-006016]. |
| Takeda relevance | **Reject building** an owned cloud lab; **buy/partner** for automated data generation [CLM-006058]. |
| Contrary evidence | Reason for sale undisclosed; may be portfolio-driven. Lilly still plans "agentic wet labs" [CLM-000281]. |
| Evidence IDs | CLM-006013–CLM-006017, CLM-006052; SRC-006005, 006006, 006028 (metadata), 006029 (metadata) |

---

## Card 5. Lilly manufacturing automation: Lebanon Advanced Therapies and Medicine Foundry — Lilly

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Capability | New genetic-medicine plant with robotic dosing/sealing equipment; planned Foundry combining process R&D and clinical-supply manufacturing; robots/digital twins in plants per NVIDIA. |
| Initial problem | Capacity for obesity/diabetes and new modalities; speed from process development to clinic. |
| Starting investment | Foundry USD 4.5 billion (2024); further USD 4.5 billion on Lebanon (2026); Indiana commitments over USD 21 billion since 2020 [CLM-006000, CLM-006002]. Capex USD 7.8 billion in 2025 [CLM-000246]. |
| Execution timeline | Foundry announced 2024-10-02, opening late 2027, still planned in May 2026 [CLM-006000, CLM-006001]; Advanced Therapies opened 2026-05-06 [CLM-006002]. |
| Enabling assets | State of Indiana infrastructure support; NVIDIA digital-twin tooling (stated) [CLM-006006]. |
| Evidence of value | Opening observed by a reporter on a guided tour; no yield, cost or cycle-time data [CLM-006002]. |
| Maturity | Advanced Therapies **operational**; Foundry **concept**; digital twins **pilot** (stated, unevidenced). |
| Durability | Capital and permitting scale are a moat; automation content unquantified. |
| Takeda relevance | **Watch**; relevance for plasma and biologics fill-finish [CLM-000279]. |
| Evidence IDs | CLM-006000–CLM-006002, CLM-006006, CLM-000246; SRC-006000, 006012 |

---

## Card 6. J&J enterprise generative-AI portfolio — J&J

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Capability | Three layers: enterprise productivity, end-to-end process AI (trial-site selection, quality, sales copilots), AI embedded in products [CLM-006018, CLM-006023]. |
| Initial problem | Productivity and trial speed across 130,000+ employees. |
| Starting investment | Not disclosed. |
| Execution timeline | Experimentation from about 2022 (the interview refers to the past two years); centrally governed review of nearly 900 use cases; refocus in 2025 on high-value cases [CLM-006018, CLM-006019]. |
| Enabling assets | AI Council and Data Management Council; training of 47,000 employees in a generative-AI course [CLM-006022]; secure enclaves for models. |
| Evidence of value | Self-reported only: "up to 2.6x" enrolment at AI-recommended high-enrolling sites [CLM-006020]; weeks-to-minutes in a quality tool [CLM-006021]; 10–15% of use cases yield about 80% of value [CLM-006019]. No audited or independent result. |
| Maturity | **pilot** to **operational** (mixed); no demonstrated_outcome. |
| Durability | Low; productivity tools are commodity. Training and governance are slow to copy. |
| Takeda relevance | **Watch / adopt practice**: prune pilots early, measure per use case [CLM-006019]. |
| Evidence IDs | CLM-006018–CLM-006024; SRC-006013, 006014 |

---

## Card 7. J&J OTTAVA robotic surgical system — J&J

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Capability | Table-integrated four-arm soft-tissue robot connected to Polyphonic, with automated arm set-up. |
| Initial problem | Footprint, set-up complexity and data locked in existing robotic platforms. |
| Starting investment | Not disclosed. |
| Execution timeline | FDA De Novo 2026-07-22 [CLM-000283]; first commercial installation 2026-11-19 [CLM-000284]; IDE trial in six ORs, 243–694 sq ft [CLM-006028]. |
| Enabling assets | Ethicon instruments, robotics/AI hires (head of robotics R&D joined in 2024), Polyphonic data layer [CLM-006028]. |
| Evidence of value | Regulator authorisation is verified; efficiency claims rest on a survey of 12 surgeons and 8 staff [CLM-006028]. No revenue or procedure data; FY2025 10-K has no OTTAVA text [CLM-006025]. |
| Maturity | **pilot** (launch phase, one installation) [CLM-006029]. |
| Durability | Architecture and instrument breadth are differentiators; incumbents hold installed base (not studied here). |
| Takeda relevance | **Reject** (device); watch only as a read-across for data-linked robotics. |
| Evidence IDs | CLM-000283, CLM-000284, CLM-006025, CLM-006028, CLM-006029; SRC-006016 |

---

## Card 8. J&J MONARCH robotic bronchoscopy — J&J

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Capability | First flexible robotic bronchoscopy platform; AI nodule segmentation and CT-to-body-divergence handling in QUEST 3 software. |
| Initial problem | Reaching peripheral lung nodules for early lung-cancer diagnosis. |
| Starting investment | Not disclosed (Auris acquisition not reviewed here). |
| Execution timeline | Cleared 510(k) K152819 (referenced in release); QUEST 3 clearance announced 2026-08-17, third launch in 18 months [CLM-006027]. |
| Enabling assets | Installed base, software-updatable design, Polyphonic video library [CLM-006027]. |
| Evidence of value | Clearance (regulator action); support documents are internal technical reviews; installed base and procedure counts not disclosed; 10-K silent [CLM-006025]. |
| Maturity | **operational**. |
| Durability | Moderate; incremental AI inside cleared device, competitors (not studied) exist. |
| Takeda relevance | **Reject** (device). |
| Evidence IDs | CLM-006025, CLM-006027; SRC-006015 |

---

## Card 9. J&J VELYS robotic-assisted orthopaedics — J&J (thin evidence)

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Capability | CT-free robotic knee solution acting as pull-through for ATTUNE implants. |
| Initial problem | Robot-share race in knee arthroplasty. |
| Evidence of value | FY2025 10-K attributes Knees growth partly to VELYS pull-through but gives no unit or procedure counts [CLM-006026]. Adoption numbers were **not located** in a primary source. |
| Maturity | **scaled** at the level of commercial presence (INTERPRETATION); installed base unknown. |
| Takeda relevance | **Reject**; included for completeness. |
| Evidence IDs | CLM-006026; SRC-000010 |

---

## Card 10. J&J Polyphonic surgical data ecosystem — J&J

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Capability | Surgical video, device and AI-insight network; "AI Fund for Surgery"; Abu Dhabi node. |
| Initial problem | Surgical data is fragmented; AI needs governed multi-site datasets. |
| Execution timeline | Announced 2024-06-20 (page blocked; stated in search metadata only); AI Fund June 2025; first awardees 2025-10-27, "early access to select hospitals only" [CLM-006030]; Abu Dhabi programme 2026-05-21, deployment "expected" [CLM-006031]. |
| Enabling assets | Hospital partnerships, AWS and NVIDIA collaboration [CLM-006030]. |
| Evidence of value | None; the programme is data-gathering stage. |
| Maturity | Polyphonic early access: **pilot**; Abu Dhabi network: **concept**. |
| Durability | Potentially high if dataset ownership and hospital integration are exclusive (HYPOTHESIS). |
| Takeda relevance | **Watch** (data-network model). |
| Evidence IDs | CLM-006030, CLM-006031; SRC-006017, 006018 |

---

## Card 11. AbbVie R&D Convergence Hub (ARCH) — AbbVie

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Capability | Knowledge graph and data lake unifying 200+ sources; search and dossier applications; machine-learning workspaces. Not described as generative AI in the source opened. |
| Initial problem | Siloed R&D data; duplicate data acquisition. |
| Starting investment | "Significant investment", price undisclosed; fewer than ten FTE plus many contractors [CLM-006032, CLM-006033]. |
| Execution timeline | Conceived 2020; Bio-IT World award talk 2023-08-24 [CLM-006032]. |
| Enabling assets | Partners (Modak, SciBite, Tellic, TXI), Cloudera ML, governance decision to open de-identified trial data to all R&D [CLM-006032, CLM-006034]. |
| Evidence of value | A Dec 2022 preprint on repurposing flags (not opened); no clinical or financial outcome [CLM-006033]. |
| Maturity | **operational**. |
| Durability | Moderate: graph and governance are slow to replicate; vendors replicable. |
| Takeda relevance | **Build-lite / partner**: governance-first data integration is transferable; Takeda reports its own data modernization [CLM-000278]. |
| Evidence IDs | CLM-006032–CLM-006034, CLM-006038; SRC-006019, 006031 (metadata) |

---

## Card 12. AbbVie external AI: BigHat Biosciences and Valkai — AbbVie

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Capability | ML-guided antibody design with a wet lab (BigHat Milliner); clinical-development AI (Valkai). |
| Starting investment | BigHat: USD 30 million upfront, up to about USD 325 million milestones [CLM-006035]. Valkai: undisclosed [CLM-000285]. |
| Execution timeline | BigHat 2023-12-05; Valkai 2026-09-29. |
| Evidence of value | None disclosed for either [CLM-006037]. |
| Maturity | BigHat **prototype**; Valkai **concept**. |
| Takeda relevance | **Partner** analogues exist (Nabla). |
| Evidence IDs | CLM-006035, CLM-006037, CLM-000285, CLM-006036; SRC-006020 |

---

## Card 13. Takeda external AI deals: Nabla Bio and Iambic — Takeda

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Capability | Generative antibody design (Nabla JAM) and small-molecule AI incl. NeuralPLexer (Iambic). |
| Initial problem | Extend early pipeline after Takeda narrowed research focus (Reuters notes exit from cell-therapy research) [CLM-006039]. |
| Starting investment | Nabla: upfront and research payments in double-digit millions; Iambic: undisclosed upfront; success-based over USD 1 billion and over USD 1.7 billion respectively [CLM-006039, CLM-006041]. |
| Execution timeline | Nabla first collaboration 2022, second 2025-10-14; Iambic 2026-02-09. |
| Evidence of value | None; Nabla expects first-in-human data in one to two years [CLM-006039]. |
| Maturity | **prototype** (Nabla), **prototype/concept** (Iambic). |
| Takeda relevance | **Partner (in progress)**; set go/no-go gates [CLM-006058]. |
| Evidence IDs | CLM-006039–CLM-006041, CLM-006045; SRC-006021, 006022 |

---

## Card 14. Federated OpenFold3 / AI Structural Biology consortium — AbbVie, J&J, Takeda (plus BMS, Astex)

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Capability | Federated fine-tuning of OpenFold3 on proprietary protein-ligand structures; follow-on "AISB Bind". |
| Initial problem | Public structure data is too sparse for drug-like complexes. |
| Starting investment | Not disclosed. |
| Execution timeline | AbbVie and J&J first members (early 2025); BMS, Takeda, Astex joined 2025-10-01 [CLM-006042]. |
| Enabling assets | Apheris secure federated platform, Columbia AlQuraishi lab, 20,000+ private structures [CLM-006043]. |
| Evidence of value | Organiser reports +10 points pose accuracy and +11 points interface quality vs the strongest public model on 1,056 held-out structures; not peer-reviewed [CLM-006043]. |
| Maturity | **pilot** (first initiative complete); AISB Bind **concept** [CLM-006044]. |
| Durability | Network effects among members; open model weights limit exclusivity. |
| Takeda relevance | **Partner (in progress)**; note absence from AISB Bind founding list [CLM-006044]. |
| Evidence IDs | CLM-006042–CLM-006044, CLM-006056; SRC-006023, 006024 |

reports.title: Evidence Gaps (A6, wave 1)
reports.markdown:
# Evidence Gaps (A6, wave 1)

## Blocked, paywalled or unopened sources
| Source | Status | Why it matters | Next query |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fierce Biotech: Lilly sells robot lab to Arctoris (SRC-006028) | HTTP 403 (2 attempts) | "Majority" sale detail; sale date | Arctoris press release; Endpoints/STAT coverage |
| Fierce Biotech: Isomorphic–Lilly (SRC-006033) | not opened | independent confirmation of terms | SEC 8-K/10-Q Lilly collaboration disclosures |
| Business Wire originals (Iambic, Nabla) | HTTP 403 | primary text; Iambic upfront | Takeda newsroom; the Yahoo reprint of Iambic was used |
| AbbVie ARCH page (SRC-006031) | HTTP 403 | company-stated scale | bioRxiv preprint 10.1101/2022.12.20.521235 |
| WSJ "Johnson & Johnson Pivots Its AI Strategy" (SRC-006032) | paywalled | independent confirmation of J&J pruning | none (paywall) |
| Federal Register notice 2024-31542 (SRC-006034) | redirected to anti-bot host | docket date | govinfo.gov mirror |
| J&J Polyphonic launch release (2024-06-20), VELYS/MONARCH adoption pages | HTTP 403 / snippets only | installed base | J&J earnings transcripts; investor.jnj.com |
| Revvity TuneLab information sheet (SRC-006035) | snippet only | second TuneLab channel | open PDF |

## Unresolved questions
1. Strateos: closed, acquired by Multiply Labs, or both? Only an aggregator snippet exists (SRC-006029). The brief's "closed 2023" is **unverified** [CLM-006015].
2. Life Sciences Studio: build start (2017 vs about 2020), true cost and sale terms conflict between sources [CLM-006014].
3. Why did Lilly divest the lab? No disclosure [CLM-006017].
4. TuneLab uptake, number of federation partners, any retraining result.
5. NVIDIA–Lilly co-innovation lab: began operating? (Only CLM-000281.)
6. Lilly Gateway Labs / Catalyze360, XtalPi, Genesis Therapeutics, manufacturing digital-twin deployments: not opened.
7. J&J: VELYS procedure counts, MONARCH installed base, OTTAVA orders, Impella connected/AI, JLABS AI deals, Innovative Medicine "biosignature" outputs.
8. AbbVie: ARCH outcomes; Allergan Aesthetics digital; manufacturing automation.
9. Takeda: DD&T organisation, named AI deployments (clinical ops, pharmacovigilance, manufacturing), Microsoft/AWS/Accenture/Insilico relationships (not verified), BioLife automation, Nimbus origin. Iambic upfront reported as USD 27 million by a secondary source: unverified.
10. Recursion/Exscientia failure data are trade-press only; Insilico Phase III start unverified [CLM-006050]; Emerald Cloud Lab not investigated.
11. Brief errors found: OpenAI–Lilly date (June 2024, not September 2025) [CLM-006011]; ARCH described as generative AI but source describes a knowledge graph [CLM-006032]; NVIDIA–Lilly lab announced 2026-01-12 (registry), AI factory October 2025 [CLM-006003].

## Method limits
- Many figures are company-stated; independent corroboration is rare (Reuters on Nabla, GEN on Recursion/Zymergen, local news on Lebanon).
- Trade pieces reproducing a single release are flagged `single_interested_source`.
- Budget: ~36 sources (26 retrieved); Takeda newsroom and PubMed validations were not searched.

## Suggested next research
- Open Nature Medicine rentosertib paper and ClinicalTrials.gov for Phase III.
- Pull Lilly/J&J/AbbVie earnings-call transcripts (2024-2026) for AI and robotics statements.
- FDA 510(k)/De Novo database entries for OTTAVA, MONARCH QUEST 3, VELYS.
- Takeda earnings decks and newsroom for DD&T metrics.

reports.title: Commercial models comparison: Lilly, J&J, AbbVie, Takeda
reports.markdown:
# Commercial models comparison: Lilly, J&J, AbbVie, Takeda

Research cutoff 2026-11-21. Takeda FY2025 = April 2025 to March 2026; others calendar/fiscal 2025. Cell text states what a source shows; "none found" means not found in the sources opened (see [evidence_gaps.md](evidence_gaps.md)). IDs in brackets resolve in `shards/A7_commercial/claims.jsonl` or the canonical registry.

## What is established

| Mechanism | Lilly | J&J | AbbVie | Takeda |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Direct-to-patient / cash channel | LillyDirect (launched Jan 2024, [CLM-001042]); self-pay Zepbound vials from Aug 2024 at $399/$549 [CLM-007000], cut to $299/$399/$449 on 1 Dec 2025 [CLM-007002]; Walmart pickup [CLM-007003]; KwikPen self-pay from $299 [CLM-007044]. Company says >1 million patients used LillyDirect in 2025 and 1 in 3 new branded weight-management starts were Zepbound self-pay vials [CLM-007004] | Listed on TrumpRx [CLM-007009]; no own cash platform found | Humira on TrumpRx under Jan 2026 agreement [CLM-003081]; Allē is a provider-and-consumer loyalty scheme for aesthetics, not a cash pharmacy [CLM-007036] | None found [CLM-007039] |
| Payer/PBM exposure | Lost preferred CVS Caremark status 1 Jul 2025 [CLM-007011] [CLM-007012]; regained as additional preferred from 1 Oct 2026 [CLM-007013] | Stelara removed from CVS Caremark template formularies from 1 Jul 2026 [CLM-007015]; nine biosimilars on market by Jul 2025 [CLM-007016] | Humira removed by CVS Caremark Apr 2024 with co-branded Cordavis supply [CLM-003008] [CLM-003009]; rebate and chargeback provisions $65.1bn in 2025 [CLM-007019] | Rebates undisclosed; exclusion risk stated [CLM-007025]; Entyvio "formulary wins" per call summary [CLM-007043] |
| Medicare negotiation / Part D | Jardiance MFP from 2026; Trulicity and Verzenio from 2028 [CLM-007023] | Stelara and Xarelto in first list; Part D redesign hurts Erleada, Invega, Opsumit, Uptravi [CLM-007018] | Imbruvica 2026, Vraylar/Linzess 2027, Botox 2028 [CLM-007022] | Entyvio selected for 2028 [CLM-007026] |
| Patient support | Insulin $35 cap and 70% list cut (Mar 2023) [CLM-007034] | J&J withMe (ex-Janssen CarePath) [CLM-007035] [CLM-002071] | Allē: >6 million members, 19,000 practices (Jan 2024) [CLM-007036]; redesign reversed [CLM-003033] | Help at Hand: >100,000 patients cumulative [CLM-007037]; EntyvioConnect (snippet only) [CLM-007038] |
| Self-administration / device shifts | Zepbound vial and KwikPen [CLM-007044] | Tremfya SC share gains [CLM-007029]; Spravato restricted to certified sites [CLM-007030] | none checked | Entyvio SC pen [CLM-007041]; HYHUB needle-free Hyqvia transfer [CLM-007042] |
| Launch curves (FY2025) | Mounjaro $22,965m vs $11,540m; Zepbound $13,542m vs $4,926m [CLM-007031] | Carvykti $1,887m vs $963m (capacity-driven); Spravato $1,696m vs $1,077m; Tremfya $5,155m vs $3,670m [CLM-007029] | Skyrizi $17,562m (+49.9%), Rinvoq $8,304m (+39.1%) [CLM-007020] | Entyvio JPY 958.0bn, 21% of revenue [CLM-007027] |

## What is contested

- Whether cash channels take volume from insured patients: copay accumulator rules and anti-kickback limits restrict use of discounts together with insurance [CLM-007010]. Lilly's "1 in 3 new starts" is a new-start measure with unverified footnotes [CLM-007004].
- Whether PBM exclusivity persists: CVS preferred Wegovy over Zepbound for 11 months, then reinstated Zepbound [CLM-007011] [CLM-007013].
- Whether TrumpRx volumes are material: CRS reports listings and manufacturer counts, not sales; agreements expire with the current term [CLM-007009].

## What is unknown

- Self-pay share of Zepbound revenue (no number in the 10-K [CLM-007005]).
- Net price per prescription and gross-to-net for any company except AbbVie's rebate provisions [CLM-007019].
- Any adherence or time-to-therapy outcome for any patient support program [CLM-007039].

reports.title: Launch execution evidence
reports.markdown:
# Launch execution evidence

## What is established
- **Mounjaro/Zepbound**: Mounjaro $22,965m (2024: $11,540m) and Zepbound $13,542m (2024: $4,926m); together 56% of Lilly revenue [CLM-007031] [CLM-001003]. Growth came with lower realized prices [CLM-007024]. Supply and channel moves: vials and self-pay [CLM-007000], retail pickup [CLM-007003], KwikPen [CLM-007044].
- **Skyrizi/Rinvoq**: Skyrizi $17,562m (+49.9%) and Rinvoq $8,304m (+39.1%); 10-K attributes growth to share uptake and market growth; Humira fell 49% [CLM-007020]. Humira defence tactics: [CLM-003085].
- **Carvykti**: $1,887m vs $963m, attributed to share gains and capacity expansion, so supply governed pace [CLM-007029].
- **Spravato**: $1,696m vs $1,077m; distribution restricted to certified healthcare settings, no home dispensing [CLM-007029] [CLM-007030].
- **Tremfya**: $5,155m vs $3,670m; Crohn's approval March 2025 and Stelara-successor framing [CLM-007029] [CLM-002053].
- **Kisunla**: $21m in Q1 2025 (snippet only, source blocked) and $484m in 9M 2026 [CLM-007032] [CLM-001032]. Reasons for slow uptake are not verified.
- **Entyvio pen (Takeda)**: US approvals Sept 2023 (UC) and April 2024 (CD); 20-F says SC drives uptake [CLM-007033] [CLM-007041]; call summary credits pen adoption and formulary wins [CLM-007043]. Planned launches: oveporexton, zasocitinib [CLM-007033].

## What is contested
- Whether Kisunla's pace reflects MRI/ARIA burden, diagnosis pathway or price: not established here [CLM-007032].
- How much of Skyrizi/Rinvoq growth is contracting versus clinical preference: 10-K gives only share language [CLM-007020].

## What is unknown
- Field-force sizes, omnichannel metrics and hub-service performance for any company (not found in sources opened).
- Qdenga launch curve beyond a +22.1% growth figure in an aggregator summary [CLM-007043].

reports.title: Patient programs and care delivery
reports.markdown:
# Patient programs and care delivery

## Patient support and adherence
- Lilly: insulin list cut of 70% and $35 monthly cap announced 1 March 2023 (company-reported $21.80 average out-of-pocket) [CLM-007034]; LillyDirect >1 million patients in 2025 (company-reported) [CLM-007004].
- J&J: J&J withMe, free, no income requirement for its savings programme [CLM-007035] [CLM-002071].
- AbbVie: Allē >6 million members, 19,000 practices (Jan 2024) [CLM-007036]; October 2024 redesign reversed in early 2025 [CLM-003033].
- Takeda: Help at Hand >100,000 patients cumulative [CLM-007037]; EntyvioConnect described in search snippets only [CLM-007038].
- Outcome evidence (adherence, persistence, time-to-therapy): none found for any company; counts are enrolment or access numbers, company-reported [CLM-007039].

## Care-delivery innovation
- Self-administration and device shifts: Zepbound KwikPen and vials [CLM-007044]; Entyvio SC pen [CLM-007041]; Hyqvia HYHUB needle-free transfer, FDA 510(k) July 2025 (clearance, not adoption) [CLM-007042].
- Counter-trend: Spravato must be administered in certified settings under observation [CLM-007030].
- Connected devices: J&J reports strong Impella adoption but the passage describes no connectivity feature [CLM-007047]. Lilly connected pens (Tempo) not found in the 10-K text searched.
- Decentralized trials: no usable disclosure in the Lilly or J&J 10-Ks [CLM-007048].
- Digital therapeutics calibration: Pear Therapeutics filed Chapter 11 on 7 April 2023 despite published evidence, with the former CEO blaming payment denial [CLM-007045]; commentary says evidence was strong but reimbursement stalled growth [CLM-007046].

## What is contested
- Whether Pear's failure was reimbursement or product-market fit: sources conflict in emphasis [CLM-007045] [CLM-007046].

## What is unknown
- Outcome data for all support programs; digital or connected-device features inside company support programs; RWE outputs (tirzepatide, Entyvio) were not retrieved in this pass.

# Pricing, access and payer dynamics

## What is established

### LillyDirect cash price history (Zepbound vials)
- Aug 2024: 2.5 mg $399, 5 mg $549 per four weeks [CLM-007000].
- 25 Feb 2025: 7.5 mg and 10 mg vials launched at $499 with the Self Pay Journey Program (snippet only) [CLM-007001].
- 1 Dec 2025: $299 / $399 / $449 (2.5 mg / 5 mg / 7.5-15 mg), down from $349 / $499 / $499; non-program prices $599-$1,049 [CLM-007002].
- Feb 2026: KwikPen at the same self-pay prices from $299 [CLM-007044].
- Nov 2025 US government agreement and TrumpRx linkage: [CLM-001036] [CLM-007007] [CLM-007008].

### Gross-to-net and rebates (as disclosed)
- AbbVie: rebate and chargeback provisions $65.1bn (2025), $59.3bn (2024), $56.8bn (2023) against 2025 net revenue of $61.2bn [CLM-007019].
- Lilly: 2025 revenue growth from volume "partially offset by lower realized prices", mostly Mounjaro and Zepbound [CLM-007024].
- Takeda: rebate details not public; formulary exclusion directly reduces usage [CLM-007025].
- J&J: no gross-to-net figure in the passages read; Stelara decline cut Innovative Medicine growth by about 10.4 points [CLM-007017].

### Formulary events
| Date | Event | IDs |
|---|---|---|
| 2024-04-01 | CVS Caremark removes Humira from template formularies; co-branded Cordavis Humira | [CLM-003008] [CLM-003009] |
| 2025-01 | Antitrust class action over Humira rebating filed | [CLM-007021] |
| 2025-07-01 | CVS Caremark prefers Wegovy, removes Zepbound; Lilly stock fell >11% on the news day | [CLM-007011] [CLM-007012] |
| 2025-07-01 | Optum Rx excludes Stelara from two main formularies; nine biosimilars on market | [CLM-007016] |
| 2026-07-01 | CVS Caremark prefers Pyzchiva and Yesintek over Stelara | [CLM-007015] |
| 2026-10-01 | CVS Caremark adds Zepbound back as additional preferred; Foundayo block lifted 2026-06-01 | [CLM-007013] |

Switching data: monthly switching away from tirzepatide rose from about 0.6% to 10.2% after the July 2025 change, then stabilized (Truveta, second-hand) [CLM-007014].

### Medicare, Part D redesign and negotiation
- J&J: Stelara and Xarelto in first list; Part D redesign reduces Erleada, Invega, Opsumit and Uptravi sales [CLM-007018].
- AbbVie: Imbruvica (2026), Vraylar and Linzess (2027), Botox (2028) [CLM-007022].
- Lilly: Jardiance (2026), Trulicity and Verzenio (2028) [CLM-007023].
- Takeda: Entyvio (2028); Part D redesign expected to reduce profit; MFN executive order of May 2025 [CLM-007026].

### 340B and litigation
- Lilly 340B suits [CLM-001069]; J&J contract-pharmacy policy and HRSA rebate-model rulings [CLM-002034] [CLM-002069] [CLM-002070]; linked in [CLM-007028].
- J&J ERISA suit over its own drug-benefit management (allegation) [CLM-007050].
- Compounded incretins: Lilly cites net-price erosion risk [CLM-007049].
- CVS Caremark ERISA class action over Zepbound denials (snippet only) [CLM-007040].

## What is contested
- Whether the 2025 CVS decision reflected a better Wegovy net price (CVS says so [CLM-007011]) or leverage over access; the reversal after about 11 months [CLM-007013] does not settle it.
- Whether PBM private labels "pop" or exploit the gross-to-net bubble: Drug Channels argues both [CLM-007016] (commentary).

## What is unknown
- Net prices, rebate rates by drug, and the share of self-pay revenue.
- Whether the Oct 2026 CVS change increased Zepbound volume.

# Deal outcomes scorecard

## What is established
**Approved products from window or lookback deals**
- J&J Momenta: nipocalimab (IMAAVY) approved 2025-04-30 [CLM-009044].
- J&J Intra-Cellular: CAPLYTA MDD indication approved Q4 2025, nine months after the $14.5B close [CLM-009030] [CLM-009031].
- Lilly Loxo ($6.92B, 2019): Retevmo 2020; Jaypirca first-line CLL/SLL 2026-10-02 [CLM-009014] [CLM-009015].
- AbbVie ImmunoGen: Elahere already marketed, with $578M revenue and $682M operating loss in the first partial year [CLM-009056].
- AbbVie/Genmab epcoritamab marketed [CLM-009072]; Takeda FRUZAQLA approved [CLM-009082].

**Write-downs and failures**

| AbbVie | Cerevel / emraclidine | Phase 2 failed Nov 2024; impairment | $4.5B of $8.7B | [CLM-009054] |
| J&J | Ottava (Auris) | Partial impairment FY2021 | $0.9B | [CLM-009047] |
| J&J | Bermekimab (XBiotech) | Impaired FY2022 | ~$0.8B | [CLM-009046] |
| J&J | M710 (Momenta) | Impaired 2023, 2024 | ~$0.2B each | [CLM-009045] |
| J&J | Laminar | Pivotal study suspended 2025 | $0.4B + $0.3B milestone | [CLM-009039] [CLM-009040] |
| Lilly | DICE DC-806 | Discontinued 2024 | $1,916M charge | [CLM-009003] |
| Lilly | Prevail GBA1 | Impaired 2022 | $244.6M charges | [CLM-009009] |
| Lilly | Vitrakvi (Loxo) | Impaired 2024 | not extracted | [CLM-009016] |
| Takeda | Maverick, soticlestat, gamma delta T-cell | Terminated / impaired | JPY 27.8B, 21.5B, 58.2B | [CLM-009083] [CLM-009084] |

## Capital deployed vs realised (audited disclosures only)
- AbbVie 2024: ImmunoGen $9.2B + Cerevel $8.3B net of cash [CLM-009056] [CLM-009053]; $4.5B (about 54% of the Cerevel net price) written off [CLM-009054].
- J&J: $15.1B (FY2024) and $17.5B (FY2025) in business acquisitions [CLM-009049]; realised revenue is not isolated except via commentary [CLM-009034].
- Lilly: $3.8B/$3.3B/$2.9B yearly IPR&D charges (2023-25) [CLM-009000]; none of those assets was approved in the sources reviewed.
- Takeda: $4.0B upfront for TAK-279, Phase 3 positive, NDA planned 2026 [CLM-009076] [CLM-009077].

## What is contested or unknown
- Revenue realised per acquisition (Impella, Shockwave, Elahere beyond year one) is not in the extracted notes; the Abiomed CVR reduction hints at lower sales expectations but gives no figure [CLM-009042].
- NM26 early termination direction unknown [CLM-009037].
- Morphic headline $3.2B vs $2.55B charge not reconciled [CLM-009002].

## Patterns *(INTERPRETATION)*
[CLM-009100] [CLM-009099] [CLM-009095] [CLM-009096] [CLM-009097] [CLM-009098]
- Deal-size distribution: J&J and AbbVie have transformative deals above $8B; Lilly's largest window outlay is Morphic ($2.5B); Takeda's is Nimbus ($4B).
- Value destruction concentrates in neuroscience (Cerevel), gene/cell therapy (Prevail, gamma delta) and robotics (Ottava).
- Speed to approval: Intra-Cellular new indication about 9 months; Momenta about 5 years; Loxo selpercatinib about 1.3 years, first-line Jaypirca about 7.6 years.

reports.title: External-innovation machinery
reports.markdown:
# External-innovation machinery

## Eli Lilly
Lilly Catalyze360 bundles Lilly Ventures (capital), Lilly Gateway Labs (lab space), Lilly ExploR&D (development expertise) and, since September 2025, TuneLab [CLM-009025]. TuneLab uses federated learning on Lilly models [CLM-009026]; Benchling plans distribution to 1,300+ customers [CLM-009027]; a vendor reports 2M Lilly and 675K partner data points by Oct 2026 [CLM-009028]. The NVIDIA lab adds up to $1B joint spend [CLM-009029]. Fund size and investment counts for Lilly Ventures were not found (gap).

## Johnson & Johnson
J&J Innovation operates regional Innovation Centers, JLABS and JJDC (venture arm) with 150+ claimed partnerships [CLM-009050]. JLABS was planned in 2016 at six sites with capacity for 225 companies [CLM-009051]; by March 2026 trade press reports closures of Houston, Toronto, Washington DC and New York [CLM-009052]. Resident-company counts and JJDC fund size are not in the sources opened (gap).

## AbbVie
AbbVie Ventures is the corporate venture group; sources conflict on founding (2009 vs about 2015) [CLM-009074] and one source is sponsored content [CLM-009075]. AbbVie's real machinery in the audited record is deal flow: yearly early-stage upfronts of $0.6-1.0B [CLM-009069], options (Calico, ADARx) [CLM-009068] [CLM-009061] and BaseLaunch membership [CLM-009094]. The brief's "external-innovation share of pipeline" figure was not found (gap).

## Takeda
Takeda's Center for External Innovation (head Alison Handley) sits on BaseLaunch's investment board [CLM-009091]; Takeda Ventures reportedly sits under it, per an aggregator only [CLM-009092]. The 20-F lists dozens of licence partners [CLM-009088]. Takeda Digital Ventures, T-CiRA and fund sizes were not verified (gap).

## Comparison *(INTERPRETATION)*

reports.title: Evidence gaps (A12)
reports.markdown:
# Evidence gaps (A12)

- CBER biologics/vaccines/devices not retrieved: Carvykti (2022-02, 2L 2024-04), Adzynma, Qdenga status, Abiomed/MedTech device approvals, Varipulse pause.
- Mirikizumab CRL (April 2023), donanemab 2024 advisory committee/delay, sintilimab CRL (2022), retatrutide regulatory status: no primary source opened.
- Rinvoq 2021-12 boxed-warning event: only the 2022-01-14 AD supplement letter was opened; boxed-warning text not verified. Rinvoq Crohn's (2023-05) letter not matched.
- Teliso-V/Emrelis accelerated-approval conversion status, Skyrizi/Tremfya supplements after 2025, Darzalex Faspro 2025 supplements: dates seen in openFDA but not claimed.
- Orforglipron/other FDA approvals are in the FDA 2026 novel page retrieved on 2026-11-21; post-approval label contents not opened.
- Takeda: Qdenga U.S. BLA withdrawal (2023-07), Alofisel EU withdrawal, TAK-279 NDA status not verified; Exkivity absent from Drugs@FDA openFDA lookup (404).
- Peer-reviewed readouts opened at abstract level only; many Phase 3 NEJM/Lancet readouts (SURMOUNT outcomes, ATTAIN-1, ICONIC-LEAD, MajesTEC-3) not individually retrieved.
- Breakthrough/priority/fast-track counts per company not disclosed in a comparable form; only individual designations noted.
- Platform items not evidenced: Lilly radioligand/gene editing, J&J ADC (Ambrx), AbbVie in-vivo CAR-T.
- openFDA is an unvalidated mirror of Drugs@FDA; FDA novel page lacks sponsor.
- ClinicalTrials.gov statuses lag events (e.g. VERONA record still active).
- Existing CT.gov inventories (companies/*/pipeline/ctgov_inventory.md) not re-used or cited.

Suggested next queries: FDA CBER approvals page; Lilly/J&J/AbbVie/Takeda 8-K exhibits for CRL dates; EMA EPARs for withdrawals.

reports.title: Pipeline quality and revenue-replacement assessment (INTERPRETATION)
reports.markdown:
# Pipeline quality and revenue-replacement assessment (INTERPRETATION)

Everything below is analyst interpretation of the cited FACT claims, not a finding of fact.

## Depth

- Lilly: eight CDER novel approvals plus the Zepbound NDA, and eight Phase 3 assets in the snapshot across incretin, lipoprotein(a), oncology and Alzheimer's [CLM-012000] [CLM-012021].
- J&J: five novel approvals (two bispecifics, an oral peptide, a TKI, an FcRn antibody) plus a bispecific/CAR-T oncology Phase 3 stack [CLM-012008] [CLM-012012].
- AbbVie: five novel approvals but the 2022-2025 growth came from Skyrizi/Rinvoq supplements [CLM-012033] [CLM-012036]; the 2023-2025 setbacks (ABBV-951 CRLs, emraclidine, navitoclax, VERONA) were larger in count than at peers [CLM-012116] [CLM-012117].
- Takeda: three novel approvals, all arriving in 2023 or 2026; two 2026 approvals plus zasocitinib Phase 3 form the replacement set [CLM-012019] [CLM-012131].

## Concentration

- Lilly is the most concentrated: Mounjaro and Zepbound were 56% of 2025 revenue [CLM-012124], and the Phase 3 list is dominated by incretin and incretin-adjacent assets (retatrutide, orforglipron, eloralintide, tirzepatide outcomes).
- J&J and AbbVie are concentrated in immunology (Tremfya, Skyrizi, Rinvoq) and oncology respectively; Stelara biosimilar erosion is described in J&J's FY2025 10-K *(not registered as a claim; gap)* and replacement sizing was not retrieved.

## Modality mix

Broadest at J&J (bispecifics, CAR-T, oral peptide, drug-device, FcRn antibody) and AbbVie (ADCs, bispecific antibody, small molecules); Lilly spans peptides, oral small molecules and siRNA (lepodisiran) [CLM-012140]; Takeda spans oral small molecules, peptides, an siRNA and an antibody, having exited cell therapy [CLM-012123]. Gene editing and radioligand programmes were not evidenced.

## Revenue-replacement adequacy

- Lilly: the pipeline mostly extends the franchise that already supplies the revenue (oral and multi-agonist incretins), so replacement need is low near term and the risk is concentration, not shortage; orforglipron's voucher and 2026-04-01 approval support timely launch [CLM-012125] [CLM-012006].
- J&J: Stelara is exposed to biosimilars; Tremfya, Icotyde and the bispecific/CAR-T stack are the identified successors, with Icotyde approved 2026-03-17 [CLM-012012]. Adequacy cannot be sized without revenue forecasts (gap).
- AbbVie: Humira revenue fell sharply in 2025 and is offset by Skyrizi and Rinvoq *(gap: the FY2025 10-K revenue table was read but not registered as a claim)*; the novel pipeline (tavapadon, ADCs) is smaller than the lost revenue, so growth depends on immunology supplements and label expansion *(INTERPRETATION)*; Rinvoq GCA supplement [CLM-012036].
- Takeda: Exkivity withdrawal, Alofisel and cell-therapy impairments, and soticlestat failure removed several late assets [CLM-012121] [CLM-012120]; oveporexton and zasocitinib are the principal replacement bets.

Confidence: moderate on counts and dates (regulator records), low on adequacy (no forecast data retrieved).

reports.title: Scientific platform capabilities (evidence-based)
reports.markdown:
# Scientific platform capabilities (evidence-based)

Each capability is an INTERPRETATION built from regulator, registry and peer-reviewed artefacts. Capability is not commercial value. Company-claimed platforms with no such artefact retrieved are excluded.

## Eli Lilly

- Lilly platform capability (oral small-molecule incretin chemistry): orforglipron is an oral GLP-1 receptor agonist that reached an FDA approval (Foundayo, 2026-04-01) and has an ATTAIN Phase 3 publication programme including a JAMA report in obstructive sleep apnea. *(INTERPRETATION)* [CLM-012138]
- Lilly platform capability (multi-agonist peptides): retatrutide, a GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, has Phase 2 (NEJM 2023) and TRIUMPH-1 Phase 3 (NEJM, 2026-11-05) publications and a 10,000-participant outcomes trial. *(INTERPRETATION)* [CLM-012139]
- Lilly platform capability (RNA therapeutics): lepodisiran, an siRNA against lipoprotein(a), is in the ACCLAIM-Lp(a) cardiovascular outcomes Phase 3 (registry record NCT06292013, about 17,300 participants). *(INTERPRETATION)* [CLM-012140]
- Lilly platform capability (precision oncology small molecules): Lilly (via Loxo Oncology) obtained FDA approval of Jaypirca in 2023 and converted CLL/SLL from accelerated to traditional approval on 2025-12-02, and Inluriyo was approved 2025-09-25. *(INTERPRETATION)* [CLM-012141]

## Johnson & Johnson

- J&J platform capability (T-cell-engaging bispecifics): Tecvayli (2022-10-25) and Talvey (2023-08-09) were both approved by FDA, Tecvayli's pivotal MajesTEC-1 was published in NEJM, and MajesTEC-7 Phase 3 (NCT05552222) combines the two engagers. *(INTERPRETATION)* [CLM-012142]
- J&J platform capability (oral targeted peptides): icotrokinra, an oral IL-23 receptor peptide, was approved as Icotyde on 2026-03-17 and its Phase 3 results are published in NEJM (2025-11-06). *(INTERPRETATION)* [CLM-012143]
- J&J platform capability (CAR-T and bispecific oncology): cilta-cel CARTITUDE-4 was published in NEJM (2023-07-27) and CARTITUDE-5 Phase 3 (NCT04923893) has an estimated primary completion of 2029-02-14. *(INTERPRETATION)* [CLM-012144]
- J&J platform capability (EGFR/MET bispecific plus TKI combination): Rybrevant plus Lazcluze received first-line FDA approval on 2024-08-19 supported by MARIPOSA (NEJM 2024), and an OrigAMI-2 colorectal Phase 3 (NCT06662786) is recruiting. *(INTERPRETATION)* [CLM-012145]

## AbbVie

- AbbVie platform capability (antibody-drug conjugates): FDA records show Elahere (2022-11-14, sponsor ImmunoGen) and Emrelis (2025-05-14, AbbVie) approvals, Decnupaz (2026-05-27) approval, and a Temab-A Phase 2/3 with osimertinib (NCT07005102). *(INTERPRETATION)* [CLM-012146]
- AbbVie platform capability (immunology lifecycle management): FDA approved Skyrizi in Crohn's disease (2022-06-16) and ulcerative colitis (2024-06-18) and Rinvoq in atopic dermatitis (2022-01-14), ulcerative colitis (2022-03-16) and giant cell arteritis (2025-04-28). *(INTERPRETATION)* [CLM-012147]
- AbbVie neuroscience capability: tavapadon (D1/D5 partial agonist) has a published fixed-dose Phase 3 (JAMA Neurol 2026), an NDA submitted September 2025 and FDA approval as Juvmo on 2026-09-25, while emraclidine failed Phase 2. *(INTERPRETATION)* [CLM-012148]

## Takeda

- Takeda platform capability (orexin biology): oveporexton, an oral orexin-2 agonist, has NEJM Phase 2 (2025) and Phase 3 (2026-09-24) publications and was approved as Orzeyful on 2026-08-05. *(INTERPRETATION)* [CLM-012149]
- Takeda platform capability (oral TYK2 inhibition): zasocitinib has a Phase 2 publication (JAMA Dermatol 2024), two completed Phase 3 psoriasis registry entries, and a completed head-to-head Phase 3 versus deucravacitinib (NCT06973291). *(INTERPRETATION)* [CLM-012150]
- Takeda platform capability (in-licensed first-in-class assets): rusfertide (hepcidin mimetic, Protagonist) has a Phase 3 VERIFY publication in J Clin Oncol (2026-10) and FDA approval as Mimrylo on 2026-08-28. *(INTERPRETATION)* [CLM-012151]
- Takeda platform capability (RNAi): fazirsiran, a GalNAc siRNA, is in Phase 3 for alpha-1 antitrypsin liver disease (NCT05677971, primary completion estimated 2029-01-17). *(INTERPRETATION)* [CLM-012152]

Not evidenced in this run (gap): Lilly radioligand (POINT) and gene editing (Verve), J&J ADC via Ambrx and Legend relationship detail, AbbVie in-vivo CAR-T (Capstan), Takeda cell-therapy exit rationale beyond the impairment disclosure [CLM-012123].
