Revenue exposure by product: use Part D gross cost figures in the claims below and the already-registered financial claims (CLM-000001..000238); product-level company revenue not re-registered here (gap).

- CMS set a negotiated 30-day price of $4,695 for Stelara (Janssen) for 2026, a 66% discount from the $13,836 2023 list price; 2023 Part D gross cost was $2,988,560,000. [CLM-008008]
- CMS set a negotiated 30-day price of $197 for Xarelto (Janssen) for 2026, a 62% discount from the $517 2023 list price; 2023 Part D gross cost was $6,309,766,000. [CLM-008009]
- CMS set a negotiated 30-day price of $9,319 for Imbruvica (Pharmacyclics) for 2026, a 38% discount from the $14,934 2023 list price; 2023 Part D gross cost was $2,371,858,000. [CLM-008010]
- CMS deselected Stelara and Xarelto from the negotiation program effective January 1, 2027, with determinations in October 2025. [CLM-008011]
- CMS set a negotiated 2027 30-day price of $136 for Linzess (AbbVie), a 75% discount from the $539 2024 list price; 2024 Part D gross cost was $1,982,587,000. [CLM-008012]
- CMS set a negotiated 2027 30-day price of $770 for Vraylar (AbbVie), a 44% discount from the $1,376 2024 list price; 2024 Part D gross cost was $1,136,814,000. [CLM-008013]
- CMS estimated the second-cycle negotiated prices would have saved about $12 billion (about 44%) of 2024 net Part D spending on the 15 drugs, excluding Coverage Gap Discount Program effects. [CLM-008014]
- On January 27, 2026 CMS selected 15 drugs for the third cycle (prices effective 2028), including Lilly's Trulicity ($4.90B Part B/D spend) and Verzenio ($1.43B), J&J's Erleada ($1.95B), AbbVie's Botox ($1.14B) and Takeda's Entyvio ($1.48B). [CLM-008015]
- CMS announced on March 13, 2026 that the manufacturers of all 15 third-cycle drugs, including Lilly, Janssen and AbbVie, chose to participate in negotiation. [CLM-008016]
- Third-cycle negotiated prices were not located in any source opened; negotiations were to end by November 1, 2026. [CLM-008017]
- AbbVie's FY2025 10-K states CMS selected Imbruvica (2023), Vraylar and Linzess (2025) and Botox (January 2026) for government-set Medicare prices. [CLM-008018]
- AbbVie recorded a pre-tax $2.1 billion impairment on the Imbruvica intangible in Q3 2023 after its IRA selection (fair value $1.9B versus carrying value $4.0B). [CLM-008019]
- AbbVie states that from January 2025 the Part D coverage gap discount was replaced by a 10% manufacturer discount (and 20% above the $2,000 out-of-pocket threshold). [CLM-008020]
- Lilly's FY2025 10-K reports Jardiance (Boehringer collaboration) in the first cycle at a 66% discount, Trulicity and Verzenio selected January 2026, and expects more Lilly products to be selected. [CLM-008021]
- Takeda's 20-F states CMS selected Entyvio, its highest-selling product in the year ended March 31, 2026, for negotiation effective January 2028. [CLM-008022]
- Janssen sued HHS/CMS in July 2023 challenging the negotiation program on First and Fifth Amendment grounds; the Third Circuit affirmed denial of its summary judgment motion and Janssen petitioned the Supreme Court in December 2025. [CLM-008023]
- The U.S. Supreme Court denied certiorari in Janssen Pharmaceuticals v. Kennedy (No. 25-749) on May 18, 2026, along with petitions from other manufacturers. [CLM-008024]
- J&J's FY2025 10-K reports U.S. Stelara sales of about $3.8 billion and Immunology sales down 11.8%, driven by Stelara biosimilars, with more biosimilar launches expected. [CLM-008025]

reports.title: Litigation with a policy dimension
reports.markdown:
# Litigation with a policy dimension

Scope: Lilly, J&J, AbbVie (Takeda briefly). Neutral: documents activity and outcomes only; no causal inference about influence. Research cutoff 2026-11-21. Sources: shard A8_policy.

## Litigation, 340B, compounding, patents
- Lilly sued HRSA in November 2024 over its rejection of a 340B cash replenishment model; the D.D.C. ruled in May 2025 that HRSA must preapprove such a model and Lilly appealed. [CLM-008038]
- On July 21, 2026 the D.C. Circuit held that manufacturers cannot adopt 340B rebate models without HRSA approval, in a consolidated appeal arising from suits that include J&J (filed 2024-11-12) and Lilly (filed 2024-11-14). [CLM-008039]
- HRSA's first 340B rebate pilot (announced July 2025) was blocked by a federal court and withdrawn in February 2026; a revised pilot notice was published August 3, 2026 for January 1, 2027, limited to drugs with negotiated prices. [CLM-008040]
- HRSA's 2027 rebate pilot cohort of 10 manufacturers and 21 drugs does not include J&J's Stelara and Xarelto, which left the negotiation program. [CLM-008041]
- Hospitals sued Lilly in July 2026 over its policy requiring 340B claims data for all covered drugs, according to HFMA. [CLM-008042]
- Lilly's 10-K says its January 2021 suit against HHS over 340B contract-pharmacy policy remains pending at the Seventh Circuit, and a Mosaic Health class action against Lilly and others is ongoing. [CLM-008043]
- J&J's 10-K describes a policy limiting contract-pharmacy 340B deliveries for non-grantee covered entities, with exceptions. [CLM-008044]
- FDA's December 19, 2024 declaratory order found the tirzepatide shortage resolved; tirzepatide was listed December 15, 2022 and delisted October 2, 2024. [CLM-008045]
- Lilly's 10-K says mass-compounded incretins persist and Lilly will consider lawsuits against unlawful practices. [CLM-008046]
- An April 20, 2026 N.D. Cal. order granted in part and denied in part a motion to dismiss in Lilly v. Mochi Health (No. 3:25-cv-03534), a case over compounded tirzepatide marketing. [CLM-008047]
- The Seventh Circuit affirmed dismissal of the Humira patent-thicket antitrust complaint (Baltimore v. AbbVie) on August 1, 2022. [CLM-008048]
- In January 2025 payors filed a putative class action alleging AbbVie's rebating practices impair Humira biosimilar competition. [CLM-008049]
- J&J's talc strategy moved from a prepackaged plan of about $6.475 billion present value (May 2024) to the Red River bankruptcy (September 2024), dismissed in March 2025; about $7 billion of reserve was reversed and about $3.4 billion remained at Q4 2025. [CLM-008050]
- J&J's July 2021 opioid settlement of state and subdivision claims was up to $5.0 billion, about 80% paid by end of FY2025; about 23 state cases and 285 MDL cases remain. [CLM-008051]
- Lilly faces insulin-pricing MDL litigation in D.N.J. and settled with New York (2023) and Minnesota (2024) without payment or admission. [CLM-008052] *Contrary/caveat:* Project brief dated the Minnesota settlement 2023.

## Congressional testimony
- Eli Lilly CEO David Ricks was listed as a witness at the Senate HELP Committee hearing on insulin affordability on May 10, 2023. [CLM-008053]
- On January 26, 2024 Sen. Sanders announced J&J, Merck and BMS CEOs agreed to testify voluntarily, ending a planned subpoena vote. [CLM-008054]

**Not covered:** AbbVie 2021 House Oversight testimony, EU pharma legislation positions, march-in proposals (gap).

- On January 8, 2026 Johnson & Johnson announced a voluntary agreement with the administration covering TrumpRx participation, Medicaid prices comparable to other developed countries and an exemption from tariffs, and reaffirmed its $55 billion investment through early 2029. [CLM-008031]
- On January 12, 2026 AbbVie announced a three-year voluntary agreement with $100 billion of U.S. R&D and capital investment over a decade, low Medicaid prices, TrumpRx offerings and exemption from tariffs and future pricing mandates. [CLM-008032] *Contrary/caveat:* Working figure of USD 10bn in the project brief is not supported by either source.
- The Federal Register published on April 16, 2025 a Commerce notice requesting comments on a Section 232 national-security investigation of imports of pharmaceuticals and pharmaceutical ingredients. [CLM-008033]
- Lilly's FY2025 10-K states pharmaceuticals are exempt from certain tariffs but that the exemptions may end, and that Lilly may be unable to share tariff cost burdens. [CLM-008034]
- Takeda's 20-F states a May 2025 executive order encouraged Most Favored Nation pricing and that the administration has negotiated MFN-style agreements with several companies, which could lower Takeda's U.S. prices. [CLM-008035]
- Takeda's 20-F states annual NHI price revisions since April 2021 have led to more frequent downward revisions in Japan, and a surcharge on long-listed originator drugs applies from June 1, 2026. [CLM-008036]
- Across Lilly, J&J and AbbVie, each January 2026 or November 2025 agreement pairs stated price or access concessions with a stated three-year (Lilly, AbbVie) or unspecified-term tariff exemption. [CLM-008037] *(INTERPRETATION)*

reports.title: A14 gap-fill findings (wave 2)
reports.markdown:
# A14 gap-fill findings (wave 2)

Research cutoff 2026-11-21. Shard `A14_gapfill` (SRC/CLM-014000..014074). Every sentence ends with claim IDs; unlabelled reading is marked *(INTERPRETATION)* or *(gap)*. Company releases are interested-party documents. Claim IDs `CLM-0140xx` resolve in `New_mediciine/evidence_library/shards/A14_gapfill/claims.jsonl`; `SRC-004xxx` / `SRC-000xxx` are canonical registry IDs.

## 1. Lilly: earnings 8-K exhibits (Q4 2025, Q3 2026)

**Established**
- Lilly's Q4 2025 release (8-K Ex. 99.1, filed 2026-02-04) reports FY2025 revenue of USD 65,179m (+45%): Mounjaro USD 22,965m, Zepbound USD 13,542m, Verzenio USD 5,723m. [CLM-014000]
- FY2025 R&D was USD 13,337m and acquired IPR&D USD 2,910m. Q4 2025 realized price fell 5% while volume rose 46%. [CLM-014004]
- Initial 2026 guidance was revenue USD 80-83bn, non-GAAP EPS USD 33.50-35.00 and performance margin 46.0-47.5%. [CLM-014001]
- The brief's "USD 91-92bn" is the raised guidance in the Q3 2026 release (2026-10-29), which lifted the revenue midpoint by USD 5.5bn from USD 85-87bn. Q3 2026 revenue was USD 24,397m (+39%). [CLM-014002]
- Q3 2026 revenue included about USD 900m of one-off benefits (USD 410m Jardiance milestones, rebate/discount estimate adjustments). Realized price fell 15% and volume rose 53%. [CLM-014003]
- The 10-K (not the 8-K) is the only filed source that quantifies LillyDirect: self-pay sales through LillyDirect were "a growing portion" of 2025 business, with no dollar figure. [CLM-014006]
- Neither earnings exhibit contains LillyDirect, self-pay, OSA or HFpEF statements. [CLM-014005]
- Zepbound/Mounjaro OSA is recorded as "approved in the U.S. and the EU in 2024" and HFpEF as "submitted in 2024"; the FY2025 10-K shows HFpEF "approved in the EU" only. [CLM-014007]

**Contested / unknown**: exact FDA action dates for OSA and the U.S. HFpEF outcome *(gap)*. Q3/9M 2026 are partial periods.

Integrate into: `New_mediciine/companies/eli_lilly/` dossier §2 (financials) and §4 (commercial/access); correct any "USD 91-92bn" attribution to "raised in Q3 2026 (Oct 29, 2026); initial Feb 2026 guidance USD 80-83bn".

## 2. Lilly manufacturing: announced vs operating

| Site | Announced (amount) | Stated operational date | Evidence of production | Claim |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Concord, NC | 2022-01-28, USD 1bn, later USD 2bn | n/a | Trade report quoting site head: commercial production and shipments from end-2024 | [CLM-014014] |
| Lebanon, IN (Advanced Therapies) | part of USD 4.5bn (2026-05-06) | opened 2026-05-06 | Opened (company release) | [CLM-014015] |
| Lebanon, IN (API) | USD 9bn total (2024), +USD 4.5bn across two sites | "opens in 2027" | Not operating (USD 9bn 2024 figure: CLM-001038) | [CLM-014015] [CLM-001038] |
| Kenosha, WI | USD 3bn expansion (2024-12-05; USD 4bn total WI) | Spokesperson: production 2028 (news snippet) | Acquired plant existing; expansion under construction | [CLM-014013] |
| Alzey, DE | USD 2.5bn (2023-11) | "beginning in 2027" | None found | [CLM-014012] |
| Limerick, IE | USD 2bn total (expansion 2024-09) | "on track to start in 2026" | Not confirmed; Kinsale (USD 800m) producing since 2023 | [CLM-014011] |
| Houston, TX | USD 6.5bn (2025-09-23) | within five years | Groundbreaking 2026-09-21 | [CLM-014008] |
| Alabama (Huntsville) | >USD 6bn (2025-12-09) | completion 2032 | None; construction from 2026 | [CLM-014009] |
| Pennsylvania (Lehigh Valley) | >USD 3.5bn (2026-01-30) | operational 2031 | None | [CLM-014010] |
| Richmond/Goochland, VA | USD 5bn (2025-09-16) | n/a | Groundbreaking listed in Q3 2026 8-K (announcement terms: CLM-001040) | [CLM-014016] [CLM-001040] |

- The FY2025 10-K names only Indiana, North Carolina, Puerto Rico and Wisconsin among "major production sites" and says more facilities "are expected to come online in future periods". [CLM-014016]
- Capex was USD 7.8bn in 2025 (USD 5.1bn in 2024); construction in progress was USD 13,013m at year-end 2025 versus USD 8,245m. [CLM-014017]
- *(INTERPRETATION)* Most of the "USD 50bn+" pledge is under construction or pre-construction; only Concord, Kinsale and the Lebanon genetic-medicine plant show operating evidence.

Integrate into: `New_mediciine/companies/eli_lilly/` dossier §9 (manufacturing).

## 3. J&J: Varipulse, aticaprant, DePuy Synthes separation, OTTAVA/MONARCH/VELYS, talc

**Varipulse.** FDA's correction notice: approved November 2024; 4 of 132 patients (about 3%) in the U.S. External Evaluation had stroke/TIA versus about 1% expected; Instructions for Use updated 2025-02-14 for all lots (most serious recall class, correction not removal); a post-approval study is planned. [CLM-014018]

**Aticaprant.** J&J discontinued the Phase 3 VENTURA programme on 2025-03-06 for insufficient efficacy; safety was acceptable. [CLM-014019]

**DePuy Synthes.** Intent to separate Orthopaedics announced 2025-10-14 (FY2024 sales about USD 9.2bn; Namal Nawana named Worldwide President). [CLM-014020] The 10-K targets completion 18-24 months after announcement; Orthopaedics FY2025 sales were USD 9.3bn (+1.1%). [CLM-014021]

**Surgical robotics.**
- OTTAVA De Novo DEN250068 was granted 2026-07-21 (received 2025-12-18), Class II, upper-abdominal general laparoscopic procedures. [CLM-014022]
- First IDE cases were early 2025; a hernia IDE was approved late 2025. [CLM-014023]
- The first early-access commercial installation was announced 2026-11-19. [CLM-014024]
- Duato had guided approval "by the end of this year, beginning of next year"; FDA acted earlier. [CLM-014070]
- MONARCH QUEST 3: J&J announced 510(k) clearance 2026-08-17; openFDA lists K260382 (Auris Health, decided 2026-07-25), whose link to the "QUEST 3" name is inferred. [CLM-014025]
- VELYS: openFDA lists K202769, K233227, K240211, K253551 (hip navigation) and K260480 (2026-06-25). [CLM-014026]
- No installed-base or procedure-count figure was found for VELYS, MONARCH or OTTAVA *(gap)*.

**Talc.**
- Judge Lopez denied confirmation of the Red River plan and dismissed the case on 2025-03-31. [CLM-014027]
- J&J reversed about USD 7bn of reserve, did not appeal, and carried a USD 3.4bn reserve at Q4 2025. [CLM-014028]
- On 2026-07-27 J&J announced a USD 5.5bn conditional resolution of about 76,000 remaining ovarian claims (first payment no more than USD 3bn in 2027; at least 95% participation required). Outcome unknown. [CLM-014029]

Integrate into: `New_mediciine/companies/johnson_johnson/` dossier (MedTech/robotics, failures, litigation, portfolio sections) and `industry_transformation/ai_data_robotics/` landscape (OTTAVA/MONARCH/VELYS regulatory record).

## 4. AbbVie: deal terms, Humira settlement history, Juvmo date

- Capstan: USD 2.1bn cash (USD 1.9bn net of cash acquired), asset acquisition expensed to IPR&D in Q3 2025; completion announced 2025-08-19. Lead asset is Phase 1. [CLM-014030]
- Other upfronts in the 10-Ks: Gilgamesh USD 906m, Ichnos Glenmark USD 700m, Gubra USD 350m, ADARx option USD 335m (2025); Aliada USD 1.4bn, Celsius USD 250m (2024). [CLM-014031]
- Aliada: USD 1.4bn cash (announced 2024-10-28, closed December 2024). AbbVie's release states J&J's venture arm JJDC co-founded Aliada and J&J scientists created its BBB-shuttle platform. [CLM-014032]
- Landos: USD 20.42/share (about USD 137.5m) plus a CVR worth up to USD 11.14/share (about USD 75m); completion 2024-05-23 per release snippet. [CLM-014033]
- Nimble: completed 2025-01-23 at USD 288m (USD 210m upfront plus contingent consideration, up to USD 130m further). [CLM-014034]
- Cerevel: USD 45.00/share, USD 8.7bn, completed 2024-08-01; assumed Pfizer licence with up to USD 1.6bn of milestones. [CLM-014035]
- Humira settlements: licences for U.S. biosimilars begin 2023 (Europe 2018); settlement terms are not disclosed. [CLM-014036] The 2019 indirect-purchaser antitrust suit was dismissed in June 2020 and appealed (later outcome not verified). [CLM-014037]
- Humira was about 27% of 2023 revenue. [CLM-014038]
- Juvmo: FDA approval 2026-09-25 (Drugs.com; Reuters snippet); AbbVie announced on 2026-09-28. The two dates are the FDA action and the company release. [CLM-014039] The NDA was submitted September 2025. [CLM-014040]

Integrate into: `New_mediciine/companies/abbvie/` dossier (M&A/pipeline/competitive sections); resolves wave-1's Juvmo 09-25 vs 09-28 question.

## 5. Takeda: Annual Integrated Report, ventures, R&D Day footnote, Entyvio, Amitiza

- The 2026 Annual Integrated Report (FY2025) was opened via pypdf (55 pages). It reports 170+ AI predictive-maintenance agents at Lessines. [CLM-014041]
- One Day Batch Release: six-site pilots, target of 60% shorter release lead time by 2028 and global rollout by 2029. [CLM-014042]
- 63.4% of the workforce actively used generative AI at 31 March 2026 (46.6% a year earlier). [CLM-014043]
- Takami transformation programme: qualitative benefits, no spend disclosed. [CLM-014044]
- AI partners named: Nabla Bio, TetraScience, APHERIS. [CLM-014045]
- On-time in-full rate was 99.6%; BioLife nomogram and Smart Donor Care were rolled out. [CLM-014046]
- R&D Day Dec-2024 footnote: the USD 10-20bn peak revenue range is not adjusted for probability of success and "should not be considered a forecast or target". [CLM-014049]
- Entyvio: some patents expire in 2032; UK/Netherlands revocation actions filed Feb-Apr 2026. [CLM-014050] Biosimilar BLAs (Alvotech AVT16, Fresenius/Polpharma PB016) accepted for FDA review. The Purple Book entry was not opened, so exclusivity status is unconfirmed. [CLM-014051]
- Takeda Ventures, Inc. is a 100%-owned subsidiary; no fund size or Center for External Innovation description exists in primary sources opened. [CLM-014052]
- Amitiza: jury verdict 2026-05-18 of USD 884.9m single damages (subject to trebling for two groups). Takeda booked a JPY 403.5bn provision and plans post-trial motions and appeal. Final judgment amount and post-trial status are unverified. [CLM-014048] [CLM-014047]

Integrate into: `New_mediciine/companies/takeda_public_baseline/` dossier (DD&T, manufacturing, pipeline footnote, IP, litigation).

## 6. AI/robotics: FDA device records, TuneLab, NVIDIA lab, Strateos

- FDA device records for OTTAVA/MONARCH/VELYS are covered in section 3. [CLM-014022] [CLM-014025] [CLM-014026]
- NVIDIA-Lilly co-innovation lab: announced 2026-01-12 with up to USD 1bn over five years; work "expected to begin in South San Francisco early this year". No source opened confirms it is operating. [CLM-014053]
- LillyPod: 1,016 Blackwell Ultra GPUs, more than 9,000 petaflops, inaugurated in Indianapolis; vendor blog, date unresolved. [CLM-014054]
- TuneLab: federated-learning platform on NVIDIA FLARE; partner releases from Charles River (2026-06-18), Twist (2026-09-16), Axcelead and Korean biotechs. No participant count or retraining result. [CLM-014055] [CLM-014056]
- Strateos: aggregators say Multiply Labs acquired it in December 2023, but no primary source was found, so it remains unverified. [CLM-014057]

Integrate into: `New_mediciine/industry_transformation/ai_data_robotics/` landscape and evidence_gaps (items 1, 4, 5).

## 7. Partnerships: deal terms and venture-arm scale

- Lilly asset-acquisition expense: DICE USD 1,915.5m, Versanis USD 604.1m, Emergence USD 406.5m, Mablink USD 256.6m, Beam opt-in USD 216.3m (2023); Morphic USD 2,548.5m (2024). [CLM-014058]
- Lilly 2021-22: Foghorn USD 316.6m, Rigel USD 125.0m, BioMarin PRV USD 110.0m; IPR&D totals USD 970.1m (2021) and USD 908.5m (2022). [CLM-014059]
- Takeda upfronts: HUTCHMED USD 400m (April 2023, up to USD 730m more) and Protagonist USD 300m (April 2024). [CLM-014060]
- Takeda upfronts: Keros USD 200m (February 2025) and Innovent USD 1.2bn (December 2025). [CLM-014061]
- Takeda upfronts: Nimbus USD 4.0bn and AC Immune USD 100m. [CLM-014062]
- Lilly's a16z fund: USD 500m, Lilly-funded (January 2025). No standalone Lilly Ventures fund size found. [CLM-014063]
- JLABS has shrunk: 11 sites (August 2025) after Toronto, Houston and Washington D.C. exits; a snippet says New York is closing, leaving three U.S. sites. [CLM-014064] [CLM-014065]
- No JJDC, AbbVie Ventures or Takeda Ventures portfolio counts were found in primary sources. [CLM-014066] [CLM-014052]

Integrate into: `New_mediciine/industry_transformation/partnerships_ecosystem/` reports (deal ledger, venture arms); update JLABS "scale" statements.

## 8. Leadership statements (one inspected source per company)

- Lilly (Ricks, podcast ~Nov 2025): GLP-1s are "probably 80% of the economic value"; R&D at 20-25% of sales. [CLM-014067] Gateway Labs/Catalyze360 are framed as an experiment that "may not work". [CLM-014068]
- J&J (Duato, Bernstein 2026-05-27): 2026 guidance 6.1% adjusted operational growth, over USD 100bn. [CLM-014069] AI is used in molecule design and clinical operations, with no named programmes or metrics. [CLM-014071] The OTTAVA approval-timing expectation was beaten. [CLM-014070]
- AbbVie (Michael, Q4 2025 call): record USD 61.2bn ex-IPR&D revenue despite about USD 16bn of U.S. Humira erosion; 90 clinical programmes; more than USD 5bn of business development. [CLM-014072]
- Takeda (Weber, Semafor Jan 2026): goal to double research productivity with AI; about 30% shorter narcolepsy development time (single-source claim). [CLM-014073] Kim's May 2026 letter sets "two horizons" and an AI-heavy reorganisation. [CLM-014074]

Integrate into: leadership sections of each company dossier under `New_mediciine/companies/*/` and the strategy inputs.

## Brief and wave-1 corrections surfaced

- "USD 91-92bn" Lilly guidance dates from Q3 2026, not the February release. [CLM-014001] [CLM-014002]
- Juvmo FDA action date is 2026-09-25 and the announcement is 2026-09-28. [CLM-014039]
- Aliada originated in J&J's JJDC/J&J scientists, then sold to AbbVie. [CLM-014032]
- JLABS network is contracting. [CLM-014064]

reports.markdown:
# Director decision record — response to the Strategic Council and Red Team (2026-11-21)

Source of the challenges: [decision_memo_to_director.md](decision_memo_to_director.md), [council_reviews.md](council_reviews.md) (119 verdicts: 45 support / 64 conditional / 10 oppose; 17 recorded disagreements), [red_team.md](red_team.md), [scenario_stress_test.md](scenario_stress_test.md), [counterarguments_and_uncertainty.md](counterarguments_and_uncertainty.md) (95 items).
This record is authoritative for strategy v2. The v1 strategy files (A11c) are revised to match it by the A11c-bis pass; the deliverables cite v2. Nothing here is a reported fact about Takeda: every number is an ASSUMPTION or a council computation and is labelled as such in the strategy data.

| # | Council proposal | Director decision | Rationale (evidence or assumption) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | BET-15 (USD 5bn+ asset purchase, DEFER) → REJECT as framed; create a funded USD 0.5–2bn Phase 2/3 licensing channel (BET-18) | **ACCEPTED.** BET-15 → REJECT. Add BET-18 "Phase 2/3 in-licensing channel" as PARTNER/INVEST, sized USD 0.5–2bn contingent on IVB-012 (Amitiza cash) and the leverage ceiling (ASM-033). | The council's leverage arithmetic (2.6x → ~3.1–3.4x) breaks the strategy's own 3.0x ceiling; Takeda's observed pattern is mid-size licensing (Nimbus USD 4.0bn upfront, Innovent USD 1.2bn upfront — A9/A5 claims). BET-18 is council-proposed: its A–M template is completed by A11c-bis and labelled "v2 addition". |
| 2 | Widen ASM-025 (Entyvio biosimilar entry) from 2030–32 to 2028–32; add early-entry stress case; move RM-026 to 2028 H1 | **ACCEPTED.** | Two biosimilar BLAs under FDA review (A14 CLM-014051); exclusivity timing outside the registry (IVB-004 remains open). No extra capital. |
| 3 | BET-06 option engine: balanced USD 700m → constrained USD 300m, scorecard-first, balance contingent | **ACCEPTED.** | Commercial and capital councils oppose at USD 700m; option conversion rate is an unvalidated assumption (ASM-028). |
| 4 | BET-02 plasma: BUILD → EXPERIMENT (baseline + shadow-mode tranche); re-base ASM-031; add demand-vs-capacity and plasma-peer tests | **ACCEPTED** (Takeda-execution council's dissent recorded). | PDT revenue −1.5% CER does not show a capacity constraint (A5); no fixed-price vendor evidence; "unique data" rests on an absent peer set. |
| 5 | BET-03 orexin: USD 500m → 300m, Phase 1 gate before the H2 tranche, additionality test, competitor scan | **ACCEPTED.** | Base R&D (JPY 675.9bn, A5) likely already funds the programme; additionality unproven; competitor orexin programmes not in the registry (research gap logged). |
| 6 | BET-04 Entyvio defence stays BUILD; add a benefit-channel gate (IVB-004, 2027 H1); outcome reframed to "delay and measure" | **ACCEPTED.** | Humira held ≥97% volume yet lost 78.6% in three years (A3); medical-vs-pharmacy benefit split for Entyvio unknown. |
| 7 | BET-07 AI-design partnerships stays PARTNER; re-wire prerequisites to BET-01/BET-09; stop rules in contracts | **ACCEPTED.** | Roadmap RM-011 not wired to its stated prerequisites (council finding). |
| 8 | BET-11 drug-device/SC stays BUILD; baseline first; resolve conflict with BET-04 (SC moves patients into the PBM channel); confidence → hypothesis | **ACCEPTED.** | Conflict is real (A7 PBM evidence). |
| 9 | BET-12 launch pathways: cap USD 50m; attach to the oveporexton launch; start 2027 H1 | **ACCEPTED.** | Approval 2026-08-05 (A5); a 2027 H2 pilot is late. |
| 10 | Housekeeping: remove BET-13 carry (−USD 80m); move BET-17 measurement owner off the CFO; relabel six "evidence_backed" bets to hypothesis where a load-bearing claim is PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED/NEEDS_MORE_RESEARCH; fix text errors (CVS 15 months; stage-gate capital ≤ bet size) | **ACCEPTED.** | Audit and council both flagged these. |
| — | Council re-rating of 19/85 scenario cells (no bet robust in SCN-3; 53% of constrained envelope breaks in SCN-5) | **ACCEPTED as the published robustness table**; strategy's original ratings kept in the file as "author rating" for transparency. | Independent challenge outranks the author's self-rating under the ROS. |
| — | "Owned labs fail" narrative softened (Lilly's reason undisclosed; Strateos link unsupported; NVIDIA joint lab reads as re-platforming) | **ACCEPTED**; BET-10 stays REJECT (zero spend) with an operational trigger set. | A10 found CLM-006017 unsupported; A14 could not source the Strateos link. |

## Net effect (ASSUMPTION-basis figures)
Balanced envelope USD 2,950m → **~1,920m committed-at-gates**, with ~1,030m contingent headroom reserved for the licensing channel (BET-18) — not a saving. Core H1 2027–29 tranche ≈ USD 465m. Capital-constrained and ambitious portfolios are rescaled proportionally by A11c-bis and re-labelled v2.

## Not accepted / deferred
- The red team's opposition to any plasma spend (keep EXPERIMENT, not REJECT): the baseline/shadow-mode tranche is cheap and produces the data the council says is missing.
- Removing BET-03 entirely: orexin is Takeda's only evidenced in-house discovery success in the window (A5); the smaller gated size is the compromise.

## Open items carried to the internal-validation backlog
IVB-004 (Entyvio exclusivity/benefit channel), IVB-012 (Amitiza cash), IVB-014 (envelope), IVB-006 (plasma economics), new: competitor orexin landscape (research gap), statutory exclusivity date for Entyvio (research gap).

reports.title: Strategic Council review of the 17 bets (A11e, wave 5)
reports.markdown:
# Strategic Council review of the 17 bets (A11e, wave 5)

Research cutoff 2026-11-21. Independent challenge by a fresh-context agent. Claim IDs were re-checked against `claims_registry.jsonl`, including `correction`, `contrary_evidence` and status fields. Takeda fiscal years run April-March (FY2025 = April 2025 to March 2026). Bet decisions are those in `strategy/data/strategy_bets.json`; this file does not change them.

**How to read the verdicts.** A verdict is the council's stance on the *proposed decision as recorded* (BUILD, INVEST, PARTNER, EXPERIMENT, DEFER or REJECT). `support` backs the decision as written. `conditional` backs it only if the stated condition is met. `oppose` disputes the decision or its sizing. For REJECT and DEFER bets, `support` means the council endorses the REJECT or DEFER, and the rationale begins 'Endorses'. Councils were run independently and their disagreements are recorded in the log below, not averaged away. Dollar figures are the strategy's ASSUMPTIONs (ASM-002 to ASM-004, ASM-101 to ASM-117); Takeda's budget is not public (IVB-014).

**Claim-quality findings that apply to every council** (re-checked against the registry):

- Of 215 distinct claim IDs cited by the 17 bets, 134 are SUPPORTED, 57 PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED, 17 NEEDS_MORE_RESEARCH and 7 INCONCLUSIVE. The NEEDS_MORE_RESEARCH claims are mostly the registry's own HYPOTHESIS entries for the AI, plasma, orexin, registry and launch-pathway bets (CLM-011027 to CLM-011081), so those bets cite hypotheses as evidence.
- Six bets (BET-04, 05, 08, 09, 11, 16) are labelled `evidence_backed` although a load-bearing claim is PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED or NEEDS_MORE_RESEARCH (for example CLM-007053 for BET-11, CLM-011065 and CLM-011066 for BET-09, CLM-011054 for BET-08).
- Known errors that remain in the strategy text: 'CVS removed Zepbound for about 11 months [CLM-007011]' (the claim records an 11% share-price fall; CVS restored Zepbound from 1 October 2026 per CLM-007013, about 15 months); stage-gate capital at risk exceeds the bet size by USD 5m for BET-02, 07, 09 and 11; BET-13 is DEFER but funded USD 80m in the balanced envelope.
