reports.markdown:
# critical_challenges map (A11e, wave 5)

Research cutoff 2026-11-21. Independent Strategic Council and red team. Challenges the 17 bets in `strategy/data/strategy_bets.json`; does not edit bets, portfolios or roadmap. No registry writes.

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [council_reviews.md](council_reviews.md) | Seven councils by 17 bets (119 verdicts with rationale, unresolved items and claim IDs), verdict matrix, disagreements log, unresolved assumptions. |
| [red_team.md](red_team.md) | Strongest case against each bet, evidence, what must be true to survive, kill criteria, exposure rating. |
| [counterarguments_and_uncertainty.md](counterarguments_and_uncertainty.md) | View 12 content: 95 items (CA-001 to CA-095) across unsupported assumptions, unresolved questions, conflicting sources, public-knowledge gaps, failed hypotheses, alternative interpretations and caveats. |
| [scenario_stress_test.md](scenario_stress_test.md) | Council re-rating of the five scenarios, which bets break, SCN-5 numbers, leverage arithmetic, three added stress cases, robust core, capital timing against the Entyvio window. |
| [decision_memo_to_director.md](decision_memo_to_director.md) | Ten ranked proposed decision changes with evidence, dissent and envelope effect. |
| `../data/council_reviews.json` | 119 reviews and 17 disagreements, contract shape in `DATA_CONTRACT.md`. |
| `../data/counterarguments.json` | 95 items, contract shape in `DATA_CONTRACT.md`. |

## Build and validation

- `_data_reviews.py`, `_data_redteam.py`, `_data_counter.py`: source text for the three JSON and markdown outputs.
- `_build.py`: writes `council_reviews.json`, `counterarguments.json`, `council_reviews.md`, `red_team.md`, `counterarguments_and_uncertainty.md`; fails if any CLM id is absent from `claims_registry.jsonl`, any ASM id is absent from `assumptions.json`, a bet is missing a council, or a verdict is invalid.
- `_build_stress.py`: writes `scenario_stress_test.md` from `scenarios.json`, `strategy_bets.json` and the council's re-rating table.
- `_check_council.py`: runs the strategy's `_check_ids.py` logic over these files as well (the shipped checker does not scan this directory).

## Conventions

- A verdict is the council's stance on the proposed decision as recorded; for REJECT and DEFER bets, 'support' endorses the REJECT or DEFER.
- 'Council arithmetic' marks calculations made here from registry values and ASM-001; they are not Takeda disclosures.
- Outside-registry knowledge (for example the statutory 12-year biologic exclusivity period, plasma-industry peers, orexin competitors) is labelled and treated as unverified.

reports.title: Red team: the strongest case against each bet (A11e, wave 5)
reports.markdown:
# Red team: the strongest case against each bet (A11e, wave 5)

Research cutoff 2026-11-21. Each entry gives the strongest argument against the bet as recorded, the evidence (registry claims re-checked, with corrections), what would have to be true for the bet to survive, and kill criteria with a date or gate where one exists. 'Exposure' rates how much of the bet's case depends on the attacked premise: HIGH means the premise is load-bearing and unproven; MEDIUM means it is contestable but the bet survives with a changed framing; LOW means little is lost if the attack is right. Entries for REJECT and DEFER bets attack the *rejection*. Kill criteria that cite the stage-gate file reuse its stop tests; criteria marked 'council' are proposed here and are not in the stage gates.

## Exposure summary

| Bet | Decision | Exposure |
|---|---|---|
| BET-01 Governed cross-franchise R&D data and decision layer | BUILD | MEDIUM |
| BET-02 Plasma process-intelligence and fixed-price automation programme | BUILD | HIGH |
| BET-03 Orexin science as a multi-asset discovery platform | BUILD | HIGH |
| BET-04 Entyvio franchise defence: payer contracting, evidence and lifecycle | BUILD | MEDIUM |
| BET-05 Zasocitinib breadth and immunology successor evidence | INVEST | MEDIUM |
| BET-06 Option-based external innovation engine incl. new-modality options | PARTNER | HIGH |
| BET-07 Milestone-gated AI-design partnerships (Nabla, Iambic and successors) | PARTNER | HIGH |
| BET-08 Federated data consortium participation | PARTNER | LOW |
| BET-09 Rented automated data generation (CRO and cloud labs) with ladder triggers | PARTNER | LOW |
| BET-10 Owned autonomous discovery lab (stage 4-5) | REJECT | MEDIUM |
| BET-11 Drug-device and home/SC administration platform | BUILD | MEDIUM |
| BET-12 Launch-pathway partnerships and patient-services outcome measurement | EXPERIMENT | MEDIUM |
| BET-13 Neutral rare-disease or plasma real-world data registry | DEFER | LOW |
| BET-14 TuneLab-style productised external model platform | REJECT | LOW |
| BET-15 Large asset purchase (USD 5bn or more) as LOE bridge | DEFER | MEDIUM |
| BET-16 U.S. cash-pay direct-to-patient channel | REJECT | LOW |
| BET-17 AI use-case measurement, decision support and reskilling | EXPERIMENT | LOW |

## BET-01 Governed cross-franchise R&D data and decision layer (BUILD; exposure MEDIUM)

**Strongest case against.** A governance layer over a platform Takeda says it already has (a Databricks agent platform for 10,000+ employees, insourced digital factories) duplicates existing spend and will be judged by usage counts, the same failure visible in J&J's 47,000 course completions. No data layer at any company has an independent outcome, and the only Takeda outcome claim (about 30% shorter narcolepsy trial development) is one executive interview. If Takeda's estate is already governed, the incremental value is near zero and USD 200m is a sunk platform that is hard to stop.

**Evidence.** No independent outcome for ARCH, TuneLab, Polyphonic or the AISB model; the 'fragmented estate' premise is a NEEDS_MORE_RESEARCH hypothesis; platform maturity is vendor self-report; 63.4% workforce use is an adoption metric. [CLM-011052] [CLM-011055] [CLM-005058] [CLM-014073] [CLM-014043] [CLM-006022]

**What would have to be true for the bet to survive.**
- IVB-001 shows production use is thin or fragmented, not already governed.
- Two decisions can be baselined before any model is applied.
- A second function adopts the standard within 12 months.

**Kill criteria.**
- No decision baselined by 2027 H2 (the bet's own test), then stop and redirect to BET-08.
- Gate 3 (RM-015, 2027 H2) shows zero of two decisions with a measured effect on cycle time, hit rate or cost.
- Run cost exceeds measured benefit at scale gate.

## BET-02 Plasma process-intelligence and fixed-price automation programme (BUILD; exposure HIGH)

**Strongest case against.** The thesis rests on three unproven links: that plasma is capacity-bound (but H1 FY2026 PDT revenue was -1.5% at constant rates), that Takeda's process data are unique (the comparison set has no plasma peers), and that a fixed-price outcome-linked automation vendor exists (NEEDS_MORE_RESEARCH; the SpaceX source says its cost gap is not isolated and every cargo partner had catastrophic failures). Takeda has no public robotics evidence, a prior warning letter and shortage, and USD 230m of expansion without commissioning data. The follow-on of USD 350m is committed on a 2% threshold that has no economic anchor.

**Evidence.** PDT revenue +8.5% AER and -1.5% CER; no yield or productivity figures; no evidence of manufacturing robotics; Hikari warning letter with a USD 505m award; plasma peers (CSL, Grifols, Octapharma and others) are not in the registry. [CLM-005064] [CLM-005060] [CLM-005067] [CLM-005020] [CLM-011031] [CLM-011006] [CLM-011008] [CLM-005065]

**What would have to be true for the bet to survive.**
- IVB-006 shows yield or cost headroom above the pilot threshold that matters in money terms (ASM-031 must be re-based on cost per litre).
- At least one vendor prices fixed-price, outcome-linked terms for GMP automation.
- Validated change control does not trigger new inspection observations.
- Plasma is capacity-bound, so lower cost per litre converts to revenue.

**Kill criteria.**
- Baseline headroom below ASM-031 (re-based) by 2027 H2.
- No vendor accepts outcome-linked terms at feasibility.
- Any new inspection observation attributable to the pilot.
- PDT revenue stays flat or negative at CER after the Los Angeles capacity is commissioned (signals demand-bound).

## BET-03 Orexin science as a multi-asset discovery platform (BUILD; exposure HIGH)

**Strongest case against.** Takeda's record in the window is one in-house orexin success against a liver-safety stop (TAK-994), a Phase 3 miss (soticlestat) and an exited cell-therapy platform. Second-asset approval is a 5-30% proposition by the strategy's own range, payoff is 2038, and USD 500m is 17% of the balanced envelope. A platform does not protect a product (EYLEA -42% in 2025). Meanwhile the Entyvio window opens in 2031 and the capital arrives after it. An orexin discovery team already sits in base R&D, so the incremental USD 500m may fund work that would happen anyway.

**Evidence.** ASM-021 15%; RM-048 platform test 2038; TAK-994 liver signal; soticlestat Phase 3 miss and JPY 21.5bn impairment; no competitor orexin review; EYLEA -42%. [CLM-005023] [CLM-012119] [CLM-012120] [CLM-009083] [CLM-011017] [CLM-011037] [CLM-005025]

**What would have to be true for the bet to survive.**
- A second orexin asset with a clean safety profile exists by 2028.
- Competitors have no faster follower in the same indications.
- The USD 500m is additive to the Shonan base budget.

**Kill criteria.**
- No second target clears safety by gate 1 (2028).
- IND-enabling package incomplete by 2031 (RM-030 target H1 2030).
- Phase 2 fails on placebo response or exposure (LES-18).
- Single approval only after 2040: withdraw the platform claim.

## BET-04 Entyvio franchise defence: payer contracting, evidence and lifecycle (BUILD; exposure MEDIUM)

**Strongest case against.** Humira is the best analogue and it argues against the premise: rebate-for-access held at least 97% of volume for 14 months, a co-brand route followed, and global Humira still fell 78.6% in three years. AbbVie and J&J already sell competing IBD products, and PBMs now prefer their own biosimilars (CVS Stelara template, July 2026). The January 2028 Medicare price is statutory and cannot be contracted away. Contracting levers work in the pharmacy benefit; Entyvio IV may largely sit outside it (not in the registry). USD 140m will not change an exposure of JPY 383-766bn a year, so the real risk is that the programme is a visible reassurance with no measurable lever.

**Evidence.** Humira -78.6% 2022-2025; US Humira -41% (2024) and -57% (2025); Skyrizi, Rinvoq and Tremfya hold IBD approvals; four of nine Stelara biosimilars are PBM-affiliated private labels; Entyvio selected for Medicare negotiation. [CLM-003002] [CLM-003007] [CLM-003010] [CLM-003016] [CLM-002053] [CLM-007015] [CLM-007016] [CLM-007026]

**What would have to be true for the bet to survive.**
- IVB-004 shows a material pharmacy-benefit share of Entyvio that contracting can act on.
- A named lever moves net price or volume by a measurable amount against the ASM-024 low case.
- Patent posture (2032 patents, UK and Netherlands revocation actions) holds long enough for the playbook to matter.

**Kill criteria.**
- IVB-004 (RM-003, 2027 H1) shows that most Entyvio volume is outside the contractable channel: redirect funds to provider and site-of-care strategy.
- Retained net revenue below the ASM-024 low case at the first annual review after the 2028 price.
- Biosimilar FDA approval and a launch date before RM-026 (playbook live 2029 H2): re-date the playbook.

## BET-05 Zasocitinib breadth and immunology successor evidence (INVEST; exposure MEDIUM)

**Strongest case against.** J&J's oral IL-23 peptide (Icotyde) was approved on 2026-03-17 with head-to-head superiority claims, so zasocitinib's head-to-head win over deucravacitinib is against the weaker comparator. Skyrizi and Tremfya hold psoriasis and IBD; Takeda would enter with a first launch under a new CEO, after 4,500 role reductions. The bet is correct to exist, but breadth is incremental money on a binary PsA readout in May 2027, and zasocitinib is not an Entyvio GI successor.

**Evidence.** Icotyde approval and head-to-head claims; PsA Phase 3 completion May 2027; milestones USD 1.0bn each at USD 4bn and 5bn net sales; USD 10-20bn peak is not probability-adjusted; inspection-driven CRLs at Lilly and AbbVie. [CLM-012012] [CLM-002065] [CLM-005034] [CLM-005037] [CLM-009076] [CLM-014049] [CLM-012134] [CLM-012112]

**What would have to be true for the bet to survive.**
- PsA is positive and coverage at 6 and 12 months meets plan.
- Payers accept TYK2 oral therapy at parity with IL-23 oral and injectable products.
- NDA-supporting sites are inspection-clean.

**Kill criteria.**
- PsA misses primary endpoint (2027).
- Coverage and uptake below plan at 12 months.
- FDA action slips beyond 2027 H2 on inspection grounds.

## BET-06 Option-based external innovation engine incl. new-modality options (PARTNER; exposure HIGH)

**Strongest case against.** No option from the window has produced an approved product, per-asset probability is 5-15%, and payoff is 2035 or later, so the engine does not bridge the 2031-34 Entyvio window. USD 700m over 14 years is smaller than one Takeda deal in 2025 (Innovent, USD 1.2bn upfront), so the 'engine' is sized to lose bidding contests to AbbVie (ADARx, Capstan) and Lilly (Verve), while the mid-size Phase 2/3 licences that actually produced Takeda's late-stage pipeline have no funded bet. Neuroscience, gene and cell therapy are where write-downs concentrate, and Takeda has just exited cell therapy at JPY 58.2bn.

**Evidence.** ASM-028 0.1; Innovent USD 1.2bn upfront; Denali and Neurocrine terminations; CEI and Ventures scope unknown; Lilly IPR&D expensed 2023-25 with no approval from those assets by cutoff. [CLM-009097] [CLM-009078] [CLM-009089] [CLM-009090] [CLM-014052] [CLM-009061] [CLM-009010] [CLM-009000] [CLM-009084]

**What would have to be true for the bet to survive.**
- Takeda's selection skill transfers from Phase 3 assets to Phase 1 options.
- Option fees stay within the scorecard bands.
- A separate funding line exists for Phase 2/3 licences.

**Kill criteria.**
- No deal-outcome scorecard by 2027 H1 (RM-007).
- Counterparty terminates one of the first three options.
- Conversion below 5% at the three-year review (ASM-028 low), or impairment above 54% of deal value (the Cerevel benchmark).

## BET-07 Milestone-gated AI-design partnerships (Nabla, Iambic and successors) (PARTNER; exposure HIGH)

**Strongest case against.** The partner owns the model and Takeda owns an invoice. Lilly holds Isomorphic, Chai, OpenAI and NVIDIA compute; AbbVie holds BigHat and Valkai; five pharmas share the AISB fine-tune. Evidence that AI-origin molecules do better is absent (Recursion four of 11 ended; AI-origin Phase 2 about conventional; rentosertib liver discontinuations). Takeda's own gates are mis-sequenced, because the Nabla window opens before the comparator infrastructure exists. Success-based payments over USD 1bn per deal are liabilities that rise only if the science works.

**Evidence.** Nabla first-in-human is a company expectation; Iambic payments could exceed USD 1.7bn; Isomorphic raised a reported USD 600m; models converge on open weights. [CLM-006047] [CLM-006048] [CLM-006049] [CLM-006039] [CLM-006041] [CLM-006012] [CLM-006010] [CLM-006035] [CLM-006043] [CLM-006056]

**What would have to be true for the bet to survive.**
- Nabla first-in-human data are positive against a conventional comparator.
- Takeda retains ownership of its assay and clinical data fed to partners.
- A benchmark exists before the data arrive.

**Kill criteria.**
- Nabla first-in-human absent or negative by 2028 H2.
- Success-based payments committed grow faster than data-gated milestones achieved.
- Phase 2 transition below conventional for two review cycles.

## BET-08 Federated data consortium participation (PARTNER; exposure LOW)

**Strongest case against.** Cheap parity: Takeda is a follower in a consortium whose founding partners for the follow-on binding model are AbbVie, AstraZeneca, BMS and J&J. A pooled model that is 10 points better on a vendor-organised benchmark may not help Takeda targets, and the advantage accrues to whoever uses it best, which depends on the BET-01 decision layer that is itself unproven.

**Evidence.** AISB Bind lists AbbVie, AstraZeneca, BMS and J&J; the benchmark is vendor-organised and not peer reviewed. [CLM-006044] [CLM-006043] [CLM-006056] [CLM-006008]

**What would have to be true for the bet to survive.**
- Held-out gain on Takeda targets beats public and Takeda-only models.
- Raw data never leaves Takeda governance.

**Kill criteria.**
- Pooled model does not beat alternatives at RM-006 (2027 H1).
- Two annual reviews without gain.

## BET-09 Rented automated data generation (CRO and cloud labs) with ladder triggers (PARTNER; exposure LOW)

**Strongest case against.** Rented capacity is available to every rival, including AI-biotech entrants, so it yields parity not advantage. The evidence for renting over owning is a divestiture with an undisclosed reason plus an industrial-biotech failure; Lilly's later USD 1bn joint lab suggests the opposite lesson. The data-schema moat requires a standard that the roadmap delays behind a BET-17 inventory.

**Evidence.** Reason for Lilly's sale undisclosed; Strateos link unsupported; Zymergen is not a drug-discovery lab; Arctoris sells data generation to AI customers. [CLM-006017] [CLM-006014] [CLM-006051] [CLM-006016] [CLM-000281] [CLM-006052]

**What would have to be true for the bet to survive.**
- CRO cost per data point is at or below Takeda's internal baseline.
- Data ownership and schema are enforceable in the contract.

**Kill criteria.**
- Cost above internal baseline at RM-018 (2028 H1).
- Vendor quality fails twice.
- No trigger fires by the 2032 ladder review: stop stage-3 planning.

## BET-10 Owned autonomous discovery lab (stage 4-5) (REJECT; exposure MEDIUM)

**Strongest case against.** (Attack on the REJECT.) The rejection leans on 'two owned-model failures' that are really one divestiture of undisclosed cause and one company in another sector, while Lilly is investing up to USD 1bn jointly with NVIDIA and USD 4.5bn in a Medicine Foundry. If an owned closed-loop lab works in 2029-31 and Takeda has not built the data layer and CRO relationships, it will be years behind. The rejection is right for 2027 and wrong if the trigger set cannot be acted on.

**Evidence.** Lilly lab at concept; no independent outcome; triggers are NEEDS_MORE_RESEARCH. [CLM-006017] [CLM-006051] [CLM-000281] [CLM-006000] [CLM-011066] [CLM-006052]

**What would have to be true for the bet to survive.**
- Triggers have dates, owners and a pre-agreed response.
- BET-01 and BET-09 exist so a stage-3 pilot can start within 12 months of a trigger.

**Kill criteria.**
- Independent, audited cycle-time or hit-rate gain from the Lilly lab or any peer by 2029: reopen as a rented stage-3 pilot, not an owned build.
- Nabla first-in-human positive versus conventional: reopen.

## BET-11 Drug-device and home/SC administration platform (BUILD; exposure MEDIUM)

**Strongest case against.** SC is table stakes: Tremfya, Skyrizi and Rinvoq are already convenient, and the biosimilars in review are IV. SC moves Entyvio patients into the pharmacy benefit, where PBM private-label biosimilar templates operate, so the pen could accelerate erosion after entry. Device IP does not outlive the drug's own protection, and Takeda has not shown persistence data.

**Evidence.** CLM-007053 is PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED yet the bet is labelled evidence_backed; PBM template from 1 July 2026; four of nine Stelara biosimilars are PBM-affiliated. [CLM-007053] [CLM-007015] [CLM-007016] [CLM-014051] [CLM-007042] [CLM-002026]

**What would have to be true for the bet to survive.**
- SC users persist better after biosimilar entry than IV users.
- SC does not cannibalise IV before exclusivity loss.

**Kill criteria.**
- SC erodes net price faster than it retains patients (stage-gate stop).
- No retention effect after entry (RM-040, 2033).
- Device recall or clearance setback.

## BET-12 Launch-pathway partnerships and patient-services outcome measurement (EXPERIMENT; exposure MEDIUM)

**Strongest case against.** No company publishes persistence or time-to-therapy outcomes, so the bet has no benchmark and the hypothesis that pathways govern launch speed is untested. Oveporexton was approved on 2026-08-05; the pilot starts in 2027 H2 and reports in 2028 H2, after the launch curve forms. Pear's failure shows payers, not evidence, decide.

**Evidence.** Help at Hand is an enrolment count; Spravato and Carvykti constraints were certification and capacity; AbbVie's Allē change reversed within months. [CLM-007039] [CLM-007037] [CLM-011070] [CLM-007045] [CLM-007046] [CLM-003033] [CLM-005029]

**What would have to be true for the bet to survive.**
- Oveporexton uptake is pathway-limited.
- Hub data can be owned and measured.

**Kill criteria.**
- No pathway bottleneck identified at the prototype gate.
- No improvement in time to first dose in the pilot.
- Any compliance finding.

## BET-13 Neutral rare-disease or plasma real-world data registry (DEFER; exposure LOW)

**Strongest case against.** (Attack on the DEFER.) A neutral registry is a different business from anything Takeda runs. Flatiron worked because Roche kept it separate and it had oncology EHR scale. DEFER with USD 80m in the envelope is a placeholder that will be spent by inertia.

**Evidence.** Flatiron regulatory-use claim is a vendor snippet; no Takeda network. [CLM-011022] [CLM-011049] [CLM-011050] [CLM-011023] [CLM-005072]

**What would have to be true for the bet to survive.**
- A neutral sponsor and patient-organisation partners exist.

**Kill criteria.**
- No neutral sponsor at the 2029 options paper (RM-028).

## BET-14 TuneLab-style productised external model platform (REJECT; exposure LOW)

**Strongest case against.** (Attack on the REJECT.) The only credible counter is that rivals will own the interface to biotechs (Lilly via Benchling to 1,300+). Takeda has no measured internal advantage, so it has nothing to sell.

**Evidence.** No TuneLab uptake disclosed; NVIDIA warns of customers replacing platform layers. [CLM-006008] [CLM-009027] [CLM-011004] [CLM-000280]

**What would have to be true for the bet to survive.**
- A measured Takeda advantage and external demand.

**Kill criteria.**
- Revisit only if BET-01 produces a measured advantage and a biotech customer asks.

## BET-15 Large asset purchase (USD 5bn or more) as LOE bridge (DEFER; exposure MEDIUM)

**Strongest case against.** (Attack on the DEFER.) Both ways. If Takeda waits for 2031 triggers, AbbVie and J&J have already bought bridges (USD 17.5bn net each in 2024 and 2025) and the best Phase 2/3 assets are gone. If Takeda buys at USD 5bn, adjusted leverage is about 3.1x before Amitiza and about 3.4x with it, against a 3.0x ceiling the strategy itself set, and a Cerevel-type write-down (54% of price) would be JPY 400bn. The binary USD 5bn framing leaves the middle (USD 0.5-2bn licences, the Nimbus and Innovent pattern) unfunded.

**Evidence.** Leverage 2.6x at March 2026; Amitiza provision JPY 403.5bn; progressive dividend JPY 313.2bn paid in FY2025; no significant acquisitions in three years. [CLM-005005] [CLM-005014] [CLM-005006] [CLM-003086] [CLM-009049] [CLM-009054] [CLM-009087]

**What would have to be true for the bet to survive.**
- Free cash flow after dividends deleverages Takeda below the ceiling within 24 months.
- A named Phase 2+ asset passes the write-down test.

**Kill criteria.**
- Any unmet trigger: no deal (the bet's own rule).
- Leverage above 3.0x after Amitiza clarity: remove BET-15 from the roadmap.

## BET-16 U.S. cash-pay direct-to-patient channel (REJECT; exposure LOW)

**Strongest case against.** (Attack on the REJECT.) Nothing material; the only open point is whether government pricing agreements (TrumpRx, MFN) will force a direct-price posture on Takeda anyway.

**Evidence.** TrumpRx agreements expire with the presidential term; Takeda's status is not in the registry. [CLM-007009] [CLM-008037] [CLM-007010] [CLM-007052]

**What would have to be true for the bet to survive.**
- Takeda's categories stay specialty.

**Kill criteria.**
- A Takeda pricing agreement that requires a direct channel: reopen.

## BET-17 AI use-case measurement, decision support and reskilling (EXPERIMENT; exposure LOW)

**Strongest case against.** The bet can become a reporting ritual. Measurement is owned by the CFO who owns the JPY 200bn savings target, role cuts are proceeding in parallel, and J&J's own numbers (10-15% of use cases drive 80% of value) come from one interview. The reskilling plan needs credibility with employees who are losing roles.

**Evidence.** J&J metrics are self-reported; Takeda 63.4% is usage; the savings target mixes technology with headcount. [CLM-006019] [CLM-006020] [CLM-006022] [CLM-014043] [CLM-005059] [CLM-005078]

**What would have to be true for the bet to survive.**
- Baselines can be set per use case.
- Measurement is independent of the savings owner.

**Kill criteria.**
- No baseline for a use case: stop that use case (stage gate).
- At the FY2028 checkpoint (RM-023) technology share of savings cannot be separated.

reports.title: Scenario stress test (A11e, wave 5)
reports.markdown:
# Scenario stress test (A11e, wave 5)

Research cutoff 2026-11-21. The five scenarios are those in `strategy/data/scenarios.json` (SCN-1 to SCN-5). They are SCENARIOs, not forecasts. The strategy's robustness table is reproduced and re-rated by the council. Where the council differs the cell is marked and the reason is given. Capital figures are the strategy's balanced-portfolio ASSUMPTIONs (cumulative 2027-2040, USD m); Takeda's budget is not public (IVB-014). Council arithmetic is derived from registry values and ASM-001 (JPY 150 per USD).

## 1. Scenario recap and what each stresses

- **SCN-1 AI materially accelerates R&D.** SCENARIO: by about 2031 independent evidence shows AI-planned discovery and development cutting cycle time or raising hit rate at several companies; first-in-human data from AI-designed molecules are positive; compute and models commoditise further.
- **SCN-2 AI incremental.** SCENARIO: AI delivers productivity gains in documents, operations and decision support but no step change in probability of success or cycle time; no independent outcome appears for platform investments.
- **SCN-3 Pricing, regulatory and biosimilar pressure intensifies.** SCENARIO: Medicare negotiation, most-favoured-nation pricing and PBM private-label biosimilars compress net price faster; Entyvio erosion lands at the high end of ASM-024; Takhzyro and others face negotiated prices.
- **SCN-4 New modalities, care models and tech-native competitors reshape value.** SCENARIO: in-vivo cell therapy, siRNA and gene editing move into the clinic; home and digital care models change where value accrues; AI-native biotechs and tech platforms (Isomorphic-type) win partnerships; platforms do not protect single products.
- **SCN-5 Combined downside.** SCENARIO: SCN-2 and SCN-3 together, plus launch slippage for 2026 approvals (inspection findings, payer delays) and Amitiza cash outflow near the full provision; leverage stays near 3x and discretionary spend is cut.

## 2. Re-rated robustness table (council view; strategy rating in brackets where different)

| Bet | Decision | Balanced USD m | SCN-1 | SCN-2 | SCN-3 | SCN-4 | SCN-5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BET-01 Governed cross-franchise R&D data and decision layer | BUILD | 200 | robust | robust | neutral | robust | **fragile** [neutral] |
| BET-02 Plasma process-intelligence and fixed-price automation programme | BUILD | 430 | robust | robust | **neutral** [robust] | neutral | **neutral** [robust] |
| BET-03 Orexin science as a multi-asset discovery platform | BUILD | 500 | robust | neutral | **neutral** [robust] | neutral | fragile |
| BET-04 Entyvio franchise defence: payer contracting, evidence and lifecycle | BUILD | 140 | neutral | robust | **neutral** [robust] | neutral | robust |
| BET-05 Zasocitinib breadth and immunology successor evidence | INVEST | 180 | neutral | robust | neutral | neutral | **fragile** [neutral] |
| BET-06 Option-based external innovation engine incl. new-modality options | PARTNER | 700 | neutral | **neutral** [robust] | **neutral** [robust] | robust | **fragile** [robust] |
| BET-07 Milestone-gated AI-design partnerships (Nabla, Iambic and successors) | PARTNER | 180 | **option_value** [robust] | fragile | neutral | option_value | neutral |
| BET-08 Federated data consortium participation | PARTNER | 35 | robust | robust | neutral | neutral | robust |
| BET-09 Rented automated data generation (CRO and cloud labs) with ladder triggers | PARTNER | 95 | robust | robust | **neutral** [robust] | neutral | robust |
| BET-10 Owned autonomous discovery lab (stage 4-5) | REJECT | 0 | option_value | fragile | fragile | neutral | fragile |
| BET-11 Drug-device and home/SC administration platform | BUILD | 190 | neutral | robust | **fragile** [robust] | neutral | **neutral** [robust] |
| BET-12 Launch-pathway partnerships and patient-services outcome measurement | EXPERIMENT | 100 | neutral | **neutral** [robust] | **neutral** [robust] | **option_value** [robust] | neutral |
| BET-13 Neutral rare-disease or plasma real-world data registry | DEFER | 80 | option_value | neutral | neutral | **option_value** [robust] | fragile |
| BET-14 TuneLab-style productised external model platform | REJECT | 0 | option_value | fragile | fragile | fragile | fragile |
| BET-15 Large asset purchase (USD 5bn or more) as LOE bridge | DEFER | 0 | neutral | **neutral** [robust] | **fragile** [option_value] | neutral | fragile |
| BET-16 U.S. cash-pay direct-to-patient channel | REJECT | 0 | fragile | fragile | fragile | neutral | fragile |
| BET-17 AI use-case measurement, decision support and reskilling | EXPERIMENT | 120 | robust | robust | neutral | neutral | robust |

The council re-rated 19 of 85 cells (22%). Reasons:

- **BET-01 in SCN-5: neutral to fragile.** First discretionary cut in a cash squeeze; only the thin slice (metadata standard, decision log) is worth protecting.
- **BET-02 in SCN-3: robust to neutral.** Immunoglobulin exposure to MFN and negotiation was not researched, and PDT revenue was -1.5% at constant rates in H1 FY2026, so lower prices do not make the cost case stronger by themselves [CLM-005064].
- **BET-02 in SCN-5: robust to neutral.** The baseline and shadow-mode tranche survives; the USD 350m roll-out is the first large item to be deferred when leverage binds.
- **BET-03 in SCN-3: robust to neutral.** Payoff is 2035-2038, after the Entyvio erosion window; it does not cushion SCN-3 and competes for the same cash.
- **BET-04 in SCN-3: robust to neutral.** Needed in every scenario, but the Medicare price from January 2028 is statutory and PBM private-label biosimilars route around contracts [CLM-007026] [CLM-007015]. Value holds only as delay.
- **BET-05 in SCN-5: neutral to fragile.** SCN-5 contains launch slippage; PsA binary readout and inspection risk sit directly on this bet [CLM-005037] [CLM-012134].
- **BET-06 in SCN-2: robust to neutral.** Option value does not depend on AI pace; 'robust' overstates it when no option has produced an approval [CLM-009097].
- **BET-06 in SCN-3: robust to neutral.** The loss is capped, but options pay after 2035 and do not defend Entyvio net price in 2028-2034; 'robust' should mean value holds, not that the loss is small.
- **BET-06 in SCN-5: robust to fragile.** Upfronts and option fees are cash (ASM-106 excludes only contingent milestones); the constrained portfolio still allocates USD 300m (19%) here, and it is the first line to cut.
- **BET-07 in SCN-1: robust to option_value.** If AI accelerates, models commoditise (the SCN-1 driver) and value accrues to partners and to owners of proprietary data, not to licensees [CLM-006056].
- **BET-09 in SCN-3: robust to neutral.** A rented-assay service is irrelevant to price pressure; its value is cost avoidance against an unknown baseline (IVB-002).
- **BET-11 in SCN-3: robust to fragile.** SC pens move patients into the pharmacy benefit where PBM biosimilar templates operate [CLM-007015] [CLM-007016]; the effect after entry is unestablished [CLM-007053].
- **BET-11 in SCN-5: robust to neutral.** Device capex is deferrable; the existing pen and HYHUB stay.
- **BET-12 in SCN-2: robust to neutral.** The pathway hypothesis has no outcome evidence in any scenario [CLM-007039]; 'robust' should be reserved for bets with evidence of value.
- **BET-12 in SCN-3: robust to neutral.** As above; compliance exposure rises under pricing pressure [CLM-007010].
- **BET-12 in SCN-4: robust to option_value.** Care-model change could make pathway data valuable; no evidence yet [CLM-007045].
- **BET-13 in SCN-4: robust to option_value.** Unproven; Flatiron's neutrality does not transfer [CLM-011050].
- **BET-15 in SCN-2: robust to neutral.** Need for a bridge does not depend on AI pace.
- **BET-15 in SCN-3: option_value to fragile.** Under pricing pressure free cash flow falls while leverage already fails the 3.0x test by council arithmetic [CLM-005005] [CLM-005014].

## 3. Which bets break in each scenario

'Breaks' means rated fragile by the council: value falls or spend is stranded. Stranded capital is the sum of the balanced totals of those bets (a ceiling, because gates would stop spend before the full total is committed).

| Scenario | Bets that break (council) | Stranded balanced USD m | Share of USD 2,950m | Robust bets (council) | Robust balanced USD m |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SCN-1 | BET-16 | 0 | 0% | BET-01, BET-02, BET-03, BET-08, BET-09, BET-17 | 1380 |
| SCN-2 | BET-07, BET-10, BET-14, BET-16 | 180 | 6% | BET-01, BET-02, BET-04, BET-05, BET-08, BET-09, BET-11, BET-17 | 1390 |
| SCN-3 | BET-10, BET-11, BET-14, BET-15, BET-16 | 190 | 6% |  | 0 |
| SCN-4 | BET-14 | 0 | 0% | BET-01, BET-06 | 900 |
| SCN-5 | BET-01, BET-03, BET-05, BET-06, BET-10, BET-13, BET-14, BET-15, BET-16 | 1660 | 56% | BET-04, BET-08, BET-09, BET-17 | 390 |

Reading *(council interpretation)*:

- **SCN-1 (AI accelerates).** Nothing funded breaks. The risk is the opposite: BET-07 and BET-08 look like winners but the model commoditisation driver means Takeda gains only where it owns proprietary data (BET-01, BET-09). The bets that would pay (BET-07 at USD 180m) are option-sized, so the portfolio under-invests relative to an SCN-1 world by design, and the ambitious portfolio (USD 4,975m) is the only one that scales on it. Trigger: Nabla first-in-human and an independent Lilly-lab result [CLM-006039] [CLM-000281].
- **SCN-2 (AI incremental).** BET-07 breaks (USD 180m, small) and BET-10 and BET-14 would break if funded. BET-01, BET-08, BET-09 and BET-17 survive as productivity and discipline spend. Note the SCN-2 world is the one the registry currently supports: no independent outcome exists for any AI platform [CLM-011052], and AI-origin Phase 2 success is cited as conventional [CLM-006049]. Treat SCN-2 as the base case for AI spending.
- **SCN-3 (pricing, regulatory and biosimilar pressure).** The most consequential scenario for the portfolio and the one the strategy treats most generously: it rates 7 bets robust, the council rates 0. BET-11 breaks (pharmacy-benefit channel), BET-15 breaks (leverage), and BET-04 is needed but insufficient because the January 2028 Medicare price is statutory. The exposure the portfolio is built to cover (JPY 383-766bn a year of Entyvio revenue at ASM-024) is addressed by no bet except through delay, so SCN-3 is where the strategy's gap is largest.
- **SCN-4 (new modalities, care models, tech-native entrants).** Few bets break because few depend on it. BET-07 holds option value, but tech-native entrants (Isomorphic reportedly raised USD 600m [CLM-011014]) win partnerships that Takeda's USD 180m cannot match; BET-06 is the only bet that buys modality exposure and its payoff comes after 2035.
- **SCN-5 (combined downside).** BET-01, BET-03, BET-05, BET-06 and BET-13 break (BET-15 by arithmetic). See section 4.

## 4. Combined downside (SCN-5) in numbers

SCN-5 combines AI incremental, pricing pressure, launch slippage and Amitiza cash near the full provision, with leverage near 3x and discretionary spend cut [CLM-005014] [CLM-005005].

Capital-constrained portfolio (USD 1,590m), council re-rating of SCN-5:

| Council SCN-5 rating | Bets | Constrained USD m | Share of USD 1,590m |
|---|---|---|---|
| robust | BET-04, BET-08, BET-09, BET-17 | 260 | 16% |
| neutral | BET-02, BET-07, BET-11, BET-12 | 480 | 30% |
| fragile | BET-01, BET-03, BET-05, BET-06 | 850 | 53% |
| option_value | none | 0 | 0% |

**Finding.** After the council's re-rating, 850 of the USD 1,590m constrained envelope (53%) sits in bets that break in the combined downside, against a strategy table in which only BET-03 was fragile (USD 300m, 19%). The strategy's statement that the constrained portfolio protects the dated defences holds (BET-04 USD 120m and BET-05 USD 130m are 16% of it); the remaining 84% is mostly long-dated or option spend.

**Leverage arithmetic behind SCN-5** *(council arithmetic from registry values; free cash flow and acquired earnings ignored)*:

| Case | Adjusted net debt JPY bn | Over EBITDA JPY 1,457.2bn |
|---|---|---|
| March 2026 as reported [CLM-005005] | 3,817.6 | 2.62x |
| Amitiza provision JPY 403.5bn debt-funded [CLM-005014] | 4,221.1 | 2.90x |
| USD 5bn purchase at JPY 150 (BET-15) only | 4,567.6 | 3.13x |
| Both | 4,971.1 | 3.41x |

Adjusted net debt may already include the provision, and free cash flow after the JPY 313.2bn dividend paid in FY2025 [CLM-005006] would reduce it; both are unknown (IVB-012, IVB-014). The Amitiza figure is also not an upper bound: JPY 403.5bn is about three times the USD 884.9m single damages at JPY 152 per USD, and the third-party-payor class, interest, fees and appeal outcome are open [CLM-014048].

## 5. Stress cases the strategy does not model (council-added, not in scenarios.json)

**S-A. Early Entyvio biosimilar entry (2028-2029) with an Amitiza outcome at or above the provision.** ASM-025 (2031, range 2030-2032) excludes this. Basis: two biosimilar BLAs are under FDA review with one decision expected Q1 2027 per trade reporting, the reference product was approved in 2014, and Takeda says earlier launches must address patent validity and infringement [CLM-014051] [CLM-014050] [CLM-005017]. Which bets break:

| Bet | Effect under S-A |
|---|---|
| BET-04 | Playbook RM-026 (2029 H2) is dated after the earliest assumed entry (2030). It would be late. Re-date to 2028 H1 at no extra capital. |
| BET-05 | Becomes the only replacement in time; PsA readout (May 2027) and launch coverage carry more weight than their USD 180m suggests. |
| BET-03 | Payoff 2035-2038 misses the window entirely. |
| BET-06 | First approval 2035 (RM-043) misses the window; capital competes with the bridge. |
| BET-11 | SC migration before entry would increase pharmacy-benefit exposure at the worst moment. |
| BET-15 | A bridge purchase is needed sooner and is infeasible at 3.13x to 3.41x. This is where DEFER becomes a decision to leave a gap. |

**S-B. AI-design success with no data advantage (SCN-1 in which Takeda is a licensee).** Partners and AI-native biotechs capture the value (SCN-1 driver: commodity models). BET-07 pays only success-based milestones, which are contingent liabilities above USD 1bn per deal [CLM-006039] [CLM-006041]. Takeda's gain depends on BET-01 and BET-09, which are small. The portfolio is not harmed but does not benefit.

**S-C. Launch-wave concentration.** Three launches within 12 months [CLM-005074] with US revenue already falling 9.0% at actual rates in FY2025 [CLM-005001]. BET-04, BET-11 and BET-12 sit in the same US organisation (stage-gate owners). A launch problem in that organisation breaks three bets together, which the scenario table treats as independent.

## 6. Robust core (least-regret set)

The core is the least-regret set: bets the council would keep funded in every scenario and in S-A, either because value holds or because the bet addresses a dated or event-driven exposure at a capped cost. BET-03 and BET-05 are rated fragile in SCN-5 yet stay in the core as floors: BET-05 is the only replacement-revenue bet acting inside the Entyvio window and BET-03 is the only in-house diversification, so their fragility is the risk being managed, not a reason to cut. Council view, balanced H1 2027-2029 tranche (strategy's initial figures, ASSUMPTION):

| Bet | Core content | H1 USD m |
|---|---|---|
| BET-04 Entyvio franchise defence: payer contracting, evidence and lifecycle | Fixed dates, cheapest against exposure; re-date the playbook to 2028. | 40 |
| BET-05 Zasocitinib breadth and immunology successor evidence | Existing asset; the evidence is the best in the set. | 60 |
| BET-11 Drug-device and home/SC administration platform | Existing capability; hold device capex to a baseline-first tranche (condition: resolve the PBM-channel conflict with BET-04). | 50 |
| BET-17 AI use-case measurement, decision support and reskilling | Cheap discipline that makes the AI claims testable; move measurement ownership away from the savings owner. | 40 |
| BET-01 Governed cross-franchise R&D data and decision layer | Thin slice only (metadata standard and decision log) until gate 3. | 60 |
| BET-09 Rented automated data generation (CRO and cloud labs) with ladder triggers | Rented, reversible; stage 1-2 only. | 25 |
| BET-08 Federated data consortium participation | Near-free and measurable. | 10 |
| BET-02 Plasma process-intelligence and fixed-price automation programme | Baseline and shadow-mode tranche only (not the roll-out). | 80 |
| BET-03 Orexin science as a multi-asset discovery platform | Floor of discovery spend with a Phase 1 safety gate before H2 (constrained size). | 100 |
| **Core total** | | **465** |

The balanced H1 tranche is USD 685m. The core is USD 465m (68%). The remaining USD 220m (BET-06 150, BET-07 40, BET-12 30) should be released only on triggers: a deal-outcome scorecard (RM-007) for BET-06, Nabla first-in-human data for BET-07 beyond existing commitments, and an identified pathway bottleneck for BET-12.

**What the core does not do.** It does not replace Entyvio revenue. It protects what is dated and measurable, keeps learning cheap and holds options open. The Entyvio gap is covered only by the existing pipeline, BET-05 breadth and, if built, a mid-size licensing channel that no bet funds (see decision memo).

## 7. Capital timing against the Entyvio window

Bets the strategy's own evaluation puts at eight or more years to payoff are BET-03 (10), BET-06 (10), BET-07 (8) and BET-13 (8). Their balanced totals are USD 1460m, 49.5% of USD 2,950m. Their payoff years (2035-2038) fall after the Entyvio erosion window that ASM-025 places at 2031-2034. The bets that act inside the window (BET-04, BET-05, BET-11) total USD 510m, 17% of the balanced envelope.

## 8. Method limits

- Ratings are interpretation. Takeda internal data (IVB-004, IVB-005, IVB-006, IVB-012) could change them.
- Stranded-capital sums are ceilings. Stage gates cap capital at risk per gate (ASM-037 convention).
- Scenario 'robust' in the strategy table means value holds or rises; the council applied the same definition and withheld 'robust' where the bet's value rests on a hypothesis with no outcome evidence.

reports.title: Partnership models: build, partner, license, acquire or invest (A11b, wave 3)
reports.markdown:
# Partnership models: build, partner, license, acquire or invest (A11b, wave 3)

Research cutoff 2026-11-21. Takeda FY2025 = April 2025 to March 2026. For ten counterpart types this file gives the competitor precedent and outcome evidence (A9, A6), Takeda's observed pattern (A5 baseline), and a suggested mode. Modes are options, labelled EVIDENCE_BACKED (follows from outcome evidence) or HYPOTHESIS (reasoned; needs non-public data). They are not endorsements. Deal sources: [deal_inventory.md](../../New_mediciine/industry_transformation/partnerships_ecosystem/deal_inventory.md), [deal_outcomes_scorecard.md](../../New_mediciine/industry_transformation/partnerships_ecosystem/deal_outcomes_scorecard.md), [platform_vs_asset_classification.md](../../New_mediciine/industry_transformation/partnerships_ecosystem/platform_vs_asset_classification.md).

## Reading the modes
- **Build**: develop internally. **Partner**: collaboration without ownership transfer. **License**: pay for rights (upfront, milestones, royalties). **Acquire**: buy the company or asset. **Invest**: minority equity, funds or venture creation.
- Outcome evidence is thin: most AI and automation deals have no disclosed result [CLM-006007, CLM-006045]; value destruction concentrates in neuroscience, gene and cell therapy and robotics [CLM-009100].

## Takeda's observed pattern (baseline)
One flagship acquisition (Nimbus, USD 4.0bn upfront), then licences, options and equity (Innovent, Protagonist, Keros), divestitures, and write-offs of earlier purchases; no significant acquisitions in the three years to March 2026; four of six late-stage programs externally sourced [CLM-011075, CLM-009098, CLM-009087, CLM-005050]. AI-oriented alliances (Nabla, Iambic, BridGene, Charles River, MIT J-Clinic) have no disclosed outcomes [CLM-005049].

## Matrix
| Counterpart | Competitor precedent and outcome evidence | Takeda precedent | Mode suggested | Label | Claim |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Academic | Few competitor academic deals in the registry; AISB uses an academic lab (Columbia) with Apheris [CLM-006043] | MIT-Takeda J-Clinic, Charles River; no outcome [CLM-005049] | Partner or license; build only where core | HYPOTHESIS | [CLM-011090] |
| Biotech (assets) | Acquire: Lilly DICE USD 1.9bn (discontinued), Morphic USD 2.5bn (Phase 2 at deal), AbbVie Cerevel (USD 4.5bn impairment), J&J Intra-Cellular (indication approved nine months after close); License/option: AbbVie ADARx, Nimble [CLM-009003, CLM-009001, CLM-009054, CLM-009031, CLM-009061, CLM-009057] | Nimbus acquired (Phase 3 positive, NDA 2026); rusfertide licensed and approved 2026-08-28; Innovent licence with USD 100m equity and option [CLM-009076, CLM-009077, CLM-012151, CLM-009078] | License or option first; acquire only with Phase 2+ data | EVIDENCE_BACKED (outcome pattern is mixed; see risks) | [CLM-011091] |
| AI companies | Partner with milestone-heavy terms: Lilly-Isomorphic USD 45m upfront; AbbVie-BigHat USD 30m upfront; Takeda-Nabla double-digit millions upfront; no candidate or independent outcome yet [CLM-006012, CLM-006035, CLM-006039, CLM-006041] | Nabla (2022, 2025), Iambic (2026) [CLM-006039, CLM-006041] | Partner with go/no-go tied to first-in-human data | EVIDENCE_BACKED | [CLM-011092] |
| Robotics / automation | Lilly divested its robotic lab to the CRO Arctoris; J&J Ottava USD 0.9bn impairment; CRO model continues [CLM-006013, CLM-009047, CLM-006016] | No disclosed programme [CLM-005067] | Buy as a service (CRO, cloud lab); do not build or acquire | EVIDENCE_BACKED | [CLM-011093] |
| Clinical organisations | J&J reports AI trial-site recommendation with "up to 2.6x" enrolment (self-reported, no baseline); Takeda lists Charles River [CLM-006020, CLM-005049] | Charles River collaboration [CLM-005049] | Partner; require measured baseline | HYPOTHESIS | [CLM-011094] |
| Health systems | J&J OTTAVA IDE at Memorial Hermann and Polyphonic early access; Abu Dhabi programme expected [CLM-002049, CLM-006030, CLM-006031] | No disclosed data network; patient services EVIDENCE_GAP [CLM-005072] | Partner for diagnosis and site networks tied to specific launches | HYPOTHESIS | [CLM-011095] |
| Diagnostics and real-world data | Roche acquired Flatiron (USD 1.9bn, 2018) and kept it neutral; regulatory-use claim is vendor marketing [CLM-011022, CLM-011023] | None found | License data or partner; acquire only a neutral entity | HYPOTHESIS | [CLM-011096] |
| Data infrastructure | Apheris for AISB (five companies); Benchling for TuneLab; Databricks for Takeda's agent platform [CLM-006043, CLM-006008, CLM-005058] | AISB member since 2025-10-01; not in AISB Bind [CLM-006042, CLM-006044] | Partner (federated); keep data ownership | EVIDENCE_BACKED | [CLM-011097] |
| Manufacturing technology | Lilly bought a site (NexPharm USD 925m) and plans the Medicine Foundry; vendor claims on plant robots [CLM-009012, CLM-006000, CLM-006006] | Los Angeles plasma expansion USD 230m; no automation partner disclosed [CLM-005065, CLM-005067] | Partner on fixed-price terms for site upgrades; build process know-how | HYPOTHESIS | [CLM-011098] |
| Venture funds / creation | Lilly Ventures inside Catalyze360; J&J JLABS closures; AbbVie Ventures founding date unresolved [CLM-009025, CLM-009052, CLM-009074] | CEI on BaseLaunch board; Ventures scope not public [CLM-009091, CLM-005052] | Invest through shared vehicles (BaseLaunch) | HYPOTHESIS | [CLM-011099] |

## Where the choice of mode changes the economics *(INTERPRETATION)*
- Licence and option payments are mostly contingent: Takeda's AI deals carry over USD 1bn and USD 1.7bn of success-based payments that cost nothing unless data are positive [CLM-006039, CLM-006041]. Acquisitions put cash up front and expose write-down: AbbVie wrote off about 54% of Cerevel's net price [CLM-009054].
- Contingent value rights and sales milestones are used to share risk (Prevail, Akouos, Verve, Abiomed, Nimbus) [CLM-009099].
- A neutral platform (Flatiron) preserves customer base; owner-led platforms (TuneLab) may deter rivals from contributing, but TuneLab and AISB show rivals will join federated models [CLM-011022, CLM-006056].

## Risks
- Counterparty risk: Neurocrine and Denali ended Takeda collaborations [CLM-009090, CLM-009089].
- Evidence risk: sources for several competitor deals are company releases or trade snippets (A9 flags single interested sources) [CLM-009028, CLM-009079].
- Compliance and antitrust: not researched in this module *(gap)*.

## Evidence and gaps
Gaps: realised revenue per acquisition, Takeda Ventures scope, external share of pipeline, deal terms for academic and health-system partnerships, outcomes of BaseLaunch companies. See [../future_of_pharma/evidence_gaps.md](../future_of_pharma/evidence_gaps.md).

**Version v2** (A11c-bis, 2026-11-21): rescaled to the Director's decision record. v1 totals were 1,590 / 2,950 / 4,975.

Research cutoff 2026-11-21. **Takeda's multi-year technology and strategic-bet budget is not public (IVB-014). Every dollar figure here is an ASSUMPTION** with an id in [assumptions_register.md](assumptions_register.md); none is a Takeda budget, plan or forecast. Amounts are USD m, cumulative by horizon, incremental to base R&D (JPY 675.9bn in FY2025 [CLM-005004]) and base plant capex (ASM-035), and are shown as planning points with the ranges set by ASM-036.

## Scale anchors *(FACT)*

- Takeda FY2025 revenue JPY 4,505.7bn; Core Operating Profit JPY 1,172.5bn; R&D JPY 675.9bn; capex including intangibles JPY 426.9bn [CLM-005002] [CLM-005003] [CLM-005004] [CLM-005007]. At ASM-001 (150 JPY per USD) R&D is about USD 4.5bn a year.
- Adjusted net debt to EBITDA 2.6x at March 2026 (3.1x at March 2024); Amitiza provision JPY 403.5bn with cash timing unknown; dividend policy progressive [CLM-005005] [CLM-005014] [CLM-005006].
- Comparators (company statements, bases differ, not summed): Lilly-NVIDIA up to USD 1bn over five years, joint [CLM-000281]; Nimbus USD 4.0bn upfront [CLM-009076]; AbbVie early-stage upfronts USD 0.6-1.0bn a year [CLM-009097]; AbbVie ARCH built by fewer than ten staff [CLM-006032].

## Horizons

H1 2027-2029: foundations, validation, dated defence (Medicare January 2028, biosimilar reviews). H2 2030-2034: scale decisions, Entyvio loss window, option exercises. H3 2035-2040: compounding or exit; value review. *(SCENARIO framing; dates beyond 2032 are assumptions.)*

## Three portfolios *(RECOMMENDATION proposals, not endorsements)*


| Portfolio | Total USD m 2027-40 (ASSUMPTION) | Horizon allocation | Theme allocation |
|---|---|---|---|
| capital_constrained | 1,130 | H1 30% / H2 44% / H3 26% | core capability 62%, adjacent 20%, long horizon bets 4%, external innovation 14% |
| balanced | 1,920 | H1 31% / H2 44% / H3 25% | core capability 58%, adjacent 21%, long horizon bets 4%, external innovation 17% |
| ambitious | 3,155 | H1 23% / H2 43% / H3 34% | core capability 55%, adjacent 22%, long horizon bets 5%, external innovation 18% |


Theme mapping (proposal): core capability = BET-01, 02, 04, 05, 11, 12, 17; adjacent = BET-03, 09; long-horizon bets = BET-07, 13; external innovation = BET-06, 08. BET-18 sits in external innovation with USD 0 committed and a contingent pool (ASM-118). Rejected or deferred bets (BET-10, 13, 14, 15, 16) carry no allocation; BET-15 is rejected (ASM-115, ASM-119).

- **Capital-constrained (1,130).** Choose if leverage is near 3x (ASM-033) or Amitiza cash approaches the full provision (ASM-034). Protects the dated defences (BET-04, BET-05), the plasma pilot (BET-02), orexin discovery at reduced size, and minimal external options; BET-13 is not funded and the BET-18 pool is at its lower bound (USD 500m, contingent). Cost: thinner pipeline refill after 2030 and slower AI capability learning.
- **Balanced (1,920).** Funds all BUILD, PARTNER, INVEST and EXPERIMENT bets at v2 size. Recommended starting point: commit only the H1 tranche (595), of which the core is 465 (BET-01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 08, 09, 11, 17) and 130 is released only on triggers (BET-06, 07, 12); release H2 only at the gates in [stage_gates.md](stage_gates.md). About USD 1,030m of contingent headroom is reserved for BET-18 (ASM-118) and is not a saving.
- **Ambitious (3,155).** Larger options and plasma roll-out, bigger orexin and external-option programmes and a BET-18 pool at its upper bound (USD 2,000m, contingent). Choose only if SCN-1 signals appear (Nabla first-in-human positive, an independent Lilly-lab result [CLM-006039] [CLM-000281]) and leverage allows. (SCENARIO-conditional.)

**Why no NPV is reported.** A risk-adjusted NPV needs Takeda's own revenue forecast, probability of success and net price, none of which is public (IVB-004, IVB-005). The company's USD 10-20bn peak estimate for six late-stage programmes is stated not to be probability-adjusted and not a forecast [CLM-005041] [CLM-014049]. Reporting an NPV from public data would convert an assumption into a number that looks like a result. (RECOMMENDATION: compute rNPV internally for BET-05, BET-06 and BET-18 named assets only.)

**Illustrative exposure arithmetic (SCENARIO, not forecast).** Entyvio FY2025 revenue JPY 958.0bn [CLM-005009]. At ASM-024 (40-80% erosion over three years after first entry) annual revenue at risk is JPY 383-766bn, about 8.5-17.0% of FY2025 revenue (JPY 4,505.7bn [CLM-005002]). The balanced strategic-bet envelope of USD 1,920m is about JPY 288bn at ASM-001 over fourteen years; BET-04 is JPY 21bn of that. The comparison shows scale, not payback.

## Real-option logic *(INTERPRETATION)*

Options are held where the loss is capped and a signal arrives within the plan: BET-06 and BET-07 (upfronts only, contingent payments cost nothing without data [CLM-006039] [CLM-009099]), BET-09 stage-3 triggers [CLM-011066], BET-13 (unfunded) and BET-18 (contingent on the leverage test). The cost of holding an option is time: the Lilly-NVIDIA lab and Nabla data arrive 2026-2028, so the first decision point on AI scale is 2028 H2.

## Sensitivities that move the allocation

1. Entyvio entry year and erosion (ASM-024, ASM-025): earlier or deeper erosion raises the case for BET-05 and BET-18 and shortens the time available for BET-03.
2. Plasma headroom (ASM-031, IVB-006): below threshold, BET-02's follow-on moves to other core uses; above, the ambitious portfolio's plasma line is justified.
3. Amitiza cash and leverage (ASM-033, ASM-034, IVB-012): drives the constrained versus balanced choice.
4. AI evidence (SCN-1 versus SCN-2): decides whether BET-01, BET-07 and BET-09 scale.

## What is deliberately not allocated

A large asset purchase (BET-15, rejected as framed; the bridge is BET-18), a TuneLab-style platform (BET-14), an owned autonomous lab (BET-10) and a U.S. cash-pay channel (BET-16). Reasons are in [strategic_bets.md](../investment_theses/strategic_bets.md).

# Stage gates (A11c v2, wave 6)

**Version v2** (A11c-bis, 2026-11-21). Gate capital is allocated in whole USD 5m units that sum to the bet size, so no bet's gates exceed its size.

Each material bet moves discovery -> feasibility -> prototype -> controlled pilot -> scale decision -> ongoing value review. Capital at risk is the balanced-portfolio capital committed between that gate and the next (USD m, ASSUMPTION ASM-037 shares of the balanced total; BET-02 and BET-18 use the explicit gate amounts shown in the JSON `capital_at_risk_usd_m`; BET-18 gates draw on its contingent pool, not on committed capital). Owner and authority are roles, not named persons; the delegated limits are not public and are an ASSUMPTION. Shorter gate lists (BET-05, 08, 12, 13, 17, 18) use the stage names that apply and the shares in the JSON. REJECT bets (BET-10, 14, 15, 16) have no gates; BET-10 and BET-14 are governed by the ladder triggers in BET-09 and the roadmap.

**Rules that apply to every gate.** (1) A gate decision is made on the evidence listed, not on spend to date. (2) A missed stop criterion ends or redirects the bet unless the decision authority records a reason in writing (RECOMMENDATION). (3) Expansion releases the next tranche only; no tranche is pre-committed beyond the portfolio horizon. (4) Evidence is reviewed against a baseline set at the preceding gate, so usage or enrolment counts do not substitute for outcomes [CLM-006022] [CLM-007039].
