reports.title: Domain 1: Data advantage (A11b, wave 3)
reports.markdown:
# Domain 1: Data advantage (A11b, wave 3)

Research cutoff 2026-11-21. Takeda fiscal years run April-March (FY2025 = April 2025 to March 2026). Options are labelled EVIDENCE_BACKED (follows from cited evidence) or HYPOTHESIS (reasoned, needs non-public data). Nothing here is an endorsement. Baseline class numbers refer to [capability_baseline.md](../../New_mediciine/companies/takeda_public_baseline/capability_baseline/capability_baseline.md).

Problem addressed: drug discovery and development decisions depend on proprietary experimental, clinical and real-world data that is fragmented inside each company and too sparse in public sources for drug-like targets. *(INTERPRETATION)*

## What the evidence shows
**Deployed versus announced (competitors)**
- Lilly TuneLab is live: launched 2025-09-09, Lilly-trained models offered to biotechs with federated learning, underlying data cost estimated by Lilly at over USD 1 billion [CLM-000280]. Distribution through Benchling (1,300+ customers) is opt-in "later this year", with no uptake figure [CLM-006008]. A vendor blog reports over 2 million Lilly and 675,000 partner data points as of October 2026 (single vendor source) [CLM-009028]. Maturity: operational platform, pilot distribution, no independent outcome [CLM-006007].
- AbbVie ARCH is operational: conceived 2020, built by fewer than ten full-time staff plus contractors over a 124 TB corpus, and governance opened de-identified data from 2,000+ clinical trials to all R&D [CLM-006032, CLM-006034]. Outcome evidence is a preprint not opened by A6.
- J&J Polyphonic is early access to select hospitals; the Abu Dhabi network is "expected" [CLM-006030, CLM-006031]. Maturity: pilot and concept.
- Five companies (AbbVie, Astex, BMS, J&J, Takeda) fine-tuned OpenFold3 on over 20,000 private structures; the organiser reports about 10 points better pose accuracy than the best public model on 1,056 held-out structures, not peer reviewed [CLM-006043]. Takeda is not on the AISB Bind founding list [CLM-006044].
- Across these four assets, none has independent outcome evidence [CLM-011052].

**Takeda baseline**
- Public evidence is a platform and an aspiration: a Databricks-hosted agent platform for 10,000+ employees (vendor-hosted, partly supported) [CLM-005058], 80% external digital workforce when the transformation was designed [CLM-005057], a stated aim to embed AI in every stage of discovery [CLM-005053], and no quantified outcome [CLM-006045, CLM-011053].

**Contrary evidence**
- NVIDIA states that customers with in-house capability can replace platform layers [CLM-011004], which applies to data platforms too *(INTERPRETATION)*. The A10 audit also marks the AISB result as vendor-organised and the CIO-reported J&J metrics as self-reported [CLM-006020].

## Where proprietary advantage exists
- Proprietary experimental data generated over decades is the one defensible asset; compute and third-party models are purchasable by rivals [CLM-006055].
- Advantage is strongest where data is expensive to regenerate (company-estimated over USD 1 billion for TuneLab) and where partners add data back, strengthening the model *(INTERPRETATION)* [CLM-011082, CLM-011087].
- Open standards or partnering fit better for public-like tasks (structure prediction, ADMET baselines) where no single company has enough data; federated consortia are the common mechanism [CLM-006056].

## Takeda fit and baseline class
| Therapeutic area | Data position | Baseline class | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Plasma-derived therapies | 270+ collection centers with adaptive donor nomograms; immunoglobulins 18% of FY2025 revenue | 2 Plasma network and PDT manufacturing (EXISTING_STRENGTH) | [CLM-005060, CLM-005063, CLM-005064] |
| GI / immunology | Entyvio is 21% of revenue; trial and real-world data scale unknown | 1 GI / immunology (EXISTING_STRENGTH) | [CLM-005009] |
| Rare disease, neuroscience (orexin) | Discovery in Shonan; patient numbers small | 3 Rare / orexin (EXISTING_STRENGTH) | [CLM-005048] |
| Enterprise data and AI platform | Platform exists; production use and outcomes unproven | 9 (EXISTING_BUT_UNDERDEVELOPED) | [CLM-005058, CLM-005080] |
| AI-enabled discovery | No outcome evidence | 10 (EVIDENCE_GAP) | [CLM-005049] |

Economics: Takeda R&D expense was JPY 675.9bn in FY2025 [CLM-005004]; the public record gives no technology capital envelope (IVB-014), so any build-size claim is an assumption *(gap)*. Evidence requirements: a data investment is justified only by a measured change in cycle time, hit rate or cost per decision, none of which Takeda or any competitor has published.

## Options (not endorsements)
| # | Option | Label | What must be true | Claim |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.1 | Keep participating in federated consortia (AISB) and evaluate follow-on tasks from measured value | EVIDENCE_BACKED | Pooled models beat Takeda-only models on Takeda targets; governance protects raw data | [CLM-011054] |
| 1.2 | One governed cross-franchise R&D data layer (ARCH-type) | HYPOTHESIS | Takeda data is fragmented as AbbVie's was; reuse of trial data is permitted | [CLM-011055] |
| 1.3 | Treat plasma donor, yield and process data as the proprietary data class | HYPOTHESIS | Data is captured consistently across centers and predicts yield or cost | [CLM-011056] |
| 1.4 | Build a TuneLab-style external model platform | HYPOTHESIS (low confidence) | Data volume and external demand comparable to Lilly; see analogy NVIDIA [CLM-011027] | [CLM-011027] |

## Success criteria
- Production inventory of data and AI products with users and outcomes (closes IVB-001).
- A named decision (target selection, trial design, supply planning) where a model changed the outcome, with a pre-agreed baseline *(HYPOTHESIS)*.
- Federated model gains on Takeda held-out data versus public models, reported with the organiser's method disclosed *(HYPOTHESIS)*.

## Risks
- Regulatory: FDA's January 2025 draft guidance proposes a risk-based credibility framework for AI used in regulatory decisions, so model evidence must be documented [CLM-006046].
- Data and liability: Takeda's 20-F warns AI models may be flawed or trained on inadequate data [CLM-005054].
- Privacy and consent limit pooling; federation reduces but does not remove this *(INTERPRETATION)*.
- Platform lock-in: a competitor-led federated platform strengthens that competitor's models as partners contribute [CLM-006055].

## Evidence and gaps
Gaps: internal AI inventory (IVB-001), TuneLab uptake, ARCH outcomes, Takeda data estate, plasma yield data (IVB-006). Details in [evidence_gaps.md](evidence_gaps.md).

reports.title: Domain 2: Next-generation R&D (A11b, wave 3)
reports.markdown:
# Domain 2: Next-generation R&D (A11b, wave 3)

Research cutoff 2026-11-21. Takeda FY2025 = April 2025 to March 2026. Options are labelled EVIDENCE_BACKED or HYPOTHESIS; none is an endorsement. Baseline classes are from [capability_baseline.md](../../New_mediciine/companies/takeda_public_baseline/capability_baseline/capability_baseline.md).

Problem addressed: replace revenue lost to patent expiry with new molecules faster and with a higher probability of success, using new modalities and computational design. *(INTERPRETATION)*

## What the evidence shows
**AI-enabled discovery: deployed versus announced**
- Lilly: Isomorphic collaboration (USD 45 million upfront, up to USD 1.7 billion milestones, 2024-01-07) is at concept stage [CLM-006012]; the Chai custom antibody model is a trade report and Chai's hit-rate claim is Chai's own [CLM-006010]; no candidate is named in any opened source [CLM-006007].
- AbbVie: BigHat (USD 30 million upfront) at prototype and Valkai at concept [CLM-006035, CLM-006037].
- Takeda: Nabla Bio second collaboration (October 2025; double-digit millions upfront, over USD 1 billion success-based) with first-in-human data expected in one to two years, and Iambic (February 2026, success-based payments could exceed USD 1.7 billion) [CLM-006039, CLM-006041]. Nabla states a three to four week design-to-test loop, a company claim [CLM-006040]. All are prototype or earlier [CLM-006045].
- Outcome evidence from the wider industry is limited and mixed: Recursion ended four of 11 programmes in 2025 [CLM-006047]; Insilico's rentosertib Phase IIa (71 patients) showed +98.4 mL FVC at 60 mg with seven discontinuations for liver injury [CLM-006048]; AI-origin Phase 2 success is cited as about the same as conventional (secondary citation) [CLM-006049]. Synthesis: [CLM-011057].

**New modalities: acquired or optioned, not built**
- AbbVie: Capstan (in vivo CAR-T, USD 2.1 billion) and the ADARx siRNA option (USD 335 million upfront, up to USD 7.5 billion milestones) [CLM-009058, CLM-009061]. Lilly: Verve (gene editing) and POINT (radioligands) [CLM-009010, CLM-009006]. J&J: Ambrx (ADC) and Halda [CLM-009035, CLM-009032]. Maturity: early clinical or concept; outcomes not yet visible [CLM-011059].

**Takeda's route to date**
- Window approvals came from conventional routes: oveporexton from in-house orexin science (approved 2026-08-05), rusfertide from Protagonist (approved 2026-08-28), zasocitinib via the Nimbus purchase (NDA planned 2026) [CLM-012149, CLM-012151, CLM-009076, CLM-009077]. Takeda exited cell therapy in October 2025, recognising a JPY 58.2bn impairment (JPY 58.0bn was the earlier expectation) [CLM-005025, CLM-009084]. Synthesis: [CLM-011058].
- Takeda's stated peak potential for six late-stage programs is USD 10-20bn [CLM-005041]; early pipeline depth beyond them is a gap (IVB-008) [CLM-005044].

**Contrary evidence**
- Platform pipelines still suffer ordinary attrition [CLM-006047]; Lilly's DICE and AbbVie's Cerevel purchases ended in discontinuation or large impairment [CLM-009003, CLM-009054], so acquiring modalities is not safer than building them.

## Where proprietary advantage exists
- Disease biology depth (orexin) and clinical execution are proprietary and not purchasable quickly [CLM-005048, CLM-005042].
- Generative models and structure tools are converging on open or shared models (OpenFold3, Boltz, Chai), so the model itself is a weaker moat than proprietary assay and clinical data [CLM-006056].
- Partnering is better for new modalities where Takeda lacks platform scale; options reduce capital at risk compared with asset purchases [CLM-009099, CLM-009061] *(INTERPRETATION)*.

## Takeda fit and baseline class
| Therapeutic area | Fit | Baseline class | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| GI / inflammation | Entyvio is the franchise to defend and extend; oral integrin and TYK2 approaches are competitor and in-house lines | 1 (EXISTING_STRENGTH), 7 LOE replacement (EXISTING_BUT_UNDERDEVELOPED) | [CLM-005017, CLM-009001, CLM-012150] |
| Rare / neuroscience | Orexin biology is a proven in-house platform | 3 (EXISTING_STRENGTH) | [CLM-005048, CLM-012149] |
| Oncology | Innovent assets (Phase 3) licensed; in-house oncology discovery limited after cell therapy exit | 5 External innovation (EXISTING_STRENGTH) | [CLM-005043, CLM-005025] |
| Vaccines | QDENGA revenue JPY 40.8bn (FY2025) | 8 launch execution (POTENTIAL_NEW_CAPABILITY) | [CLM-005045] |
| PDT | Manufacturing-led; discovery role small | 2 | [CLM-005064] |
| AI-enabled discovery | Alliances only; no outcomes | 10 (EVIDENCE_GAP) | [CLM-005049] |

Economics: Takeda spent JPY 675.9bn on R&D in FY2025 and paid USD 4.0bn upfront for Nimbus; the same cash buys several option agreements of the ADARx size *(INTERPRETATION)* [CLM-005004, CLM-009076, CLM-009061]. Evidence requirements: first-in-human or Phase 2 data before scaling AI-partner spend [CLM-006058].

## Options (not endorsements)
| # | Option | Label | What must be true | Claim |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2.1 | Milestone-gated AI partnerships tied to first-in-human data | EVIDENCE_BACKED | Contracts allow stop decisions; Nabla data arrive in 1-2 years | [CLM-011060] |
| 2.2 | Option agreements for one or two new modalities adjacent to existing assets (RNAi) | HYPOTHESIS | Option fees small versus asset buys; Takeda disease depth transfers | [CLM-011061] |
| 2.3 | Run orexin science as a platform with a second differentiated asset | HYPOTHESIS | A second asset beyond oveporexton is credible (TAK-994 was stopped) [CLM-005023] | [CLM-011038] |
| 2.4 | Match Lilly's owned compute and model builds | not supported by evidence | No outcome from LillyPod [CLM-006007]; A6 advises partner-and-watch [CLM-006058] | none |

## Success criteria
- First-in-human data from Nabla-designed molecules within the stated one to two years, with candidate quality compared against conventional molecules [CLM-006039] *(HYPOTHESIS)*.
- Share of Phase 1 starts originating in AI or option programmes by FY2028 and their Phase 2 transition rate versus the conventional rate (target to be set internally) *(HYPOTHESIS)*.
- Late-stage delivery to the announced timetable continues (three Phase 3 readouts, then filings in FY2025-FY2029) [CLM-005042].

## Risks
- Spending on AI deals with success-based payments above USD 1 billion each, which are contingent liabilities rather than demonstrated value [CLM-006039, CLM-006041].
- Impairments after failed acquisitions (Takeda JPY 58.2bn cell therapy, JPY 27.8bn Maverick, JPY 21.5bn soticlestat) show portfolio stop decisions have a cash cost [CLM-009083, CLM-009084].
- FDA draft AI guidance is non-binding but sets expectations for model credibility in regulatory submissions [CLM-006046].

## Evidence and gaps
Gaps: Takeda early-pipeline depth (IVB-008), internal probabilities of success (IVB-005), AI usage in target selection (IVB-010), the Insilico Phase III start (snippet only) [CLM-006050]. See [evidence_gaps.md](evidence_gaps.md).

reports.title: Domain 3: Robotics and autonomous science (A11b, wave 3)
reports.markdown:
# Domain 3: Robotics and autonomous science (A11b, wave 3)

Research cutoff 2026-11-21. Options are labelled EVIDENCE_BACKED or HYPOTHESIS; none is an endorsement. Technical maturity is taken from A6's [autonomous_lab_reality_check.md](../../New_mediciine/industry_transformation/ai_data_robotics/autonomous_lab_reality_check.md) and [maturity_matrix.md](../../New_mediciine/industry_transformation/ai_data_robotics/maturity_matrix.md), with the A10 corrections applied: the claim that Lilly's lab was a "Strateos" venture launched about 2020 is unsupported (CLM-006017), the reason for the sale is undisclosed, and the Studio dates to 2017 in the sources that support it [CLM-006014].

Problem addressed: wet-lab throughput and reproducibility limit how many hypotheses can be tested; Lilly cites about 2,000 molecular ideas per target per year because each needs physical synthesis and testing [CLM-006005]. *(INTERPRETATION)*

## What the evidence shows
**Deployed**
- High-throughput scripted automation is operational and commodity: Arctoris runs the former Lilly platform as a CRO service, with five biochemistry modules, a screening module, a BSL2 cell-biology module and 4 million compound storage, and expanded biophysics capacity ten-fold [CLM-006013, CLM-006016].
- Plant automation that operates is conventional: Lilly Lebanon Advanced Therapies opened 2026-05-06 with robotic dosing and sealing seen on a tour, no performance data [CLM-006002].

**Announced or prototype**
- Lilly-NVIDIA co-innovation lab (up to USD 1bn over five years, jointly) targeting a continuous learning system linking agentic wet labs and dry labs: concept [CLM-000281]. LillyPod is operational compute with no reported result [CLM-006004, CLM-006007].
- Fast AI-to-wet-lab loops are vendor claims: Nabla three to four weeks design-to-test [CLM-006040]; BigHat pairs ML with a high-speed lab under an AbbVie deal [CLM-006035]. Robots and digital twins in Lilly plants are a vendor-blog capability claim, the audit calls the pilot tag generous [CLM-006006].
- Medicine Foundry (USD 4.5bn, opening late 2027) is concept [CLM-006000, CLM-006001].

**Failures and exits**
- Lilly's Life Sciences Studio went to the CRO Arctoris in 2024; a reported USD 90m build cost conflicts on dates [CLM-006013, CLM-006014]. Zymergen sold to Ginkgo for about USD 300m, one-tenth of its IPO valuation, after USD 1.2bn cumulative net losses [CLM-006051]. Pattern: owned and venture-funded cloud lab or biofoundry models ended in divestment or distressed sale; the service model continues [CLM-006052, CLM-011063].
- J&J's Ottava (Auris) took a USD 0.9bn partial impairment in fiscal 2021 [CLM-009047]. This is device robotics, not lab robotics, but shows robotics capital risk.

**Takeda baseline**
- No public evidence of lab automation, continuous manufacturing or manufacturing robotics [CLM-005067]. Plasma network grew from 233 to 275 centers (FY2022-FY2024) and a USD 230m Los Angeles fractionation expansion adds up to 2 million litres per year [CLM-005063, CLM-005065]. Hikari FDA warning letter (June 2020) caused a supply shortage [CLM-005020]. Synthesis: [CLM-011064].

## Staged automation ladder and technical maturity today
| Stage | Hardware | Data | Oversight | Validation | Regulatory | Investment evidence | Barriers | Metrics | Maturity today |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 Assisted | Benchtop liquid handlers, instruments | LIMS, electronic notebooks | Scientist runs each step | Instrument qualification | GLP/GMP on existing rules | Not disclosed (gap) | Training, integration | Throughput, error rate | Operational, commodity [CLM-006013] |
| 2 Automated | Integrated HTS and dosing lines | Structured assay data | Protocol-driven, operator checks exceptions | Process validation per assay | As stage 1; GMP lines validated | Lilly Studio about USD 90m reported (conflicting dates) [CLM-006014] | Utilisation, maintenance | Cost per data point, uptime | Operational; Lilly plant robotics unquantified [CLM-006002] |
| 3 Integrated smart lab | Robotic labs tied to scheduling and ML planning | Closed data pipeline from instrument to model | Human approves designs and exceptions | Model credibility and data provenance | FDA draft AI credibility framework if used in submissions [CLM-006046] | Co-innovation lab up to USD 1bn over five years (joint) [CLM-000281] | Data quality, interfaces, vendor lock-in | Cycle time design-to-result, model hit rate | Prototype to pilot; vendor claims only [CLM-006040, CLM-006035] |
| 4 Bounded autonomous experimentation | Same plus closed-loop selection of next experiments within set limits | Active-learning loops with logged decisions | Humans set bounds, audit trails | Prospective validation against human-run controls | Unsettled for submission use | Zymergen: USD 1.2bn cumulative loss without a commercial product [CLM-006051] | Reproducibility, failure modes, evidence of benefit | Experiments per decision, success versus control | Not demonstrated by any source opened [CLM-011062] |
| 5 Scaled automation | Multi-site, GMP-integrated autonomous operation | Enterprise digital thread | Exception-based | Continuous verification | GMP expectations for automated release | Foundry USD 4.5bn at concept [CLM-006000] | Capital, workforce transition, validation burden | Cost per batch, deviation rate, speed to clinic | Concept; no operating example in the set [CLM-006001] |

Reading: stages 1-2 are mature enough to rent or buy; stage 3 can be piloted with strict gates; stage 4 and above have no independent demonstration, so any commitment is an option on technology not yet shown to work [CLM-011062].

## Where proprietary advantage exists
- Not in the robots: automation and CRO capacity are purchasable, and the one open-access owned lab was divested [CLM-006016, CLM-006052].
- In the data the automation generates and the process knowledge in manufacturing (for example plasma yield) [CLM-005064] *(INTERPRETATION)*.
- Open standards and partnering are better for stages 1-3 data generation; ownership is plausible only where a process is core and unique, such as plasma fractionation *(HYPOTHESIS)*.

## Takeda fit and baseline class
| Therapeutic area | Fit | Baseline class | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| PDT | Fractionation and fill-finish automation have clearest unit economics; process and quality record includes one warning letter | 2 (EXISTING_STRENGTH), 12 Manufacturing quality (EXISTING_BUT_UNDERDEVELOPED) | [CLM-005065, CLM-005020] |
| Rare / neuroscience / GI discovery | Rent data generation (CRO) rather than own | 11 Lab automation and robotics (EVIDENCE_GAP) | [CLM-005067, CLM-006016] |
| Oncology, vaccines | No evidence of fit | 11 | none |

Economics: no Takeda automation spend is public (IVB-002, IVB-014) *(gap)*.

## Options (not endorsements)
| # | Option | Label | What must be true | Claim |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3.1 | Rent automated data generation from CROs and cloud labs; do not build an owned robotic lab | EVIDENCE_BACKED | CRO capacity and data quality meet Takeda needs | [CLM-011065] |
| 3.2 | Pilot fixed-price, outcome-linked automation upgrades at one plasma site before network roll-out | HYPOTHESIS | Yield and cost per litre show headroom (IVB-006) | [CLM-011031] |
| 3.3 | Set triggers for moving up the ladder (independent Lilly-lab result, Nabla first-in-human data, CRO cost benchmark) | HYPOTHESIS | Triggers are observable within 12-24 months | [CLM-011066] |
| 3.4 | Build an owned autonomous discovery lab (stage 4-5) | not supported by evidence | No independent demonstration; two owned models divested or sold distressed [CLM-006052] | none |

## Success criteria
- Cost per data point and turnaround from a CRO pilot versus internal baseline *(HYPOTHESIS)*.
- Plasma site: yield per litre of plasma, deviation rate and cost per litre before and after upgrade (company-defined, IVB-006) *(HYPOTHESIS)*.
- Evidence gate for stage 3+: prospective comparison of AI-planned versus human-planned experiments on the same target *(HYPOTHESIS)*.

## Risks
- Capital risk: documented distressed outcomes [CLM-006051, CLM-006052].
- Quality and compliance risk: Takeda has a documented warning letter and supply shortage, so automation in GMP settings needs validation before scale [CLM-005020].
- Workforce framing: automation changes tasks; do not describe it as replacing staff (see Domain 7).
- Safety: an autonomous system selecting experiments needs human-set bounds and audit trails *(INTERPRETATION)*.

## Evidence and gaps
Gaps: Takeda lab and plant automation footprint (IVB-002), cost per experiment for any pharma robotic lab, Emerald Cloud Lab and other cloud labs (not investigated by A6), reason for Lilly's sale [CLM-006017 unsupported detail], and whether the Lilly-NVIDIA lab has started. See [evidence_gaps.md](evidence_gaps.md).

reports.title: Domain 4: Care models (A11b, wave 3)
reports.markdown:
# Domain 4: Care models (A11b, wave 3)

Research cutoff 2026-11-21. Takeda FY2025 = April 2025 to March 2026. Options are labelled EVIDENCE_BACKED or HYPOTHESIS; none is an endorsement. Evidence draws on A7's [commercial_patient](../../New_mediciine/industry_transformation/commercial_patient/) reports.

Problem addressed: time to therapy, adherence and site-of-care cost for chronic, rare and plasma-derived treatments. *(INTERPRETATION)*

## What the evidence shows
**Deployed versus announced**
- Lilly: LillyDirect self-pay (Zepbound vials from August 2024 at USD 399/549, cut to USD 299/399/449 on 1 December 2025; KwikPen from USD 299); Lilly says over 1 million patients used LillyDirect in 2025 and one in three new branded weight-management starts was Zepbound self-pay vials (company-reported, footnotes unverified) [CLM-007000, CLM-007002, CLM-007044, CLM-007004].
- J&J: OTTAVA robot has De Novo authorisation (FDA decision 2026-07-21; announced 2026-07-22) and one announced installation, pilot maturity [CLM-000283, CLM-006029]; the A10 audit notes the release says the hospital "will be the first to install", so completion is not shown [CLM-000284]. Polyphonic is early access to select hospitals [CLM-006030].
- AbbVie Allē (over 6 million members, Jan 2024) is a loyalty scheme for aesthetics [CLM-007036]. Takeda Help at Hand: over 100,000 patients cumulative [CLM-007037].
- Convenience shifts: Entyvio subcutaneous pen approved in US, Europe, Japan and cited by Takeda as driving uptake; HYHUB needle-free transfer for Hyqvia received 510(k) clearance in July 2025 (clearance, not adoption) [CLM-007041, CLM-007042]. Counter-example: Spravato is restricted to certified sites under observation [CLM-007030].
- No adherence, persistence or time-to-therapy outcome was found for any company's programme; reported figures are enrolment or access counts [CLM-007039]. Synthesis: [CLM-011067].

**Contrary evidence**
- Pear Therapeutics, a prescription digital therapeutics company, filed for Chapter 11 on 7 April 2023 after payers could deny payment; commentary says evidence was strong but reimbursement stalled [CLM-007045, CLM-007046]. Decentralised-trial disclosures were not usable in the Lilly or J&J 10-Ks [CLM-007048].

## Where proprietary advantage exists
- Drug-device integration and formulation (an SC pen, a needle-free transfer device) is proprietary and tied to the product and its patents [CLM-007041, CLM-007042].
- Patient-services hubs are replicable by vendors; advantage would come from measured outcomes, which no company publishes *(INTERPRETATION)* [CLM-007039].
- Open standards and partnering suit diagnosis pathways, site networks and data sharing with health systems (Polyphonic-type networks are still pilots) [CLM-006030].

## Takeda fit and baseline class
| Therapeutic area | Fit | Baseline class | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| GI / immunology | SC pen conversion already under way | 1 (EXISTING_STRENGTH); 8 launch execution (POTENTIAL_NEW_CAPABILITY) | [CLM-007053, CLM-007041] |
| PDT | Device-led home infusion of immunoglobulin fits | 2 | [CLM-007056, CLM-007042] |
| Rare / neuroscience (oveporexton) | Diagnosis pathway and site network may govern launch pace | 3, 8 | [CLM-007055, CLM-012149] |
| Oncology, vaccines | Not assessed | none | gap |
| Patient services overall | No public inventory or outcomes | 14 (EVIDENCE_GAP) | [CLM-005072, CLM-007058] |

Economics: patient-support spend and hub performance are not public (IVB-013) *(gap)*. Evidence requirements: adherence, persistence and time-to-therapy measured against a comparator.

## Options (not endorsements)
| # | Option | Label | What must be true | Claim |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4.1 | Continue SC and home-administration conversion with devices | EVIDENCE_BACKED | SC share grows without cannibalising too fast ahead of Entyvio exclusivity loss (IVB-004) | [CLM-011068] |
| 4.2 | Attach digital support to the drug instead of standalone digital therapeutics | EVIDENCE_BACKED | Support is funded through the drug's price, not a separate payer decision | [CLM-011069] |
| 4.3 | Launch-pathway partnerships (diagnosis, certified-site network) for oveporexton | HYPOTHESIS | Narcolepsy type 1 diagnosis or administration is a launch bottleneck | [CLM-011070] |
| 4.4 | US cash-pay channel on the LillyDirect model | not supported by evidence | See Domain 5 [CLM-007052] | none |

## Success criteria
- Time from prescription to first dose and persistence at 12 months by channel, for oveporexton and Entyvio SC *(HYPOTHESIS)*.
- Share of Entyvio patients on SC and of Hyqvia patients on device-assisted home use *(HYPOTHESIS)*.

## Risks
- Compliance: patient-support and cash-pay programmes interact with anti-kickback and copay accumulator rules [CLM-007010].
- Reimbursement risk for anything sold as a separate digital product [CLM-007045].
- Safety: restricted-distribution or home-use designs need risk management plans (Spravato REMS shows the model) [CLM-007030].

## Evidence and gaps
Gaps: Takeda hub and patient-assistance inventory (IVB-013), Entyvio IV/SC mix, RWE outputs for tirzepatide and Entyvio not retrieved, connected-device features not found [CLM-007047]. See [evidence_gaps.md](evidence_gaps.md).

reports.title: Domain 5: Commercial models (A11b, wave 3)
reports.markdown:
# Domain 5: Commercial models (A11b, wave 3)

Research cutoff 2026-11-21. Takeda FY2025 = April 2025 to March 2026. Options are labelled EVIDENCE_BACKED or HYPOTHESIS; none is an endorsement. Evidence draws on A7's [commercial_models_comparison.md](../../New_mediciine/industry_transformation/commercial_patient/commercial_models_comparison.md) and [transfer_to_takeda.md](../../New_mediciine/industry_transformation/commercial_patient/transfer_to_takeda.md).

Problem addressed: protect and grow net revenue as payers, PBMs and price negotiation compress margins, and launch new brands on time. *(INTERPRETATION)*

Design rule for this domain: separate **decision support** (AI that advises people) from **automation that creates compliance risk** (AI that generates, sends or targets promotional or patient-facing content without review). Evidence below is assigned to one or the other.

## What the evidence shows
**Payer, PBM and policy dynamics (largest effect on commercial models)**
- CVS Caremark preferred Wegovy over Zepbound from 1 July 2025 (Lilly stock fell over 11% on the announcement) and restored Zepbound as an additional preferred option from 1 October 2026 [CLM-007011, CLM-007013].
- From 1 July 2026 CVS template formularies prefer interchangeable Stelara biosimilars [CLM-007015]. AbbVie reports USD 65.1bn of rebate and chargeback provisions in 2025 [CLM-007019]. AbbVie delayed Humira erosion by rebate-for-access contracting and a co-branded supply route [CLM-003085].
- Takeda: Entyvio was selected for Medicare price negotiation effective January 2028 [CLM-007026]. Synthesis: [CLM-011071].

**Launch execution**
- Mounjaro USD 22,965m and Zepbound USD 13,542m in 2025, 56% of Lilly revenue, with lower realised prices [CLM-007031, CLM-007024]. Skyrizi USD 17,562m and Rinvoq USD 8,304m [CLM-007020]. Carvykti USD 1,887m was capacity-limited; Spravato USD 1,696m was site-limited [CLM-007029].
- Takeda: Entyvio JPY 958.0bn (21% of revenue) and QDENGA JPY 40.8bn; oveporexton and zasocitinib launches are pending [CLM-007027, CLM-005045, CLM-007033]. New-brand launch execution is POTENTIAL_NEW_CAPABILITY [CLM-005069, CLM-005074].

**AI in commercial work: deployed versus announced**
- J&J reports AskJIA (sales assistant), Engagement.AI (provider insights, 14 countries) and a quality-control answer tool, with no usage or outcome data [CLM-006023, CLM-006021]. Maturity: operational per executive, self-reported.

**Contrary evidence**
- Cash-pay channels are limited by copay accumulators and anti-kickback rules; the self-pay share of Zepbound revenue is not in the 10-K [CLM-007010, CLM-007005]. Whether TrumpRx volumes are material is unknown [CLM-007009].

## Where proprietary advantage exists
- Contracting scale and payer relationships (AbbVie Humira, Skyrizi/Rinvoq) and launch infrastructure are slow to copy but removable by a PBM template change [CLM-011086, CLM-007015].
- Clinical differentiation drives pull; commercial AI tools are commodity and replicable *(INTERPRETATION)* [CLM-006023].
- Open standards or partnering suit data-sharing with payers and health systems, and specialty distribution *(HYPOTHESIS)*.

## Takeda fit and baseline class
| Therapeutic area | Fit | Baseline class | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| GI / immunology | Payer defence needed before Entyvio biosimilar or preferred competitor | 1, 7 LOE replacement (EXISTING_BUT_UNDERDEVELOPED) | [CLM-007054, CLM-007026] |
| PDT | Device and site-of-care shift, not DTC | 2 | [CLM-007056] |
| Rare / neuroscience | Site- or capacity-limited launch lessons (Spravato, Carvykti) | 3, 8 (POTENTIAL_NEW_CAPABILITY) | [CLM-007055] |
| Patient services / market access | No public inventory | 14 (EVIDENCE_GAP) | [CLM-005072] |

Economics: Takeda rebates are undisclosed and exclusion risk is stated [CLM-007025]; the Entyvio erosion curve is an open backlog item (IVB-004). Evidence requirements: net price and persistence by payer segment.

## Options (not endorsements)
| # | Option | Label | What must be true | Claim |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5.1 | Build payer-contracting and formulary-defence depth for Entyvio ahead of biosimilar entry | EVIDENCE_BACKED | Biosimilar or PBM template risk materialises on a known timetable | [CLM-011072] |
| 5.2 | Do not copy a US cash-pay channel | EVIDENCE_BACKED | Takeda products remain infused, specialty or plasma-derived | [CLM-011073] |
| 5.3 | Pilot AI decision support for field and medical teams (advises humans only) | HYPOTHESIS | Measurable time or quality gain; compliance review of every output | [CLM-011074] |
| 5.4 | Automated generation and delivery of promotional content to HCPs or patients | not supported by evidence | No competitor outcome data; creates compliance risk | none |

## Success criteria
- Entyvio net price and formulary position retained at target after 2028 negotiation and any biosimilar entry *(HYPOTHESIS)*.
- Launch metrics for oveporexton and zasocitinib: time to first prescription, site activation rate, payer coverage at 6 and 12 months *(HYPOTHESIS)*.
- For decision-support pilots: hours saved or pre-call quality score against a control group *(HYPOTHESIS)*.

## Risks
- Compliance: promotional content and patient communication are regulated; FDA draft guidance treats AI credibility as risk-based [CLM-006046]. Keep humans accountable for outbound content *(INTERPRETATION)*.
- Policy: Part D redesign and IRA selection affect profitability [CLM-007026].
- Dependence on a single PBM decision (Zepbound swing in either direction) [CLM-007011, CLM-007013].

## Evidence and gaps
Gaps: net price per prescription except AbbVie provisions, Takeda patient-assistance and field-force detail, self-pay share of Zepbound revenue [CLM-007005, CLM-007058]. See [evidence_gaps.md](evidence_gaps.md).

reports.title: Domain 6: Partnerships and ecosystem (A11b, wave 3)
reports.markdown:
# Domain 6: Partnerships and ecosystem (A11b, wave 3)

Research cutoff 2026-11-21. Takeda FY2025 = April 2025 to March 2026. Options are labelled EVIDENCE_BACKED or HYPOTHESIS; none is an endorsement. Counterpart-by-counterpart build/partner/license/acquire/invest guidance is in [partnership_models.md](../ecosystem_partnerships/partnership_models.md). Evidence draws on A9's [deal_inventory.md](../../New_mediciine/industry_transformation/partnerships_ecosystem/deal_inventory.md) and [deal_outcomes_scorecard.md](../../New_mediciine/industry_transformation/partnerships_ecosystem/deal_outcomes_scorecard.md).

Problem addressed: refill a pipeline and add platforms faster than internal research alone, at tolerable capital at risk. *(INTERPRETATION)*

## What the evidence shows
**Competitor patterns (deployed deals with disclosed terms)**
- Lilly splits deals into early asset purchases expensed as IPR&D (DICE USD 1.9bn, Morphic USD 2.5bn, Scorpion USD 1.4bn, others), capability purchases (POINT, Verve, NexPharm USD 925m) and ecosystem platforms (TuneLab, NVIDIA lab) [CLM-009095, CLM-009012, CLM-009026, CLM-009029].
- J&J makes a few large commercial or late-stage purchases (Abiomed USD 17.1bn, Shockwave USD 11.5bn, Intra-Cellular USD 14.5bn) plus smaller platform buys [CLM-009096].
- AbbVie combines two large purchases (ImmunoGen USD 9.2bn net, Cerevel USD 8.3bn net) with a steady stream of USD 130m-2.1bn early-stage assets and options (ADARx USD 335m upfront) [CLM-009097, CLM-009061].

**Outcomes (audited)**
- Write-downs: AbbVie emraclidine USD 4.5bn of USD 8.7bn; J&J Ottava USD 0.9bn and bermekimab about USD 0.8bn; Lilly DICE DC-806 discontinued after a USD 1,916m charge; Takeda JPY 58.2bn, 27.8bn and 21.5bn [CLM-009100, CLM-009054, CLM-009003, CLM-009083, CLM-009084].
- Approvals: J&J Momenta (nipocalimab, FDA approval 2025-04-29; company announcement 04-30), Intra-Cellular (CAPLYTA MDD, about seven months after the 2025-04-02 close) [CLM-009044, CLM-009031]. Value destruction concentrates in neuroscience, gene and cell therapy and robotics [CLM-009100].

**Takeda's pattern**
- One flagship asset purchase (Nimbus, USD 4.0bn upfront plus two USD 1.0bn sales milestones), then licences, options and equity (Innovent: USD 1.2bn upfront including USD 100m equity, up to USD 11.4bn total), and write-offs of earlier purchases; Takeda states no significant acquisitions in the three years to March 2026 [CLM-009076, CLM-009078, CLM-009087, CLM-011075]. Four of six late-stage programs are externally sourced [CLM-005050].
- Ecosystem machinery: the Center for External Innovation is on the BaseLaunch board; Takeda Ventures scope is not public [CLM-009091, CLM-005052]. Terminations show partner risk: Neurocrine ended TAK-041/831; Takeda ended the Denali collaboration in April 2026 [CLM-009090, CLM-009089].

**Contrary evidence**
- J&J closed JLABS sites (Houston, Toronto, Washington DC, New York reported) [CLM-009052]. The AbbVie Ventures founding date conflict (2009 versus about 2015) is unresolved, so ecosystem-arm claims are inconclusive [CLM-009074]. Synthesis: [CLM-011076].

## Where proprietary advantage exists
- Proprietary advantage is clinical execution plus selection skill (deal choice and stop decisions), shown by Takeda's three late-stage approvals or filings on schedule and discipline in stopping soticlestat and cell therapy [CLM-005042, CLM-005024, CLM-005025].
- Partnering is better for new modalities, AI models and automation, where evidence of internal advantage is absent and open or shared models exist [CLM-006056, CLM-006058].

## Takeda fit and baseline class
| Therapeutic area | Fit | Baseline class | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| GI / immunology | Defence and successor assets (zasocitinib) from external source | 1, 7 | [CLM-009076, CLM-005017] |
| Rare / hematology | In-licensed first-in-class assets (rusfertide, elritercept) | 5 External innovation (EXISTING_STRENGTH for deals; organisation EVIDENCE_GAP) | [CLM-012151, CLM-005050] |
| Oncology | Innovent licence and option | 5 | [CLM-009078] |
| PDT | Manufacturing and plasma partners, little public detail | 2 | [CLM-005065] |

Economics: Takeda leverage was 2.6x adjusted net debt/EBITDA at March 2026 (A10 flags this value as unverified in the 20-F text) [CLM-005005]; large cash buys are constrained and options or licences fit the balance sheet better *(INTERPRETATION)*.

## Options (not endorsements)
| # | Option | Label | What must be true | Claim |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6.1 | Milestone-gated AI partnerships (see Domain 2) | EVIDENCE_BACKED | Stop rules honoured | [CLM-011060] |
| 6.2 | Option agreements in 1-2 modalities adjacent to existing disease depth | HYPOTHESIS | Option fee small; exercisable on Phase 1/2 data | [CLM-011061] |
| 6.3 | Deeper role in shared venture creation (BaseLaunch) instead of an owned incubator network | HYPOTHESIS | BaseLaunch portfolio outcomes acceptable (not assessed) | [CLM-011077] |
| 6.4 | Continue federated consortia | EVIDENCE_BACKED | See Domain 1 | [CLM-011054] |
| 6.5 | Another USD 5bn+ asset purchase | not assessed here; A11c finance module | Leverage and LOE-gap sizing | [CLM-009098] |

## Success criteria
- Share of Phase 3 and filing assets sourced externally that reach approval at or above the in-house rate, tracked by deal *(HYPOTHESIS)*.
- Contingent payments committed versus data-gated milestones achieved, per AI partnership *(HYPOTHESIS)*.
- Impairments as a percentage of deal value over a three-year window versus AbbVie (54% of Cerevel net price) [CLM-009054] *(HYPOTHESIS)*.

## Risks
- Single-asset concentration (Nimbus) and binary Phase 3 risk [CLM-009076].
- Partner termination (Denali, Neurocrine) [CLM-009089, CLM-009090].
- Antitrust and policy review of large transactions *(gap; not researched in this module)*.

## Evidence and gaps
Gaps: Takeda Ventures and CEI scope (IVB-007), external share of pipeline, deal-level realised revenue, full term sheets. See [evidence_gaps.md](evidence_gaps.md).

reports.title: Domain 7: People and operating model (A11b, wave 3)
reports.markdown:
# Domain 7: People and operating model (A11b, wave 3)

Research cutoff 2026-11-21. Takeda FY2025 = April 2025 to March 2026. Options are labelled EVIDENCE_BACKED or HYPOTHESIS; none is an endorsement. This is the thinnest domain in public evidence.

Framing rule: this file does not treat workforce change as replacement of people by automation. Roles change when tasks are automated; the evidence below separates efficiency programmes, which Takeda describes in its own terms, from AI and automation effects, which are unquantified.

Problem addressed: build the skills, governance and structure to use data, AI and new modalities while changing the cost base. *(INTERPRETATION)*

## What the evidence shows
**Competitors**
- J&J: nearly 900 generative-AI use cases were reviewed for risk, with 10-15% driving about 80% of value, and AI project ownership moved to departments to focus on high-value use cases (CIO interview relayed by a newsletter) [CLM-006018, CLM-006019]. 47,000 employees completed a required generative-AI course, which A10 treats as a training metric, not a deployment [CLM-006022]. Maturity: self-reported pilot to operational.
- AbbVie: ARCH was built by fewer than ten full-time staff plus contractors, with a governance decision to open data to all R&D [CLM-006032, CLM-006034].
- Lilly: a chief AI officer organisation exists, with compute and data investments but no workforce data [CLM-006003, CLM-006007].

**Takeda**
- 80% of the digital workforce was external when the transformation was designed, leading to large-scale insourcing through internal "digital factories" (executive interview via BCG, interested source) [CLM-005057]. Gabriele Ricci has been CDTO since February 2022 [CLM-005056].
- A March 2026 transformation targets over JPY 200bn gross annual savings by FY2028 through streamlining corporate functions, moving teams closer to patients and customers and process simplification; the cost series is JPY 150bn, 170bn then 160bn in successive company figures, and trade press reported about 4,500 role reductions (under 10% of roles) [CLM-005059, CLM-005078]. The May 2024 programme booked JPY 128.1bn and JPY 70.8bn of restructuring expense in FY2024 and FY2025 [CLM-005077].
- Julie Kim, with PDT and US commercial background, became CEO on 24 June 2026 [CLM-005073, CLM-005074]. Synthesis: [CLM-011078, CLM-011079].

**Contrary evidence and caveats**
- The share of the JPY 200bn attributable to technology versus other levers is unknown (IVB-003) [CLM-005078]. J&J's value-concentration figure rests on one interview [CLM-006019]. Digital-factory insourcing has no reported outcome [CLM-005057].

## Where proprietary advantage exists
- Governance, training and operating cadence are slow to copy but not secret; Takeda's advantage would be organisational (decision speed, stop discipline) rather than a technology asset *(INTERPRETATION)* [CLM-005025].
- Partnering is better for scarce specialist skills (AI model building) via the alliances already in place [CLM-005049].

## Takeda fit and baseline class
| Area | Fit | Baseline class | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Enterprise data and AI | Insourcing digital talent; agent platform for 10,000+ employees | 9 (EXISTING_BUT_UNDERDEVELOPED) | [CLM-005057, CLM-005058] |
| Cost transformation | Plan, not yet realised | 16 (EXISTING_BUT_UNDERDEVELOPED) | [CLM-005059, CLM-005078] |
| R&D (Shonan, Boston, Vienna) | Skills in AI-supported discovery unknown | 10 (EVIDENCE_GAP) | [CLM-005047, CLM-005049] |
| Manufacturing and plasma | Operator skills and quality culture matter after the Hikari warning letter | 2, 12 | [CLM-005020] |

Economics: realised savings and the technology capital envelope are not public (IVB-003, IVB-014).

## Options (not endorsements)
| # | Option | Label | What must be true | Claim |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 7.1 | Measure a small set of AI use cases against pre-agreed baselines and prune early | HYPOTHESIS | Baselines exist; owners accountable per department | [CLM-011080] |
| 7.2 | Pair the efficiency programme with a published reskilling and redeployment plan, measured by capability (tasks done with tools) rather than course completions | HYPOTHESIS | HR data can track task-level adoption | [CLM-011081] |
| 7.3 | Continue insourcing digital capability | HYPOTHESIS | Insourcing lowers cost or improves speed (no outcome reported) | [CLM-005057] |

## Success criteria
- Number of AI use cases in production with owner, baseline and measured benefit at 12 months *(HYPOTHESIS)*.
- Proportion of savings attributed to technology versus other levers, disclosed internally (closes IVB-003) *(HYPOTHESIS)*.
- Retention and internal-mobility rate in roles affected by automation *(HYPOTHESIS)*.

## Risks
- Execution load: a CEO transition, a restructuring and several launches in the same period [CLM-005073, CLM-005074, CLM-005078].
- Morale and capability loss if efficiency and AI are conflated in communication *(INTERPRETATION)*.
- Adoption-failure risk is disclosed by competitors (AbbVie 10-K) [CLM-006036].

## Evidence and gaps
Gaps: Takeda headcount by function, AI skill inventory, retention data, J&J and Lilly workforce effects, any independent study of AI productivity in pharma. See [evidence_gaps.md](evidence_gaps.md).

reports.title: Evidence gaps (A11b, wave 3)
reports.markdown:
# Evidence gaps (A11b, wave 3)

Research cutoff 2026-11-21.

## Could not open or verify
- Healthcare Dive (HTTP 403) and CNBC pages on the Google Health dissolution: only search snippets seen; registered metadata_only (SRC-011008, SRC-011009). Suggested next query: Alphabet statements or a primary report on the August 2021 reorganisation.
- Isomorphic Labs USD 600m Series A (Yahoo Finance snippet, SRC-011010): not opened; confirm with a company release.
- Flatiron regulatory-use claim (trastuzumab Japan approval): vendor snippet only (SRC-011016); needs a regulator record.
- NASA OIG IG-16-025 PDF (June 2015 failure): not readable with the available PDF library (encrypted); failure evidence taken from the NTRS COTS/CRS assessment (SRC-011005) instead.
- NASA COTS/CRS assessment author names and exact date not read (SRC-011005 notes this).
- TSMC "does not compete with its customers" wording not located in the 20-F passages read; kept as a labelled interpretation.

## Looked for and not found
- Any independent outcome (peer-reviewed, regulator or audited) from a competitor data, AI or autonomous-lab platform; independent TuneLab uptake data.
- Takeda: lab and plant automation, internal AI inventory, patient-services inventory, Ventures scope, headcount by function, technology share of the JPY 200bn savings (IVB-001, 002, 003, 007, 013).
- Realised revenue per acquisition for competitor deals (A9 gap).
- Moderna, Genentech/Roche research model, ASML and Epic analogies were not researched; the brief listed them as examples only.
- Public evidence for Domain 7 people effects of AI at Lilly, J&J, AbbVie beyond training metrics and interview statements.

## Source-quality warnings carried over from audit
- CLM-006017 (Strateos link, 2020 start) NOT_FOUND_IN_SOURCE: not used. CLM-006052's Zymergen element is supported by CLM-006051 instead. CLM-006020 maturity is self-reported pilot level. CLM-000284 describes an announced, not completed, installation. CLM-006054 wording is stronger than sources support. CLM-005005 leverage figure unverified in the 20-F text. CLM-009074 and CLM-009101 inconclusive.

## Suggested next research
1. Open a primary or regulator record for Google Health and Isomorphic claims.
2. Obtain NVIDIA developer-count methodology to reconcile 7.5 million vs 11 million.
3. Pull Lilly Q3 2026 release for any TuneLab or LillyPod outcome statement.
4. Research Moderna and Genentech models if the bets module needs a biotech platform analogue with outcome data.
5. Resolve the internal-validation backlog items cited above before any option labelled HYPOTHESIS is carried into a business case.

reports.title: Evidence gaps for Module 2 (A11c v2, wave 6)
reports.markdown:
# Evidence gaps for Module 2 (A11c v2, wave 6)

**Version v2** (A11c-bis, 2026-11-21).

Research cutoff 2026-11-21. Each gap names what is missing, which bets depend on it, and the internal-validation backlog item. An EVIDENCE_GAP in the Takeda baseline means public evidence is missing, not that the capability is absent [CLM-005080]. Takeda's internal data was not accessed.

| # | Gap | Bets affected | Effect on decisions | IVB |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Takeda multi-year technology and strategic-bet budget; every dollar figure here is an ASSUMPTION | All | Envelopes (ASM-002 to ASM-004) could be off by a multiple | IVB-014 |
| 2 | Inventory of AI and data products in production, users, outcomes | BET-01, 08, 17 | Maturity of class 9 determines whether BET-01 is a small extension or a larger build [CLM-005058] | IVB-001 |
| 3 | Lab automation footprint at Shonan, Boston, Vienna | BET-09, 10 | Whether renting is needed or capability exists [CLM-005067] | IVB-002 |
| 4 | Realised versus targeted savings; share attributable to technology | BET-17 | Separates AI from other levers [CLM-005078] [CLM-005059] | IVB-003 |
| 5 | Entyvio erosion scenarios, net price, SC share, litigation posture | BET-04, 11, 15 | ASM-024 and ASM-025 drive the exposure range [CLM-005017] [CLM-014050] | IVB-004 |
| 6 | Probability of success and launch forecasts for six late-stage programmes | BET-05, 06, 15 | USD 10-20bn is not probability-adjusted [CLM-014049] | IVB-005 |
| 7 | Plasma yield per centre, cost per litre, fractionation automation | BET-02 | Whether plasma is a platform strength; ASM-031 threshold [CLM-005063] | IVB-006 |
| 8 | Scope of Takeda Ventures and Center for External Innovation; external pipeline share | BET-06 | Capacity to run an option engine [CLM-014052] [CLM-005052] | IVB-007 |
| 9 | Early pipeline depth beyond six late-stage programmes | BET-03, 06 | Size of refill gap after 2030 [CLM-005044] | IVB-008 |
| 10 | Use of AI in target selection and alliance results | BET-07 | Nabla and Iambic outcomes unknown [CLM-005049] | IVB-010 |
| 11 | Inspection status of Hikari and other sites | BET-02, 05 | Launch timing and automation validation [CLM-005020] | IVB-011 |
| 12 | Amitiza judgment, trebling, cash timing; reserve adequacy | BET-18 (and rejected BET-15) and all envelopes | Leverage headroom (ASM-033, ASM-034) [CLM-005014] [CLM-014048] | IVB-012 |
| 13 | Patient-assistance and market-access inventory; hub outcomes | BET-04, 12, 13, 16 | No public rebate or persistence data [CLM-005072] [CLM-007039] | IVB-013 |
| 14 | Competitor orexin programmes (research gap, v2) | BET-03 | Competitor scan is a gate before the H2 tranche (RM-052) | none yet (new) |
| 15 | Statutory exclusivity date for Entyvio and Purple Book or U.S. litigation record (research gap, v2) | BET-04 | Early-entry stress case S-A (ASM-038) and the 2028-2032 range of ASM-025 | IVB-004 |
| 16 | Entyvio medical-benefit versus pharmacy-benefit split | BET-04, BET-11 | Benefit-channel gate 2027 H1 (RM-003) | IVB-004 |
| 17 | Plasma peer set for yield and cost per litre; demand-versus-capacity evidence | BET-02 | Plasma-peer benchmark and demand-versus-capacity test are gates (RM-004, RM-051) | IVB-006 |

## Gaps in competitor evidence

- No independent outcome for any data, AI or automation platform at Lilly, J&J or AbbVie; the audit worded the 'no demonstrated outcome' point more strongly than its sources support [CLM-006054] [CLM-011052].
- TuneLab uptake and retraining counts, ARCH outcomes beyond a preprint, Lilly-NVIDIA lab operating status [CLM-006007] [CLM-006032] [CLM-000281].
- Reason for Lilly's sale of its robotic lab; the Strateos link is unsupported [CLM-006017].
- Option outcomes: none from the window had produced an approved product by cutoff [CLM-009097].
- Antitrust and policy review of large transactions was not researched [CLM-009098].
- Devices and care models: no adherence, persistence or time-to-therapy outcome for any company [CLM-007039].
- Analogies (NVIDIA, SpaceX, Google, Regeneron, TSMC, AWS, Intuitive, Flatiron) generate hypotheses and are not proof; several sources are snippets [CLM-011024] [CLM-011013].

## Method limits of this module

- PTS and commercial probability ranges are judgment (ASM-020, ASM-021, ASM-022, ASM-028), not derived from Takeda data.
- Scenario robustness is an interpretation of bet design and competitor evidence.
- Stage-gate capital is a convention (ASM-037); owner roles are generic and delegated limits are an ASSUMPTION.
- No registry or shard writes were made; new evidence needs would be added under A11_strategy ids from 011500.

## Changes from v1 (evidence gaps)

- Row 5 and row 2: research gaps 14 (competitor orexin landscape) and 15 (statutory Entyvio exclusivity date) added as carried by the decision record's open items.
- Row 6: gap 16 (benefit-channel split) is now a hard gate for BET-04.
- Row 4: gap 17 (plasma peers, demand versus capacity) is now a gate for BET-02.
- Row 1: gap 12 re-pointed to BET-18.

reports.markdown:
# Strategic bets for Takeda, 2027-2040 (A11c v2, wave 6)

**Version v2** (A11c-bis, 2026-11-21): revised to the Director's decision record [DIRECTOR_DECISION_RECORD.md](../critical_challenges/DIRECTOR_DECISION_RECORD.md). v1 sizes, decisions and labels are listed in the Changes section below.

Research cutoff 2026-11-21. Takeda fiscal years run April-March (FY2025 = April 2025 to March 2026); Takeda amounts stay in JPY unless converted at ASM-001 for sizing only. This file proposes candidates; it does not endorse any of them. Eighteen candidates are assessed on a common template A-M (BET-18 is a v2 addition, council-proposed); five carry a decision other than BUILD, PARTNER, INVEST or EXPERIMENT (four REJECT, one DEFER) so the reader can see the alternatives that were considered and set aside.

**Labels.** FACT (registry claim), INTERPRETATION (reading of facts), HYPOTHESIS (reasoned, needs non-public data), SCENARIO (conditional future), RECOMMENDATION (proposed action). ASSUMPTION marks any number that is not a registry claim; each carries an ASM- id defined in [assumptions_register.md](../financial_cases/assumptions_register.md) and `strategy/data/assumptions.json`. Takeda's budget, headcount and internal data are not public (IVB-014); no figure here is a Takeda budget.

**Audit corrections honoured.** Takeda cell-therapy impairment is JPY 58.2bn (JPY 58.0bn was the earlier expectation) [CLM-005025]; the restructuring-cost series is about JPY 150bn, 170.0bn, then 160.0bn [CLM-005078]; Morphic headline USD 3.2bn versus audited charge 2.55bn [CLM-009002]; OTTAVA installation is announced, not shown complete [CLM-000284]; the Strateos link and 2020 date for Lilly's lab are unsupported [CLM-006017]; the 'no independent outcome' claim is worded more strongly than its sources support [CLM-006054]; J&J AI metrics are self-reported [CLM-006020] [CLM-006022]; AbbVie ImmunoGen is USD 9.2bn net of cash [CLM-003086]. **Invalid comparisons not used:** the share of FY2025 revenue from post-2021 molecules is not used as a productivity ranking; deal values across companies are not summed; Takeda capex including intangibles is not compared with Lilly property, plant and equipment capex; a Takeda revenue-share-from-new-molecules figure is not computable [CLM-012013] [CLM-009098] [CLM-005007].

## Summary


| ID | Bet | Decision | Confidence | Baseline class | Horizon | Balanced USD m 2027-40 (ASSUMPTION) | Hard prerequisites |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BET-01 | Governed cross-franchise R&D data and decision layer | BUILD | hypothesis | EXISTING_BUT_UNDERDEVELOPED | H1 | 200 | none |
| BET-02 | Plasma process-intelligence and fixed-price automation programme | EXPERIMENT | hypothesis | EXISTING_STRENGTH | H1 | 230 | none |
| BET-03 | Orexin science as a multi-asset discovery platform | BUILD | hypothesis | EXISTING_STRENGTH | H2 | 300 | none |
| BET-04 | Entyvio franchise defence: payer contracting, evidence and lifecycle | BUILD | hypothesis | EXISTING_STRENGTH | H1 | 140 | none |
| BET-05 | Zasocitinib breadth and immunology successor evidence | INVEST | hypothesis | EXISTING_BUT_UNDERDEVELOPED | H1 | 180 | none |
| BET-06 | Option-based external innovation engine incl. new-modality options | PARTNER | hypothesis | EXISTING_STRENGTH | H2 | 300 | none |
| BET-07 | Milestone-gated AI-design partnerships (Nabla, Iambic and successors) | PARTNER | hypothesis | EVIDENCE_GAP | H2 | 80 | BET-01, BET-09 |
| BET-08 | Federated data consortium participation | PARTNER | hypothesis | EXISTING_BUT_UNDERDEVELOPED | H1 | 35 | none |
| BET-09 | Rented automated data generation (CRO and cloud labs) with ladder triggers | PARTNER | hypothesis | EVIDENCE_GAP | H1 | 95 | none |
| BET-10 | Owned autonomous discovery lab (stage 4-5) | REJECT | hypothesis | EVIDENCE_GAP | H3 | 0 | BET-01, BET-09, BET-07 |
| BET-11 | Drug-device and home/SC administration platform | BUILD | hypothesis | EXISTING_STRENGTH | H1 | 190 | none |

Balanced total 1,920; constrained 1,130; ambitious 3,155 (USD m, cumulative 2027-2040, ASM-002 to ASM-004; v1: 2,950 / 1,590 / 4,975). The balanced total is committed at gates; about USD 1,030m of contingent headroom is reserved for BET-18 (ASM-118) and is not a saving. BET-15 is rejected and outside every envelope.

## Sequencing: does data infrastructure have to come first? *(HYPOTHESIS argued from evidence)*

Three positions are possible: (a) data infrastructure first, then automation; (b) a bounded lab-automation initiative that seeds its own data foundation; (c) both in parallel with a defined hand-off. The evidence supports (c) with a hard gate at stage 3.

- Stages 1-2 of the automation ladder (assisted and scripted high-throughput work) are operational and commodity, and the continuing model is a service: Arctoris runs the former Lilly platform as a CRO and sells data generation to AI customers [CLM-006013] [CLM-006016] [CLM-011062]. A rented initiative (BET-09) therefore produces data without Takeda owning robots, and it can seed a structured assay dataset if a minimal schema is enforced from the first contract. This is a thin slice of BET-01, not the full layer.
- Stage 3 and above (AI planning tied to wet labs) has no independent demonstration [CLM-011062]. Judging it needs a decision log and baselines (BET-01), because without them a vendor claim such as Nabla's three to four week loop cannot be tested against a conventional comparator [CLM-006040]. Zymergen paired automation and ML and sold at about one-tenth of its IPO-era valuation after USD 1.2bn of cumulative net losses [CLM-006051]. (INTERPRETATION)
- The data layer is cheap relative to the cost of automating without it: AbbVie's ARCH was built by fewer than ten full-time staff plus contractors [CLM-006032]. This is one company's example, so the point is about order of magnitude, not a Takeda cost (see ASM-101).
- Plasma operations are the exception: nomogram and process data already exist at site level [CLM-005060], so BET-02 can seed its own data foundation and does not wait for BET-01.

**Dependency chain (hard):** BET-01 and BET-09 (H1 2027) -> BET-07 benchmarking (needs both; RM-020 now depends on RM-015 and RM-018) -> stage-3 pilot only if three triggers fire (independent Lilly-lab result, Nabla first-in-human data, measured CRO cost) [CLM-011066] -> any owned-lab reconsideration (BET-10, rejected now). BET-13 needs BET-01 and BET-12. BET-14 needs BET-01 and a measured advantage. BET-18 is released only after the leverage test (ASM-033, IVB-012) and takes sizing input from BET-05 launch curves. **Soft dependencies:** BET-02 on BET-01 standards from 2028; BET-12 on BET-17.

## Template

A thesis; B future market change; C problem; D evidence (claim IDs); E moat mechanism; F practical architecture; G investment (balanced and the other portfolios, ranges per ASM-036); H time to value; I measurable outcomes; J risks; K strategic options; L decision; M evidence and confidence (known / assumed / needs Takeda internal validation).


---

## BET-01 Governed cross-franchise R&D data and decision layer

**Decision: BUILD** | Horizon H1 | Baseline class: EXISTING_BUT_UNDERDEVELOPED | Confidence: hypothesis

**A. Thesis.** Make Takeda's own trial, real-world, assay and plasma data reusable under one governed layer so that a small number of named decisions (target choice, trial design, supply planning) can be measured against a pre-agreed baseline. (RECOMMENDATION, conditional on IVB-001.)

**B. Future market change.** Competitors are building proprietary data assets and opening them internally: AbbVie ARCH holds 124 TB and opened de-identified data from 2,000+ trials to all R&D; Lilly TuneLab rests on data Lilly estimates cost over USD 1bn [CLM-006032] [CLM-006034] [CLM-000280]. Compute and third-party models are purchasable by rivals, so proprietary data is the one defensible input [CLM-006055]. (INTERPRETATION)

**C. Problem.** Takeda's public record shows a platform and an aspiration but no quantified AI or data outcome [CLM-006045] [CLM-011053]. Without an inventory of products, users and outcomes, spending cannot be linked to value (IVB-001). Whether Takeda's data estate is fragmented as AbbVie's was is unknown (HYPOTHESIS) [CLM-011055].

**D. Evidence.**

- FACT: ARCH was built by fewer than ten full-time staff plus contractors; a governance decision opened trial data to all R&D [CLM-006032] [CLM-006034]. Outcome evidence is a preprint not opened by A6.
- FACT: across ARCH, TuneLab, Polyphonic and the AISB model, none has independent outcome evidence [CLM-011052] [CLM-006054 as corrected by the audit: wording stronger than sources support].
- FACT: Takeda reports 63.4% of workforce using gen-AI tools; this is a usage measure, as are J&J's course completions and unbaselined enrolment multiple [CLM-014043] [CLM-006022] [CLM-006020].
- HYPOTHESIS: one governed layer raises reuse of Takeda's own trial and real-world data if the estate is fragmented [CLM-011055].
- FACT (risk): FDA's January 2025 draft guidance proposes risk-based credibility for AI used in regulatory decisions, so model evidence must be documented [CLM-006046]; Takeda's own 20-F warns models may be flawed or trained on inadequate data [CLM-005054].

*Takeda baseline.* Class 9, enterprise data and AI platform: a Databricks-hosted agent platform for 10,000+ employees exists, outcomes unproven [CLM-005058] [CLM-005080]. Maturity must be assessed first (IVB-001), so this bet extends and governs an existing platform; it does not start a new one.

*Competitor analogues.* ABBV: [CLM-006032] [CLM-006034]; LLY: [CLM-000280] [CLM-006008]

**E. Moat mechanism.** data, learning, workflow_integration. Data and learning: decision-linked data that is costly to regenerate improves each later model and trial design; workflow integration comes from embedding the layer in named decisions. It compounds only if each decision is logged against a baseline so the layer learns from outcomes (INTERPRETATION) [CLM-011082].

**F. Practical architecture.** Build: Governance, data catalogue, decision log and metrics on the existing platform; Reuse policy for de-identified trial and real-world data. Buy: none. License: Commodity data tooling from the existing Databricks relationship [CLM-005058]. Partner: Federated consortia for pooled tasks (BET-08).

**G. Investment (USD m, cumulative by horizon, ASSUMPTION; ranges per ASM-036; ids ASM-101).**


| Portfolio | H1 2027-29 initial | H2 2030-34 follow-on | H3 2035-40 scaled | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| capital_constrained | 40 (30-50) | 50 (30-70) | 30 (20-40) | 120 |
| balanced | 60 (45-75) | 80 (50-110) | 60 (35-85) | 200 |
| ambitious | 90 (70-110) | 130 (80-180) | 120 (70-170) | 340 |


**H. Time to value.** Near term: 12-24 months: production inventory, 2-3 decisions with baselines (closes IVB-001). Long horizon: 2030-2035: model-informed target and trial-design decisions with measured cycle-time or hit-rate effect; 2035-2040: compounding only if measured.

**I. Measurable outcomes.**

- Inventory of data and AI products in production with owner, users, baseline and measured benefit
- Named decisions where a model changed the outcome versus a pre-agreed baseline
- Share of trial data reusable across franchises

**J. Risks.**

- data: Estate may already be well governed, so the incremental value is small (IVB-001).
- regulatory: AI credibility documentation expectations [CLM-006046].
- adoption: Usage is mistaken for value, as in competitor metrics [CLM-006022].
- capital: Platform spend without outcome evidence is hard to stop once started.

**K. Strategic options.** expand, redirect, partner, stop. Expand if two decisions show measured gains by gate 3; redirect to federated use (BET-08) if Takeda data proves too sparse; stop if no baseline can be set.

**L. Decision: BUILD.** Small, ring-fenced and a prerequisite for stage-3 automation and for judging AI partnerships; the maturity assessment (IVB-001) gates the follow-on. Hard prerequisites: none. Sequencing: Start with a thin slice (metadata standards and decision log) in H1 2027 alongside BET-09; the full layer is a hard prerequisite for any stage-3 closed-loop pilot (HYPOTHESIS). Argument: AbbVie built ARCH with fewer than ten staff [CLM-006032], so the data layer costs little relative to running automation without it; Zymergen paired automation and ML and still failed commercially [CLM-006051].

**M. Evidence and confidence (hypothesis).** Known: Platform exists; competitors' data layers exist; no outcomes anywhere [CLM-005058] [CLM-011052]. Assumed: Cost and fragmentation level (ASM-101); that decisions can be baselined. Needs Takeda internal validation: IVB-001, IVB-010, IVB-014 ([backlog](../../New_mediciine/companies/takeda_public_baseline/internal_validation_backlog/backlog.md)).

**v2 changes from v1.** (decision record row 7) Roadmap: RM-015 (decision log gate) is now a wired prerequisite of RM-020 (BET-07 stop-or-expand). Size unchanged.


---

## BET-02 Plasma process-intelligence and fixed-price automation programme

**Decision: EXPERIMENT** | Horizon H1 | Baseline class: EXISTING_STRENGTH | Confidence: hypothesis

**A. Thesis.** Test whether donor, yield and process data from the plasma network are a proprietary data class (no plasma peer is in the comparison set, so uniqueness is untested) by funding only a baseline, a demand-versus-capacity test, a plasma-peer benchmark and a one-site shadow-mode tranche before any fixed-price automation or network roll-out. (HYPOTHESIS) [CLM-011056] [CLM-011031]

**B. Future market change.** Plasma-derived therapies sit outside the biosimilar mechanism that threatens Entyvio; immunoglobulins were JPY 790.6bn (18% of FY2025 revenue) with PDT revenue +8.5% AER in H1 FY2026 (-1.5% CER), which does not show that capacity rather than demand binds [CLM-005064]. Lilly's record shows capacity bound a blockbuster until 2024, but that is an obesity-drug analogue, not plasma [CLM-001066] [CLM-000172]. (INTERPRETATION)

**C. Problem.** Whether plasma is a platform strength or only a large business depends on yield per centre and cost per litre, which are not public (IVB-006). Automation in GMP settings carries validation burden and Takeda has one documented warning letter and supply shortage [CLM-005020].

**D. Evidence.**

- FACT: nomogram programmes rolled out across 270+ centres; AI-powered donor tools reported in FY2025 [CLM-005060] [CLM-014046]; 170+ predictive-maintenance agents at Lessines with expansion planned by 2027 (company-reported, no outcome) [CLM-014041].
- FACT: NASA documents record Falcon 9 development at about USD 390m against model estimates of USD 1.7-4.0bn under fixed-price contracts, but the cause of the gap is not isolated and each cargo partner suffered catastrophic failures [CLM-011005] [CLM-011006] [CLM-011008]. Analogy only.
- FACT (counter-evidence): no public evidence of Takeda lab, continuous-manufacturing or manufacturing robotics [CLM-005067]; Lilly's Lebanon robotics were seen on a tour with no performance data [CLM-006002]; Medicine Foundry (USD 4.5bn) is concept [CLM-006000] [CLM-006001].
- HYPOTHESIS: a neutral-capacity or shared-analytics role could follow if spare capacity exists; sponsors guard process and liability [CLM-011041] [CLM-011040].
- FACT: PDT revenue was -1.5% at constant rates in H1 FY2026, so the public record does not show a capacity constraint; a demand-versus-capacity test is a gate [CLM-005064].
- INTERPRETATION: 'no competitor holds this data' holds only because the comparison set has no plasma peer; the registry holds none, so a plasma-peer benchmark is a gate [CLM-011056] [CLM-009091].
- FACT (counter-evidence): fixed-price vendor terms are a NEEDS_MORE_RESEARCH hypothesis and there is no fixed-price vendor evidence for plasma plants [CLM-011031].

*Takeda baseline.* Class 2, plasma network and PDT manufacturing: 233 to 275 centres (FY2022-FY2024), 270+ with adaptive nomograms, 99.6% on-time in-full, USD 230m Los Angeles fractionation expansion; yield and cost per litre are not public (IVB-006) [CLM-005063] [CLM-005060] [CLM-014046] [CLM-005065]. Class 12 manufacturing quality is EXISTING_BUT_UNDERDEVELOPED after the Hikari warning letter [CLM-005020]. This bet builds on a strength; it must first measure headroom.

*Competitor analogues.* LLY: [CLM-001066] [CLM-000172] [CLM-006002]

**E. Moat mechanism.** data, infrastructure, learning, regulatory_experience. Infrastructure and data: fractionation capacity takes years to copy and process data compounds with each batch; learning if yield models are retrained on every lot. Regulatory experience is the support layer: automated steps must be validated, which is slow for rivals and for Takeda (INTERPRETATION) [CLM-011085] [CLM-011039].

**F. Practical architecture.** Build: Process-data capture and yield models; Single-site (Los Angeles) pilot design and acceptance criteria. Buy: none. License: Nomogram and donor-tool vendors already used [CLM-005060]. Partner: Automation vendors on fixed-price, outcome-linked terms [CLM-011031].

**G. Investment (USD m, cumulative by horizon, ASSUMPTION; ranges per ASM-036; ids ASM-102).**


| Portfolio | H1 2027-29 initial | H2 2030-34 follow-on | H3 2035-40 scaled | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| capital_constrained | 25 (20-30) | 55 (35-75) | 45 (25-65) | 125 |
| balanced | 80 (60-100) | 100 (60-140) | 50 (30-70) | 230 |
| ambitious | 65 (50-80) | 170 (100-240) | 160 (95-225) | 395 |


**H. Time to value.** Near term: 2027-2029: yield and cost-per-litre baseline, demand-versus-capacity test, plasma-peer benchmark and a one-site shadow-mode run; remainder released only if all pass. Long horizon: 2030-2035: network roll-out if headroom is shown; 2035-2040: possible neutral analytics offer (low confidence).

**I. Measurable outcomes.**

- Yield per litre of plasma, deviation rate and cost per litre before and after pilot (company-defined)
- On-time in-full held at or above FY2025 99.6% [CLM-014046]
- Inspection record without new observations
- Demand-versus-capacity test result (is plasma demand- or capacity-bound?)
- Plasma-peer benchmark of yield and cost per litre against the ASM-031 threshold re-based on money

**J. Risks.**

- regulatory: GMP validation of automated steps; prior warning letter [CLM-005020].
- execution: Vendor fixed-price terms may not be available at plant complexity.
- data: Donor data capture may be inconsistent across centres (IVB-006).
- capital: Incremental to the base USD 230m expansion; double-counting risk [CLM-005065].
- competition: Plasma peers' data position is unbenchmarked; the uniqueness claim may fail [CLM-011056] [CLM-009091].
- adoption: Demand-bound, not capacity-bound, would remove the case for automation capex [CLM-005064].

**K. Strategic options.** expand, redirect, partner, stop. Expand to a pilot only if the baseline shows headroom and demand is capacity-bound; redirect to other core uses if demand-bound; stop if headroom is below the re-based ASM-031 threshold.

**L. Decision: EXPERIMENT.** Cheap baseline and shadow-mode tranche produces the data the council says is missing; the remainder of the programme is contingent on the demand-versus-capacity test, the plasma-peer benchmark and ASM-031 re-based on money (value of a gain per litre against pilot and run cost). Takeda-execution council dissent recorded: it supports BUILD because the CEO led the PDT unit and the network runs 270+ centres at 99.6% on-time in-full [CLM-005074] [CLM-005063] [CLM-014046]. The red team's call to reject any plasma spend is not accepted. Hard prerequisites: none. Sequencing: Baseline and shadow-mode tranche first (about USD 65m at risk in the first two gates, ASSUMPTION ASM-102); the pilot, roll-out and neutral-analytics decision are contingent. Nomogram and process data already exist at site level [CLM-005060], so the tranche does not wait for BET-01; soft dependency on BET-01 standards from 2028.

**M. Evidence and confidence (hypothesis).** Known: Network scale, capacity expansion, on-time in-full [CLM-005063] [CLM-005065] [CLM-014046]. Assumed: Yield and cost headroom (ASM-031); cost of upgrades (ASM-102). Needs Takeda internal validation: IVB-006, IVB-011, IVB-014 ([backlog](../../New_mediciine/companies/takeda_public_baseline/internal_validation_backlog/backlog.md)).

**v2 changes from v1.** (decision record row 4) BUILD -> EXPERIMENT; balanced USD 430m -> 230m (baseline and shadow-mode tranche about USD 65m at risk, remainder contingent); ASM-031 re-based on money; demand-versus-capacity and plasma-peer tests added as gates; Takeda-execution council dissent recorded.


---

## BET-03 Orexin science as a multi-asset discovery platform

**Decision: BUILD** | Horizon H2 | Baseline class: EXISTING_STRENGTH | Confidence: hypothesis

**A. Thesis.** Run orexin biology as a platform with a second differentiated asset, funded at the constrained discovery size, with a Phase 1 gate before the H2 tranche, an additionality test against base R&D and a competitor orexin scan. (HYPOTHESIS) [CLM-011038]

**B. Future market change.** A platform does not protect a single product (Regeneron EYLEA net sales -42% in 2025), so the value of a platform is repeated assets (INTERPRETATION) [CLM-011017] [CLM-011037]. Neuroscience and psychiatry is the common failure site of the window across AbbVie, J&J and Takeda [CLM-003054] [CLM-002039] [CLM-012120].

**C. Problem.** After 2030 the six late-stage programmes carry the pipeline; refill depends on early depth that is not public (IVB-008). TAK-994 was stopped for liver safety, so a second asset is not assured [CLM-005023].

**D. Evidence.**

- FACT: oveporexton approved 2026-08-05 from in-house discovery; efficacy statements are company-reported [CLM-012149] [CLM-005048].
- FACT: TAK-994 stopped (liver-related signal); soticlestat Phase 3 missed (June 2024), JPY 21.5bn impairment [CLM-012119] [CLM-012120] [CLM-009083].
- FACT (analogue): Regeneron built VelociSuite and a genetics centre with over 3 million samples; contribution to approvals is not quantified [CLM-011015] [CLM-011016].
- INTERPRETATION: the lesson from AbbVie, J&J and Takeda is to gate CNS assets on Phase 2 quality and placebo response, and not to infer that orexin success transfers to other CNS bets [CLM-003057] [CLM-012135].
- INTERPRETATION: the orexin discovery team already sits in base R&D (JPY 675.9bn), so the incrementality of the spend cannot be tested without an additionality test [CLM-005004] [CLM-005048].
- FACT (research gap): competitor orexin programmes are not in the registry; a competitor scan is a gate [CLM-005029].

*Takeda baseline.* Class 3, rare disease and orexin science: oveporexton discovered in Shonan, FDA-approved 2026-08-05; Takeda calls itself world leader in orexin science [CLM-005048] [CLM-012149]. Pipeline refill beyond the six late-stage programmes is unknown (IVB-008) [CLM-005044].

*Competitor analogues.* ABBV: [CLM-003054] [CLM-003057]; JNJ: [CLM-002039]

**E. Moat mechanism.** ip, learning, regulatory_experience. IP and learning: disease-biology depth is slow to buy and each asset's clinical data sharpens the next; regulatory experience from a first approval lowers review risk for follow-ons. Compounding requires a second asset and is unproven (HYPOTHESIS) [CLM-011036].

**F. Practical architecture.** Build: Discovery and early clinical team in Shonan with a multi-asset plan. Buy: none. License: Tools and models for design as needed. Partner: Academic and AI-design collaborators milestone-gated (BET-07).

**G. Investment (USD m, cumulative by horizon, ASSUMPTION; ranges per ASM-036; ids ASM-103).**


| Portfolio | H1 2027-29 initial | H2 2030-34 follow-on | H3 2035-40 scaled | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|

## BET-04 Entyvio franchise defence: payer contracting, evidence and lifecycle

**Decision: BUILD** | Horizon H1 | Baseline class: EXISTING_STRENGTH | Confidence: hypothesis

**A. Thesis.** Build payer-contracting and formulary-defence depth, outcomes evidence and lifecycle plans for Entyvio ahead of Medicare negotiation (January 2028) and biosimilar entry, to delay erosion and measure it. The outcome is 'delay and measure', not 'retain revenue': the January 2028 price is statutory and PBM private-label biosimilars route around contracts. **B. Future market change.** Entyvio loses regulatory exclusivity in the latter half of the decade, some patents expire in 2032 with revocation actions filed, two biosimilar BLAs are under FDA review, and Entyvio is selected for Medicare negotiation from January 2028 [CLM-005017] [CLM-014050] [CLM-014051] [CLM-007026]. PBM template changes decide outcomes: from 1 July 2026 CVS template formularies prefer interchangeable Stelara biosimilars [CLM-007015], and Takeda's 20-F says rebate details are undisclosed and formulary exclusion can directly reduce usage [CLM-007025].

**C. Problem.** Entyvio is the largest single exposure and Takeda's contracting depth is unknown. Humira lost 78.6% in three years even with rebate-for-access contracts and a co-brand route, and U.S. Humira fell 41% in 2024 and 57% in 2025 [CLM-003002] [CLM-003007] [CLM-003010] [CLM-007016].

- FACT: AbbVie's settlements put Rinvoq generic entry not before April 2037, four years after the 2033 composition patent [CLM-003021] [CLM-003087].
- FACT: Lilly realised prices fell 5% (Q4 2025) and 15% (Q3 2026) while volume rose 46% and 53% [CLM-014003] [CLM-014004]; CVS Caremark removed Zepbound for about 15 months (1 July 2025 to restoration on 1 October 2026) [CLM-007011] [CLM-007013].

- FACT (gap): the registry has no Entyvio medical-benefit versus pharmacy-benefit split, so the contractable share of volume is unknown; this is the benefit-channel gate (IVB-004) [CLM-005072] [CLM-007016].

Decision: REJECT.** The strategy's own leverage test fails by arithmetic (ASM-033, ASM-119) and Takeda's pattern is mid-size licensing (Nimbus, Innovent); the gap is covered by BET-18, not by a trigger-based purchase.
