| A13 App | `executive_application/**`, `data/**` | none (reads registries only) |

NEVER write to: `map.md`, `PROJECT_STATE.md`, `CONTINUE.md`, `New_mediciine/evidence_library/*_registry.jsonl`, another agent's shard or company directory.

## 2. How to register evidence

Shard files are plain JSONL: `New_mediciine/evidence_library/shards/<shard>/sources.jsonl` and `claims.jsonl`.
You may append lines directly with a script, or use the CLI (validates as it writes):

```bash
PY=~/.local/share/mise/installs/python/3.12/bin/python3
cd ~/Desktop/MEDICINE
$PY tools/evidence.py ids A1_lilly                  # shows next free IDs
$PY tools/evidence.py fetch "https://..." --grep "tirzepatide" --store-raw   # retrieves, hashes, extracts text, greps
$PY tools/evidence.py add-source --shard A1_lilly --json /tmp/src.json
$PY tools/evidence.py add-claim  --shard A1_lilly --json /tmp/clm.json
$PY tools/evidence.py validate --shard A1_lilly --path New_mediciine/evidence_library/shards/A1_lilly/sources.jsonl
```

### Source record (all keys shown; required ones marked *)

```json
{"source_id":"SRC-001001"*, "title":"Eli Lilly Q4 2025 earnings release (8-K Ex. 99.1)"*,
 "publisher":"Eli Lilly and Company via SEC EDGAR"*, "company":"eli_lilly"*,
 "domain":"financials"*, "source_type":"earnings_release"*,
 "original_url":"https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/59478/..."*, "canonical_url":"..."*,
 "publication_date":"2026-02-05", "reporting_period":"FY2025", "access_date":"2026-11-21"*,
 "credibility":"T1_primary_official"*, "access_status":"retrieved"*,
 "document_identifier":"0000059478-26-000xxx", "locator":"Table 'Revenue by product', p.7",
 "inspected_passage":"<= 600 chars verbatim from the document, exactly as it appears>",
 "sha256":"optional from fetch", "raw_path":"optional", "extracted_text_path":"optional",
 "licensing":"public record | company IR (fair-use excerpt) | paywalled (metadata only)",
 "notes":"limitations, e.g. interested party; PDF page numbering offset"}
```

Enumerations: company `eli_lilly|johnson_johnson|abbvie|takeda|industry|other`; domain `business|financials|pipeline|scientific_rd|data_ai|robotics_automation|commercial_market_access|patient_care|partnerships_ma|policy_regulation|leadership|successes_failures|competitive_advantage|methodology|strategy`; source_type `sec_filing|annual_report|earnings_release|earnings_transcript|investor_presentation|press_release|company_web|regulatory_record|clinical_trial_registry|peer_reviewed|preprint|patent|lobbying_disclosure|government_record|news_tier1|news_trade|industry_report|academic_report|interview_transcript|podcast_video|dataset_api|other`; credibility `T1_primary_official|T2_company_technical|T3_independent_reputable|T4_expert_commentary|T5_speculative`; access_status `retrieved|api_json|metadata_only|blocked|paywalled|unavailable`.

Rule: `access_status: retrieved` REQUIRES `inspected_passage`. If you could not open it, use `metadata_only` and say so in notes. Never paste a passage you did not see.

### Claim record

```json
{"claim_id":"CLM-001001"*, "statement":"<= 600 chars, one factual sentence with date/period>"*,
 "kind":"FACT|INTERPRETATION|HYPOTHESIS|SCENARIO|RECOMMENDATION"*,
 "status":"SUPPORTED|PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED|CONTRADICTED|INCONCLUSIVE|NEEDS_MORE_RESEARCH"*,
 "companies":["eli_lilly"]*, "domain":"data_ai"*, "supporting_source_ids":["SRC-001001"]*,
 "locator":"section/table/page/timestamp inside the source", "dates":{"event":"2025-09-16","period":"FY2025"},
 "contrary_evidence":"text or null", "contrary_source_ids":[],
 "confidence_rationale":"why we believe it: who said it, interested party?, corroborated?"*,
 "single_interested_source":true, "last_verified":"2026-11-21"*,
 "maturity":"concept|prototype|pilot|operational|scaled|demonstrated_outcome|not_applicable|unknown",
 "entities":{"products":["tirzepatide"],"partners":["NVIDIA"],"technologies":["foundation model"]},
 "implication":"analyst interpretation, clearly separated from the fact",
 "related_reports":["New_mediciine/companies/eli_lilly/data_ai/ai_initiatives.md"], "tags":[]}
```

Rules: one statement per claim; FACT claims cite only sources you opened; the `implication` field is the only place for your interpretation; a company statement about intent is a FACT *that the statement was made*, not a FACT about outcome; every AI/robotics claim carries `maturity`.

## 3. Minimum deliverables per research agent

1. Markdown reports in your allowed directory (one per sub-domain) — every material sentence cites `[CLM-xxxxxx]`.
2. `map.md` inside your company/domain directory listing every file you wrote, one line each with relative link.
3. `evidence_gaps.md`: what you looked for and could not find/open; blocked URLs; unresolved questions.
4. `timeline.md` (company agents): dated events 2021-11 to 2026-11 with claim IDs.
5. Shard JSONL files validated with `evidence.py validate --shard <shard>` (0 errors) before you finish.
6. A completion report (your final message) in this exact shape:

```
FILES WRITTEN: <relative paths, one per line>
SOURCES: <n> (retrieved <n>, metadata_only <n>, blocked <n>)   CLAIMS: <n> (FACT <n>, other <n>)
VALIDATION: evidence.py validate output (0 errors required)
TOP 10 FINDINGS: <one line each, with claim IDs>
EVIDENCE GAPS: <bullets>
RECOMMENDED NEXT RESEARCH: <bullets>
```

## 4. Research conduct

- Source hierarchy T1 > T2 > T3 > T4; T5 never as fact. Press release = announcement happened, not value realized.
- Search by: company+domain, molecule/target, platform+partner, executive name, period, NCT number, deal identifier, DOI, and explicitly for *failure / delay / discontinued / criticism / lawsuit*.
- Open the primary document. Quote the passage. Record the locator.
- For every "capability" claim, ask: problem, what was built/bought, enablers (data/talent/IP/infra/partners), pilot vs production, operational change, measurable outcome, cost (if disclosed), defensibility.
- Seek contrary evidence for each major finding; record it in `contrary_evidence`.
- Rate-limit yourself (>= 1 s between requests to one host). Respect robots/terms. Do not bypass paywalls or logins. `investor.lilly.com` blocks scripted clients: use SEC EDGAR 8-K exhibits (`https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0000059478&type=8-K`) and `lilly.com/news`.
- Bounded retries: 2 attempts per URL, then record `blocked|unavailable` and move on.
- Do not read the entire encyclopedia. Read `map.md` + your company/domain `map.md` + `tools/evidence.py ids <shard>` and begin.

## 5. Handoff hygiene

Save progressively (after every ~5 sources). Leave the shard valid at all times. If you run low on budget, write `evidence_gaps.md` and the completion report rather than another half-finished report.

reports.title: Evaluation rubric (the fixed evaluator — do not edit to make a batch pass)
reports.markdown:
# Evaluation rubric (the fixed evaluator — do not edit to make a batch pass)

Score each axis 0 (fails), 1 (partial), 2 (meets). Write one sentence of justification per axis. A batch is ACCEPT if no axis is 0 and total >= 12/16; REVISE if total 9-11 or any single 0 that is repairable; RESEARCH_FURTHER if coverage or corroboration is 0; BLOCKED if sources are inaccessible.

| Axis | 0 | 1 | 2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Source authenticity | invented or unverifiable sources | all sources exist, some metadata-only | all cited sources opened, passages stored |
| Relevance | material off-topic | mostly on question | each source maps to a sub-question |
| Coverage | mandatory source families missing | most families covered, gaps listed | all families attempted, gaps explained |
| Independence of corroboration | single interested source for key claims | key claims have 2 sources incl. one independent | key claims corroborated by T1/T3 |
| Temporal accuracy | periods mixed/wrong | minor ambiguity | period/currency/basis explicit |
| Contradiction handling | conflicts ignored | conflicts noted | conflicts recorded in conflicts.jsonl with resolution or `unresolved` |
| Traceability | claims lack IDs | most claims cite IDs | every material sentence cites CLM, each CLM cites SRC with locator |
| Significance | lists announcements | explains mechanism for some | explains problem->investment->capability->outcome->moat with evidence |

Hypothesis statuses: SUPPORTED / PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED / CONTRADICTED / INCONCLUSIVE / NEEDS_MORE_RESEARCH.
No numeric confidence percentages. Use the ordinal scores and the written rationale.

## Golden-question protocol
Answer only from the encyclopedia (registries + reports). For each answer list claim IDs. An auditor checks each cited claim's statement and source. Record: answered_fully / answered_partially / not_answerable / confabulation_detected. Negative tests (questions the corpus should not answer) must return not_answerable.

reports.title: Source quality rules
reports.markdown:
# Source quality rules

## Hierarchy
| Tier | What | Treat as |
|---|---|---|
| T1_primary_official | SEC/EDGAR filings (10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, 20-F, proxy), FDA/EMA/PMDA records, ClinicalTrials.gov, peer-reviewed journals, patents, court records, government lobbying disclosures | Fact for what the document states |
| T2_company_technical | Company technical blogs, R&D-day decks, earnings transcripts, published operating results, executive interviews (verbatim) | Fact that the company said it; outcome claims need T1/T3 corroboration |
| T3_independent_reputable | Reuters, FT, WSJ, Bloomberg, STAT, Endpoints, Fierce, Nature/Science news, NBER/university research, recognised consultancies | Reportage; check for reliance on the same press release |
| T4_expert_commentary | Analyst notes, expert blogs, podcasts | Interpretation, labelled |
| T5_speculative | Forums, unverified social media, rumour | Never fact; may motivate a search |

## Rules
1. Inspect before citing. Store a verbatim passage (<= 600 chars) and locator.
2. One original = one source. Syndicated repeats of a press release do not add independence.
3. Interested-party claims are flagged. "Company says X improved Y%" is a FACT about the statement, INTERPRETATION about the outcome unless independently corroborated.
4. Numbers carry period, currency, accounting basis (GAAP/non-GAAP/IFRS; continuing vs total operations). J&J pre/post-Kenvue (Aug 2023) and AbbVie post-Allergan (May 2020) are not comparable without adjustment.
5. Dates: distinguish event date, publication date, access date.
6. Access: `retrieved` (opened), `api_json` (machine-read), `metadata_only` (known to exist, not opened), `paywalled`, `blocked` (403/robot), `unavailable` (404/down). Never bypass paywalls/logins; respect robots and rate limits (>= 1 s/host).
7. Preserve conflicts in `conflicts.jsonl` with both source IDs and a resolution note (or `unresolved`).
8. Lawful storage: full copies only for public records (SEC, FDA, CT.gov, government). Otherwise metadata + short excerpt + own notes.
9. Causality: two events in sequence are not cause and effect. Mark `causal: asserted_by_company | corroborated | unknown`.
10. Failure search is mandatory: for every company and domain, run at least one query for discontinued/failed/delayed/recall/lawsuit/criticism.

# A12 — Scientific, Pipeline & Regulatory Intelligence (horizontal, wave 1)

Shard: `A12_pipeline` (SRC/CLM-012000..012999). Output dir: `/Users/palrahma/Desktop/MEDICINE/New_mediciine/industry_transformation/pipeline_regulatory/`. Companies: Lilly, J&J, AbbVie, Takeda.

## Research question
What did each company actually get approved, what failed or was delayed, and how good is the late-stage pipeline (quality, concentration, modality mix, scientific platforms) 2021-11→2026-11 — measured from regulator records, trial registries and peer-reviewed primary publications rather than company pipeline slides?

## Inputs
- Existing CT.gov inventories (do not redo): `/Users/palrahma/Desktop/MEDICINE/New_mediciine/companies/<co>/pipeline/ctgov_inventory.md` and `New_mediciine/financial_models/ctgov_<co>.jsonl` (lead-sponsor Phase 2/3 registrations by start year). Cite the A4 shard claim for the dataset.
- 10-K/20-F text on disk (`extracted_text/sec/`) sections "Research and Development" / "Pipeline" / "Regulatory" for each year — company-stated late-stage lists and discontinuations.

## Mandatory sub-questions
1. **FDA novel approvals 2022–2026 per company** from `https://www.fda.gov/drugs/novel-drug-approvals-fda/novel-drug-approvals-2022` (…2023, 2024, 2025, 2026): product, active ingredient, approval date, indication, sponsor; plus BLA/CBER approvals (Carvykti 2022-02, Tecvayli, Talvey, Kisunla, Imaavy…) from FDA biologics pages. One FACT claim per approval (≈25–35 claims). Verify sponsor attribution (e.g., Imbruvica J&J/AbbVie; Epkinly AbbVie/Genmab).
2. **Major supplemental approvals that drove revenue** (Mounjaro→Zepbound obesity 2023-11; Zepbound OSA 2024-12; Skyrizi UC 2024-06 / Crohn's 2022-06; Rinvoq UC/Crohn's/GCA; Tremfya UC 2024-09 / Crohn's 2025-03; Darzalex Faspro expansions; Carvykti 2L 2024-04; Rybrevant+Lazcluze 1L 2024-08; Entyvio SC 2023-09/2024-04; Vyvanse pediatric?) — ≈15 claims.
3. **CRLs, failures, withdrawals, delays** (≥15 claims): Lilly (lebrikizumab CRL 2023-10 manufacturing; mirikizumab CRL 2023-04; donanemab adcomm/delay 2024; sintilimab CRL 2022; Olumiant alopecia OK; retatrutide? ; Verzenio? ; tirzepatide shortages), J&J (RSV vaccine discontinued 2023-03; bermekimab 2022; aticaprant Phase 3 stop 2025-03; nipocalimab in some indications; Varipulse pause 2025-01; talc not pipeline), AbbVie (ABBV-951 CRL 2023-03; emraclidine EMPOWER-1/2 failures 2024-11; Rinvoq boxed warning 2021-12; navitoclax; Vraylar MDD?; teliso-V accelerated → confirm), Takeda (TAK-994 2021-10; soticlestat Phase 3 miss 2024-06; Exkivity withdrawal 2023-10; Alofisel withdrawal 2024; TAK-279?; mobocertinib; Eohilia OK 2024-02; fruquintinib OK 2023-11; Qdenga U.S. BLA withdrawal 2023-07).
4. **Late-stage pipeline quality snapshot at cutoff** per company: top ~8 Phase 3 assets with NCT IDs, primary completion dates, modality, mechanism novelty (first-in-class vs best-in-class), and peer-reviewed primary readouts where published (NEJM/Lancet DOIs — abstract-level inspection via PubMed is fine). Flag concentration (e.g., Lilly incretins) and modality breadth (ADC, bispecific, cell therapy, RNA, gene editing, radioligand, oral peptides).
5. **Scientific platform capabilities** (≥10 claims): Lilly (oral GLP-1 chemistry, radioligand via POINT, gene editing via Verve, siRNA lepodisiran), J&J (bispecific T-cell engagers, CAR-T with Legend, ADC via Ambrx, oral peptide icotrokinra via Protagonist), AbbVie (ADC platform ImmunoGen/Temab-A, in-vivo CAR-T Capstan, neuroscience small molecules), Takeda (TYK2 oral, orexin agonists, plasma-derived, siRNA via Arrowhead fazirsiran, cell therapy exit?). Evidence: approvals, Phase 3 starts, peer-reviewed data.
6. **Regulatory relationships**: breakthrough / priority / fast-track counts if disclosed; National Priority Vouchers (Lilly orforglipron 2025); FDA accelerated-approval withdrawals (Exkivity, etc.).

## Evidence standard
T1 = FDA/EMA/CT.gov/PubMed/peer-reviewed. Company press releases establish the announcement; regulator record establishes the approval. Each approval claim: product, date, indication, FDA page locator. Each failure claim: date, what failed (endpoint/CRL reason if disclosed), source.

## Deliverables
`fda_approvals_2022_2026.md` (table per company with claim IDs), `setbacks_crls_withdrawals.md`, `late_stage_pipeline_snapshot.md` (per company table with NCTs), `scientific_platforms.md`, `pipeline_quality_assessment.md` (INTERPRETATION: depth, concentration, modality mix, revenue-replacement adequacy — label clearly), `map.md`, `evidence_gaps.md`. Shard target ≥35 sources (≥25 retrieved), ≥90 claims.

# WAVE 1 — common brief for every specialist research agent (read fully before any research)

Project root: `/Users/palrahma/Desktop/MEDICINE` (use absolute paths; your shell cwd is NOT the project).
Python for the evidence CLI: `PY=/Users/palrahma/.local/share/mise/installs/python/3.12/bin/python3`
Research cutoff: 2026-11-21. Primary window: 2021-11-21 → 2026-11-21 (lookback allowed to explain an advantage).

## 0. Start-up (do these first, in this order; ~5 minutes)
1. `cat /Users/palrahma/Desktop/MEDICINE/research_methodology/agent_protocols.md` — record formats, enums, rules.
2. `cat` your company/domain `map.md` if it exists; `ls -R` your allowed output directory.
3. `$PY /Users/palrahma/Desktop/MEDICINE/tools/evidence.py ids <your_shard>` — note your next free IDs.
4. `grep -c . /Users/palrahma/Desktop/MEDICINE/New_mediciine/evidence_library/claims_registry.jsonl` and grep it for your company/topic — REUSE existing claim IDs (CLM-000001..000286) by citing them; do not re-register facts already there (revenue/R&D/net income FY2021-25 are already in CLM-000001..000238 and in `companies/<co>/financials/xbrl_annual_facts.md`).
5. Only then begin retrieval.

## 1. Evidence rules (non-negotiable)
- The filesystem is the system of record. Save after every ~5 sources. Never end with unsaved findings.
- Every source you cite must have been OPENED by you (web_fetch, the CLI `fetch`, or a file on disk). `access_status: retrieved` REQUIRES a verbatim `inspected_passage` (≤600 chars) you actually saw. If you only saw a search snippet, register it as `metadata_only` and say so in `notes`.
- No invented URLs, page numbers, quotes, numbers, dates. If a locator is unknown write `"locator": "unknown — full text not paginated"`.
- Distinguish kinds: FACT (directly substantiated) / INTERPRETATION / HYPOTHESIS / SCENARIO / RECOMMENDATION. A company statement of intent is a FACT *that the statement was made*, not a FACT about outcome. Put your reading in `implication`, never in `statement`.
- Press release = announcement happened ≠ value realized. Multiple outlets repeating one release are NOT independent corroboration; a regulator record, filing, registry, peer-reviewed paper or an independent investigation is.
- Every AI / data / robotics / automation claim carries `maturity` ∈ concept|prototype|pilot|operational|scaled|demonstrated_outcome|unknown, with the evidence that justifies the level.
- For every major finding, search explicitly for contrary evidence (`failure`, `delay`, `discontinued`, `complete response letter`, `lawsuit`, `criticism`, `impairment`, `write-down`) and record it in `contrary_evidence` / `contrary_source_ids`.
- Reporting periods explicit (J&J fiscal years end late Dec/early Jan; Takeda FY ends 31 March — "FY2025" = Apr 2025–Mar 2026). Never present a partial 2026 period as a full year.
- Source hierarchy T1 (filings, regulators, registries, peer-reviewed) > T2 (company technical/IR) > T3 (Reuters, FT, STAT, Endpoints, Fierce, BioPharma Dive, Nature/Science news) > T4 (expert commentary) > T5 (speculative; never as fact).
- Neutral on policy: document lobbying/advocacy/litigation; never infer impropriety or causal influence without credible substantiation.

## 2. Retrieval mechanics
- Prefer the `web_fetch` tool for reading pages (it passes bot challenges that block curl: investor.lilly.com, investor.jnj.com, fiercepharma.com, lda.senate.gov, opensecrets.org). Use `web_search` for discovery, then OPEN the page.
- Use the CLI for bulk/primary documents when you also want a stored hash:
  `$PY tools/evidence.py fetch "<url>" --grep "<term>" --store-raw --context 400 --max-hits 8` (run from `/Users/palrahma/Desktop/MEDICINE`). It respects a 1 s sleep; keep ≥1 s between requests to one host; max 2 attempts per URL then record `blocked|unavailable|paywalled`.
- SEC EDGAR for anything a company files: 8-K exhibits (earnings releases, deal announcements) via `https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=<CIK>&type=8-K&dateb=&owner=include&count=40` (CIKs: LLY 0000059478, JNJ 0000200406, ABBV 0001551152, Takeda 0001395064). Full-text search: `https://efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index?q="<phrase>"&forms=8-K` (JSON).
- 20 annual reports (FY2021–FY2025) are ALREADY on disk as plain text: `/Users/palrahma/Desktop/MEDICINE/New_mediciine/evidence_library/extracted_text/sec/*.txt` (500 KB–1 MB each). Use `grep -n -i "<term>" <file> | head` then `sed -n '<start>,<end>p'` to read the passage; cite `line N` as the locator. Their source records already exist in the canonical registry (`grep '"document_identifier"' …` or grep the accession number in `source_registry.jsonl`) — cite that `SRC-0000xx` rather than re-registering.
- ClinicalTrials.gov v2 API: `https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/<NCT>` (JSON). FDA: `https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/scripts/cder/daf/` and the yearly "Novel Drug Approvals" pages on fda.gov. PubMed: `https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/?term=...`. EMA: `https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/medicines/...`.
- Do not bypass paywalls or logins. Paywalled: register `access_status: paywalled`, metadata only.

## 3. Writing your shard (your only registry write path)
Append JSON lines to `/Users/palrahma/Desktop/MEDICINE/New_mediciine/evidence_library/shards/<shard>/sources.jsonl` and `claims.jsonl` using your allocated ID range (sequential). Easiest: write small Python/JSON then
`$PY tools/evidence.py add-source --shard <shard> --json /path/to/src.json` and `add-claim` (they validate). Or append directly, then validate:
`$PY tools/evidence.py validate --shard <shard> --path New_mediciine/evidence_library/shards/<shard>/sources.jsonl` (0 errors required before you finish; same for claims.jsonl).
Field formats are in agent_protocols.md §2 (singular `domain`, lowercase `company` enums `eli_lilly|johnson_johnson|abbvie|takeda|industry|other`, `supporting_source_ids` as a list of IDs, `locator` string).
You MAY cite canonical IDs `SRC-0000xx` / `CLM-0000xx` in `supporting_source_ids` / report text; the validator accepts registry IDs.

## 4. Reports (Markdown, in your allowed directory only)
- Every material sentence ends with `[CLM-xxxxxx]` (one or more IDs). Sentences without an ID must be labelled *(INTERPRETATION)*, *(HYPOTHESIS)* or *(gap)*.
- Use relative links between your own files. Keep each file focused (one sub-domain per file). Headings: what is established / what is contested / what is unknown.
- Mandatory files: `map.md` (every file you wrote, one line each with link + one-line purpose), `evidence_gaps.md` (what you looked for and could not find/open: blocked URLs, unresolved questions, suggested next queries), plus the files named in your task.

## 5. Do NOT

- Run `git commit`/`git add` (the Director commits). Do not delete or rewrite files you did not create, except where your task explicitly says you may replace `master_report.md`.
- Spend more than ~15 minutes on any single source. Loop on a blocked host. Pad with promotional content when primary questions remain open.

## 6. Budget and stop condition
Target 75–100 minutes of work. Stop when (a) your mandatory questions each have SUPPORTED / CONTRADICTED / INCONCLUSIVE status with evidence, or (b) you reach ~90% of budget — then write `evidence_gaps.md`, validate both shard files, and return the completion report in exactly this shape:

# A7 — Commercial, Market-Access & Patient-Experience Intelligence (horizontal, wave 2)

Shard: `A7_commercial` (SRC/CLM-007000..007999). Output dir: `/Users/palrahma/Desktop/MEDICINE/New_mediciine/industry_transformation/commercial_patient/`. Companies: Lilly, J&J, AbbVie, Takeda (baseline depth).

## Research question
How does each company actually win and defend market share — launch execution, payer/PBM contracting, patient support and access programs, direct-to-patient channels, pricing posture, distribution, real-world evidence, HCP engagement — and which new care-delivery models (home administration, connected devices, remote monitoring, decentralized trials, digital therapeutics) have they deployed with evidence of adoption? Which of these transfer to Takeda's therapeutic mix (GI, rare, PDT, neuroscience, oncology, vaccines)?

Already in registry (cite, do not redo): grep `claims_registry.jsonl` for `LillyDirect`, `Cordavis`, `CVS`, `withMe`, `gross-to-net`, `Allē`, `patient support`, `Entyvio SC`, `Medicare` — company agents captured some (e.g., CLM-001042 LillyDirect launch; CLM-003007/8/10 Humira/CVS/Cordavis; CLM-001036/37 Nov-2025 pricing agreement).

## Mandatory sub-questions
1. **Direct-to-patient and cash channels**: LillyDirect (launch, cash-pay Zepbound vial prices and their cuts 2024-08, 2025-02, 2025-11; TrumpRx), Novo comparison only as context; J&J and AbbVie DTC/cash programs if any; Takeda none? Evidence of volume (any disclosed share of self-pay).
2. **Payer/PBM dynamics and gross-to-net**: disclosed gross-to-net pressure (10-K language), rebate levels where disclosed, formulary events (CVS Caremark Humira removal 2024-04; Stelara biosimilar formulary moves 2025; Zepbound/Wegovy exclusive formulary deals 2025 e.g., CVS Caremark choosing Wegovy 2025-07; employer coverage trends), Medicare Part D redesign impact statements, 340B.
3. **Launch execution**: launch curves disclosed (Mounjaro/Zepbound quarterly, Skyrizi/Rinvoq, Tremfya, Carvykti capacity-constrained launch, Spravato REMS centres, Vyalev, Kisunla slow uptake and reasons, Qdenga), launch-readiness mechanisms (field force size, omnichannel statements, specialty pharmacy, hub services).
4. **Patient support and adherence**: Lilly (Lilly Cares, savings cards, insulin USD 35 cap), J&J (withMe, Janssen CarePath), AbbVie (myAbbVie Assist, Complete programs, Allē loyalty with member counts), Takeda (Help at Hand, Takeda Patient Support); evidence of outcomes (adherence, time-to-therapy) if any — mostly company-reported; flag.
5. **Care-delivery innovation**: home/self-administration shifts (Entyvio SC pen, Tremfya SC, Darzalex Faspro, Vyalev pump, Zepbound vials), connected devices/digital (J&J Impella Connect?, Abiomed; Lilly connected pens Tempo; AbbVie Vraylar? no), remote monitoring in trials, decentralized/hybrid trials statements (Lilly, J&J), digital therapeutics (any evidence; most pharma retreated — e.g., Pear bankruptcy 2023 as industry calibration), site-of-care economics (infusion vs SC).
6. **Real-world evidence & HCP engagement**: RWE programs with published outputs (e.g., tirzepatide RWE, Entyvio RWE), omnichannel/HCP engagement statements with any metrics, medical affairs digital.
7. **Pricing posture & access controversies**: list prices vs net, price cuts (insulin), international reference pricing/MFN exposure, access litigation (compounding), reputation events.
8. **Transfer to Takeda** (INTERPRETATION, labelled): which mechanisms fit Takeda's portfolio and which do not (e.g., cash-pay DTC fits obesity, not rare disease), with the evidence IDs behind the judgment.

## Web targets
10-K/20-F text on disk (grep `gross-to-net|rebates|formulary|patient support|direct-to-consumer|LillyDirect|specialty pharmacy|hub`), company newsrooms, earnings-release 8-K exhibits (EDGAR), FDA label/REMS pages, KFF/Health Affairs/STAT/Reuters/Endpoints/Fierce (web_fetch) for formulary events and uptake, PubMed for RWE publications. Respect blocked hosts (2 tries → record and move on).

## Deliverables
`commercial_models_comparison.md` (table per mechanism × company with evidence IDs), `patient_programs_and_care_delivery.md`, `launch_execution_evidence.md`, `pricing_access_and_payer_dynamics.md`, `transfer_to_takeda.md` (INTERPRETATION, each item tied to a Takeda baseline class from `New_mediciine/companies/takeda_public_baseline/capability_baseline/capability_baseline.md`), `map.md`, `evidence_gaps.md`. Shard target ≥25 sources (≥15 retrieved), ≥50 claims. HARD CAP: 100 tool calls — batch fetches; write shard + reports by call ~85.

WAVE1_COMMON.md §1; the Takeda baseline (`New_mediciine/companies/takeda_public_baseline/master_report.md`, `capability_baseline/capability_baseline.md`, `internal_validation_backlog/backlog.md`); A6 reports (`industry_transformation/ai_data_robotics/*.md`, esp. `autonomous_lab_reality_check.md`, `capability_mechanism_cards.md`); A9 (`partnerships_ecosystem/*.md`); A12 (`pipeline_regulatory/scientific_platforms.md`); A7 (`commercial_patient/*.md`, if present); the three competitor dossiers' `competitive_advantage/moats.md`. Also `moat_mechanisms_taxonomy.md`: data, learning, IP, infrastructure, workflow integration, network effects, regulatory experience, ecosystem — with the strongest competitor example and claim IDs for each.

## Part 3 — Partnership models (`strategy/ecosystem_partnerships/partnership_models.md`)
Academic, biotech, AI, robotics, clinical organisations, health systems, diagnostics, data infrastructure, manufacturing tech, venture funds: when to build / partner / license / acquire / invest, with the competitor precedent and outcome evidence (A9), and Takeda's observed pattern (baseline).

Every file: headings "What the evidence shows", "Where proprietary advantage exists", "Takeda fit and baseline class", "Options (not endorsements)", "Success criteria", "Risks", "Evidence and gaps". reports.title: A13 (wave 3b) — Turn the application into the final "go-to" content hub: Takeda white/red design, full report reader, pillar architecture, grounded Q&A, single-file export
reports.markdown:
# A13 (wave 3b) — Turn the application into the final "go-to" content hub: Takeda white/red design, full report reader, pillar architecture, grounded Q&A, single-file export

You exclusively own: `executive_application/**`, `scripts/build_app_data.py`, `scripts/build_single_file.py` (new), `data/**`, `launch.sh`, `deliverables/OPEN_APPLICATION.md`. Read-only elsewhere. No registry writes. No git. `npm install` from the public registry is allowed (`marked` is available: 18.x; `minisearch` optional).

## User requirements (verbatim intent)
"Final HTML webpage with very professional and visually engaging UI and very detailed content; divide all research content very well and in detail. Clean Q&A without heavy LLMs — free / open-source LLM APIs — but Q&A is one feature; the aim is detailed, clear, best content, best visuals and analytics, amazing UI to read. Professional white background and red theme aligned to Takeda. Very clear differentiation between Commercial, R&D, future plan, etc. The web page must be the final go-to content hub."

## 1. Design system (replace the current dark/neutral theme)
- Background `#FFFFFF`; surfaces `#FAFAFA`; borders `#E5E7EB`; ink `#111827`; muted `#6B7280`.
- Takeda red primary `#E60012`; hover `#C5000F`; deep `#8F000B`; tints `#FFF1F2`, `#FDE1E4`. Red is used for structure (section rules, active nav, primary buttons, key figures), never as a background for long text.
- Company palette for charts (distinct, print-safe): Lilly `#0F766E`, J&J `#1D4ED8`, AbbVie `#7C3AED`, Takeda `#E60012`; neutral grey for industry.
- Type: headlines in a serif stack (`"Source Serif 4", "Iowan Old Style", Georgia, serif`), body in `Inter, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", sans-serif`, tabular numerals for figures; 16px base, generous line-height, max text width ~72ch, page width 1280px.
- Badges: kind (FACT solid red outline; INTERPRETATION grey; HYPOTHESIS amber; SCENARIO blue; RECOMMENDATION deep red) and maturity ladder (concept → demonstrated_outcome) rendered consistently everywhere. Claim IDs are red mono chips that open the Evidence drawer.
- Motion: subtle (150–200 ms), no decorative animation. Print stylesheet (A4, hide nav, show URLs of sources).
- Keyboard: skip-link, focus rings, drawer trap, Esc closes.

## 2. Information architecture — pillar navigation (top bar + per-pillar left sub-nav)
1. **Overview** (View 1): the story spine — What is changing → Who is winning → Why → What is defensible → What Takeda already has → Where the opportunity is → What to build → What to invest → How to execute → How to measure. Each block binds to claim IDs (from `src/narrative.ts`), KPI tiles from registry values, "proven vs emerging" split, reading guide to the pillars, and the research-integrity note (counts, audit result, cutoff).
2. **Companies**: Lilly · J&J · AbbVie — each a company page with tabs: Dossier (rendered `master_report.md`), Timeline (`timelines.json` strip + table), Business & Financials (XBRL small multiples + `business_model.md`), Pipeline, Commercial, Successes & Failures, Moats, Leadership, Evidence gaps. Plus **Compare** (View 2) and **Differentiators** (View 3).
3. **Commercial & Market Access**: A7 reports (`industry_transformation/commercial_patient/*.md`) + `cross_company_analysis/commercial_capabilities_comparison.md` when present + LOE/product dependence charts.
4. **R&D, Science & Pipeline**: A12 reports (approvals table, setbacks, late-stage snapshot, scientific platforms, quality assessment) + View 4 timelines + `rd_investment_and_productivity.md` when present.
5. **Data, AI & Robotics**: A6 reports (landscape, 14 mechanism cards, maturity matrix, autonomous-lab reality check) + View 5 Observatory.
6. **Partnerships & Ecosystem**: A9 reports + View 6 graph + `partner_ecosystem_comparison.md` when present.
7. **Policy & Regulation**: A8 reports (IRA exposure table, pledges, 340B, litigation, lobbying).
8. **Takeda Baseline**: View 8 + rendered Takeda dossier, capability baseline, LOE exposure, IVB backlog.
9. **Future Plan** (clearly separated visual language — a thin red "FORWARD-LOOKING / SCENARIO" banner on every page): Future of Pharma (7 domain files under `strategy/future_of_pharma/`), Platform analogies (`strategy/platform_moats/`), Strategic Bets (View 9), Capital Allocation (View 10), Roadmap 2027–2040 (View 11), Scenarios, Council & Red Team, Counterarguments & Uncertainty (View 12). Files may be absent while waves 3–5 run: render the explicit "not yet produced" notice.
10. **Evidence & Method**: Encyclopedia (View 7), Sources browser, Conflicts & audit (conflicts.json + `quality/citation_audits/*.md` + `quality/evaluation_results/*.md` rendered), Coverage (`coverage_summary.md`), Research operating system + research graph (interactive), Research runs & experiments log, Project state / Continue.
11. **Ask** — grounded Q&A (section 4).
Global: search box in the top bar (jumps to Encyclopedia), breadcrumb, "Evidence" drawer everywhere, footer with cutoff date, counts, and "FACT ≠ INTERPRETATION" legend.

## 3. Report reader (the content backbone)
Pipeline: bundle every Markdown file under `New_mediciine/**`, `strategy/**`, `research_methodology/**` (incl. briefs), `quality/**`, root `map.md`/`PROJECT_STATE.md`/`CONTINUE.md`/`COORDINATION.md` into `reports.json` entries `{path, title (first H1), pillar, company, section, markdown, word_count, claim_ids[], updated}`. Render with `marked` (install) in a `Reader` component: tables become responsive styled tables; `[CLM-xxxxxx]`/`SRC-xxxxxx` tokens become evidence chips; relative `.md` links route inside the app (`#/read/<path>`); a right-hand "On this page" outline; "Open source file path" shown. Every pillar page lists its reports with word counts and last-updated.

## 4. Ask — grounded Q&A without heavy LLMs
- Pipeline builds `qa_index.json`: passages = every claim (statement + implication + entities + company + domains + ids), every report section (heading + ~300-word chunk, path, pillar) and every source title. In the browser implement BM25 (own ~80-line TS or `minisearch`) with field boosts; stemming light (lowercase, strip plurals).
- Retrieval-only answer (default, always works, zero cost): top 8–12 passages → "Grounded answer" composed as cited bullets (claim statement + kind badge + company + source link), grouped by company/domain, with a "What the evidence base does not say" line when fewer than 3 strong matches, and the golden questions as suggestions. The negative test must hold: a question with no evidence returns "no evidence in the corpus", never an invented answer.
- Optional "Synthesize with an open-source LLM" toggle: provider A = **local Ollama** (`http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/chat`, model default `qwen2.5:3b`, OpenAI-compatible path also fine), provider B = any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (base URL + key entered by the user, stored only in localStorage; e.g. Groq/HF free tiers). Status pill checks `/api/tags`. Strict grounding prompt: "Answer only from the numbered evidence passages; cite [CLM-…]; if the passages do not answer, say so"; temperature 0; stream tokens; show the retrieved passages beneath the answer; label "LLM synthesis — verify against the cited claims". Fallback to retrieval-only when unreachable, with one-line setup instructions (`brew install ollama && ollama pull qwen2.5:3b && ollama serve`). The Director is installing Ollama in parallel; do not install anything yourself. Never send anything except the question and retrieved passages.

## 5. Single-file export
`scripts/build_single_file.py`: after `vite build`, inline CSS/JS and every `public/data/*.json` into one `deliverables/MEDICINE_2040_Hub.html` (data as `<script type="application/json" id="medicine-data">` or `window.__MEDICINE_DATA__`); `src/data.ts` must prefer the inlined data when present and fall back to `fetch`. Hash routing must work from `file://`. Target < 15 MB; report the size. Keep the served build (`./launch.sh` → 127.0.0.1:4173) as the primary path.

## 6. Quality bar
`npm run build && npm test` green; extend tests: reports.json covers ≥ 95 Markdown files, every claim chip id exists, every pillar route renders, Q&A negative test (query "TuneLab revenue 2025" yields the no-evidence state), single-file HTML exists and contains the data blob. Responsive check at 360px and 1280px by dumping the rendered markup (no visual tools available). ## Inputs (read in order)
`strategy/DATA_CONTRACT.md` (your JSON must validate against it; every `claim_ids` entry must exist in `New_mediciine/evidence_library/claims_registry.jsonl` — check with grep before you cite); `New_mediciine/cross_company_analysis/master_comparison.md` + `lessons_for_takeda.md` + `strategy/data/takeda_lessons.json`; `strategy/future_of_pharma/*.md` (7 domains; options labelled EVIDENCE_BACKED/HYPOTHESIS); `strategy/platform_moats/*.md`; `strategy/ecosystem_partnerships/*.md`; Takeda baseline (`master_report.md`, `capability_baseline.md`, `loe_risk/loe_exposure.md`, `internal_validation_backlog/backlog.md`); `industry_transformation/ai_data_robotics/autonomous_lab_reality_check.md`; `quality/evaluation_results/wave1_scorecard.md` (what evidence is accepted).

## Central question
What should Takeda start building and investing in now that could compound into durable advantage by 2030, 2035 and 2040 — maximising resilience to LOE and disruption (not eliminating LOE), reducing dependence on single blockbusters?

## Deliverables
1. `investment_theses/strategic_bets.md` — ≥12 candidate platforms (the master prompt's 12 plus any you derive from the evidence; do NOT auto-endorse). For EVERY candidate the full template A–M: thesis; future market change; problem; evidence (claim IDs from competitor research + science); moat mechanism (which of data/learning/IP/infrastructure/workflow/network/regulatory/ecosystem, and why it compounds); practical architecture (build/buy/license/partner); investment (initial/follow-on/scaled, scenario-based with stated assumptions — Takeda's budget is NOT known: use ranges anchored to disclosed comparables, e.g., Lilly–NVIDIA up to USD 1bn/5y [CLM-000281], Nimbus USD 4bn [see A5/A9 claims], Takeda R&D JPY 675.9bn FY2025 [A5 claims], and label every number ASSUMPTION with an `ASM-` id); time to value; measurable outcomes; risks (scientific, regulatory, execution, data, competition, capital, adoption); strategic options (expand/redirect/partner/divest/stop); decision BUILD/PARTNER/INVEST/ACQUIRE/EXPERIMENT/DEFER/REJECT; evidence & confidence (known / assumed / needs Takeda internal validation → IVB ids). Sequencing dependencies explicit (e.g., is data infrastructure a prerequisite to automated science, or can a bounded lab-automation initiative seed its own data foundation? argue from evidence).
2. `financial_cases/capital_allocation.md` — horizons H1 2027–29 / H2 2030–34 / H3 2035–40; three portfolios (capital-constrained, balanced, ambitious) with allocation % by horizon and theme (core capability / adjacent / long-horizon bets / external innovation) as proposals with assumptions; evaluation per bet (risk-adjusted NPV only where meaningful — otherwise say why not; expected value & downside; real-option value qualitatively; PTS; commercial probability; time to payoff; capability reuse; differentiation; capital efficiency; regulatory feasibility; execution complexity; synergy with Takeda assets; follow-on options). No false precision: ranges, not point estimates; every input traceable to a claim or an `ASM-`.
3. `financial_cases/stage_gates.md` — per material bet: discovery → feasibility → prototype/initial evidence → controlled pilot → scale decision → ongoing value review; at each gate capital at risk, evidence required, commercial milestone, stop criteria, expansion criteria, accountable owner role, decision authority.
4. `scenarios/scenarios_2027_2040.md` — ≥4 futures (AI materially accelerates R&D; AI incremental; pricing/regulatory/biosimilar pressure intensifies; new modalities/care models/tech-native competitors reshape value) + combined downside; for each bet: robust / fragile / option-value / neutral with rationale; which investments need early start because capability building takes years; which can be postponed.
5. `pipeline_resilience/loe_resilience_strategy.md` — how the bets reduce dependence on Entyvio-class single products; tie to A5 LOE evidence and competitor replacement evidence (AbbVie Skyrizi/Rinvoq; Lilly incretin concentration as a counter-example of concentration risk).
6. `strategic_roadmap/roadmap_2027_2040.md` — foundations, validation milestones, pilot decisions, scale-up points, dependency chains, decision gates, partnerships, measurable outcomes by half-year where meaningful.
7. `takeda_future_2030_2040/executive_strategy_narrative.md` — the storyline: what is changing → who is winning → why → what is defensible → what Takeda already has → where the opportunity is → what to build → what to invest → how to execute → how to measure. CEO/CFO/R&D/CTO/commercial readers each get one explicit paragraph.
8. JSON per `strategy/DATA_CONTRACT.md`: `strategy_bets.json`, `assumptions.json`, `portfolios.json`, `stage_gates.json`, `roadmap.json`, `scenarios.json`. Validate: `python3 -c "import json;json.load(open(...))"` and grep every claim id against the registry (write a tiny checker script in `strategy/data/_check_ids.py`; it must report 0 unknown IDs).
9. `map.md`, `assumptions_register.md` (all ASM ids with rationale, sensitivity, IVB link), `evidence_gaps.md`.

## Rules
FACT / INTERPRETATION / HYPOTHESIS / SCENARIO / RECOMMENDATION never collapsed. Do not recommend building what the baseline shows Takeda already has without assessing maturity. Do not invent Takeda's budget, headcount or internal data. Separate disclosed numbers from estimates. Budget 400 tool calls; save progressively (JSON early, refine later). # RUN-0004 — Wave 1 multi-agent deep research (2026-11-21, session 2)

**Question.** Can parallel specialist agents (A1 Lilly, A2 J&J, A3 AbbVie, A5 Takeda, A6 AI/robotics, A8 policy, A9 partnerships, A12 pipeline/regulatory) produce evidence-grade, shard-isolated research on the eight briefs in `briefs/WAVE1_*.md` that survives the fixed rubric?
**Hypothesis.** Company agents on on-disk 10-K/20-F text + primary web sources will reach ≥30 sources / ≥70 claims each with 0 validation errors; horizontals will reach ≥25 / ≥50.
**Search strategy.** On-disk filings first (grep + line locators), then EDGAR exhibits, FDA/CT.gov/PubMed APIs, company newsrooms, T3 corroboration; explicit failure/contradiction queries.

## Outcome
| Agent | Sources (retrieved) | Claims | Validation | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 Lilly | 36 (36) | 70 | 0 errors | cut at tool cap after steer; several `~` locators need audit |
| A2 J&J | 38 (32+5 api) | 76 | 0 errors | first run killed at 100-call cap AFTER writing all files; dashboard retry added 6/10 |
| A3 AbbVie | 39 (20+7 api) | 91 | 0 errors | corrected brief errors (Cerevel impairment USD 4.5bn Q4-2024; USD 100bn pledge) |
| A5 Takeda | 40 (31) | 83 | 0 errors | capability baseline + IVB backlog produced |
| A6 AI/robotics | 36 (28) | 60 | 0 errors | 14 mechanism cards; every claim maturity-tagged |
| A8 policy | 36 (22) | 55 | 0 errors | runs 1 and 2 died at the cap with nothing saved; run 2 completed after Director steer |
| A9 partnerships | 23 (11) | 102 | 0 errors | audited 10-K deal notes; venture-arm scale not found |
| A12 pipeline | 117 (38+79 api) | 153 | 0 errors | 21 CDER novel approvals as FACT claims; 19 setbacks |
| **Merged** | **431** | **1,165** | canonical PASS | via `scripts/merge_shards.py`; 1 status downgrade logged (CLM-006019) |

## New evidence vs reused
Reused: 20 on-disk annual reports (SRC-000003..000028) cited by line; 286 session-1 claims. New: 396 sources, 879 claims.

## Contradictions found (kept, not deleted)
Morphic headline USD 3.2bn vs audited IPR&D charge 2.55bn; Lilly FY2021 IPR&D 874.9 vs 970.1 (restated comparative); Takeda restructuring cost 150/160/170bn JPY across sources; AbbVie Ventures founding 2009 vs ~2015; Strateos lab start 2017 vs ~2020; Lilly 2024 lobbying USD 7.89m vs 8.43m; Medicare obesity access "as early as 2026-04-01" vs 10-K "by 2026-07-01"; CT.gov status lag for VERONA and EXCLAIM-2.

## Evaluation (rubric, Director's provisional; A10 audit pending)
Source authenticity high (T1 share high; FDA/CT.gov/EDGAR records); coverage uneven (leadership interviews, lobbying totals, venture-arm scale, CBER products missing); independence of corroboration moderate (company releases dominate AI claims); temporal accuracy good (periods explicit); traceability good (locators; `~` approximations flagged).

## Decision
**ACCEPT with REVISE items** → wave 2: independent audit (A10), gap-fill (A14), commercial horizontal (A7), policy second pass declined (A8 coverage adequate; gaps recorded).

## Process findings (keep)
- Subagent default tool-call cap is 100, not 1000; two runs lost all work. Fix: `max_turns` raised to 400 and save-as-you-go in every brief.
- Agents reading on-disk filings produced the most reliable numeric claims; web-only agents produced more metadata_only records.
- Horizontal/company overlap (AI, deals) produced duplicate sources with different IDs → alias records; acceptable, but the auditor should check for conflicting statements about the same event.

reports.title: RUN-0005 — Waves 2–5: audit, gap-fill, synthesis, strategy, council, hub (2026-11-21, session 2)
reports.markdown:
# RUN-0005 — Waves 2–5: audit, gap-fill, synthesis, strategy, council, hub (2026-11-21, session 2)

**Questions.** (a) Does the wave-1 evidence survive independent re-inspection? (b) Can a fresh-context synthesis layer and a Takeda strategy be built only on accepted claims? (c) Does an independent council change the strategy?
**Hypotheses.** Audit will find locator drift and announcement-vs-regulator date errors but few numeric errors; the synthesis will need to refuse several cross-company rankings; the council will cut long-horizon spend.

## What ran
| Wave | Agents | Output |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | A10 audit · A7 commercial · A8 policy (3rd attempt) · A14 gap-fill · A13 app v2 | 99-claim re-inspection; +26/59, +36/55, +50/75 shard records; 12 views on real data |
| 3 | A11a comparison · A11b future-of-pharma + analogies · A15 dossier integrator · A13 hub (white/red, reader, Q&A, single file) | 13 comparison files, 21 lessons; 7 domains, 7 analogies, moat taxonomy; dossiers v1.1; hub v3 |
| 4 | A11c bets/capital · A10-bis audit round 2 | 17 bets, 3 portfolios, 67 gates, 5 scenarios, 50 milestones; 88-claim re-inspection + 46 FDA dates + 43 CT.gov statuses |
| 5 | A11e council/red team · A13 final · A11c-bis strategy v2 · A16 deliverables | 119 verdicts, 95 counterarguments; strategy v2 (18 bets); 6 deliverables |

## Results vs hypotheses
- (a) **Confirmed.** Numeric accuracy high (all reachable numbers matched in round 2); defects were labels (debt basis), dates taken from announcements instead of FDA records (3), mis-cited IDs (4), unsupported link (Strateos), maturity over-tagging (6 + 24 missing). All applied with audit trail; statements never edited.
- (b) **Confirmed.** `master_comparison.md` refuses five rankings; A11c built strategy only from registry claims + explicit ASM ids (0 unknown IDs).
- (c) **Confirmed and stronger than expected.** Council cut the balanced envelope 2,950 → 1,920 committed (+1,030 contingent), rejected the USD 5bn purchase as framed, moved plasma to EXPERIMENT, and re-rated 19/85 robustness cells. The Director accepted 10 changes and declined 2 (recorded).

## New vs reused evidence
+129 sources / +291 claims in waves 2–3 (total 524 / 1,401); reused: all wave-1 shards and the 20 filings on disk.

## Contradictions found (kept)
Juvmo 09-25 vs 09-28; OTTAVA De Novo 07-21 vs 07-22 and receipt 2025-12-18 vs announcement 2026-01-07; Imaavy 04-29 vs 04-30; AbbVie IPR&D 5,016 vs 4,808 (definitional); bermekimab 0.6 vs 0.8bn (estimate vs final); CUDA developers 7.5m (10-K) vs 11m (blog); Lilly lobbying 7.89 vs 8.43m (open); Medicare obesity start Apr vs Jul 2026 (open).

## Evaluation
Coverage up (commercial, policy, gap-fill); traceability high; independence still weak structurally (`independent_corroboration` empty); contradiction handling now recorded (110 conflict records). Decision: **ACCEPT**; next research directions in `quality/final_validation.md` §4.

## Process findings (keep)
- Fresh-context auditors found errors the authors could not see (announcement dates, mis-cited IDs). Keep one audit round per wave.
- Builder-script regeneration (A11c's `_a11c_*.py`) made the v2 revision cheap and consistent across Markdown and JSON.
- Agents must never derive durations/counts in prose without a claim ("11 months", "nine months", "29 entries" errors).

# Final system validation — MEDICINE 2040 (session 2 close, 2026-11-21 ~20:15 IST)

Director (A0) sign-off against the master prompt's gates (§17) and quality standard (§25). Every check below was executed in this session; commands are given so a future agent can re-run them. "PASS" means the automated check passed; judgement calls are labelled as such.

## 1. Automated checks (re-runnable)

| Check | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Registry schema, ID uniqueness, referential integrity, period discipline, T4/T5-only FACT rule | `python3 scripts/validate_registries.py` | **PASS** — 524 sources / 1,401 claims, 0 errors (warnings listed in `quality/citation_audits/registry_validation_2026-11-21.json`) |
| Shard-level validation (12 shards) | `~/.local/share/mise/installs/python/3.12/bin/python3 tools/evidence.py validate --shard <s> --path <file>` | 0 errors on every merged shard at merge time (`quality/citation_audits/shard_merge_2026-11-21.json`) |
| Every `[CLM-…]` cited in 192 Markdown files resolves | inline check (see RUN-0005) | **PASS** — 0 unknown references |
| Strategy JSON vs `strategy/DATA_CONTRACT.md`; every CLM/ASM/BET/RM/IVB id resolves | `python3 strategy/data/_check_ids.py` | **PASS** — 18 bets, 37 assumptions, 69 gates, 54 milestones, 5 scenarios; 0 unknown IDs |
| Council JSON (119 verdicts, 95 counterarguments) | `python3 strategy/critical_challenges/_check_council.py` | **PASS** (BET-18 explicitly listed as not independently reviewed) |
| Relative Markdown links | `python3 scripts/check_links.py` | **PASS** (report in `quality/coverage_reports/link_check_2026-11-21.json`) |
| Data pipeline (encyclopedia → 22 app datasets; fails on any unknown ID) | `python3 scripts/build_app_data.py` | **PASS** — 9/9 strategy files present |
| Application build + tests | `cd executive_application && npm run build && npm test` | **PASS** — 109 data-integrity + 145 route/Q&A tests, 0 failures |
| Single-file export | `python3 scripts/build_single_file.py` | **PASS** — `deliverables/MEDICINE_2040_Hub.html`, 8.5 MB, 22 datasets, verified loading from `file://` (screenshots in `quality/application_tests/screenshots/`) |
| Q&A negative tests | `tests/llm_probe.mjs` + route tests | **PASS** — "TuneLab revenue 2025" and "Takeda approved AI budget 2027" return the no-evidence state; retrieval-only and LLM paths both refuse to invent |
| Coverage ledger recomputed | `python3 scripts/update_coverage.py` | 85 computed company × source-family rows + 27 Director rows (`New_mediciine/research_coverage/coverage_summary.md`) |

## 2. Independent audits (not self-assessment)

| Audit | Scope | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| A10 round 1 (`quality/citation_audits/audit_wave1_*.md`, `gate1_verdicts.md`, `quality/evaluation_results/wave1_scorecard.md`) | 99 claims re-inspected; 151 XBRL pairs reconciled; 7 controlled questions | 72 pass, 25 locator fixes, 1 label error (debt), 1 not-found (Strateos link); 146/151 reconcile (5 definitional); Gate 1: Lilly PASS, J&J / AbbVie CONDITIONAL PASS, Takeda FAIL (repairable) |
| A10-bis round 2 (`*_wave2.md`) | 88 claims + all 46 FDA approval dates + 43 CT.gov statuses re-checked live; ≥120 synthesis citations | All reachable numbers matched; 4 mis-cited IDs, 3 announcement-vs-regulator dates, 2 derived-number errors found; A12/A14/A11 ACCEPT, A7/A8 REVISE; `master_comparison.md` decision-grade with conditions |
| Director application | `scripts/apply_audit.py`, `scripts/apply_audit2.py` | 27 proposals accepted into `conflicts.jsonl` (110 records total); 82 claim amendments with `audit_history` (statements immutable); 2 new debt claims; policy/synthesis text repaired; dossiers v1.1 (A15) applied the Gate 1 repairs incl. Takeda's missing files |
| Strategic Council / Red Team (`strategy/critical_challenges/`) | 7 councils × 17 bets | 45 support / 64 conditional / 10 oppose; 17 disagreements; 19/85 robustness cells re-rated; 10 decision changes accepted by the Director (`DIRECTOR_DECISION_RECORD.md`) → strategy v2 |

**Gate status at close.** Gate 0 (operating system) PASS. Gate 1: Lilly PASS; J&J, AbbVie CONDITIONAL PASS with repairs applied in v1.1; Takeda repairs applied in v1.1 but **not re-audited** — formally still FAIL (repairable) until a third audit round confirms. Gate 2 (Takeda baseline + gaps documented) PASS — 16 capability areas classified, 14-item internal-validation backlog. Gate 3 (only accepted evidence feeds conclusions): the deliverables cite 184 claims, all SUPPORTED/PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED or used only for "no evidence" statements; INCONCLUSIVE claims are not used as facts. Application gate PASS.

## 3. Judgement against the §25 standard (Director's honest assessment)

| Question | Assessment |
|---|---|
| Research — what companies did vs their ambitions | Strong on financials, approvals, deals, LOE and policy (filings, FDA, CT.gov, courts). AI/robotics evidence is mostly company-reported by nature of the subject; the system says so (no demonstrated outcome at any of the four companies). |
| Evidence traceability | Every number in dossiers, comparisons, strategy and deliverables resolves to a claim → source → locator; 294 T1 sources. |
| Comparison — explains *why*, not ranks | `master_comparison.md` explains mechanisms and lists the rankings it refuses (LOE score, approvals per R&D dollar, margin/leverage, ecosystem "defensibility"). |
| Science | Approval dates, CRL reasons and trial statuses verified against regulator/registry records; peer-reviewed readouts read at abstract level only (limitation). |
| Business | Mechanisms (Humira contracting, incretin capacity, Stelara→Tremfya, Allergan synergies) are evidence-backed with numbers. |
| Technology maturity | 110 maturity-tagged claims; retags applied where the auditor disagreed; autonomous-lab reality check separates commodity stages from undemonstrated ones. |
| Strategy grounded in Takeda's position | Every bet carries a baseline class and IVB pointers; council challenge changed 10 decisions. |
| Capital allocation | Three portfolios with ranges and 37 explicit assumptions; no NPV (needs Takeda forecasts) — stated rather than faked. |
| Multiple futures | 5 scenarios + early-entry stress case; robustness published with council re-ratings. |
| Product | 11-pillar hub; insight → claim → source navigation; 197 reports in-app; Q&A grounded, zero-cost by default. |
| Persistence | `map.md`, `PROJECT_STATE.md`, `CONTINUE.md`, run logs, experiments log, briefs for every agent, 29 commits. |

## 4. Known gaps and limitations (carried forward, not hidden)
1. **Takeda Gate 1 re-audit pending** (repairs applied in v1.1, not independently re-checked).
2. **A7 (commercial) and A8 (policy) shards rated REVISE**: single-interested-source flag over-applied in A7; lobbying totals for J&J/AbbVie missing because the Senate LDA and OpenSecrets block scripted access; FEC totals not obtained (DEMO_KEY rate limit).
3. **Independent corroboration field is empty on almost all claims** — independence was assessed in prose and tiers, not recorded structurally; the rubric's "independence" dimension cannot exceed 2 until this is back-filled.
4. **Peer-reviewed sources read at abstract level**; no full-text safety tables.
5. **Leadership interviews**: only metadata and a handful of inspected transcripts.
6. **Unresolved conflicts** (kept, not forced): AbbVie Ventures founding date; Lilly robotic-lab start (2017 vs ~2020) and the Strateos link; Lilly 2024 lobbying (7.89m vs 8.43m); Medicare obesity access start (April vs July 2026); Entyvio statutory exclusivity date.
7. **No evidence found for**: installed bases of OTTAVA/MONARCH/VELYS; TuneLab uptake; NVIDIA–Lilly lab operating status; venture-arm fund sizes; competitor orexin landscape; Takeda Ventures/CEI scale.
8. **BET-18 (licensing channel)** is council-proposed and not independently reviewed.
9. **Strategy numbers are assumptions**: Takeda's actual budget, PTS and forecasts are not public; portfolios are proposals.
10. **Mobile layout** verified only by CSS review and headless Chrome at ≥1024 px; **LLM path from `file://`** requires `OLLAMA_ORIGINS=*` and was not browser-tested.
11. Subagent default tool-call cap (100) cost two wave-1 runs; later waves used 400 with save-as-you-go. Recorded in `research_methodology/research_runs/RUN-0004-wave1-multiagent.md`.

## 5. Verdict
The system is **usable, auditable and maintainable**: a future agent can open `map.md`, run the four validators above, and extend any shard without re-reading the encyclopedia. It is **not** finished research: items 1–8 above are the next session's queue (see `CONTINUE.md`).

# A10 audit: numeric reconciliation (Task 2)

Date 2026-11-21. Machine-readable proposals: `New_mediciine/evidence_library/conflicts_proposed_A10.jsonl` (14 records).

## (a) RUN-0001 XBRL claims versus A4_financial shard
All A4 claims whose metric has an XBRL counterpart (revenue, R&D, net income, operating cash flow, capex, pre-tax income, operating income, acquisitions cash, acquired IPR&D, IPR&D payments) were joined to RUN-0001 by company, concept and fiscal year and compared in USD m / JPY bn.

- 151 pairs compared; 146 agree to rounding (Lilly 45/45, J&J 37/37 (incl. FY2021 52-week-end 2022-01-02 mapped to FY2021), Takeda 24/24, AbbVie 40/45).
- 5 differences, all AbbVie net income and all definitional: RUN-0001 uses consolidated net earnings (11,549 / 11,845 / 4,873 / 4,286 / 4,233), A4 uses net earnings attributable to AbbVie (11,542 / 11,836 / 4,863 / 4,278 / 4,226). Verified in the 10-Ks (FY2021 lines 1178-1180; FY2025 lines 1306-1308). Neither is wrong; each needs a basis note.
- A4 metrics with no XBRL counterpart (dividends paid, buybacks, ctgov counts) were not compared. A4 holds four Takeda fiscal years for several metrics where RUN-0001 holds four as well, so no gap.
- No restatement was found between the original and later filings for these metrics. Two classification changes were found: Lilly FY2021 acquired IPR&D 874.9 (FY2021 10-K) versus 970.1 (FY2022 10-K, line item widened to include development milestones); J&J FY2021 segment recast (Pharmaceutical 52,080 -> 51,680; Consumer Health 14,635 -> 15,035).

AbbVie FY2025: 64,503 total vs 58,941 non-current; J&J FY2025: 41,438 subtotal vs 39,438 non-current. Lilly uses `LongTermDebtNoncurrent` and is correct. reports.title: A10 audit: wave-1 claim re-inspection (Task 1)
reports.markdown:
# A10 audit: wave-1 claim re-inspection (Task 1)

Auditor: A10 (independent). Date: 2026-11-21. Registry snapshot: 1,110 claims / 395 sources (the brief cites 957 / 278; the registry grew after A12/A8/A7/A14 merges). Companion data: [audit_wave1_reinspection.jsonl](audit_wave1_reinspection.jsonl).

## Method
Every sampled claim was re-checked against the source text myself: 10-K/20-F text on disk via `grep -n`/`sed -n` (line numbers are lines of the extracted `.txt`), the Takeda H1 FY2026 PDF re-extracted with pypdf, web pages fetched in this session or read from stored extracted text, ClinicalTrials.gov via the v2 API, PubMed via NCBI E-utilities. The agents' `inspected_passage` was not used as proof. Components I could not open are written as UNVERIFIED in the note column, not as PASS. As an additional screen, all 320 claims of shards A1/A2/A3/A5 were machine-checked for number presence in their cited on-disk source text: 209 passed, 23 flagged (all reviewed by hand; 3 real findings below), 88 have only web/PDF sources and were not machine-checkable.

## Result

Sample: **99 claims**. PASS 72, PASS_WITH_LOCATOR_FIX 25, NUMBER_MISMATCH 1, NOT_FOUND_IN_SOURCE 1.

Strata: A (FACT with `~` locator, all 17 in registry) · B (A1/A2/A3/A5 claims carrying a >=1,000 USD m / JPY bn figure; the wave-1 shards leave the `value` field null, so the stratum was selected from statement text: 41 audited of ~145 candidates) · C:A6 (12 random) · C:A9 (12 random) · C:Dir (10 random RUN-0002/0003) · C:extra (pipeline and web claims examined while following up flags).

### Substantive findings

1. **NUMBER_MISMATCH / mislabel, CLM-003042 (and its sources CLM-000066..000070, CLM-000128..000132).** "Non-current" long-term debt is in fact total long-term debt including the current portion for AbbVie (XBRL tag `LongTermDebt`) and J&J. AbbVie FY2025: 64,503 is "Long-term debt, including current portion" (current 6,000; long-term 58,503 in the contractual-obligations table) and the balance-sheet non-current line is 58,941 (FY2024 60,340; FY2023 52,194; FY2022 59,135; FY2021 64,189). J&J FY2025: 41,438 is the debt-note subtotal; "Total long-term debt" after the current portion of 2,000 is 39,438 (FY2024 32,400 vs 30,651). Lilly (`LongTermDebtNoncurrent`) is correct. 20 claims carry the wrong label.

2. **NOT_FOUND_IN_SOURCE, CLM-006017.** The claim about a "Lilly-Strateos remote robotic laboratory (public launch about 2020)" cites two BiopharmaTrend articles that never mention Strateos. They describe the Lilly Life Sciences Studio (established 2017, USD 90m). The 2020 date and the Strateos link are unsupported by the cited pages.

3. **Maturity labels not justified by the evidence.** CLM-006026 (VELYS) is tagged SCALED although the 10-K gives no system or procedure counts; CLM-006022 (course completions) is tagged SCALED; CLM-006047, -006049, -006051 are tagged DEMONSTRATED_OUTCOME but describe failures at Recursion, Exscientia/BenevolentAI and Zymergen, not AI applications at the four companies. CLM-006020 (J&J 2.6x enrollment) is tagged OPERATIONAL on a single self-reported interview statement. Maturity values are also upper-case, whereas the protocol enumerates lower-case.

4. **Registry understates retrievability.** SRC-000034 (J&J OTTAVA release), SRC-009022 (CDD TuneLab blog) and SRC-009017 (BioPharma Dive) are registered `metadata_only` but returned full pages in this audit. The OTTAVA page says Memorial Hermann "will be the first hospital to install" the system (future tense); CLM-000284 and the J&J master report ("first install 2026-11-19") present the installation as completed. The 19-Nov-2026 date does not appear in the page text I read.

5. **Partly unreachable component.** CLM-005025: the JPY 58.0bn cell-therapy impairment is confirmed in the Takeda release, but the "137 Massachusetts roles" element rests on a Fierce Biotech page that returned HTTP 403 to this audit (UNVERIFIED).

6. **Locator drift.** 25 claims have correct figures but approximate or wrong locators; 15 of the 17 `~` locators needed a corrected line number (e.g. CLM-001009 cites Item 5 while the sentence is in the equity note at line 2255; CLM-009086 cites lines ~2070-2072, the text is at 2075-2076). Corrected locators are in the table.

7. **Cash vs expense.** CLM-001014 states FY2025 cash paid for acquired IPR&D as "3,008.0"; the filing reports 3,008 (whole millions). Date 2026-11-21. Scope: all 1,110 claims in `claims_registry.jsonl`. Proposals only; no registry edits.

## Summary

| Check | Count | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| FACT + SUPPORTED, every source T2, `single_interested_source` not set, no independent corroboration | 8 | Propose flag (all J&J). |
| FACT whose statement contains interpretive wording | 0 needing retype | 28 keyword hits were reviewed; all are quotations, source field names ("indications", "signals" in "no new safety signals") or attributed company statements. Wave-1 shards separate FACT and INTERPRETATION well (47 INTERPRETATION, 4 HYPOTHESIS, 3 RECOMMENDATION). |
| AI / robotics claims (domain `data_ai`, `robotics_automation`, or shard A6) with no `maturity` | 24 | Propose tags (below). |
| SUPPORTED claims whose only support is a `metadata_only` source | 0 | Agents already downgraded. 6 SUPPORTED/PARTIAL claims mix a metadata_only source with retrieved ones (below). |
| Maturity tags not justified by the cited evidence | 6 | Propose retag (below and conflicts_proposed_A10.jsonl). |
| Absence-of-evidence statements typed FACT | 9 | All INCONCLUSIVE or flagged in the statement; recommend a distinct `gap` record type instead of FACT. |

## 1. FACT + SUPPORTED resting only on company (T2) sources, not flagged

## 2. Interpretive language typed as FACT
No claim needs retyping. Borderline cases that should keep the quotation marks in the statement: CLM-003052 ("best-in-class" attributed to the announcement), CLM-009050 (J&J "claims more than 150 partnerships"), CLM-006025 ("competitive advantage" inside a risk-factor paraphrase). Also: maturity values are stored upper-case (OPERATIONAL, PILOT, ...) whereas `agent_protocols.md` lists lower-case enums; normalise. The A1 claims CLM-001056..001060 carry DEMONSTRATED_OUTCOME for Phase 3 drug trial results: that is a clinical outcome, not AI maturity (the field was designed for AI/data/robotics). Consider `not_applicable`.

## 5. Claims citing metadata_only sources
No SUPPORTED claim relies on a metadata_only source alone. Mixed cases to re-read: CLM-006029, CLM-006059, CLM-009015, CLM-003072, CLM-003081, CLM-008040. Claims left PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED/INCONCLUSIVE solely because their source is metadata_only although the page is retrievable (A10 opened them): CLM-000284 (J&J OTTAVA), CLM-009028 (CDD TuneLab data points, confirmed), CLM-009055 (BioPharma Dive headline, confirmed). Propose re-registering SRC-000034, SRC-009022 and SRC-009017 as `retrieved` with the inspected passage and upgrading CLM-009028 and CLM-009055 to SUPPORTED (FACT about the vendor blog / headline only).

## 6. Absence claims
CLM-005052, -005067, -005070, -005072, -005080, -007039, -014057 record searches that found nothing. They are correctly INCONCLUSIVE. Typing them FACT mixes "a document says X" with "I could not find X"; use a gap record. CLM-014057 (no primary Strateos/Multiply Labs release) is consistent with this audit: CLM-006015 should stay NEEDS_MORE_RESEARCH.

reports.markdown:
# A10-bis Task 2: citation consistency of the synthesis layer

Date 2026-11-21. Auditor A10-bis. Scope: `New_mediciine/cross_company_analysis/master_comparison.md` and `lessons_for_takeda.md`; the seven `strategy/future_of_pharma/domain*.md`; `strategy/platform_moats/analogies_platform_strategies.md` (lines 1-83 read in full); and the five `industry_transformation/policy/*.md` files that carry citations.

Method: for every cited line I printed the cited claim statements next to the sentence and judged support at sentence level. 788 citation occurrences were read this way (master 167, lessons 171, domain1-7 296, analogies about 80 in the lines read, policy 74). About 200 were compared number by number against the claim text. A script then listed every sentence containing a number that does not occur in any cited claim (74 hits, most are rounding, dates, table row numbers or computed values; the real ones are below). Every cited ID exists in the registry (0 dangling IDs).

Codes: OK, MISCITED (the cited claim says something else or lacks the number), OVERSTATED (sentence stronger than the claim), STALE (a later claim or fact supersedes the sentence).

## Verdict by file

| File | Citations read | MISCITED | OVERSTATED / STALE | Reading |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| master_comparison.md | 167 | 3 | 4 | Mostly sound; the debt-basis repair and two basis notes cite claims that do not carry the repaired numbers |
| lessons_for_takeda.md | 171 | 0 | 3 | Sound; one derived duration is wrong |
| domain1 data | 39 | 0 | 1 | Recommendation 1.1 labelled EVIDENCE_BACKED on weaker evidence |
| domain2 R&D | 65 | 0 | 2 | |
| domain3 robotics | 52 | 0 | 0 | Cleanest file; maturity and conflict notes are honest |
| domain4 care models | 38 | 1 (inherited date) | 0 | |
| domain5 commercial | 39 | 0 | 0 | |
| domain6 partnerships | 48 | 1 | 2 | Two wrong numbers carried from A9 claims |
| domain7 people | 35 | 0 | 0 | |
| analogies | about 80 | 1 | 0 | Table cells cite the hypothesis instead of the fact claim |
| policy/*.md | 74 | 4 | 0 | The alleged pledge mis-citations are real (see below) |

## The alleged policy mis-citations: confirmed, four in total

`industry_transformation/policy/pricing_tariffs_manufacturing_pledges.md` (the pledge IDs):

| Line | Sentence | Cites | Claim says | Correct ID |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 12 | Lilly 1 March 2023 insulin 70% cut | CLM-008030 | J&J USD 55bn investment | CLM-008026 |
| 14 | Lilly FY2025 10-K preliminary agreements, three-year Section 232 grace | CLM-008032 | AbbVie USD 100bn agreement | CLM-008028 |
| 17 | J&J 8 January 2026 voluntary agreement, TrumpRx, USD 55bn reaffirmed | CLM-008035 | Takeda 20-F MFN statement | CLM-008031 |

`ira_negotiation_exposure.md` line 32: AbbVie USD 2.1bn Imbruvica impairment in Q3 2023 cites CLM-008021 (Lilly Jardiance 66% discount). Correct ID CLM-008019.

`cross_company_analysis/evidence_gaps.md` section 3 already admits the pledge-ID inconsistency ("for example CLM-008030 and CLM-008032 for Lilly 10-K points") and the OTTAVA 21/22 July difference, but the policy files were not corrected; I have located the exact lines. All four sentences are true; the IDs are shifted. The correct claims exist and I verified their numbers against primary sources (see audit_wave2_reinspection.md). Effect: a reader following the ID lands on a different company. All other lines of the five policy files match their claims, including the CMS price table, the pledge table rows 7-10 and the litigation list.

## Other findings (master, lessons, domains, analogies)

1. **master_comparison.md line 7 (MISCITED).** States non-current debt of USD 58,941m (AbbVie) and USD 39,438m (J&J) and cites CLM-000070, CLM-000132 and CLM-003042. Those claims carry 64,503, 41,438 and the 75,962 to 64,503 series, which are the figures the line says are wrong. The two non-current values are correct (AbbVie FY2025 10-K lines 1372, 2063; J&J FY2025 10-K lines 1203, 2038) but no registered claim contains them. CLM-003042 is still labelled "non-current" and still carries the mislabelled series, although Gate 1 required the correction. Fix: register two claims for 58,941 and 39,438 and relabel CLM-003042, CLM-000066..000070.
2. **master line 11 (MISCITED).** "3.35bn cash paid" cites CLM-009002, which contains 3.2bn and 2.55bn only. The 3.35bn is in the Lilly FY2024 10-K (line 1039) and in conflicts_proposed_A10, not in the cited claim. "AbbVie net income differs by basis" cites CLM-000026, a single XBRL value with no basis statement.
3. **master line 10 (MISCITED, partial).** "Cell-therapy impairment recognised is JPY 58.2bn, not 58.0bn" cites CLM-005025, which states the 58.0bn expectation. The recognised 58.2bn is CLM-009084 and CLM-009100 (verified: JPY 58,173m, Takeda FY2025 20-F line 5386).
4. **master line 28 (OVERSTATED).** "Of 29 company-level entries, 18 sit at concept, prototype or pilot" cites CLM-006054, which has no such count (the numbers appear only in data_ai_maturity_matrix.md line 25). My count from A6 FACT claims with a company and a maturity tag is 36 tagged claims (15 OPERATIONAL, 21 concept, prototype or pilot). Unit differs (entries vs claims); the matrix should state the unit.
5. **master line 52 (OVERSTATED).** "outcome trials read out 2029-2031" cites ClinicalTrials.gov records whose primary completion dates are estimates (2029-02, 2029-03, 2031-08). A primary completion estimate is not a readout date.
6. **master line 16 (OVERSTATED, minor).** "capex USD 1.3bn to 7.8bn" cites CLM-000172 (7.8bn only); the 1.3bn is CLM-000168, cited in lessons but not here.
7. **master line 12 and CLM-000286 (STALE).** The sentence correctly says completed installation is not shown, but CLM-000286, cited in the same sentence, still reads "regulator-verified milestone and a commercial installation".
8. **lessons line 63 (OVERSTATED, wrong number).** "CVS Caremark removed Zepbound for about 11 months". CLM-007011 gives removal from 1 July 2025 and CLM-007013 gives restoration effective 1 October 2026: 15 months. About 11 months is the time to the 28 May 2026 announcement.
9. **lessons line 35 (OVERSTATED).** "Operating evidence only for Concord, Kinsale and the Lebanon genetic-medicine plant" cites the Houston claim and the Concord claim; Kinsale (CLM-014011) and Lebanon (CLM-014015, CLM-006002) are not cited. Concord's operating status rests on one trade article (T3, CLM-014014 PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED).
10. **lessons line 175 (OVERSTATED).** "TREMFYA subcutaneous share gains accompanied USD 5,155m": the 10-K attributes growth to share gains and market growth (CLM-000256), and says nothing about the subcutaneous route.
11. **domain1 line 40 (OVERSTATED).** Recommendation 1.1 reads "EVIDENCE_BACKED: pooled models beat Takeda-only models on Takeda targets". The only evidence (CLM-006043) says a five-company model beat the best public model by about 10 points on pose accuracy, vendor-reported and not peer reviewed. No Takeda-only comparison exists in the corpus.
12. **domain2 line 22 (OVERSTATED).** "AbbVie's Cerevel purchase ended in discontinuation or large impairment, so acquiring is not safer than building". The same purchase delivered tavapadon, approved as Juvmo on 2026-09-25 (CLM-012017); the sentence omits it.
13. **domain2 line 18 (STALE).** "zasocitinib ... (NDA planned 2026)". CLM-005035 records FDA acceptance of the NDA with Priority Review on 14 September 2026.
14. **domain6 line 15 (wrong numbers).** "J&J Momenta (nipocalimab, 2025-04-30)": FDA approved Imaavy on 2025-04-29 (openFDA BLA761430; CLM-012011 is right, CLM-009044 uses the company announcement date). "CAPLYTA MDD, nine months after close": the acquisition closed 2025-04-02 and openFDA shows the efficacy supplement approved 2025-11-05, seven months.
15. **domain6 line 36 (STALE).** "A10 flags 2.6x as unverified". Takeda FY2025 20-F lines 2353 and 2669 show 2.8x (March 2025) and 2.6x (March 2026). The 2.6x (March 2023) and 3.1x (March 2024) values remain unchecked.
16. **domain4 line 10 and analogies line 67 (inherited error).** OTTAVA De Novo "2026-07-22" is taken from CLM-000283 and CLM-006029. The FDA De Novo database gives decision date 2026-07-21 and receipt 2025-12-18 (DEN250068). CLM-014022 has it right.
17. **analogies table rows 4 and 7 (MISCITED style).** "Flagship product still eroded 42%" and "Installed base drives 84% recurring revenue" cite the HYPOTHESIS claims (CLM-011038, CLM-011048). The numbers sit in CLM-011017 and CLM-011021. Table cells should cite the fact claim for a figure.

## OK, with notes

- The CMS price table, the Part D cost figures, the IRA cycle dates, the litigation list, and the AbbVie, J&J and Lilly revenue, R&D and capex rows of the master table match their claims.
- Computed values I recomputed and found correct: Humira -78.6% (21,237 to 4,540), Skyrizi plus Rinvoq +18,179m, Tremfya +1,485m offsetting 34.7% of Stelara's 4,283m loss, emraclidine 4.5bn as 54% of Cerevel's 8.3bn net price, AWS 57% of Amazon operating income, Alphabet Other Bets loss +3.1bn.
- Novel-approval counts in master line 40 (Lilly 8, J&J 5, AbbVie 5, Takeda 3) match the registry. AbbVie's five include Elahere (sponsor of record ImmunoGen) and Epkinly (sponsor Genmab), which the text calls "mostly acquired or partnered".
- Takeda's AMITIZA, Nimbus split, Keros and Innovent payments, Entyvio revenue share and Growth and Launch share were checked in the 20-F and agree.

## What this means for use

Citation hygiene is good: no invented IDs, no unsupported company-level number found in the policy, domain and analogy layers beyond items 1, 2, 4, 8, 11 and 14. The items most likely to mislead a reader are 1 (debt), 8 (11 months), 11 (EVIDENCE_BACKED on vendor evidence) and 14 (dates in the partnership domain).

# A10-bis Task 1: re-inspection of wave 2/3 shards

Date 2026-11-21. Auditor A10-bis. Method: every verdict below comes from a source I opened myself in this session (openFDA and ClinicalTrials.gov APIs queried live, FDA De Novo database, CMS fact-sheet PDFs, SEC filings on disk and from EDGAR, NASA NTRS PDFs, Nobel, Roche and company releases). Codes: PASS / LOCATOR_FIX / NUMBER_MISMATCH / PERIOD_MISMATCH / NOT_FOUND / UNREACHABLE. UNREACHABLE means I could not open the source (HTTP 403 or block page), not that the claim is wrong.

**Sample size:** 92 claim verdicts in the stratified sample (A12 20, A8 13, A7 14, A14 22, A11 19, plus 4 cross-shard findings), plus a full sweep of 46 A12 FDA approval-date claims (46 of 46 match openFDA) and 43 of 43 A12 ClinicalTrials.gov status claims (all match the live record). Full machine-readable list: audit_wave2_reinspection.jsonl (165 records).

## Result in one paragraph

No wrong number was found in A12, A8, A7, A14 or A11 FACT claims. The defects found are (1) date-label errors where a company announcement date is stored as the FDA action date (CLM-003063 Juvmo 09-28 vs FDA 09-25; CLM-000283 and CLM-006029 OTTAVA De Novo 07-22 vs FDA 07-21), (2) seven claims I could not re-open because investor.lilly.com, jnj.com and computerweekly.com return 403, so those rest on the stored passage only, (3) CLM-007002 whose stored passage does not contain half of the prices the statement lists, (4) CLM-012109 bermekimab 0.6bn which is a subsequent-event estimate later booked at 0.8bn, and (5) CLM-012137 whose registry date (2026) postdates the 2023 withdrawal it is paired with.
