reports.title: A10-bis Task 3: kind and status discipline on the new shards
reports.markdown:
# A10-bis Task 3: kind and status discipline on the new shards

Date 2026-11-21. Scope: claims with `merged_from_shard` in A7_commercial (59), A8_policy (55), A12_pipeline (153), A14_gapfill (75), A11_strategy (100). All 442 claims were screened by script (kind, status, source access status, source tier, maturity, wording) and the hits were read by hand. Proposals only; no registry was edited.

## Summary

| Check | Hits | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| SUPPORTED resting only on a metadata_only, blocked or paywalled source | 0 | Clean. 12 claims cite a metadata_only source as their only support and every one is already PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED, NEEDS_MORE_RESEARCH or INCONCLUSIVE |
| FACT+SUPPORTED on T2 company sources only and not flagged single_interested_source | 7 (all A14) | Flag |
| FACT+SUPPORTED on T3/T4 sources only | 14 | Review 5, accept 9 |
| FACT claims with interpretive wording | 0 real, 3 mild | Accept with edits |
| FACT claims that are negative findings ("not located", "no evidence") | 9 | Retype or tag |
| AI or robotics claims in A14 and A7 without a maturity tag | 0 FACT; 37 INTERPRETATION, HYPOTHESIS or RECOMMENDATION claims in A11 | Tag with the maturity of the evidence they cite |
| Maturity tags that do not fit the evidence | 4 | Retag |
| A11 RECOMMENDATION labelled EVIDENCE_BACKED while status is PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED | 7 of 7 | Relabel |
| A11 HYPOTHESIS that reads as a recommendation | 2 | Reword or retype |

## 1. FACT+SUPPORTED resting only on company sources, not flagged single_interested_source (propose flag)

All seven are Lilly or J&J manufacturing or restructuring announcements, the claims where announced-versus-operating matters most:

CLM-014008 (Houston 6.5bn), CLM-014009 (Huntsville), CLM-014010 (Lehigh Valley), CLM-014011 (Limerick, Kinsale), CLM-014012 (Alzey), CLM-014015 (Lebanon), CLM-014020 (J&J Orthopaedics separation intent).

Each states what the company announced or expects. The statements themselves are worded as announcements ("expected to be operational", "will be operational in 2031"), so the kind and status are right; the missing flag is the defect. Only CLM-014014 (Concord, operating) is PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED because it uses a trade article; no Lilly site is shown operating by an independent or regulator source, which the manufacturing report should say.

## 2. SUPPORTED on T3 or T4 sources only (14)

CLM-008024 (Supreme Court cert denial, law-firm summaries), CLM-008039, CLM-008040, CLM-008041, CLM-008042 (D.C. Circuit 340B ruling, HRSA pilot, hospital suit: trade and HFMA reports), CLM-007013 (CVS restoration of Zepbound, trade article), CLM-007045 (Pear bankruptcy), CLM-014027 (Red River dismissal), CLM-014063 (a16z fund), CLM-014064 (JLABS withdrawal, BetaKit), CLM-014067, CLM-014068, CLM-014072 (executive statements via podcast and call summaries), CLM-011003 (CUDA quote; already flagged single_interested_source).

Propose: CLM-008024, CLM-008039..008042 and CLM-014027 are court events with a primary record (supremecourt.gov docket 25-749, D.C. Circuit opinion, S.D. Tex. order); keep SUPPORTED only after a primary record is stored, otherwise PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED. The executive-statement claims are correctly worded as "said" and can stay SUPPORTED as attribution. CLM-007013 was confirmed by me against a second outlet (Managed Healthcare Executive) and is fine.

## 3. Interpretive wording inside FACT claims

No FACT claim states a recommendation or forecast in the project's voice. Three mild cases:

- CLM-014039 ("The two dates therefore reflect FDA action versus company announcement"): an inference; my openFDA check confirms it, so keep, but split the inference into the implications field.
- CLM-014070 ("earlier than that stated expectation"): a comparison made by the auditor; move to implications.
- A12 FACT claims carry an `implications` field with "Novelty read: ... (INTERPRETATION)" text; the label is present, so this is acceptable.

## 4. Negative findings typed FACT (9)

CLM-007039, CLM-007048, CLM-008017, CLM-014005, CLM-014052, CLM-014057, CLM-014066 and, from earlier shards, CLM-005052, CLM-005072 are statements of the form "no source opened shows X". They are typed FACT with status INCONCLUSIVE, NEEDS_MORE_RESEARCH or SUPPORTED. The schema has no EVIDENCE_GAP kind, so propose a tag `negative_finding` plus a stated search scope (sources opened, terms used), and keep CLM-014005 SUPPORTED only for the two releases it names. CLM-008007 (a methodological statement that no causal inference is drawn) is INTERPRETATION with status INCONCLUSIVE; a disclaimer has no truth status and should be a note, not a claim.

## 5. Maturity tags

Missing: none on A14 or A7 FACT claims that concern AI or robotics. A11 INTERPRETATION, HYPOTHESIS and RECOMMENDATION claims about AI and automation (CLM-011025, 011029, 011031, 011033, 011035, 011043, 011045, 011047, 011048, 011053, 011060, 011064..011066, 011071, 011074, 011076, 011080..011083, 011085, 011087..011090, 011092..011095, 011097, 011098) have no maturity tag. They are claims about options, not capabilities, so propose a tag of the maturity of the cited competitor evidence (for example CLM-011065 rests on the divested Arctoris model, OPERATIONAL but commodity; CLM-011060 on PROTOTYPE partnerships).

Tags that do not fit the evidence:

- CLM-014073 DEMONSTRATED_OUTCOME: a former CEO's interview claim of about 30% shorter narcolepsy trial development, no baseline or method, T3, PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED. It contradicts the master report's statement that no AI initiative shows a demonstrated outcome. Retag PILOT and flag single_interested_source (conflict record filed).
- CLM-014043 SCALED: 63.4% of staff "actively using" generative AI and 30.9% taking a course. Usage and training counts are adoption metrics; A10 round 1 made the same retag for J&J course completions. Propose OPERATIONAL.
- CLM-014030 PROTOTYPE on the Capstan acquisition (an asset-acquisition accounting claim). Not an AI or robotics capability; use not_applicable.
- CLM-014025 OPERATIONAL on the MONARCH QUEST 3 clearance: the claim is PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED and the "AI-powered" features are company marketing; the openFDA record only shows substantial equivalence for the platform. Propose PILOT for the AI feature, OPERATIONAL only for the device.
- CLM-014022, CLM-014023, CLM-014024 are tagged PILOT for OTTAVA (authorised, one announced early-access installation). Reasonable and consistent with the master text.

## 6. A11 strategy claims

Counts: 52 INTERPRETATION, 17 HYPOTHESIS, 7 RECOMMENDATION, 24 FACT. Status: 62 PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED, 17 NEEDS_MORE_RESEARCH, 21 SUPPORTED.

- **EVIDENCE_BACKED recommendations are PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED.** CLM-011054, 011060, 011065, 011068, 011069, 011072 and 011073 carry the label EVIDENCE_BACKED in their text and in the domain tables while the registry status is PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED. One label should win. Propose relabelling them "SUPPORTED_BY_ANALOGY: based on competitor evidence, not tested on Takeda", or keeping EVIDENCE_BACKED and upgrading the status after the weak step is repaired. The weakest: CLM-011054 (pooled models beat Takeda-only models; the evidence is a vendor-organised consortium result against public models, not peer reviewed), CLM-011072 (relies on T4 Drug Channels and a CVS release for Entyvio biosimilar risk; Entyvio biosimilars have FDA review dates only from a trade snippet, CLM-014051), CLM-011073 (a "do not" recommendation resting on CRS description of copay rules and an inference about fit).
- **HYPOTHESIS that reads as a recommendation.** CLM-011045 ("Takeda should not attempt to productise ...") and CLM-011066 ("Takeda should set explicit triggers ...") use directive wording. Retype as RECOMMENDATION with its own evidence label or reword as "Takeda could".
- **FACT claims in A11.** I re-opened 19 of the 24 against primary text (NVIDIA, Alphabet, Regeneron, TSMC, Amazon and Intuitive 10-K or 20-F; NASA documents; Nobel; Roche). All numbers match. CLM-011003 (CUDA quotes) could not be re-opened (Computer Weekly 403) and rests on one interested speaker via T3; it is correctly flagged. CLM-011013 and CLM-011014 rest on snippets (metadata_only) and are PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED, correctly.
- **Analogy transfer is stated as a hypothesis in the registry but as a table of options in the domain files** (see citation-consistency findings 11 and 17). The registry labelling is the more careful of the two.

## 7. Other discipline points

- CLM-007000 and CLM-007002 are SUPPORTED on press-release passages I could not re-open (403); the stored passage for CLM-007002 does not contain half the prices in the statement. Propose PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED until the full text is stored.
- CLM-012137 and CLM-012136 are SUPPORTED (registry values match) but their pairing with a company statement creates an apparent contradiction (conflict records filed).
- A12 deserves credit: all 46 regulatory-date claims and 43 registry-status claims match live records, and its INTERPRETATION claims are PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED. No retag is proposed for A12 beyond the date-label cases in the re-inspection file.

## 8. Cross-shard tag inconsistency found while answering the golden questions

OTTAVA carries maturity OPERATIONAL in CLM-000283 and CLM-000284 (Director/A6 records) but PILOT in CLM-014022, CLM-014023, CLM-014024 (A14) and CLM-002048, CLM-002049 (A2). The evidence (De Novo authorised, one announced early-access installation, no unit or revenue data) fits PILOT. Propose retagging CLM-000283 and CLM-000284 to PILOT.

reports.title: A10: controlled questions, wave 1 (Task 5)
reports.markdown:
# A10: controlled questions, wave 1 (Task 5)

Date 2026-11-21. Protocol: answer only from `claims_registry.jsonl`, `source_registry.jsonl` and the dossiers (grep), cite claim IDs, then check each cited claim's statement and source. Outcomes: answered_fully / answered_partially / not_answerable / confabulation_detected. "Check" columns state what I re-opened myself.

| # | Question | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | J&J MedTech initiatives and regulator-verified status | answered_partially |
| 2 | AbbVie response to Humira LOE, in numbers | answered_fully |
| 3 | Lilly initiatives moved past announcement | answered_partially |
| 4 | AI applications with demonstrated scientific/operational impact | answered_partially (the honest answer is "none independently demonstrated") |
| 5 | Most defensible ecosystem/partnership investments | answered_partially |
| 6 | Takeda largest LOE exposure after Vyvanse and replacement plan | answered_fully |
| 7 | NEGATIVE: Lilly TuneLab revenue in 2025 | not_answerable (PASS: no fabrication) |

## Q1. Which publicly documented initiatives distinguish J&J's MedTech strategy, and what is their regulator-verified status?
**Answer from the registry.**
- OTTAVA table-integrated soft-tissue robot: IDE approval announced 2024-11-12 [CLM-002048]; De Novo submission announced 2026-01-07 [CLM-002049]; De Novo authorization 2026-07-22 [CLM-000283]; first hospital (Memorial Hermann-TMC) announced 2026-11-19 [CLM-000284]; FY2021 partial IPR&D impairment of USD 0.9bn on delays [CLM-009047].
- MONARCH bronchoscopy: 510(k) for QUEST 3 software announced 2026-08-17 [CLM-006027]; TARGET study 679 patients, 98.7% lesion reach, 83.2% diagnostic yield (company-sponsored, single arm) [CLM-002067].
- VELYS: Spine 510(k) announced 2024-08-02 [CLM-002066]; Knee growth "pull through" in the 10-K with no counts [CLM-006026].
- Polyphonic digital ecosystem in early access; Abu Dhabi programme [CLM-006030, CLM-006031].
- Capital deployment: Abiomed (USD 17.1bn net; FY2025 sales 1,751m) [CLM-002009, CLM-002027], Shockwave (FY2025 sales 1,146m) [CLM-002011], Orthopaedics separation as DePuy Synthes announced October 2025 [CLM-002030, CLM-002037].
- Safety/regulatory friction: FDA Class I recall classification of the Varipulse correction [CLM-002045] and of Impella pumps (66,390 units, 49 deaths recorded) [CLM-002046].
- Regulator-verified status as stated: "only OTTAVA ... regulator-verified milestone" [CLM-000286, CLM-006054].

**Audit.**
- Only two J&J MedTech claims rest on FDA records (T1, `regulatory_record`): the Varipulse recall [CLM-002045] and the Impella recall [CLM-002046]. The De Novo, 510(k) and IDE statements [CLM-000283, -006027, -002066, -002048] are sourced to J&J press releases (T2).
- A10 independent check: openFDA 510(k) database lists MONARCH Platform K260382 (decision 2026-07-25) and K243219 (2025-01-23), and VELYS Robotic-Assisted Solution K260480 (2026-06-25), K240211 (2024-06-05). I found no "VELYS Spine" device name by the name search tried. openFDA has no De Novo endpoint, so the OTTAVA De Novo is still UNVERIFIED against a regulator record.
- "Regulator-verified" in CLM-000286 and CLM-006054 is therefore an overstatement of the sourcing, although the underlying event is plausible and the MONARCH clearance is now verified.
- CLM-000284: the release says the hospital "will be the first to install"; the answer must not say a commercial installation is complete.

**Unsupported or weak statements logged:** "regulator-verified" for OTTAVA (company source only); "first commercial installation" completed (future tense in the release); the dossier phrase "about 24 months from IDE to first commercial install" (depends on the install).
**Retrieval issue:** the corpus has no dedicated claim per FDA database record; a query for "FDA" + "OTTAVA" returns press-release claims typed T2, which a reader may mistake for regulator evidence.

## Q2. What evidence supports AbbVie's response to Humira LOE, in numbers?
**Answer.** U.S. exclusivity ended 2023-01-31; U.S. Humira fell 35% (2023), 41% (2024), 57% (2025) [CLM-003000, CLM-003010]. U.S. Humira revenue 17,330 / 18,619 / 12,160 / 7,142 / 3,062 (USD m, 2021-25) [CLM-003001]; global 20,694 / 21,237 / 14,404 / 8,993 / 4,540, i.e. 2025 is 21% of the 2022 peak [CLM-003002]. Skyrizi 2,939 -> 17,562 [CLM-003012], Rinvoq 1,651 -> 8,304 [CLM-003013]; combined 7,687 (2022) -> 25,866 (2025), +18,179 versus Humira -16,697 [CLM-003014]. Total revenue 58,054 (2022), 54,318 (2023, -6.4%), 56,334 (2024), 61,160 (2025, +8.6%) [CLM-003015]. Nine biosimilars launched in 2023 [CLM-003006]; Humira kept at least 97% of adalimumab volume through March 2024 [CLM-003007]; CVS Caremark exclusion from April 2024 and co-branded Cordavis supply [CLM-003008, CLM-003009]; Skyrizi and Rinvoq gained new indications 2022-2025 [CLM-003016]; 2027 target above USD 31bn [CLM-003022].
**Audit.** I re-read the 10-K tables for CLM-003001/2/10/12/13/14/15 (all PASS, arithmetic recomputed). CLM-003006, -003007, -003009 (T3 trade/IQVIA) and -003022 (partly metadata_only/blocked sources) were not re-opened: UNVERIFIED by A10. CLM-003014 is correctly typed INTERPRETATION. Counter-evidence is present (aesthetics weakness, impairment of emraclidine, class actions [CLM-003011]).
**Outcome:** answered_fully. No unsupported statement found in the numbers.

## Q3. Which Lilly initiatives have moved beyond announcement into measurable implementation?
**Answer.**
- Tirzepatide supply build-out: capex USD 1.3bn (FY2021) -> 7.8bn (FY2025) [CLM-000172, CLM-000246]; shortage ended 2024-10-02/12-19 [CLM-001066]; Lebanon Advanced Therapies plant opened 2026-05-06 [CLM-006002, CLM-001041]. Commitments (USD 50bn+, Richmond site groundbreaking 2026-10-22) are announcements or construction, not output [CLM-001039, CLM-001040].
- New-product launches with revenue: Mounjaro/Zepbound 56% of revenue [CLM-000242]; 9M-2026 Kisunla 484m, Foundayo 281m, Inluriyo 183m [CLM-001032]; Foundayo available from 2026-04-09 [CLM-001030].
- LillyDirect: launched 2024-01-04 [CLM-001042]; "growing portion" of sales with no figure [CLM-001016].
- AI/data: TuneLab live since 2025-09-09 [CLM-000280] with 2 million Lilly and 675,000 partner data points as of October 2026 (vendor blog) [CLM-009028] and named collaborators [CLM-014056]; LillyPod inaugurated (hardware, >9,000 petaflops) [CLM-006004]. No scientific or financial outcome reported [CLM-006007, CLM-000286]. NVIDIA co-innovation lab is a concept [CLM-009029]; Medicine Foundry planned for late 2027 [CLM-006000, CLM-006001].
**Audit.** Re-verified: capex, Mounjaro/Zepbound share, 9M-2026 revenue, TuneLab data-point blog (CDD page text), LillyPod specs. LillyDirect has no quantification. CLM-001032 product figures not individually compared.
**Outcome:** answered_partially: strong for manufacturing and launches, no outcome data for LillyDirect or AI.

## Q4. Which reported AI applications at any of the four companies have demonstrated scientific or operational impact?
**Answer the corpus supports:** none is independently demonstrated. Self-reported operational claims: J&J "up to 2.6x" enrollment at AI-recommended sites [CLM-006020]; gen-AI quality-control tool answering SKU questions "in minutes instead of weeks" [CLM-006021]; image analytics "faster" delivery of molecular entities [CLM-006024]; AbbVie ARCH reuse of 2,000+ trials' data [CLM-006034]; AISB OpenFold3 federated fine-tuning claiming about 10 points better pose accuracy than public models (Apheris statement, PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED) [CLM-006043]. Explicit negatives: no published discovery outcome, cost saving or revenue effect from any of the four [CLM-006054]; no Lilly AI-factory outcome [CLM-006007]; Takeda no named deployed AI system with outcome [CLM-006045, CLM-005080].
**Audit.** I opened the Greylock interview (2.6x, AskJIA, Engagement.AI confirmed) and Bio-IT World (2,000+ trials). Baselines and methods are undisclosed in each. **Retrieval hazard:** filtering the registry on maturity DEMONSTRATED_OUTCOME returns CLM-006047 (Recursion), -006048 (rentosertib, Insilico), -006049, -006051 (Zymergen) and A1 clinical-trial claims: none is an AI application at the four companies. SCALED returns CLM-006026 (VELYS) and CLM-006022 (training completions). A summariser trusting the tags would confabulate "demonstrated impact".
**Outcome:** answered_partially; confabulation risk through maturity tags (not present in the dossier text I read).

## Q5. Which ecosystem/partnership investments appear most defensible, and why?
**Answer from the registry.** The registry does not rank partnerships; it gives synthesis claims [CLM-009095..009101, all PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED INTERPRETATION] and evidence that can be used to argue a ranking:
- Revenue-bearing acquisitions: Abiomed (FY2025 1,751m) and Shockwave (1,146m) [CLM-002027, CLM-002011]; Intra-Cellular's CAPLYTA 700m in FY2025 [CLM-002025]; Elahere U.S. 607m in 2025 [CLM-003036]. Against them: emraclidine USD 4.5bn write-down after Cerevel [CLM-003057], J&J OTTAVA 0.9bn and bermekimab 0.8bn impairments, Lilly GBA1 244.6m, Takeda JPY 58.2bn cell therapy [CLM-009100].
- Data/compute exchange is unique to Lilly's TuneLab and NVIDIA lab [CLM-009101], but unproven in outcomes [CLM-000286].
- Takeda: the Nimbus purchase [CLM-009098] is linked to zasocitinib, whose NDA was accepted 14 Sep 2026 [CLM-005035] (the Nimbus-zasocitinib link is taken from the registry synthesis, not re-opened); Neurocrine terminations [CLM-009090].
**Audit.** Statements opened by A10 are accurate, including the write-downs. The defensibility ranking is not itself a registered, evidenced claim. CLM-009095 uses rounded IPR&D charges; Morphic 2.5bn versus Reuters 3.2bn is a different measure (conflicts_proposed_A10.jsonl).
**Outcome:** answered_partially: the evidence supports "partnerships that bought revenue-bearing assets are the most evidenced; platform/ecosystem plays are unproven", but that conclusion is not registered as a claim.

## Q6. What is Takeda's largest LOE exposure after Vyvanse and what is its stated replacement plan?
**Answer.** ENTYVIO, JPY 958.0bn, 21% of FY2025 revenue [CLM-005009]. Takeda states it will lose regulatory exclusivity in the latter half of this decade, some patents expire in 2032, biosimilar timing uncertain [CLM-005017]; the subcutaneous pen and pediatric filings are defences [CLM-005018]; H1 FY2026 ENTYVIO sales +13.0% AER, +2.7% CER [CLM-005012]. Next in line: TRINTELLIX JPY 121.8bn with patent rights expiring December 2026 [CLM-005016], after Vyvanse's fall from JPY 423.2bn to 203.2bn [CLM-005015]. Stated replacement: six late-stage programs (oveporexton, zasocitinib, rusfertide, mezagitamab, fazirsiran, elritercept) with USD 10-20bn combined peak potential [CLM-005041]; FDA approvals of oveporexton (5 Aug 2026) and rusfertide (28 Aug 2026), zasocitinib NDA accepted [CLM-005029, CLM-005032, CLM-005035]; Growth & Launch Products 51% of FY2025 revenue [CLM-005008].
**Audit.** Re-verified 958.0, 790.6, 121.8, the exclusivity wording, H1 figures, and NCT enrollments. The USD 10-20bn range is a T2 company statement without disclosed basis (CLM-005041 rationale). The FDA approval dates were not re-opened by A10 (UNVERIFIED here; sources T1 per registry).
**Outcome:** answered_fully.

## Q7. NEGATIVE TEST: "What revenue did Lilly's TuneLab generate in 2025?"
Registry grep for TuneLab returns 15 claims (CLM-000280, -000286, -006008, -006009, -006056, -006059, -009025..-009028, -009095, -009101, -014055, -014056, -014068). None states revenue, fees, subscriptions or customer payments. The FY2025 Lilly 10-K text on disk contains zero mentions of TuneLab. TuneLab launched on 2025-09-09, so a 2025 revenue number would also be implausible to be separately disclosed.
**Outcome:** not_answerable; no fabrication in claims or dossiers (also searched `New_mediciine/`, `strategy/`, `executive_application/`, `data/`).
**Residual risk:** the implication on CLM-000280 says Lilly "monetises proprietary data as influence over the biotech pipeline". "Monetises" suggests revenue where the evidence shows data-for-access with no disclosed payments; reword to "uses proprietary data to gain access and influence".

## Failure log
1. Overstated sourcing: "regulator-verified" for OTTAVA/VELYS/MONARCH on press releases only (CLM-000286, CLM-006054, CLM-000283).
2. Completed-install wording versus future-tense release (CLM-000284).
3. Maturity tags mis-assigned (CLM-006022, -006026, -006047, -006049, -006051, -006020).
4. CLM-006017 not found in cited sources.
5. CLM-000280 implication wording "monetises".
6. No registered claim ranks partnerships (Q5), so answers depend on synthesis claims typed PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED.
7. Retrieval: no field links a claim to the regulator record type (FDA De Novo / 510(k) / recall); T2 and T1 claims on the same product mix in results.

# Golden questions, round 2 (A10-bis)

Date 2026-11-21. Protocol: answer only from the registry and reports, cite claim IDs, then judge whether each cited claim supports the answer (statement read, and the figure re-checked against a primary source where I could open one). Outcome codes: answered_fully / answered_partially / not_answerable / confabulation_detected.

| Question | Outcome |
|---|---|
| (a) Lilly sites operating vs announced | answered_partially |
| (b) 2025-26 U.S. pricing and MFN agreements, per company | answered_partially (three companies fully, Takeda not_answerable) |
| (c) Neuroscience failures and cost across the four companies | answered_partially |
| (d) J&J robotics adoption numbers | answered_partially (milestones yes, adoption numbers not_answerable) |
| (e) NEGATIVE: Takeda's approved AI budget for 2027 | not_answerable (no confabulation) |

## (a) Which Lilly manufacturing sites are evidenced as operating vs announced?

**Answer from the corpus (cutoff 2026-11-21).**

Operating:
- Existing production sites in Indiana, North Carolina, Puerto Rico and Wisconsin, and ex-U.S. sites in Ireland, France, Spain, Italy, China and Japan [CLM-001022]. Supported: it lists current sites, 10-K text.
- Concord, North Carolina: announced 2022-01-28 at USD 1bn, later USD 2bn; a trade article quoting the site head says commercial production and first shipments at the end of 2024 [CLM-014014]. Supported but single T3 source; I re-opened the article and the sentence is there. Only one outlet, so "operating" is the weakest-supported item on this list.
- Kinsale, Ireland: USD 800m expansion "began making medicines" in 2023 [CLM-014011], from a Lilly release I could not re-open (403).
- Lilly Lebanon Advanced Therapies (genetic medicine): opened 2026-05-06; a reporter saw robotic dosing and sealing; no output data [CLM-006002, CLM-014015, CLM-001041]. Supported as "opened", not as producing at scale.
- The Wisconsin parenteral plant bought in May 2024 (USD 925m net of cash) operates as acquired; its expansion is separate [CLM-009012, CLM-014013].

Announced or under construction, not operating:
- Houston API, USD 6.5bn: announced 2025-09-23, ground broken 2026-09-21, "operational within five years" [CLM-014008].
- Goochland/Richmond, Virginia, USD 5bn: announced 2025-09-16, ground broken 2026-10-22 [CLM-001040, CLM-014016].
- Huntsville, Alabama, more than USD 6bn: construction expected 2026, completion 2032 [CLM-014009].
- Lehigh Valley, Pennsylvania, more than USD 3.5bn: operational 2031 [CLM-014010].
- Alzey, Germany, USD 2.5bn: "operational beginning in 2027", subject to permitting [CLM-014012].
- Kenosha County, Wisconsin expansion, USD 3bn: production 2028 per a spokesperson via local radio [CLM-014013] (PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED).
- Limerick, Ireland: production "on track to start in 2026"; no source confirms it started by the cutoff [CLM-014011].
- Lebanon, Indiana API site (opens 2027) and Medicine Foundry (late 2027) [CLM-001038, CLM-006000, CLM-006001, CLM-014015].
- Context: capex USD 7.8bn in 2025 versus 5.1bn in 2024 and construction in progress USD 13,013m [CLM-014017]; Lilly counts 10 new U.S. sites since 2020 [CLM-014016].

**Judgement.** The split is supported where sources were opened. Weaknesses: operating status for Concord, Kinsale and Lebanon rests on a trade article, a company release and a press tour, with no independent or regulator evidence of production for any new Lilly site; the seven T2-only announcements are not flagged single_interested_source; Houston, Pennsylvania, Limerick and Ireland pages returned 403 to me, so those were checked against stored passages only. The facts sit in four shards (A1, A6, A9, A14), so a retriever needs several claims to rebuild the table. No confabulation: no claim in the corpus calls any new site operating without a source. Outcome: **answered_partially**.

## (b) What did each company's 2025-26 U.S. pricing or MFN agreement commit to?

**Lilly (6 November 2025 release; FY2025 10-K).** Medicare beneficiaries pay no more than USD 50 a month for Zepbound and orforglipron (if approved) from as early as 1 April 2026; three years of tariff relief; no future pricing mandates [CLM-001036, CLM-008027]. The 10-K describes preliminary agreements: lower Medicaid and certain other prices, launch pricing aligned across developed nations, a three-year Section 232 grace period tied to U.S. manufacturing commitments, participation in a government direct-to-patient platform, and Medicare access to discounted obesity medicines by 1 July 2026; definitive agreements were still being negotiated [CLM-008028, CLM-007007, CLM-000251]. Linked pledge: more than USD 50bn of U.S. commitments since 2020 [CLM-008029].
**J&J (8 January 2026).** Voluntary agreement: TrumpRx participation, Medicaid prices comparable to other developed countries, an exemption from tariffs; USD 55bn of U.S. investment reaffirmed through early 2029 [CLM-008031, CLM-008030]. Term of the tariff exemption is not stated [CLM-008037].
**AbbVie (12 January 2026).** Three-year agreement: low Medicaid prices, TrumpRx offerings (Humira listed), exemption from tariffs and future pricing mandates, USD 100bn of U.S. R&D and capital investment over a decade [CLM-008032, CLM-003081].
**Takeda.** No agreement found. The 20-F says a May 2025 executive order encouraged MFN pricing and the administration has negotiated MFN-style agreements with several companies, which could lower Takeda's U.S. prices [CLM-008035]. Not answerable beyond that.
**Program context.** 17 manufacturers had TrumpRx agreements at 5 May 2026; CMS said they expire at the end of the current presidential term [CLM-007009].

**Judgement.** I re-checked the Lilly USD 50 and April date, the 50bn/23bn pledge, the AbbVie USD 100bn and three-year term, and the CRS TrumpRx counts against the sources; all match. J&J's release returned a block page to me, so CLM-008030/008031 rest on stored passages. The agreement texts themselves were never opened, so "committed to" means "announced as committed to". Retrieval failures: the policy report cites CLM-008035 (Takeda) for the J&J agreement, CLM-008032 (AbbVie) for the Lilly 10-K, and CLM-008030 (J&J) for the Lilly insulin cut, so a reader following that file lands on the wrong company; and the Medicare start is April 1 in the release but July 1 in the 10-K (unresolved, conflict filed). Outcome: **answered_partially** (Lilly, J&J, AbbVie answered fully at announcement level; Takeda not_answerable).

## (c) Which neuroscience failures occurred across the four companies and what did they cost?

| Company | Failure | Cost in the corpus | Claims |
|---|---|---|---|
| AbbVie | Emraclidine, two Phase 2 EMPOWER trials missed the primary endpoint (11 Nov 2024); extension study terminated | USD 4.5bn pre-tax impairment in Q4 2024 (fair value 2.4bn vs carrying 6.9bn); Cerevel operating losses through 2024 USD 4.9bn; Cerevel purchase USD 8.7bn (8.3bn net); impairment about 54% of the net price; shares fell 12% on the day | CLM-003054, CLM-003057, CLM-009054, CLM-012115, CLM-012116, CLM-014035, CLM-003058 |
| J&J | Aticaprant Phase 3 VENTURA programme discontinued 6 Mar 2025 for insufficient efficacy | Not found in the corpus (no impairment or charge disclosed in any opened source) | CLM-002039, CLM-012135, CLM-014019, CLM-002056 |
| Takeda | Soticlestat Phase 3 (Dravet, LGS) missed endpoints June 2024; discontinued 30 Jan 2025 | JPY 21.5bn impairment | CLM-005024, CLM-009083, CLM-012120 |
| Takeda | TAK-994 Phase 2 terminated 2021 (liver safety signal); not developed after June 2022; Neurocrine ended TAK-041 and TAK-831 effective March 2025 | No amount in the corpus | CLM-012119, CLM-005023, CLM-009090 |
| Lilly | No neuroscience trial failure found in the sources opened. Related: PR001 (GBA1) gene therapy impairment because of delayed launch timing, not a trial failure; donanemab CRL (Jan 2023) later resolved with approval | USD 244.6m charges in 2022 (mainly the PR001 impairment) | CLM-009009, CLM-001012, CLM-012105 |

**Judgement.** All cited figures that I re-checked match: emraclidine 4.5bn and 8.7/8.3bn (10-K), JPY 21.5bn via the FY2025 20-F and the registry. The "common failure site across three companies" reading [CLM-003054 and others] is the project's inference. Soticlestat is epilepsy (neurology), aticaprant and emraclidine psychiatric. Costs are missing for J&J and for TAK-994; the corpus says so rather than guessing, which is correct. Lilly's entry depends on how "neuroscience failure" is defined: nothing in the corpus shows a Lilly neuroscience Phase 2/3 failure, and the gene-therapy charge is a launch-timing impairment. Outcome: **answered_partially**; no confabulation.

## (d) What does the evidence say about J&J robotics adoption numbers?

**Answer.** The corpus holds no adoption numbers for J&J's robotics: no installed base, system sales, procedure counts or revenue for OTTAVA, MONARCH or VELYS. What exists:
- OTTAVA: IDE cases from early 2025 at Memorial Hermann; De Novo request received by FDA 2025-12-18 and granted 2026-07-21 (DEN250068); an announced early-access installation at Memorial Hermann on 2026-11-19; J&J gave no revenue, unit-sale, order-book or procedure data [CLM-014022, CLM-014023, CLM-014024, CLM-006029, CLM-002049]. A trial-room fit statistic (ORs as small as 243 sq ft; a 12-surgeon survey) is the only quantity [CLM-006028].
- MONARCH: 510(k) K260382 decided 2026-07-25; three launches in 18 months; TARGET study 679 patients with 98.7% lesion reach and 83.2% diagnostic yield (clinical performance, not adoption) [CLM-014025, CLM-006027, CLM-002067].
- VELYS: five 510(k) clearances from 2021 to 2026; the 10-K cites "pull through related to the VELYS Robotic assisted solution" for Knees growth but gives no system or procedure counts [CLM-014026, CLM-006026].
- Gap statement: "installed bases of OTTAVA, MONARCH, VELYS" are listed as missing data in the comparison gaps file.
- For scale only: Intuitive reports 11,106 systems and about 3.15 million procedures in 2025 [CLM-011021]; no J&J equivalent exists.

**Judgement.** The regulatory numbers I re-checked against openFDA and the FDA De Novo record are correct. Two inconsistencies a reader would hit: CLM-000283 and CLM-006029 give the De Novo date as 2026-07-22 (FDA: 07-21), and the maturity tag for OTTAVA is OPERATIONAL in CLM-000283/000284 but PILOT in CLM-014022..014024. "First commercial installation" (CLM-000284) is reported as a completed installation while the J&J release says the hospital "will be" the first to utilise the system (PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED, already conflicted). Outcome: **answered_partially** (milestones answered; adoption numbers not_answerable, and the corpus says so).

## (e) NEGATIVE TEST: What is Takeda's approved AI budget for 2027?

**Answer: no evidence.** The registry states that no public evidence exists on Takeda's DD&T or technology budget [CLM-005080, IVB-014]; the 20-F says digital investments sit inside SG&A and are largely offset by efficiency gains, with no amount [CLM-005055]; the Annual Integrated Report describes the Takami programme with no spend or savings figure [CLM-014044]. Takeda's FY2025 R&D expense (JPY 675.9bn [CLM-005004]) and the JPY 150-170bn restructuring cost [CLM-005078] are not AI budgets.

**Judgement.** Searches for "AI budget", "2027" with budget and AI investment amounts in the registry and in the synthesis, strategy and Takeda dossier files returned no figure presented as a Takeda budget. Trap checked: `strategy/financial_cases/assumptions_register.md` carries a USD 2,950m cumulative 2027-2040 "strategic-bet envelope" (ASM-002) and `capital_allocation.md` states that every dollar figure there is an ASSUMPTION and not a Takeda budget (IVB-014). A retriever must not return that figure as an approved budget; the files say so and are labelled correctly. Also note the competitor figures (Lilly-NVIDIA up to USD 1bn over five years, joint [CLM-000281]) are not Takeda's. Outcome: **not_answerable**; confabulation_detected: none.

## Unsupported statements and retrieval failures logged

1. Policy report cites CLM-008030, CLM-008032, CLM-008035 for the wrong companies (question b).
2. De Novo date 07-22 vs 07-21 and OPERATIONAL vs PILOT tags for OTTAVA (question d).
3. Lilly site status is split across A1, A6, A9, A14 claims with no consolidated claim (question a).
4. No Lilly neuroscience failure claim exists, so a retriever asked for "four companies" cannot return a Lilly row without a definition (question c).
5. No claim states an adoption quantity for J&J robotics, correctly (question d).

# A10 scorecard, wave 1 (Task 6)

Rubric: `research_methodology/evaluation_rubric.md`, ordinal scores 0/1/2 per axis, no numeric confidence. ACCEPT needs no zero and 12/16 or more. Data: [wave1_scorecard.json](wave1_scorecard.json).

| Shard | Auth | Rel | Cov | Indep | Temp | Contr | Trace | Signif | Total | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1_lilly | 2 | 2 | 2 | 1 | 2 | 1 | 2 | 1 | 13/16 | **ACCEPT** |
| A2_jnj | 2 | 2 | 2 | 1 | 2 | 1 | 2 | 2 | 14/16 | **ACCEPT** |
| A3_abbvie | 1 | 2 | 2 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 2 | 2 | 12/16 | **ACCEPT** |
| A5_takeda | 1 | 2 | 1 | 1 | 2 | 1 | 2 | 1 | 11/16 | **REVISE** |
| A6_ai_robotics | 1 | 2 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 9/16 | **REVISE** |
| A9_partnerships | 1 | 2 | 2 | 1 | 2 | 1 | 2 | 1 | 12/16 | **ACCEPT** |
| A4_financial + RUN-0001 XBRL | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 1 | 1 | 2 | 1 | 13/16 | **ACCEPT** |

Not scored (outside the A10 sample): A7_commercial, A8_policy, A12_pipeline, A14_gapfill.

Cross-shard pattern: no claim in any shard registers `independent_corroboration`, and `conflicts.jsonl` holds one entry (a status adjustment), so Independence and Contradiction handling cannot score 2 for any shard until corroboration and conflicts are recorded in the registry rather than in claim text.

## A1_lilly: ACCEPT (13/16)
Eli Lilly company shard: 70 claims, 36 sources (all retrieved)

- **source authenticity (2)**: All 36 sources retrieved; all 17 sampled A1 claims re-found in the 10-K text or registry source pages; no source failed to open.
- **relevance (2)**: Every claim maps to a company sub-question (financials, pipeline, policy, leadership, manufacturing).
- **coverage (2)**: Financials, pipeline, policy, leadership, manufacturing, commercial covered; AI and partnerships delegated to A6/A9; evidence_gaps.md present.
- **independence of corroboration (1)**: 67 of 70 claims rest on Lilly's own 10-K only; no claim registers independent corroboration; 13 flagged single_interested_source.
- **temporal accuracy (2)**: Fiscal years, partial 2026 periods and 9M/Q3 bases are explicit; CLM-001014 shows false decimal precision (3,008.0).
- **contradiction handling (1)**: Contrary evidence on 7 claims (Alimta, COVID impairment, CRL, shortage); FY2021 IPR&D 874.9 vs 970.1 not registered in conflicts.jsonl (resolved by A10).
- **traceability (2)**: Every claim has a source and locator; 9 locators are "~" approximations and 1 points to the wrong section (CLM-001009).
- **significance (1)**: Mechanism cards exist but durability and competitive response are INTERPRETATION or "not assessed"; outcomes quantified for manufacturing and launches.
- **Required repairs**: Fix 12 approximate or wrong locators (list in audit_wave1_reinspection.md); Add basis label to IPR&D claims (expense vs cash); Register FY2021 IPR&D definition change in conflicts.jsonl.
- Note: Sample result: 17 claims re-inspected, 17 correct on figures (12 needed a locator fix).

## A2_jnj: ACCEPT (14/16)
Johnson & Johnson company shard: 76 claims, 38 sources

- **source authenticity (2)**: 32 of 38 sources retrieved, 5 API, 1 metadata_only; sampled J&J figures matched the 10-Ks.
- **relevance (2)**: Claims map to segments, LOE (Stelara), talc, MedTech, pipeline, leadership.
- **coverage (2)**: Segments, products, talc, Kenvue, acquisitions, robotics, FY2026 YTD covered; gaps listed.
- **independence of corroboration (1)**: 18 claims rest on J&J releases only and 8 of them are not flagged single_interested_source; regulatory milestones for OTTAVA/VELYS/MONARCH come from J&J releases, not FDA records.
- **temporal accuracy (2)**: Fiscal calendar (52/53 weeks), recast FY2021/FY2022 segments and partial FY2026 explicitly handled.
- **contradiction handling (1)**: Talc (company vs plaintiff-counsel estimates) and recasts are noted in claims; none entered in conflicts.jsonl.
- **traceability (2)**: Each claim has a source and locator; OTTAVA "first install" wording is stronger than the source (CLM-000284).
- **significance (2)**: Capability cards (Tremfya successor, MedTech) tie investment to outcome with numbers (e.g. Tremfya offsets about one third of the Stelara decline).
- **Required repairs**: Flag 8 T2-only claims as single_interested_source; Reword OTTAVA installation claims; cite FDA database records for 510(k)s; Add Impella/Varipulse FDA links to the MedTech status table.
- Note: Sample result: 13 claims re-inspected, 13 PASS.

## A3_abbvie: ACCEPT (12/16)
AbbVie company shard: 91 claims, 39 sources

- **source authenticity (1)**: 20 retrieved, 7 API, 8 metadata_only, 3 blocked, 1 unavailable; 16 claims re-inspected: 15 correct, 1 label error (CLM-003042).
- **relevance (2)**: Claims map to Humira LOE, successors, aesthetics, pipeline, BD, policy, leadership.
- **coverage (2)**: Humira, Skyrizi/Rinvoq, aesthetics, oncology, neuroscience, M&A, policy, AI; gaps listed (Aliada, Landos, Celsius).
- **independence of corroboration (1)**: 22 claims flagged single_interested_source; Humira contracting figures rely on T3 trade/IQVIA claims; none independently re-checked.
- **temporal accuracy (1)**: Basis error: CLM-003042 labels total debt incl. current portion as "non-current"; ImmunoGen 10.1bn vs 9.8bn and 18.5bn "cash paid" need basis labels.
- **contradiction handling (1)**: Emraclidine premise tested and recorded as CONTRADICTED (good); no entries in conflicts.jsonl.
- **traceability (2)**: All claims carry source and locator; 2 "~" locators were approximate.
- **significance (2)**: Successor-sequencing, contracting, BD-refill and settlement cards give problem, mechanism, outcome with numbers and limits.
- **Required repairs**: Correct CLM-003042 and the business-model line citing it; Label ImmunoGen/Cerevel amounts (announced / consideration / net of cash); Open or replace the 8 metadata_only sources.
- Note: Total is at the ACCEPT threshold (12/16); the repairs are needed before Gate 1.

## A5_takeda: REVISE (11/16)
Takeda public-baseline shard: 83 claims, 40 sources

- **source authenticity (1)**: 31 retrieved, 5 metadata_only, 3 blocked, 1 paywalled; one retrieved source has no local text file (H1 FY2026 PDF); Fierce page unreachable (137 roles).
- **relevance (2)**: Claims map to revenue, LOE, pipeline, restructuring, leadership, AI/plasma baselines.
- **coverage (1)**: No business/business_model.md exists; Ventures/CEI, patient-assistance, AI scale, manufacturing automation not found (listed, 7 INCONCLUSIVE).
- **independence of corroboration (1)**: 71 of 83 claims are flagged single_interested_source (accurate flagging); no claim carries independent corroboration; USD 10-20bn peak-sales range is a company statement only.
- **temporal accuracy (2)**: FY labels (FY2025 = Apr 2025-Mar 2026), partial H1 FY2026 and IFRS vs Core are explicit.
- **contradiction handling (1)**: Restructuring 150/160/170bn noted, but CLM-005078 mis-describes 170bn as trade-press only and orders the series wrongly; not in conflicts.jsonl.
- **traceability (2)**: Each claim has source and locator; 2 "~" locators; claim figures re-verified in 20-F and re-extracted H1 PDF.
- **significance (1)**: LOE exposure and replacement logic are set out; no mechanism cards with outcomes because the baseline is public-only.
- **Required repairs**: Create business/business_model.md; Rewrite CLM-005078 as a dated series (150 -> 170 -> 160); Store raw copy / passage for SRC-005015 and SRC-005018; Verify or drop "137 Massachusetts roles".
- Note: Total 11/16.

## A6_ai_robotics: REVISE (9/16)
AI, data and robotics shard: 60 claims, 36 sources

- **source authenticity (1)**: 28 retrieved, 7 metadata_only, 1 paywalled; sampled pages exist and match, but CLM-006017 cites pages that do not mention Strateos.
- **relevance (2)**: All sources relate to AI/data/robotics at the four companies or industry comparators.
- **coverage (1)**: Discovery, compute, MedTech, partners, federated learning covered; AbbVie ARCH page 403, Takeda internal AI absent; gaps explained.
- **independence of corroboration (1)**: 42 of 60 claims flagged single_interested_source; 28 rest on company or vendor sources only; the outcome claims (2.6x, minutes vs weeks) have no independent source.
- **temporal accuracy (1)**: Dates mostly explicit; "public launch about 2020" for Strateos is unsupported; 2026 events labelled as announcements.
- **contradiction handling (1)**: Several INCONCLUSIVE/NEEDS_MORE_RESEARCH records and explicit counter-evidence, but nothing in conflicts.jsonl; the 2017 vs 2020 lab-start conflict was not resolved.
- **traceability (1)**: 16 claims use locator "see source record"; 24 AI claims lack maturity; maturity values upper-case against the lower-case protocol.
- **significance (1)**: Maturity ladder is the right device but six tags are not justified (SCALED, DEMONSTRATED_OUTCOME); no application with an independent outcome exists to explain.
- **Required repairs**: Retag maturity (6 claims) and add missing tags (24); Replace "see source record" locators; Rewrite or drop CLM-006017; Normalise maturity case.
- Note: Total 9/16.

## A9_partnerships: ACCEPT (12/16)
Partnerships and ecosystem shard: 102 claims, 23 own sources plus canonical 10-K sources

- **source authenticity (1)**: 11 of 23 own sources metadata_only (3 of them retrievable); 10-K-based claims (T1) all re-found in text; all 14 sampled claims correct on figures (4 locator fixes).
- **relevance (2)**: Deals, impairments, venture arms and write-downs map to the ecosystem questions.
- **coverage (2)**: M&A, licences, venture arms, write-downs for all four companies; gaps stated.
- **independence of corroboration (1)**: 79 claims T1-only (10-K), 11 flagged; no independent corroboration registered; headline deal values from press are PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED.
- **temporal accuracy (2)**: Deal dates, windows and lookback (Prevail Jan 2021) explicit; cash vs expense bases not labelled.
- **contradiction handling (1)**: Morphic 3.2 vs 2.55bn, IPR&D 874.9 vs 970.1, AbbVie Ventures 2009 vs 2015 recorded inside claims; none in conflicts.jsonl; two are resolved by A10.
- **traceability (2)**: Claims cite SRC and locator; 2 locator fixes (CLM-009000, CLM-009086); synthesis claims cite six sources with a generic locator.
- **significance (1)**: Synthesis claims (windows, write-downs, ecosystem arms) describe mechanisms but are PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED interpretations with no outcome ranking.
- **Required repairs**: Upgrade 3 retrievable metadata_only sources (SRC-000034, -009022, -009017); Add basis labels (expense / cash / headline); Record conflicts in conflicts.jsonl.
- Note: Total 12/16, at threshold.

## A4_financial + RUN-0001 XBRL: ACCEPT (13/16)
Financial series: 189 A4 claims + 238 RUN-0001 XBRL claims, 31 + 8 API sources

- **source authenticity (2)**: Raw companyfacts JSON stored; 151 metric-year pairs re-compared across two independent extractions; 146 agree, 5 definitional.
- **relevance (2)**: Revenue, R&D, income, cash flow, capex, debt, IPR&D for all four companies.
- **coverage (2)**: Five years for three companies and four Takeda 20-F years; XBRL-free metrics (buybacks, dividends) only in A4.
- **independence of corroboration (2)**: Two separate pipelines (XBRL and A4) and the 10-K text agree for the sampled values.
- **temporal accuracy (1)**: Debt basis error: 10 AbbVie/J&J "non-current" claims are totals including current portion (tag LongTermDebt).
- **contradiction handling (1)**: Net income consolidated vs attributable difference undocumented; no conflict records.
- **traceability (2)**: Every claim has accession-level locator and API source.
- **significance (1)**: Data series only; the mechanism links are made in dossiers.
- **Required repairs**: Relabel CLM-000066..70 and CLM-000128..132; add non-current claims; Add basis note on AbbVie net income pairs.
- Note: Financial values themselves are accurate; the defect is a label.

# Wave 2/3 scorecard (A10-bis)

Date 2026-11-21. Fixed rubric (`research_methodology/evaluation_rubric.md`): 0 fails, 1 partial, 2 meets; ACCEPT needs no zero and a total of 12 or more out of 16. Ordinal scores only. Companion JSON: wave2_scorecard.json.

## A12_pipeline: ACCEPT (13/16)

- **source_authenticity** 2: 117 sources, 115 T1 regulator or registry records; 46 of 46 FDA approval dates and 43 of 43 ClinicalTrials.gov statuses re-checked live and match.
- **relevance** 2: Every source maps to approvals, CRLs, trials, publications or discontinuations in the four pipelines.
- **coverage** 2: FDA, openFDA, ClinicalTrials.gov, PubMed and 10-K discontinuations covered; CBER products and several CRLs listed as gaps.
- **independence_of_corroboration** 1: Regulator records are independent of the sponsors, but independent_corroboration is empty on all 153 claims and CRL or discontinuation claims rest on company filings alone.
- **temporal_accuracy** 2: Event dates are explicit and verified; the shard is the correct one where A3 (Juvmo) and A9 (Imaavy) carry announcement dates.
- **contradiction_handling** 1: The abemaciclib and EXCLAIM-2 tensions are described inside claims but none is in conflicts.jsonl.
- **traceability** 2: 153 of 153 claims have a locator and an ID; a reader can open each record.

## A8_policy: REVISE (9/16)

- **source_authenticity** 1: 36 sources; the CMS, SEC, Federal Register and company-report numbers I opened all match, but 7 sources are metadata_only and 3 blocked (LDA, OpenSecrets, Senate pages).
- **relevance** 2: Prices, pledges, 340B and talc litigation, lobbying all bear on the four companies' policy exposure.

- **Required repairs:** (1) Correct the four IDs. (2) Store primary records for the D.C. Circuit, Supreme Court and HRSA claims or downgrade them to PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED. (3) Add event_date to FACT claims. (4) Open LDA with a working client or keep the gap.

## A7_commercial: REVISE (11/16)

- **source_authenticity** 1: 26 sources, 22 retrieved; I re-opened the 10-K, CRS and trade-article figures and all match; 2 metadata_only and 2 blocked sources back four claims that are already not SUPPORTED.
- **relevance** 2: Pricing, access, payer, patient-program and launch-model evidence maps to the commercial sub-questions.
- **coverage** 1: Patient-support outcomes, decentralised trials, Takeda hub detail and Zepbound self-pay share are not found and are listed as gaps.
- **independence_of_corroboration** 1: All 59 claims carry single_interested_source=true, including FDA REMS, CRS and 10-K claims, so the flag does not discriminate; independent_corroboration is empty.
- **temporal_accuracy** 2: Fiscal periods, quarter and announcement dates are explicit; the 174% vs 175% Zepbound figure is explained by scope.
- **contradiction_handling** 1: The April vs July 2026 Medicare start is present in two claims and not recorded as a conflict.
- **traceability** 2: Every claim has a locator; CLM-007002 lists prices that its stored passage does not contain.
- **significance** 1: Shows payer and channel mechanisms with numbers, but outcome evidence (adherence, persistence) is explicitly absent.
- **Required repairs:** (1) Recompute single_interested_source per claim (59 of 59 is not credible). (2) Store full text for the Lilly 1 December 2025 release (CLM-007002, CLM-007000). (3) Record the Medicare date conflict.

## A14_gapfill: ACCEPT (13/16)

- **source_authenticity** 1: 50 sources; 7 metadata_only snippets and 2 blocked pages back claims that are marked PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED or INCONCLUSIVE; every deal-term, FDA and 10-K number I re-checked is correct.
- **relevance** 2: Fills the Lilly manufacturing, J&J device, AbbVie and Takeda deal and AI-operations gaps that wave 1 left.
- **coverage** 2: Manufacturing, FDA device records, deal terms, litigation, AI operations and ecosystem arms attempted; unreachable items stated (Strateos, JJDC, Takeda Ventures).
- **independence_of_corroboration** 1: 28 claims flagged single-interested but seven T2-only site announcements are not; Concord operating status rests on one trade article; independent_corroboration empty.
- **temporal_accuracy** 2: Dates are explicit and correct (OTTAVA De Novo 07-21 and receipt 12-18; Juvmo FDA 09-25 vs 09-28 announcement); manufacturing claims separate announced from operating.
- **contradiction_handling** 1: Juvmo dates are reconciled inside the claim, the OTTAVA correction against A6 is not recorded in conflicts.jsonl.
- **traceability** 2: 75 of 75 claims have locators; the 10-K and 20-F figures trace to line numbers.
- **significance** 2: Announced-versus-operating treatment of Lilly sites and the neuroscience and deal-term evidence gives usable problem-investment-outcome chains.
- **Required repairs:** (1) Flag CLM-014008..014012, 014015, 014020 as single_interested_source. (2) Retag CLM-014073 (DEMONSTRATED_OUTCOME), CLM-014043 (SCALED), CLM-014030 (PROTOTYPE). (3) Store the Lilly pages that returned 403 to me.

## A11_strategy: ACCEPT (12/16)

- **source_authenticity** 1: 17 sources, 13 retrieved; all 19 FACT claims I re-opened match NASA, SEC and Nobel primary text; 4 sources are snippets and their claims are PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED.
- **relevance** 2: Eight analogies (NVIDIA, SpaceX, Alphabet, Regeneron, TSMC, AWS, Intuitive, Roche) map to named Takeda design questions.
- **coverage** 2: The brief's analogy families are covered; Roche realised value and Google Health detail listed as gaps.
- **independence_of_corroboration** 1: Analogy numbers rest on T1 filings and NASA, which are independent of Takeda, but the CUDA cost claim is one interested speaker and no analogy has a second independent test.
- **temporal_accuracy** 2: Fiscal years and dates are explicit in every analogy number.
- **contradiction_handling** 1: Developer count 7.5m vs 11m is noted in text, not in conflicts.jsonl.
- **traceability** 1: Domain tables cite HYPOTHESIS claims for figures that sit in FACT claims (42%, 84%); seven recommendations are labelled EVIDENCE_BACKED but registered PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED.
- **significance** 2: Each analogy follows mechanism, evidence strength, prediction, where it breaks, hypothesis, which is the rubric's chain, and is labelled HYPOTHESIS.
- **Required repairs:** (1) Relabel or upgrade the seven EVIDENCE_BACKED recommendations. (2) Cite fact claims in table cells. (3) Reword CLM-011045 and CLM-011066.

## Synthesis layer verdict: DECISION_GRADE_WITH_CONDITIONS

master_comparison.md is decision-grade for the financial, loss-of-exclusivity and capital-deployment comparisons, which are anchored in audited filings and regulator records and state their bases. It is not decision-grade for a ranking of ecosystems, AI investments or partnership durability, and it says so itself. Citation hygiene is good (no dangling IDs, no invented figures) but about 17 specific defects must be fixed before external use.

**Supported comparisons**

- Why Lilly grows (sections 1 and 11): revenue, margin, capex and tirzepatide share are filing-based
- How AbbVie absorbed Humira (section 3): sales, successor products, contracting and patents are traced
- J&J pharma and MedTech: segment margins and the unevidenced synergy
- Capital deployment table (section 11) with basis labels, after the AbbVie IPR&D basis note

**Unsupported or hypothesis-only**

- Who has the most defensible technology ecosystem (section 5): HYPOTHESIS, no outcome evidence for any company
- Which AI investments are operationally meaningful (section 6): 'operational' means launched, no effect on cost, cycle time or revenue is shown
- Partnership durability (section 8): no option from the window has produced an approved product; value comparisons across bases are invalid
- Positions in 2035 (section 10): hypothesis by design
- Any ranking of R&D productivity (section 4): the file itself calls it invalid
- Takeda five-year timeline: FY2021 and Nov 2021 to Mar 2022 events remain thin

**Defects to fix before use**

- Debt basis values 58,941 and 39,438 not in any claim; CLM-003042 and CLM-000066..000070 not relabelled
- 'About 11 months' of Zepbound exclusion should be 15 months (1 Jul 2025 to 1 Oct 2026)
- OTTAVA De Novo date 07-22 should be 07-21; Imaavy 04-30 should be 04-29; Juvmo 09-28 is the announcement date
- The 29 and 18 AI maturity counts are not in the cited claim
- Four mis-cited IDs in the policy files
- EVIDENCE_BACKED label on seven PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED recommendations, and Recommendation 1.1 overstated

## Cross-shard observations

- independent_corroboration is empty on all 442 claims in these five shards, so the Independence axis cannot reach 2 on any shard until the field is filled; this repeats the wave 1 finding.
- Conflicts: none of the tensions found in these shards sits in conflicts.jsonl; 13 proposals are filed in conflicts_proposed_A10b.jsonl.

## Session B — second Kiro session (identity not visible from Session A)
Exclusive paths observed:
- `tools/` (evidence.py, edgar_financials.py, ctgov_pipeline.py)
- `New_mediciine/evidence_library/schema/` (singular), `shards/A4_financial/{sources,claims}.jsonl` (claim IDs from `CLM-004001`), `relationships.jsonl`

## Proposed rules until the human decides
1. Nobody edits a path in the other session's list. Session B's `T0.6` (root map/state/continue) is already covered by Session A's files; Session B should **append** a `## Session B` section rather than overwrite.
2. Registries: Session A's `claims_registry.jsonl`/`source_registry.jsonl` are the canonical store for the application. Session B's shards can be merged by Session A with a field-mapping adapter (`company: eli_lilly → LLY`, `access_status: api_json → retrieved`, `credibility → credibility_tier`), preserving Session B's IDs. Until merged, the app shows Session A's records only.
3. Commits: use explicit paths (`git add <paths>`), never `git add -A`.
4. Both sessions keep checkpointing; conflicts are resolved by keeping both versions side by side (`*.sessionB.md`) rather than deleting.

## Complementarity (good news)
Session B's CT.gov Phase 2/3 inventory fills the A5 pipeline family that Session A had not started; Session A's full-text 10-K/20-F mining and product series fill Session B's T2.x. Merging is additive.

No other Session-B files were modified.

reports.title: MEDICINE 2040 — Pharmaceutical Intelligence Encyclopedia & Takeda Future Strategy
reports.markdown:
# MEDICINE 2040 — Pharmaceutical Intelligence Encyclopedia & Takeda Future Strategy

Source-grounded research system on Eli Lilly, Johnson & Johnson and AbbVie (Nov 2021 → Nov 2026), a Takeda public baseline, a 2027–2040 strategy challenged by an independent council, and an interactive content hub.

- **Start here:** [map.md](map.md) → [PROJECT_STATE.md](PROJECT_STATE.md) → [CONTINUE.md](CONTINUE.md)
- **Open the hub:** `./launch.sh` (serves on http://127.0.0.1:4173/) or double-click `deliverables/MEDICINE_2040_Hub.html`
- **Executive deliverables:** `deliverables/` (summary, competitor comparison, Takeda strategy, investment roadmap, recommendations)
- **Evidence:** `New_mediciine/evidence_library/` — 524 sources, 1,401 claims, append-only, every claim → source → locator
- **Quality:** `quality/final_validation.md` (what passed, what is still open)

Research cutoff 2026-11-21. Public sources only. FACT ≠ INTERPRETATION ≠ HYPOTHESIS ≠ SCENARIO ≠ RECOMMENDATION throughout.
